Not yet named. Rakshasa are named at their first successful hunt; before that they are simply 'the young one'. Dangerous, and aware it has something to prove.
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_shyena_l: Territorial boss; might perks give enrage-style bonuses when below 50% HP
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_shyena_s: Aerial dive attacker; flying tag; martial_arts perks give first-strike on initial dive
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_uluka_ni: Fires black magic from range in darkness; high awareness gives initiative advantage
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_uluka_om: Ill omen debuffer; performance perks like heckle_the_will and stage_fright lower party morale/stats
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_vanara_e: Troop director; leadership perks give formation bonuses to nearby vanara
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_vanara_s: Throws rocks and alchemical bombs; taunt forces party member to attack it; TODO: confuse special attack
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_varaha_c: Tusk charge; maces perk concussive_force gives knockback on crits
fields.enemies:animal:archetype:animal_varaha_e: Sounder tactician; heals allies via medicine perks; raises aggression when sounder-mates are wounded
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_any_pred: Generic predator encounter — one devil-tier hunter, region-appropriate
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_any_swar: Generic swarm — shade-tier insects or small creatures
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_boss_sim: The King of Beasts — boss encounter guarding the portal. Solo but with two varaha honour guard.
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_converge: Rare multi-faction encounter at zone borders — predator plus prey in uneasy company
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_dura_bur: Hard — burrower teleports to flank while soldiers hold the line
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_forest_m: Cross-zone predator encounter — rakshasa and marjara sharing territory briefly
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_gana_ful: Runner leads, howler provides enchantment cover
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_kapota_f: Large flock — primarily defensive, skirmishes if threatened. Usually neutral.
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_karka_ve: Karka guarding a thermal vent — one heavy frontliner, one support crusher
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_khadga_p: Two khadga — rare but devastating charge encounter
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_makara_t: Solo boss-tier — slow, enormous, devastating. Rare encounter.
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_makara_w: A makara escorted by matsya — the current-rider positions the attack
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_marjara_: Marjara ambush — both start hidden, ambusher flanks
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_matsya_a: Matsya with a current-rider laying down water suppression
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_matsya_s: Fast, numerous — skirmisher swarm from below
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_meadow_m: Cross-zone meadow encounter — yaksha-led mixed force
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_mriga_he: Grazing herd — usually neutral, dangerous only if pressed
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_mriga_st: Rutting bucks holding a clearing; sentinels on the edge
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_naga_cou: Hard ocean encounter — full naga formation
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_naga_sor: Lone caster — opens with water/space magic, retreats behind the warrior
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_ocean_mi: Cross-zone ocean patrol — naga leading a matsya screen
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_patanga_: Ascetic with a seeker escort — the ascetic may be neutral depending on approach
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_rakshasa: Solitary hunter — high threat multiplier, acts alone
Boss-tier rakshasa alone — the maneater does not need help
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_shyena_d: Fast pair attack from above — high initiative, dive on the first turn
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_shyena_l: Shyena lord alone — stationary on a height, attacks if approached
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_shyena_w: Lord and two stoopers — aerial formation, attacks in sequence
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_uluka_om: Omen alone — rare, high-threat. Uses black magic and debuffs.
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_vanara_e: Elder holds back, skirmishers pressure — elder uses white/earth magic if engaged
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_varaha_e: Varaha elder leads a sounder — elder uses earth magic support
fields.enemies:animal:encounter:animal_yaksha_c: Yaksha shaman directing a guardian — territorial challenge
fields.enemies:domain:encounter:cloud_naga_pack: Naga courtiers of the Cloud Palace — aerial-adapted warriors and sorcerers
fields.enemies:domain:notes#design_archetypes: Archetypes for domain-specific encounters. These enemies are realm-agnostic — they appear in rare domain events regardless of which realm the party is in.
fields.enemies:domain:notes#design_encounters: Fixed encounters for domain events. Realm-agnostic — these spawn regardless of which realm the party is currently in.
fields.enemies:hell:archetype:hell_tormented_sh: Reworked: now a true shade-tier enemy (was formerly a devil-tier caster)
fields.enemies:hell:encounter:blizzard_patrol#d: Cold_hell mixed: blue devils with sleet imps harassing ranged
fields.enemies:hell:encounter:demon_elite#desig: Bone arena champion — a hardened hell_demon_elite with warrior escort
fields.enemies:hell:encounter:devil_with_imps#d: Tough devil flanked by flying imps
fields.enemies:hell:encounter:fire_brigade#desi: Fire_hell mixed: red devils plus smoke imps
fields.enemies:hell:encounter:imp_court#design: A devil with imp escorts — classic mixed encounter
fields.enemies:hell:encounter:shade_and_devil#d: A devil commanding a pair of shades — mixed encounter
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_bone_h: Heavy construct assembled from many skeletons. Reassembles once after death, returning at 50% HP after one turn. Needs 'reassemble' perk implementation.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_carrio: Slow bloated tank. Explodes on death dealing rot/disease damage in an area. Needs explodes_on_death behavior in combat AI.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_charne: Stronger incorporeal from the charnel grounds — more focused and more dangerous than a lost preta.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_lost_p: Dissolving consciousnesses barely present in the physical world. Analogous to hell's tormented shade. Appear in all three zones.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_rolang: The rare preserved rolang - alchemical or yogic arts kept the body intact. Rot caster and support.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_swamp_: Attaches to a target and drains HP/stamina per turn until removed. Needs attach behavior in combat AI.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_vampir: Life drain on hit; in mixed encounters, healing feeds the paired vetala. Needs life_steal behavior in combat AI.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:archetype:hg_vultur: Prioritizes low-HP or downed targets. Needs scavenger targeting behavior in combat AI.
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:bone_horr: Solo bone horror — massive animated skeleton, anchor of the undead mob
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:bone_pack: Skelepuppies with a bone horror keeping them in line
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:carrion_f: Vultures and carrion dogs — opportunistic scavengers with no vetala leader
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:charnel_w: Stronger incorporeal haunt of the charnel grounds
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:grave_hou: Skelepuppy packs that roam the graveyard
A full pack of grave hounds — fast, numerous, and vicious
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:hungry_wr: Dense cluster of lost pretas drawn to the charnel grounds by the smell of blood
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:insatiabl: Realm boss — the Insatiable King with two charnel wraith courtiers
Sated variant — offered food/honesty first, fights alone with reduced power
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:lost_pret: Dissolving spirits drifting through all zones — early/filler encounter
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:mud_golem: A mass of rot and earth animated by the swamp — carrion worms packed into a shambling form
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:rolang_an: A preserved ancient directing newly-risen dead
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:rolang_wi: Shamblers advancing behind a screen of centipedes
Shamblers using carrion worms as living siege weapons
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:rotting_s: Hard stationary — a preserved ancient with worm bodyguards
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:skeleton_: Hard encounter — full skeleton formation with bone horror anchor
Skeletons roosting with harpies in the upper graveyard reaches
Boss duel — fight stops when skeleton king drops to 10% HP (special win condition)
A mage animating a bone horror as bodyguard
Casters sheltering behind a skelepuppy screen
Classic skeleton formation: sword, bow, skelepuppy screen
Two skeleton warriors — basic graveyard disturbance encounter
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:swamp_ver: Early encounter — pure support-tier creatures, no faction leader
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:swamp_wra: Hard swamp encounter — drowned rolang with leech swarm
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:undead_co: All three factions present — rare encounter where territories overlap
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:vetala_no: Hard encounter — vetala elder holding court
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:encounter:vetala_wi: Vetala with bats and dogs — air and ground pressure
fields.enemies:hungry_ghost:notes#design_archet: Hungry Ghost realm (Pretaloka) enemy archetypes. Three playable factions each have devil-tier combat variants plus shade/imp-tier support creatures. Mechanics marked with _comment may need new perks or combat AI behaviors.
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan#text:
No one told you the tree existed, but you found it anyway. The banyan's aerial roots form a labyrinth; its canopy covers a quarter mile in every direction. The Vanara Elder sits in the first great fork, weaving something from spider silk and what you eventually realize is solidified starlight.

The tree has the attention of something older than itself. Earth magic and summoning traditions have always known about this place.
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan/leave#resul: You leave the labyrinth of roots behind. The canopy covers you until you are out of the grove, and then the light returns all at once.
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan/leave#title: Walk away from the ancient tree
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan/meditate#re: You sit with your back against a root as wide as a wall and close your eyes. The tree breathes. You breathe. After a time — you cannot say how long — something shifts: a sense of patience that is not your own, accumulated over centuries, seeping in through the bark.
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan/meditate#ti: Sit beneath the roots in silence
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan/study#resul: The Elder looks down from the fork with unhurried eyes. She names a price for her teaching. It is not small.
fields.events:animal:ancient_banyan/study#title: Approach the Elder and ask to study
fields.events:animal:animal_black_lodge#text: The entrance is low, partially hidden by undergrowth. You would miss it if you were not looking. Inside: incense so thick it stings, a khatvanga propped against the wall streaming black ribbons. The practitioner here works alone, without students, without oversight — the animal realm affords the privacy that the human realm did not. They turn when you enter, without surprise.
fields.events:animal:animal_black_lodge/learn#r: A hand gestures to a list scratched into the bark of the wall. Spells. Prices. No preamble.
fields.events:animal:animal_black_lodge/leave#r: You step back into the daylight. The khatvanga watches you leave.
fields.events:animal:animal_boss_simha_king#tex:
The oldest part of the forest is where he sits — where the trees are so wide you could sleep in their roots and the canopy blocks all direct sun. The simha king does not rise when you approach.

He is the largest lion you have ever imagined possible. His mane is the color of old wood. He is already ancient in legends that are themselves old. The portal to the Human Realm shimmers behind him in the roots of the oldest tree.

He is not blocking it, exactly. He is simply here, as he has always been here — at the threshold, at the end of the animal realm, where the path changes.

His gaze crosses your party without hurry, taking careful measure.
fields.events:animal:animal_boss_simha_king/bow:
You approach slowly and bow — low and long. When you rise, he has not moved, but something in his posture has changed: the calculation has left it.

'You have learned something here,' he says, in a voice like the ground settling. 'Go forward. Don't waste it.'

He stands and walks aside. The portal is clear.
fields.events:animal:animal_boss_simha_king/cir:
The gap is there. It is exactly where you judged it to be, and it closes while you are still committed to it.

He has not moved quickly. He has simply been in the place you were going to be, for some time, waiting to see whether you had understood the ground as well as you believed.

'No,' he says, almost kindly. 'Again, or not at all.'

You study the roots, the shadows, the angles. There is a gap — not much of one, but enough.

As you slip through, his voice reaches you from the center of the clearing: 'Clever. But you'll find cleverness has limits, further on.'

He does not pursue.
Attempt to find another way through
fields.events:animal:animal_boss_simha_king/fig:
He rises slowly — no urgency, no anger. He has simply agreed to your terms. His voice carries one last note before the charge:

'Good. I wanted to see if you could.'
fields.events:animal:animal_boss_simha_king/tri:
He looks at what you have brought for a long, unhurried moment.

'You have given me,' he says, 'what you could spare.' There is no anger in it. That is the difficulty — there is nothing in it at all. 'Tribute is what you cannot spare. Otherwise it is only tidying.'

He returns it. The goods are yours again and worth rather less than they were.

You present what you have with the ceremony the moment deserves. He examines it without touching it — not the goods, but the gesture.

'Adequate,' he says. He steps aside without further ceremony. 'The realm of humans is expecting something. Try not to disappoint it.'
Offer tribute worthy of a king
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_shrine#t: Where three animal trails cross, someone built a cairn of stones. Prayer flags, thread, feathers pressed flat between layers of bark, bones arranged with obvious care — offerings that don't specify any particular tradition but cover their bases. A single butter lamp burns in a notch in the topmost stone.
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_shrine/m: You sit at the base of the cairn. At a crossroads, all directions are valid — this is what makes them sacred. For a moment you remember all of them.
Sit for a moment and breathe
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_shrine/o: You add something of yours to the cairn. The butter lamp flickers once in still air.
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_shrine/p: You leave the lamp to its burning.

That is the whole point of it and almost nobody notices. The cairn faces the trails, the offerings are the kind an animal would take, and the person who built it was making an argument.

You add to it in the same spirit.
Somebody built this where the animals cross, not where people do.
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_stupa#te: Where the old game trails intersect, someone built a stupa centuries ago. The mortar between the stones includes offerings pressed in during construction — seeds, feathers, a cracked egg. Butter lamps burn at the base. The place smells of juniper smoke and something that has been burning for a very long time.
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_stupa/ap: A practitioner emerges from behind the stupa. Summoning magic — the crossroads is the right place for it. Gold is the price.
fields.events:animal:animal_crossroads_stupa/ob: You watch the butter lamps in the wind. Some things are better left undisturbed.
fields.events:animal:animal_eternal_fire#text: The fire burns at the entrance to a cave, or near a volcanic vent, or at the base of an ancient tree struck by lightning and somehow still alive — wherever the ground produces heat that can be consecrated. The priests who tend it wear white and speak rarely. Creatures of many species come to pay respects. The fire does not discriminate.
fields.events:animal:animal_eternal_fire/approa: A priest turns from the flame and regards you. He names the spells, and then the prices.
fields.events:animal:animal_eternal_fire/respec: You bow before the flame and step back. The fire reflected in your eyes for some time after.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_banyan_hollo:
The banyan has been walking for a thousand years — dropping roots, standing on them, letting the original trunk rot away — and what is left is a hollow cathedral of living wood a hundred paces across, with a floor of soft mast and a roof you cannot see.

Things have been left here. Not hidden. Left.

You call, and something enormous and extremely slow turns a fraction of its attention toward you. It is not a spirit inhabiting the banyan; it is the banyan, thinking, at a speed that makes a human life look like a spark. It permits you one question. You are still deciding whether you asked the right one.
You walk through and out the other side. The quality of the silence stays with you for days.
Coins, tools, a folded cloth with something heavy inside. Nobody stops you. Nothing happens at all, which somehow makes it worse.
You set down coin and lift a small carved thing in its place, and the exchange feels correct in a way you could not defend to anyone. The banyan does not comment.
Leave something of your own and take something in exchange
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_cliff_aerie#:
The nest is a cartload of branches wedged into a fissure two hundred feet up a limestone face, and it has been in continuous use for generations — the bones of a great many meals are cemented into its base by weather.

The adults are out. Something in the nest is not.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_cliff_aerie/:
Bone, wool, a length of dyed cord that did not come from anywhere nearby, and — under all of it — the thing the cord was tied to.

The aerie's owner has been collecting from a settlement that is not on your map, and the direction it must lie in is now obvious.
Look at what is in the nest, not at the nest.

It has gotten a leg through a gap in the branch weave and has been there long enough to be past panic. Freeing it takes an hour of very careful work at a height that does not bear thinking about. The adults arrive while you are doing it, and hang in the air twenty feet out, watching, and do not attack. When you finish, one of them escorts you down — pacing your descent, ledge by ledge, the whole way.
The chick is tangled — free it
You are eighty feet up and fully committed when the shadow crosses you, and shyena do not need to land to fight.

Two hundred feet of limestone and then a nest full of two generations of shiny things nobody has ever come to reclaim. You are down and gone before the adults return. Your hands will not stop shaking for an hour.
Climb and take what the nest has collected
You are a mile off when two shapes cross the sun on their way home. Good timing, you reflect.

There is a standing column against the rock that will take a light body most of the way if it is not fought. You ride it up, take what is loose, and step off into it again on the way down. Whether the shyena saw you is unclear. If they did, they seem to have approved of the method.
Read the face for the updraught and go up on it
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_gana_ceremon:
The clearing is full of gana, arranged in concentric rings, and every one of them is dancing — not chaotically, but in a slow interlocking pattern that has clearly been going on for hours and shows no sign of ending.

Nobody is watching. That is not what it is for.

You do not know the steps and you join the outer ring anyway, and the outer ring is precisely where people who do not know the steps are supposed to be.

By the third round you have most of it. By the fifth you are being corrected, kindly, by a gana half your height.
Whatever it is for, they are glad about it. Be glad too.

You step in on the beat and the ring absorbs you without breaking stride. It is harder than it looks and then, abruptly, much easier — the pattern does the thinking if you let it. Somewhere in the third hour you stop being a visitor. At dawn the eldest presses her forehead to yours and says nothing at all.

The rings are moving at different rates — outer fast, inner slow, the centre almost still. It is a calendar. They are dancing a year, and the still figure at the centre is the year that has ended. It is a funeral. You take your hat off and stay until it finishes.
Work out what the ceremony is for
You add an hour to the day's walk and disturb nothing. The drumming follows you for a long way.
Go around the clearing without disturbing it
You stay for an hour, understanding none of it, moved anyway. When you leave nobody has acknowledged you, and it does not feel like a slight.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_gana_pack#te:
They do not surround you so much as *arrive around* you — six gana, drifting out of the undergrowth at intervals, each one taking a position that closes an option you had not yet realised you were relying on.

The last to appear is the smallest, and she is the one the others keep glancing at.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_gana_pack/ad: You ignore the big males entirely and address the small female directly, which is both correct and clearly unexpected. She holds your eye for an uncomfortably long time. Then she yawns — enormous, deliberate, a gesture of dismissal that is also a gesture of safe-conduct — and the whole pack loses interest at once. One of them walks you to the ridge, for reasons of its own.
Speak to the small one — the others already are
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_gana_pack/fe: They let the food sit until you are forty paces on. Behind you there is a brief, businesslike scuffle over shares, and then nothing. You are not followed.
Put meat on the ground and keep walking
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_gana_pack/ho: Someone's nerve goes. A foot shifts. That is all it takes.
Twenty minutes. Nobody moves; nobody blinks first, exactly, but the pack's attention frays the way attention does, and one by one they are simply elsewhere.
Stand absolutely still and let them lose interest
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_gana_pack/hu:
It is the shape you would use yourself, if you had six people and needed them to arrive around something at once.

You say so, out loud, with the technical terms. The gana stop what they are doing and reconsider you from the beginning.
This is not an ambush. This is a working formation.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_healer_camp#:
Someone has strung a canvas between four trees and turned the space under it into a clinic. There is a queue: a gana with a bad leg, two vanara holding a third between them, a varaha piglet being extremely brave about something.

The healer — a gana, grey-muzzled, working fast — glances at your party and evidently sees nothing urgent. "Back of the line."
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_healer_camp/: She hands you the gana's leg without discussion and watches your first two minutes out of the corner of her eye. After that she stops watching. You work until the light goes. When the last patient limps off she treats your party for free, restocks your kit from hers, and says "come back" in a tone that means it.
Roll up your sleeves and work the queue with her

You do, and you do it without complaining, which the healer notices from the other end of the line and files away.

When your turn comes she spends longer on you than the queue can really afford, and does not mention why.
You know how to wait in a queue like this.

You settle the whole line's account and leave before anyone can make it into a moment. The healer catches you at the treeline anyway and presses herbs into your hand, scowling, as though you had done something inconvenient.
Pay for the queue's treatment and move on
You go. Behind you the piglet is informed it has been very brave, which it clearly already knew.
Leave the queue to those who need it

You give up your place, and then the next one, and by the end of the afternoon you have not been treated at all and have carried four people to the front of the line.

The healer finds you at dusk and treats you without being asked.
Somebody here is worse off. You have had worse than this.
It takes two hours. When she gets to you she is thorough, blunt, and charges exactly what the work is worth.
Take your place in the queue
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_hedonist_cam:
Someone has been living extremely well out here. There is a fire, a great deal of fermented something in gourds, the remains of a genuinely impressive meal, and a marjara lying on his back in the middle of it all, utterly at peace.

"You look," he says, "like people who have been walking."

You decline everything — the gourd, the cushions, the extremely good food — politely and without comment, and your host finds this so novel that he follows you to the edge of the clearing asking questions.

He is, under all of it, lonely. You had guessed that from the size of the camp.
You have opinions about this camp and you keep them to yourself.

He does. The two of you spend an hour agreeing about a number of things that will not survive contact with morning, and one thing that will: he tells you where the good stands are, and he is not wrong.
He has more than drink out here and you can smell it.
"Suit yourselves," he says, wounded on your behalf rather than his own, and pours another.

You are not. The evening is genuinely excellent and the following day is not, and somewhere in the middle you agreed to something you cannot reconstruct.

Your host, when you leave, looks briefly like someone watching a colleague go.
He is pouring and you are not going anywhere.
You do not remember the end of the contest. He does, and tells everyone in the forest about it for the next several years.

At some point around the fourth gourd he stops treating it as a joke. At the sixth he concedes with enormous grace, declares you a person of substance, and gives you the good stuff — the sealed one he had not been intending to open for anybody.

The question lands like a dropped plate. For a moment the whole performance is visible from the inside — the fire, the gourds, the impressive meal, all of it built nightly against a silence he cannot sit in. He does not answer. But he stops pouring, and after a while he asks you how one learns to sit still, and you tell him, and he listens.
Ask what he is drinking away
It is a very good night. It is a considerably less good morning. You lose most of a day and some indeterminate amount of money, and the party is in a better mood than it has been in weeks.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_high_canopy_:
A shyena is perched at the very top of the tallest tree in sight, motionless, looking out over the whole forest canopy. She has clearly been there for hours.

When she notices you at the base she does not startle. She simply looks down, once, and returns to looking out — which somehow communicates, precisely, that you are welcome to climb if you think you can.

Everyone calls up. That is why the shyena is at the top of the tallest tree and not talking to anyone.

You sit at the base for two hours. It comes down in its own time, which is the only time it was ever going to come down in.
Do not call up to it. Wait until it comes down.

"Everything," she calls back, unhelpfully. Then, relenting: the smoke to the north-east, the migration two days out, the gap in the ridge that the maps do not have. She gives it freely and goes back to watching.
Call up and ask what she can see

You get two-thirds up before a branch you had committed to informs you it is dead. The fall is survivable, mostly because of the branches you hit on the way. From above, faintly, comes what is unmistakably laughter.

Forty minutes of climbing to sit beside something that got there in nine seconds. She says nothing about it, which is its own kind of courtesy. From up here the forest is not trees; it is one continuous green surface with weather moving over it, and you can see the ridge, the meadow, the sea. You stay until the light goes.
She does not look down again.

"That you live in a tunnel and call it a world." She says it without cruelty — it is simply the view from up there. Then she describes the wind-roads: the thermals, the standing waves off the ridge, the column over the meadow that will lift a body a thousand feet if it is patient. You will never use them. You are glad to know they are there.
Ask her what the sky-people make of the ground-people
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_jungle_merch:
His entire stock is on his back and his back is enormous. A varaha trader, three days out from anywhere, working a circuit that he clearly holds entirely in his head.

"You're the second party this month," he says, delighted. "Business is booming."
He unpacks with practiced speed, laying everything out on a groundsheet in an order that makes his own sense.

Half a day of company. He talks the entire time — prices, gossip, a long involved grievance about a vanara bridge toll — and when your roads part he presses supplies on you and refuses payment on the grounds that conversation is worth more than goods out here.
Walk with him as far as your roads agree
"Tell people I'm out here!" he calls after you. "Nobody knows I'm out here!"
Wish him luck and move on

You give him the state of the ridge crossings and where the marjara boundary now runs; he gives you a price no one else in this forest will ever see, and adds two items to the pile that were not for sale. Both of you leave convinced you got the better end of it, which is the mark of a good trade.
Trade him route information for stock
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_marjara_terr:
Claw-marks at head height on every fourth trunk, running as far as you can see in both directions. The marks are fresh, deliberate, and evenly spaced — this is not an animal scratching. It is a boundary, maintained.

The forest beyond the line is very quiet.
You are forty paces past the marks when the pale shape detaches from a trunk that it had, until that moment, appeared to be part of.
It takes most of a day. The line ends at a river, and something pale watches you from the far bank the whole time you are fording — but the marks stop at the water, and so does she.
Follow the boundary until it ends

You cut your mark at the same height, the same depth, and sit down with your back to it. She comes within the hour. For a long time she just looks at the two marks side by side. Then she cuts a third — above both — and withdraws. You have been given passage and put in your place simultaneously, which is, you gather, the marjara way of being generous.
Add your own mark beside hers and wait

Downwind, on stone and root, never breaking a stem. You are through her range and out the other side and she never knows — which is worth more than her permission would have been, and cost more to earn.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_mercenary_gu: A fortified outpost at the forest edge, flying a plain black banner between two old trees. The figures inside are armoured in hide and shell-plate — practical for the terrain. They look up when you enter with the universal expression of people who do this professionally.
The quartermaster opens a case and waits.
You leave the mercenaries to their sharpening.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_mushroom_maz:
The fruiting bodies here are the size of buildings, and they have grown close enough together to make corridors. The light under them is the colour of weak tea, the air is thick with spores, and sound does not carry the way it should.

After twenty minutes you pass the same distinctively split cap for the second time.
It takes an unnerving amount of time to find the edge again, but you find it. The party is quiet for a while afterwards.
Retrace your steps and go around

You mark every third turning, consistently, on the same side, at the same height.

It is fussy and slow and the party complains about it right up until the point where you walk everyone back out in a fifth of the time it took to walk in.
Nobody is getting lost in here on your watch.

The others stop and tilt their heads and go quiet, and you watch them do it and understand only that something has been heard.

By the time it has been explained the thing that made the sound has moved, and the party's route with it.
There is something to be heard here and you are not going to hear it.

You stop trying to get out and start trying to get value, which turns out to be the correct relationship with the place. Half a day later you leave by the entrance you came in, loaded, having mapped the good stands by the smell of the air in each corridor.
Work the maze deliberately for what grows here

The corridors are not a maze. They are one organism's idea of a shape, and it is not trying to trap you — it has simply never had a reason to consider the concept of a straight line. Once you stop expecting corridors to behave like corridors, the way out is obvious, and always was.
Stop moving and listen to the maze

Hours. The spores get into everything, and by the end at least two of you are seeing things in the corridors that the others are not. You come out somewhere you did not intend to be, tired and rattled.

You keep the slope on your left and refuse to be argued out of it, and the corridors eventually run out of ways to disagree with you. You come out the far side having crossed in a third of the time the detour would have taken — and having gathered a great deal on the way.
Push on and trust your sense of direction
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_mycelium_ten:
The varaha is on her knees in the leaf-litter with her snout an inch from the ground, doing something that is unmistakably horticulture. Around her, over perhaps an acre, the forest floor has been coaxed into patterns — fruiting bodies in arcs and spirals, each species where it does best.

"Don't step there," she says without looking up. "That one took nine years."
"Some." She sells you the ones that fruit fast and refuses to discuss the others. The transaction takes ten minutes and eight words.
Ask whether any of it is for trade

The varaha does not stop or explain. She does move over slightly, which is permission.

What she is doing is grafting — one network into another, at a join she has prepared over what must be months. Nobody in the party had known this was a thing that could be done.
She is doing something specific. Get down and look.

She tests you with one question about rot, decides you are not a fool, and puts you to work. You spend an afternoon thinning a fungal bed under instruction from a boar with better hands than yours. At the end she gives you a wrapped bundle and tells you what each one treats, twice, until you have it.
Offer to help with the nine-year patch
"Good," she says, still not looking up. It is the warmest thing anyone has said to you all week.
Step carefully back the way you came

She looks up for the first time. "Everything. That is the whole point." And she shows you: hands flat on the soil, the slow enormous conversation running under the entire forest, older than the trees standing in it, patient beyond any possible use. You take your hands off the ground eventually. She lets you sit with it for as long as you need.
Ask what the mycelium is connected to
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_rakshasa_amb:
The birds stopped a hundred paces back. You noticed, and kept walking, because there was nowhere else to walk.

He drops out of the canopy directly into your path — a rakshasa, orange-eyed and unhurried, blocking the trail with the relaxed posture of something that has already counted you and likes the number.
You retreat facing him, slowly, for two hundred paces. He follows for one hundred and fifty of them and then simply stops, having established whatever he needed to establish. You go the long way.
Back down the trail without turning around

You stopped with them, which is why the party is already off the trail and in cover when the rakshasa commits to a charge at where you were going to be.

It is very fast. It is not faster than being somewhere else.
The birds stopped a hundred paces back. You stopped too.

You do not threaten him. You simply plant, shift your grip, and let him read what taking you would cost. Rakshasa are predators, not gamblers. He tilts his head, makes a sound that might be a laugh, and steps off the trail to let you pass — then follows at fifty paces for an hour, just to be sure you leave.
Make yourself expensive — show him the arithmetic
You are still looking for the second one when she lands behind you.

There. Above and behind, flattened along a branch, the actual ambush. You point at her without looking away from him, and the whole shape of the encounter collapses. Caught out, they withdraw with what dignity they can — and leave the kill they had been guarding.
He is too relaxed — look for the other one
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_rakshasa_den:
The cave mouth is screened by hanging root and would be invisible from ten paces. Inside, the floor is dry sand, deliberately swept, and the walls are stacked with what a rakshasa considers worth keeping.

The den is empty. The bedding is warm.
You are a quarter-mile away before you let yourself breathe properly. It is, on reflection, the best decision you have made today.
You grab from the nearest stack and are out in ninety seconds. Something calls, far off and unhurried, and you do not stop moving for an hour.
Take what you can and go

You do not steal anything. You rearrange: the bedding, the stacks, the sand, all of it shifted an inch or two out of true. Then you wait outside. The rakshasa comes home, stops dead in the entrance, and spends the next twenty minutes in a state of profound existential unease. It leaves the valley that night. You take the den at your leisure.
Prepare the den before its owner returns
You are elbow-deep in the sand at the back of the cave when the light from the entrance changes shape.

Under the sand at the back, where the sweeping is most careful, there is a hollow lined with cloth. What is in it has nothing to do with hunting and everything to do with whatever this rakshasa was before it came out here to be a predator.
Search it properly — the good things will be buried
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_sounder_matr:
She is enormous, grey around the snout, and lying in a wallow with the contentment of someone who has nothing left to prove to anybody. Two dozen varaha of assorted sizes are arranged around her in the mud.

One eye opens. "You are in my forest," she observes, without any particular concern about it.

She tells you, in detail, with landmarks, and includes which stretches are contested and by whom and at what hours. It is the single most useful conversation you have had since arriving in this realm.
Ask her the safe way through

You come in downwind, slowly, at an angle, and you stop at the distance she chooses rather than the one you would prefer.

She lets you stop there. For a sounder matron with young in the trees behind her, this is an extraordinary concession, and both of you know it.
She is lying in a wallow, not guarding a pass. Approach accordingly.

"Eat last," she says. "Sleep where they can see you. Never explain a decision twice — they stop believing the first one." She has run a sounder of forty for thirty years. You take notes, mentally, and use them for the rest of your life.
Ask her advice on leading people

You have seen what a sounder does to something that got between the matron and the young, and the memory is specific enough to be useful.

You take the party the long way without arguing about it, and nobody finds out how it would have gone.
You know exactly how this goes if it goes wrong.
"Mm," she says, and closes the eye. The audience is over.

You get into the wallow. It is warm and appalling and after ten minutes you understand it completely. Nobody says anything for two hours. Piglets walk over you. When you finally rise, the matron says: "You may come back," which from a varaha of her standing is close to adoption.
Sit down in the mud and stay a while
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_teahouse#tex: A platform structure high in the canopy, reachable by rope bridges from three directions. The vanara who run it have been doing so since before any of them can remember. The tea is brewed from forest herbs you don't recognize and tastes like rain, bark, and something that is not quite spice. It is very good.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_teahouse/ear:
The proprietor is doing the first firing of the day when you come up the rope ladder, and there is a particular understanding between people who are awake at that hour by choice.

You get the first pot. The first pot is not the same as the others and she does not explain why.
You are up before the canopy is light. So is she.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_teahouse/lea: The smell of forest tea follows you along the rope bridge.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_teahouse/sit: You take a platform seat. A vanara sets down cups without ceremony.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_teahouse/tea:
You do the whole form on a swaying platform in the canopy, which is objectively ridiculous and which the proprietor watches with total seriousness.

At the end she brings out the other pot — the one that does not get offered — and does the form back at you.
A teahouse a hundred feet up. Do this properly.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_town_magic#t: A forest settlement where the mycelium network runs under every building and the practitioners who use it for communication have built a small trade in that adjacency. Alchemy, earth magic, summoning — the disciplines that grow from understanding what is underground. The shelves smell of soil and something fermented.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_town_magic/l: You leave the forest scholars to their arguments.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_town_supplie: A clearing settlement where four game trails meet. Sounder matrons and herb-walkers tend most of the stalls. Food preserved in bark and clay, medicines extracted from things most travelers walk past without recognizing, tools for the deep forest. It is honest trade in a place that doesn't demand credentials.
The matron at the nearest stall sizes you up and names a fair price.
You keep walking. The smell of drying herbs follows you down the trail.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_town_weapons: A market at the forest's edge where different territories agree, briefly, to exchange. Dura shell-wright craftsmanship, vanara jugaad improvisation, marjara-claw handles on daggers sold by gana traders who got them somewhere no one is explaining. The weapons here are practical and tell stories.
You skirt the settlement and continue into the trees.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_training_cam: A clearing used by those who hunt without being hunted — trackers, scouts, the nimble-fingered and the quick-footed. The vanara here share techniques that have been refined over many generations in this specific forest. Some of it translates; all of it is worth knowing.
You leave the clearing. The forest returns to its own lesson.
A vanara elder with patient eyes names two skills. 'Which two? Choose once.'
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_vanara_elder:
The troop's elder holds court in the crown of a strangler fig, surrounded by an accumulated lifetime of stolen objects: brass buckles, a broken astrolabe, forty-odd single boots, a temple bell with no clapper.

"Sit," he says, indicating a branch. "Tell me something I don't know. Then you may have one thing."
"Everyone's in a hurry," he says sadly, and goes back to sorting buckles.

"Your second-youngest is not stealing food for herself. She has been running it up the east ridge every third day for a month." The elder goes completely still. Then he is gone through the canopy without a word, and comes back an hour later much older and much gentler, and gives you three things instead of one, and asks you not to mention it.
Tell him something about his own troop he doesn't know

You palm his own tally-stick, produce it from behind a piglet's ear, and return it with the notches recut into a joke about him. The canopy comes apart with noise. He declares you troop-adjacent, grants you the freedom of every bridge in the forest, and immediately begins trying to learn the palm, badly.
Show him a sleight he has never seen

You describe the reef wall, the standing stones, the state of the northern trails. He listens with total attention and interrupts twice for detail. At the end he considers, then hands you a boot. Then, seeing your face, he laughs and gives you something better.
Tell him what you have seen in this realm
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_vanara_toll#:
A rope bridge crosses the gorge, and it is in excellent repair, which in this forest means somebody maintains it, which means somebody charges for it.

Four vanara are sitting on the far anchor. One of them is holding your water-skin. You are still wearing your pack.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_vanara_toll/:
None of it happened. The vanara are, however, professionals of the form, and they can tell a good account from a true one and prefer the former.

You cross for a story instead of a coin. They will be telling your version by winter, improved.
Tell them what you did at the last bridge.

It is not a good joke. It is a joke about a monkey, told to four monkeys, by someone standing over a very deep gorge — and the sheer nerve of it lands where wit would not have. They let you cross on the strength of it and demand you tell it again to the elder.

By the time you reach the far anchor you are holding the toll-keeper's belt, her tally-string, and the pin from the bridge's tensioner — which you hand back immediately, because you are not insane. The vanara are delighted. This is the funniest thing that has happened to them this season. You cross free and they wave you off like family.

The coins vanish. The water-skin comes back. So, unexpectedly, does a knife you had not noticed was missing, and a small carved bird that was never yours. "Overpayment," says the one holding it, with the air of someone who considers this a serious matter.
fields.events:animal:animal_forest_varaha_charg:
You have walked into the middle of a sounder and the middle of a sounder is where the young are.

The boar between you and the trail is not large. The one coming through the undergrowth behind her at considerable speed is.

Standing still in front of a charging sounder is a terrible idea that happens to be the correct one, and you are the only person present capable of doing it.

The matron breaks off four feet short. She was never going to commit; she needed to see whether you would.
Undignified, effective. The sounder mills below for half an hour, working itself down from fury to irritation to boredom, and moves off. Someone's pack does not survive the experience.
Get everyone up a tree, immediately

You go down on one knee, put your eyes below hers, and make the low sound the old ones make when the sounder is settling for the night. The charge does not stop so much as forget itself. She stands over you breathing hard, and then, with enormous dignity, pretends none of it happened and shepherds her young past you into the trees.
Greet the matron the way a varaha would

A varaha charge is a commitment, not a decision — she is going to arrive exactly where she is pointed. You get everyone four paces left and she goes past close enough to feel, and does not turn, because turning is not part of it. The sounder follows her through and the trail is clear.
Read the charge line and move the party off it
fields.events:animal:animal_garuda_roost#text: A horned pole rises from the high ground — above the canopy where it can be seen from the air, or from a cliff edge visible to anything that flies. The garudas pass through this realm regularly on their circuits between worlds. Followers of all species gather here to wait, to offer, and sometimes to receive teachings when the great birds land. Shyena and kapota are among the most devoted.
fields.events:animal:animal_garuda_roost/offeri: You set something at the base of the pole and move on. The ribbons flutter.
fields.events:animal:animal_garuda_roost/speak#: One of the worshippers looks up. They teach Air magic here. The price is negotiable, but only within reason.
fields.events:animal:animal_hidden_gompa#text: A structure of woven branches and packed earth, half-reclaimed by the forest. Inside, mantric syllables are audible — not quite human in their cadence, adjusted over years of practice to harmonize with birdsong and the sounds of the forest. Monks who withdrew from the human realm into the animal realm for solitude. They have been here a long time. The animals have grown accustomed to them.
fields.events:animal:animal_hidden_gompa/enter#: After a pause, the door opens. A monk gestures you inside. Space magic. What do you need?
fields.events:animal:animal_hidden_gompa/pass#r: You walk past quietly. The mantras continue without interruption.
fields.events:animal:animal_karka_reef_warden#t:
The pass through the coral barrier is narrow and long. Halfway through, a karka fills it completely — shell the width of the passage, claws braced against the coral walls, eyes fixed on you.

She is not sleeping. She has been watching since you entered the corridor.

The thermal vent behind her produces a faint heat that rises through the passage. This is her vent. This is her pass. These things are not in question.
fields.events:animal:animal_karka_reef_warden/f: She braces. Her claws score the coral walls. Whatever comes next, she will not move from this vent.
fields.events:animal:animal_karka_reef_warden/n:
You make the argument. It is a decent argument, and she listens to all of it with her claws folded.

'No,' she says, when you have finished. She does not explain, and it becomes clear she does not consider an explanation to be part of the transaction. The reef is hers. You are not from the reef.

You go the long way, and it costs you most of a day.

You speak to her in terms she respects — this is her territory, you acknowledge it; you need to pass, you explain why; you will not return unless invited.

Her eyes do not change. But after a long pause, she steps aside — just enough. The passage is tight. She watches every inch of it.
fields.events:animal:animal_karka_reef_warden/p:
She looks at the gold. She looks at you. She reaches out one claw and takes it with surprising delicacy.

Then she moves aside. The passage is yours. She adds the gold to a pile you hadn't noticed — there is a system here, practiced over years. You are not the first to find this more efficient than the alternative.
Offer gold as a crossing toll
fields.events:animal:animal_karka_reef_warden/r:
You back out of the passage the way you came. There are other passes — you will find them.

Behind you, the karka returns to her vigil without comment. This happens, too.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_bhramara_hiv:
The hive is built around a dead tree and has entirely replaced it — forty feet of grey papery architecture humming at a pitch you feel in your teeth.

There is a doorway. It is guarded, but it is unmistakably a doorway, which suggests visitors are a category that exists here.

You touch the wall and let the hum have you, and the distributed mind on the other side takes an interest. Inside there is no darkness — the whole structure glows faintly with worked wax — and the hive shows you its nurseries, its stores, its dead, with the unselfconsciousness of something that has never had a private thought in its existence. You come out three hours later, changed in a way that takes weeks to name.

It is. You trade properly for it rather than raiding, because you are greedy and not stupid, and you are given a comb still warm from the wall.

You make it last four days. Everyone else in the party gets some, eventually, after negotiation.
Whatever else this is, it is also the best food in the realm.
The hum changes pitch as you withdraw. Acknowledgement, possibly. Or just weather.
Admire it from a safe distance
The wall is not as cold as you judged, and the hum coming through it is rising.
Cold night, slow hive, and a clean cut through the papery outer wall into a store gallery. You are away with a fortune in worked honey and wax before the temperature comes back up.
Take from the outer stores at night

Nobody asks. The hive-mind takes some time over the answer, which is itself interesting, and the answer is: some, but not much, and less than you would think, and thank you for asking.

You are given more than the traders get.
Ask whether taking it costs the hive anything.
The guards will not let you in, but they will exchange: your metal for their stores, at a rate they clearly consider generous and you cannot argue with because you cannot argue.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_bhramara_swa:
The sound arrives before anything else — a low chord in three parts, coming from a shadow on the grass that is moving against the wind.

The swarm is perhaps four thousand strong. It has noticed you. The chord changes key.

You stop, and you make everyone else stop, which is much harder.

The chord passes over and around and does not descend, because nothing in the party is behaving like something worth descending on.
Do not run from a swarm. Nobody has ever outrun one.

You find the root note and hold it, and then the fifth, and the swarm — which is a single distributed mind conducting a conversation with itself — abruptly has something else to talk to. The chord resolves into something almost welcoming. They escort you across their range in a loose column and peel away at the boundary, still singing.
Smoke makes them sluggish and, more importantly, makes the chord fall apart — a swarm that cannot hear itself is just a lot of individual insects. You walk out through the confusion, coughing.
Burn damp grass and go through the smoke

You put a shear across their line of advance. The swarm is not hurt — it is *edited*, the coherent shape torn into six shapes that have to spend the next several minutes deciding which of them is in charge. You are long gone before they settle it.
Break the swarm's formation with moving air
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_cliff_oracle:
The uluka is upside down in the mouth of a cliff hollow, wings folded, eyes closed, and has been described to you by three separate strangers as the only honest oracle in the meadow.

"I only answer questions people don't want answered," she says, without opening her eyes. "It saves everyone's time."

She sighs, opens one eye, and answers your dull question about the northern route accurately and at length, with the air of a scholar asked to fetch tea. The information is excellent. She is visibly disappointed in you.

Both eyes open. She listens to the whole question, including the part you did not mean to say out loud, and then answers it in one sentence that you will be turning over for months. It is not comforting. It is, unmistakably, true.
Ask the one you have been avoiding
"Wise," she says. It does not sound entirely like a compliment.

You show her the death you have been carrying since the last realm — the shape of it, not the fact. Uluka trade in ill omens the way other people trade in grain, and this is good stock. She takes it off you, which is a service you did not know you needed, and pays for it besides.
Offer her an omen of your own in trade

There is a way of asking, and you know it, because you have always known these things without being able to say where from.

The uluka answers the question you asked rather than the one you meant, which is the risk you accepted by asking properly.
An upside-down owl in a cliff. Ask the question properly.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_dura_artisan:
The surface entrance to the warren has been decorated — and not modestly. Somebody has spent years carving the entire rim into an interlocking relief of the colony's history, and is currently, delicately, adding to it.

"Careful of the edge," she says. "It's wet."
She is entirely unembarrassed by praise and walks you through forty years of colony politics rendered in bas-relief, including two wars, a schism, and a section she describes flatly as "the mistake".
Admire the work and say so

It is very good work. It is also, you notice, made from about nine different things that do not occur within a hundred miles of here.

You say so. The artisan is delighted — nobody has ever recognised the sourcing before, only the arrangement.
Look at the work rather than the doorway.
She takes your measure — literally, with a length of knotted cord — and produces a small carved token in under an hour. It is a likeness. It is uncomfortably good.

She hands you a chisel and a corner of blank rim and does not offer advice, which is the highest compliment available. You carve the hell-gate: frost, the four-armed judge, the door. When you finish she studies it for a long while and then cuts her own mark beside yours — colony work, permanent, load-bearing history. Some dura in two hundred years will wonder who you were.
Ask to add a panel of your own

The colony sealed a corridor with a work party still inside it, to stop a flood, and saved nine hundred lives. The panel does not editorialise; it simply records, in the same careful hand as everything else, each of the forty-one names. "We carve it so nobody has to argue about whether it happened," she says. "Only about whether it was right."
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_dura_patrol#:
The ground gives slightly under your boot, and then a great deal more, and you are standing knee-deep in the roof of somebody's corridor.

Six dura come up out of the break in perfect order, mandibles first. They are not surprised. They have clearly done this exact drill many times.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_dura_patrol/: You back off twenty paces and sit down, hands visible. Within the hour the breach is sealed by a work party that ignores you completely. The patrol watches you until the repair is done, then goes back down without a word.
Withdraw slowly and let them repair it

You cut and set a timber brace across the break before they can decide what to do about you, and the work party arrives to find the roof already held. There is a long silence. Then the patrol leader taps her mandibles twice — the dura acknowledgement — and someone brings up worked metal from below and puts it in your hands.

This is a containment formation, not an attack formation — they are protecting the corridor, not hunting you. You move to the position a dura auxiliary would take on the flank and simply hold it. The whole patrol relaxes at once. You are, briefly and administratively, part of the colony.
Recognise the drill and stand where a friendly would
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_dura_warren#:
The entrance slopes down out of the sunlight into a corridor that is perfectly round, perfectly smooth, and perfectly dark. Warm air comes up out of it smelling of earth and formic acid.

Somewhere below, a great many things are working.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_dura_warren/: You take a wrong branch and come out into a gallery that is not storage. The soldiers here are bigger.

Four levels down you find the treasury — not gold; *metal*, worked and stockpiled over generations, the colony's entire strategic reserve. You take what two people can carry and navigate back out by the draught, and nothing ever knows you were there.
The warm air follows you for the first hundred paces, like a held breath.

You do it properly: stand at the threshold, state your names and your business, and wait. It takes three hours. Then a delegation comes up and conducts you down to trade, with an escort, through galleries no thief would ever have found. The colony deals fairly and at volume, and you leave through the front door.
Announce yourself at the entrance and request an audience
Storage. Rank on rank of it, meticulously sorted, and nobody in this section to object to a modest withdrawal.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire#te:
The smoke line is on the southern horizon and it is wider than it was ten minutes ago. Grassfire moves faster than a running person when the wind is behind it, and the wind is behind it.

There is a rocky rise a mile east. There is a river two miles north. Neither is close enough to be comfortable.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire/ba: You light your own fire downwind and let it eat a patch bare, then stand in the ash while the main front arrives and finds nothing to eat. It is loud, and hot, and completely survivable, and the party looks at whoever suggested it with new respect.
Burn a firebreak and shelter in the black
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire/fi: You do not put it out — it is a mile wide and older than your involvement. You persuade it to part. Two walls of flame go by on either side of a corridor thirty feet across, and for about four minutes the party walks through the middle of a grassfire in perfect safety and total terror.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire/pe:
There are, and you are already moving toward them, and the argument about whether this is sensible happens behind you at volume.

You get perhaps a third of them out. The third is a real number of living things and you decline to be told otherwise.
There are animals in front of that fire.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire/ru: You make it, barely, and stand chest-deep watching a mile-wide front of fire go past on both banks. Somebody's pack is gone. Everybody's eyebrows are gone.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire/sa: There is a pocket of young khadga penned against a gully and no time to do this and get clear yourself. You do it anyway, shouting and waving and running the gully line until they break the right way. You reach the river with the front close enough to read by. Later, in the meadow, khadga will not charge you. Word travels.
Drive the trapped grazers out ahead of the front
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_grassfire/wa:
You stop the party from running, which is the entire job, and then you give four people four tasks in the order they need doing.

It is not courage. It is that panic is a thing you stopped being able to do some years ago, and it turns out to be worth more than courage here.
A fire front is a line. You have worked a line before.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_khadga_charg:
The grass ahead is flattened in a long straight line, and at the far end of it a khadga is turning around.

There is no cover between you and it. There is no cover behind you either. It lowers its head.

You step off the line with time to spare, and having time to spare means you can watch the whole thing go past from a yard away, which almost nobody gets to do.

It is enormous. You will be describing it for weeks.
You will not need to hold until the last moment. You are faster than the last moment.

The party breaks in five directions. It commits to one, misses, ploughs a hundred paces of grass, and by the time it has turned everyone is somewhere else. You regroup a mile on, minus one pack and most of your composure.
Scatter — it can only follow one of you
You step the wrong way. It adjusts. They can adjust, it turns out, right at the end.

You wait until you can see the individual hairs on its horn and then take one long pace left. It goes past close enough to knock you flat with the wind of it, and keeps going, because that is what a committed khadga does.
Hold until the last moment, then step off the line

A khadga charges movement. You stop being movement. It comes to a halt six feet away, snorting, genuinely confused, and stands there for a full minute trying to resolve you into something worth hitting. Then it wanders off to eat. The rest of the party unfreezes considerably later than you do.

You are, and the running is the problem — a khadga follows movement, and you have supplied the only movement on the plain.

It follows you a long way before losing interest. The party finds you eventually.
You are already running and it has not started yet.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_khadga_herd#: Forty khadga, grazing, spread across a mile of grassland directly across your route. Individually each one could end your afternoon. Collectively they are entirely occupied with eating and have not looked up.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_khadga_herd/: Four extra hours and total safety. Nobody complains, which tells you something about the party's opinion of khadga.

They make room. It is not tameness — nothing here is tame — it is that you are moving at a speed that reads as weather rather than as threat.

The party follows in your wake, and the crossing takes an hour instead of a day.
Walk in slowly. They will make room.

The old cows set the herd's mood, and they are downwind and settled. You cross in their lee, where the bulls take their cues from and therefore will not initiate anything, and are through in twenty minutes.
Read the herd and cross behind the matriarchs

Second rank, north side, not grazing. Everything the herd will do in the next minute is already decided by her.

You plan the crossing around one animal instead of forty, and the herd never breaks.
Forty animals and one of them is doing the watching.

Third group from the left, lying down, wrong shoulder line.

It has been in among them for some time and the herd has accepted it, which tells you considerably more about the thing than about the herd.
Something in that herd is not a khadga.
A bull on the flank decides he does not care for the shape of you and makes a short, emphatic demonstration run. Nobody is gored. Everybody runs. The crossing is abandoned.

The trick, it turns out, is to move exactly as slowly as they do and never once change direction. It takes ninety minutes to cross a mile. Two calves follow you for part of it out of curiosity. Nothing else happens at all, which is a triumph.
Walk straight through at grazing pace
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_mercenary_gu: A stockaded compound at a crossroads of migration routes, flying the universal mercenary banner on a pole tall enough to be seen from a distance. Inside, armoured figures play dice and argue rates. The work in the open meadow is the most visible and the most dangerous, and the prices reflect that.
The quartermaster nods and produces a list. Standard rates. Meadow surcharge.
You skirt the compound and keep moving.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_merchant#tex:
The cart is enormous, the draught animal is a khadga in a padded harness, and the merchant is a yaksha who has clearly been doing this route for decades.

"Don't touch the wheels," she says by way of greeting. "Everything else is negotiable."
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_merchant/bro: The cart opens out into a shop-front with practiced efficiency.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_merchant/hag: Forty minutes of extremely enjoyable commerce. She opens by insulting your boots; you close by pointing out that her khadga is favouring a foreleg and she is four days from anyone who can shoe it. You both leave delighted. Your prices are excellent.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_merchant/lea: "Suit yourself. I'll be at the standing stones in four days if you change your mind."
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_merchant/sho: There is a stone bruise under the plate and the beginnings of an abscess. You open it, drain it, pack it, and explain the aftercare twice. The merchant watches the whole thing without a word, then loads your packs with whatever you point at and refuses money. "That animal is my business," she says. "You just saved my business."
Offer to see to the khadga's foreleg
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_migration#te:
It has been passing for two days and shows no sign of ending: a river of bodies, twenty species deep, moving north across the entire visible width of the meadow. Predators walk in it openly, unmolested, because during the migration that is the arrangement.

You need to be on the other side.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_migration/cr: Somebody stumbles and the party fragments. You spend the rest of the day being carried north by a river of grazers and the following morning walking back south.

You go with the current at an angle, never against it, the way you would ford a river. Forty minutes inside a moving wall of animals that mostly ignore you. You come out a mile north of where you meant to and entirely intact.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_migration/ho:
Two days of animals that know exactly where they are going and why, and will be there by a particular week, and have been doing it since before anyone was counting.

You watch a good deal more of it than the crossing requires.
It is going somewhere. That is the part that gets you.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_migration/jo: You match the pace and join it, and for six hours you are simply part of the thing, walking north among a hundred thousand animals under the truce. A marjara walks beside you for a mile. Neither of you acknowledges the other. It is, on later reflection, one of the great experiences of the run.
Walk with the migration as long as it goes your way
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_migration/wa: Another day and a half. You spend it watching, and eat well — the migration sheds food the way a cart sheds straw.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_patanga_asce:
He is standing in the open with his wings fully spread, facing directly into the sun, and has evidently been doing so since it rose. The grass around him is scorched in a perfect circle.

"Don't stand in front," he says pleasantly. "You'll shade me."

You put it to him: that standing at the edge for eleven years is not restraint but an extended indulgence, the wanting kept alive deliberately because he is afraid of what he would be without it. He is silent for a very long time. Then: "Yes." Just that. He folds his wings and walks away north, and you never learn where he goes.
Argue that the discipline is just a slower burning

Wings spread, in the open, in full sun, until sundown. It is a stupid practice and you both know it is a stupid practice and that is not an argument against it.

When the light goes he folds his wings and says one sentence to you, and it is not about the practice.
You know what he is doing. Stand in it with him.
"To want the fire and not enter it. Anyone can burn. Standing at the edge is the discipline." He has been at it, he mentions, for eleven years. His wings are scarred to lace.
Ask what the practice is for
"Thank you," he says, without moving. "Very few people think of it."
Step out of his light and go

Nine hours. The heat is unspeakable and the boredom is worse and somewhere in the seventh hour the two stop being different from each other. At sundown he folds his wings and looks at you for the first time. "You wanted to leave at the fourth hour," he says. "You stayed. That is the whole teaching. There is nothing else."

You stand past sundown, which he does not, and he comes back at moonrise to find out what you are doing.

The conversation that follows is the first one in months in which neither of you has to explain the premise.
You have already given up more than a day of sun.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_patanga_clou:
A column of patanga is rising off the warm ground in a slow spiral, thousands of them, catching the light — the whole thing perhaps two hundred feet high and turning like something being poured upward.

They are not going anywhere. This appears to be the entire activity.
The column is still turning when you look back an hour later.
Somebody inhales. There follows a great deal of coughing, some panic, and an undignified exit at speed.

Wings against every inch of exposed skin, light coming through in fragments, absolute disorientation for about ninety seconds. You come out the far side laughing and covered in scale-dust that will not brush off for a week.
Twenty minutes of doing nothing at all, in good light, watching something beautiful that has no purpose. The party is measurably better afterwards.
Stop and watch it for a while
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_teahouse#tex: A low structure at the edge of the great watering hole, where the land slopes gently down to the water. The truce of thirst holds here — every creature in the meadow observes it, because the keeper enforces it, and the keeper has been here longer than any of them. Inside: food, drink, and improbable peace.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_teahouse/gos:
Everything does, and everything talks, and a watering hole in the dry season is the single most informative place on the plain.

You leave knowing which route the migration will take, which is worth more than the tea cost.
Everything that lives here comes to this water eventually.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_teahouse/lea: You walk past the watering hole without stopping. The smell of water and cooking carries far on open ground.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_teahouse/sit: You take a table. Nobody challenges you. This is the truce.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_thermal_colu:
A bare patch of dark rock in the middle of the grass throws up heat all afternoon, and everything with wings in the meadow knows it. Shyena, kapota and uluka circle in a lazy stacked column half a mile high, none of them flapping, all of them going up.

At ground level it is simply a warm rock. It makes a good place to stop.
You make good distance. The column is still there behind you at dusk, thinning as the rock cools.
Keep moving while the light holds
An hour in the sun on hot stone with birds turning overhead. The party's aches ease and nobody says anything of consequence the entire time.

You put a twist in the thermal — a stutter in the rising air that reads, to anything riding it, as an invitation. A kapota comes down to see what happened. She carries messages for a living, is intensely curious about ground-walkers, and trades you an hour of the meadow's news for the novelty of the conversation.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_town_magic#t: A settlement gathered around a yaksha standing stone, which functions as both landmark and practice anchor. Enchantment, earth magic, white healing — the disciplines that thrive in open country where the sky is visible and the earth is close. The practitioners here are travelers themselves, stopping as they always stop.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_town_magic/e: You find the practitioners' quarter around the standing stone.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_town_magic/l: You leave the stone to its practitioners.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_town_supplie: A trading post at the great watering hole, where the migration routes converge and every creature passes through eventually. The merchants here have learned not to ask where anyone is going. Essential goods for the long traversal: food for crossing open ground, medicine for what open ground does to you, equipment for what you find at the end of it.
The shopkeeper glances up briefly and goes back to counting stock.
You keep moving. The watering hole glitters to your left.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_town_weapons: An armorer's compound at a crossroads of migration routes, built low and solid to survive the open-ground seasons. Dura shell-wright work alongside yaksha-enchanted blades and khadga-horn handles. The merchants here have traveled to get here and priced accordingly. Everything for sale is worth carrying a long way.
You continue across the open ground.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_training_cam: A camp at the edge of the open plain where fighters train in the exposed, unforgiving style demanded by meadow combat — no cover, long sight lines, everything decided by strength and endurance. The yaksha veterans who run it have a simple philosophy: you learn to take a hit, and then you learn to give one back harder.
The veteran returns to drilling her students.
'We can teach two things. Once each. Make your choices.'
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_yaksha_chall:
He has planted his spear in the ground across the trail and is standing beside it with his arms folded — a yaksha of considerable size and, evidently, considerable free time.

"Nobody crosses my ground without giving me something to remember them by," he announces. "Gold, a fight, or a story. Your choice. I'd prefer the fight."

First fall, no weapons, no grudge. He lights up like a festival. You lose — he is enormous — but you lose well enough that he hauls you up laughing and declares the toll paid twice over, then walks you to the edge of his ground telling you about every fight he has had this year.
Accept the fight, but set the terms

There is, and there is only one thing a spear planted across a trail has ever meant, and you have been walking all morning.

The yaksha is pleased. The bout is formal, brief, and settled on a technicality that you both agree to call a win for him.
There is a spear in the ground across the trail.
He takes it with visible disappointment and stands aside. "That's the boring one," he says. "Everyone picks the boring one."

You tell him about the hell realms — the frost, the Warden's gate, a thing with four arms that judged souls at a doorway. He sits down halfway through and does not move again until you finish. When you do, he pulls his spear out of the ground, hands you a drinking-horn from his belt, and asks whether you would consider coming back this way.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_yaksha_shama:
She has laid out a divination on a hide: knucklebones, seed-pods, a scatter of bright beetle-wings, all of it arranged in a pattern that is clearly precise and entirely opaque.

"Sit down," she says. "You're in it. You've been in it since yesterday."

She looks for a long time. Then she gathers the bones up without answering and says, gently: "It is not fixed. That is the good news, and it is also the only news." You get the distinct impression she saw something and chose kindness over accuracy — and that she was right to.
Ask her what she can see of where you are going after this life

The bones land where she puts them. That is not a fraud — she is not pretending otherwise, and when she sees you watching her hands she nods as though a question has been settled.

What she tells you afterwards, without the bones, is the useful part.
Watch her hands, not the bones.
"Sensible," she says, and sweeps the beetle-wings into her palm. "Most of it is weather anyway."

You know a different system, but the grammar is the same, and for an hour the two of you argue happily about correspondences like colleagues at a conference.
