She teaches you her reading of the beetle-wings; you show her something about the seed-pods that genuinely surprises her. She insists on gifting you her spare set.

She tells you three things. One is about the road north and is immediately useful. One is about somebody in your party and you decide not to repeat it. The third she will not explain at all — "It hasn't got a shape yet" — but she writes it on a scrap of bark and makes you take it.
fields.events:animal:animal_meadow_yaksha_stand:
Nine stones in a ring, each taller than a khadga, each carved with a face that has weathered to a suggestion. The grass inside the ring is a different species from the grass outside it.

The yaksha put these up. Nobody currently alive remembers why.
It is markedly quieter inside. Not silent — quieter, as though the ring holds a slightly smaller amount of world. Nothing happens. You leave feeling that something declined to.
You give it a wide berth, and are aware of doing so, and cannot entirely say why.

You count them again. There are nine. You count a third time from the other direction and there are nine, and the fact that you needed to check three times is the thing worth paying attention to.

You make the offering at the one you kept losing.

The stones are not aligned to the sun. They are aligned to each other, in a pattern that only makes sense if you assume a tenth stone that is no longer there. Something was held in this ring, by nine, and one of the nine failed. You do not find the tenth stone. You do find, at its position, a hollow where nothing will grow.
Work out what the ring was for

You put your hands on the northern stone and give it what it has been waiting a long time for. The nine faces do not move — they simply become, briefly, faces again, and the ring remembers that it is a ring. For about four heartbeats you are standing somewhere else, in a much older meadow, among a great many yaksha who are all looking at you with enormous surprise. Then it is a field with rocks in it.
fields.events:animal:animal_medicinal_garden#te: A clearing carved from the forest floor, every inch cultivated with medicinal plants. Some healers here were born in these forests; others retreated from human settlements to practice more freely. The knowledge is older than any of them — root-knowledge, bark-knowledge, the deep grammar of the healing forest. The teachers share it openly, for a fee.
fields.events:animal:animal_medicinal_garden/le: A healer looks up from her work and nods. She names her price without ceremony.
fields.events:animal:animal_medicinal_garden/pa: You leave without disturbing them. The scent of growing things follows you for some time.
fields.events:animal:animal_mirror_lake#text: A lake so still it seems to reflect a different sky — no wind reaches it, or the water ignores the wind. Enchantment practitioners gather at the shore to meditate on appearance and reality. In a realm where a deer's world and a wolf's world overlap in the same territory and neither sees what the other sees, the question has obvious urgency.
fields.events:animal:animal_mirror_lake/leave#r: You step back. The image on the water holds for a moment longer than it should, then dissolves.
fields.events:animal:animal_mirror_lake/leave#t: Walk away from the still water
fields.events:animal:animal_mirror_lake/sit#res: A practitioner meets your eyes in the reflection before turning around. They can teach Enchantment. The lake makes everything seem like a fair price.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_current_cross: The channel here runs fast and cold between two rock shelves. It is not deep. It is simply moving faster than a person can stand up in, and it goes somewhere you cannot see.

Round stones and a fast current and a foot that has never once been reliable on either.

You go down mid-channel and the rope saves you, which is what the rope is for, and the pack you were carrying is not saved by anything.
Roped or not, the bottom here is round stones.
Half a day of walking and no drama whatsoever. There is something to be said for it.
There is a seam of nearly-still water behind a submerged boulder, and a queue of patient fish holding station in it. You use their road. It is knee-deep and calm the whole way.
Find the slack line the fish are using

You take the upstream end and plant yourself, and the cold gets into your legs and stays there while five people cross a rope you are personally holding in place.

You go last. You are shaking by then and it does not matter.
Somebody has to be the anchor and it is obviously you.
The rope holds. The packs do not. You reach the far shelf intact and noticeably lighter.
Four in a line, each holding the next, moving on the count. Halfway across the current takes the smallest of you off their feet and the rope does exactly what rope is for.
You walk over water that is trying very hard to be somewhere else, and it does not get a vote. The others follow in your footprints, which hold just long enough.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_drowned_carav:
The tide has gone out over a mudflat and left a caravan standing in it — carts, packs, a cooking pot still upright on its stones. Everything is exactly where it was set down. Nothing is broken.

There are no bodies, and no tracks leading away.
You do not know their names or their rites. You say the words you do know, badly, and go. The tide comes back in behind you and takes the cooking pot.
Set the packs upright, say something, and leave it be

They have not gone. They are standing exactly where they stood, in the same arrangement, facing the water, and they have been standing there through every tide since. One of them notices you noticing. She raises a hand — not a warning. A greeting, from someone with nothing left to warn anyone about. You leave the goods and go.
Feel for what is still standing here
You load up fast and do not look at the cooking pot, which has three bowls set beside it.
Take what you can carry and move on quickly

No struggle, no scatter, no drag-marks. Everyone set down what they were holding and walked into the water together, in step, and the last set of prints is the smallest. You take nothing from the caravan after that. Further up the flat you find a cache they had buried before it happened — the only thing here that was hidden rather than surrendered.
Read the mud — find out what happened here
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_karka_merchan:
The karka has built his workshop out of his own moults — a spiral of discarded shells, each larger than the last, the oldest ones worn smooth as furniture. Inside, he is fitting plate to a customer's cracked carapace with the total absorption of a craftsman who has forgotten there is a world.

He raises one claw: *wait*. Then, a moment later: *now*.
He lays out work in shell, chitin and salvaged metal, and names prices in a clicking dialect that somehow leaves no ambiguity.
See what the shell-wright has made

He works on your armour for two hours without once looking at you, and hands it back better than it was when it was new. There is a small spiral scored inside the collar. His mark, presumably. Or a joke.
Commission a repair on your own gear
He has already forgotten you. The claw moves; the plate settles a hair truer.

You show him how a lap joint is scarfed in metal; he shows you how a moult is scored so it splits along a chosen line instead of the line it wants. Neither of you can fully use the other's craft. Both of you leave better. He presses salvage on you and will not discuss payment.
Offer a smith's technique in trade for a shell-wright's
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_karka_standof:
A karka the size of a fishing boat has wedged itself into the only gap in the reef wall. Its shell is crusted with a century of coral growth — it has been here long enough to become part of the reef.

One claw opens. Closes. It has not decided about you yet.
The claw takes the offering with a delicacy that seems impossible for something that size. It shifts perhaps a hand's width — enough, if you go sideways and do not touch the shell.
Set food on the rock and step back

You count the coral bands aloud — the lean years, the warm years, the year something tore a notch from its left claw. By the time you finish it has lowered itself flat to the rock, which you understand is not submission but welcome. Behind it, in a hollow it has clearly been guarding, are things the sea brought and it never ate.
Read the growth on its shell and speak to its age
A handhold gives. You land badly, directly in front of it, and the claw is already opening.
Coral opens your palms in a dozen places but the karka never looks up. You come down on the far side bleeding and past it.
Climb the reef wall over the top of it
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_makara_feedin:
Something enormous is feeding in the shallows ahead. The makara's back breaks the surface in a long slow arc, over and over, as it works through a shoal that has nowhere left to go. The water is pink for fifty paces.

It has not noticed you. It is, for the moment, extremely busy.

The makara's rhythm is written in the current as clearly as a heartbeat. You cross in the trough of each pass, four paces at a time, and are on the far shore before it lifts its head. It never knew you were there — which, you reflect, is the only victory available here.
Read the water and time your crossing between its passes
The arc of its back does turn your way. It has been aware of you for some time and simply had not finished eating.
You work the tideline while it works the deep, and you are gone with an armload before the arc of its back turns your way.
Dart in and take what it has driven ashore

It takes most of an hour. You spend it face-down on hot rock listening to a thing the size of a barge eat. When the water finally stills, you find the shoal's survivors stranded in the pools — more fish than your party can carry.
Lie flat and wait for it to finish
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_makara_tribut: A line of poles has been driven into the seabed across the whole width of the channel, and from each hangs an offering — fish, coins, a bronze bell, a child's carved boat. At the centre, coiled in water too deep to see the bottom of, something very large is waiting to see what you add to the line.

They do, and the poles record them — the makara's terms are carved on the landward side of the third post, which nobody reads because nobody thinks of a makara as an institution.

It turns out you have already overpaid by walking this far, and you say so.
Somebody set this toll. Tolls have terms.
The coil beneath shifts once, settling, and the channel is simply open. Whatever governs this arrangement, it is scrupulous about its side of it.
Hang gold on the empty pole
You are two poles along when the water beneath you stops being water and starts being throat.
Walk the line without adding anything

You hang the offering and then speak over it, naming the water, the channel, and the thing beneath by the titles owed to something that has held one place since before the reef existed. The response is not sound. It is the entire channel going warm, all at once, like a held breath released. On the far bank you find a second offering waiting: yours, returned, with something added.
Make the offering properly — with the words, not just the goods
The bell rings. Of course the bell rings. That is what the bell is for.

You lift the bronze bell and three purses without disturbing the line, and are across and gone. Somewhere behind you the coil sleeps on. You have gotten away with it. That is not the same as it not counting.
Take from the poles instead of adding to them
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_matsya_ambush:
The water on both sides of the sandbar goes suddenly, completely still — the stillness of a great many things deciding to stop moving at once.

Then the matsya break surface in a ring around you, spears already levelled. They have done this before. They are not in a hurry.
The young one you chose is not the weak point. He was bait.
You go through the youngest of them shoulder-first and are in deep water before the ring can turn. They do not follow past the drop-off.
Pick the weakest point in the ring and charge it
Fight your way off the sandbar

You describe their own trap back to them: the two swimmers who went wide an hour ago, the deliberate noise upstream, the way they let you commit to the bar before closing. The ring loosens. Professionals recognising a professional. They let you go and, unprompted, tell you where the next three ambushes are set.
Compliment the ambush — the placement, the patience, the silence

They take methodically, without malice, leaving you your water and one blade between you. As they sink away the nearest one taps her spear twice on the sand — which you will later learn is how the matsya say 'nothing personal'.
Put down your packs and let them take what they want
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_mercenary_gui: A fortified reef structure flying a plain banner — the same universal mercenary symbol, translated into something that can survive salt water. Inside, armed figures clean weapons or sleep. The work available in the ocean is different from the work available on land, and the going rate reflects the depth.
The quartermaster produces a list. Rates, availability, terms.
You leave the mercenaries to their maintenance.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court#te:
The court convenes in a natural amphitheatre of coral, the assembled naga arranged by age with the oldest lowest and deepest. They are hearing a grievance: two families, one oyster bed, four generations of argument.

The proceedings pause. Every head turns. A visitor is, apparently, more interesting than the oyster bed.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court/ar: You propose that the bed be worked by both families and the harvest split by the tide that brought it — an arrangement neither could have offered without losing face, but which a stranger can suggest freely. There is a very long silence. Then the eldest laughs, a sound like a cave flooding, and the court adopts it on the spot. Four generations, settled by someone who will be gone by evening.
Offer an outsider's judgment on the oyster bed
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court/as: "We remember all of it," she says. "That is the affliction. Your kind forgets and calls it healing." She tells you three things about the world above the water. Two of them you already knew. The third rearranges something.
Ask the eldest what the naga remember of the realms above
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court/at:
It decides quickly and it decides well, and the seat you are given has a view of the proceedings that a trade delegation would have argued for.

You are aware this has nothing to do with anything you have done. It is still the better seat.
The court is deciding where to put you.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court/fl:
Within an hour you are on genuinely warm terms with two junior members of a delegation and one archivist, and the archivist is the one who matters.

What you learn from her is not on the agenda and would not have been raised at it.
A court is only people, and people are your subject.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court/ob: You sit through four hours of argument conducted entirely in a register of extreme courtesy, and understand perhaps a third of it. At the end nobody has won and everybody seems satisfied. The naga consider this an excellent outcome and are pleased you stayed.
Bow and watch the proceedings in silence
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_court/tr: An attendant is detached from the proceedings to deal with you — politely, and with the air of someone glad of the excuse.
Ask leave to trade with the court
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_greeting:
A naga rises from the reef ahead — long, scaled, regarding you with amber eyes that haven't blinked. She circles once, slowly, then stops with her coils wound loosely around a pillar of coral.

'You are not of this water,' she says. It is not quite a question.

She is assessing you. This happens every time something new arrives in the ocean realm. She does not find it alarming — only relevant.

You speak plainly. She listens without interrupting, which is the naga equivalent of a warm welcome.

When you finish, she unwinds from the coral pillar and gestures toward the open water. 'The western currents carry the faster trade. The eastern ones are watched.' She does not explain by whom.

You have been received.
Introduce yourself and explain your purpose

She examines the gift with the patience of someone for whom time is elastic. Then she accepts it.

In return, she describes three things: where the food is, where the danger is, and where the old temple lies. You did not ask about the temple. She offers it anyway, as though it were simply the correct exchange.

You hold it as long as you can, which is not as long as you thought.

The eyes are wrong in a way that takes a moment to locate — there is no lid, and no blink, and nothing behind them that recognises the courtesy you are attempting. When you look away she does not comment on it, which is worse.

'Mm,' she says, and coils back. The audience is over, and you have been placed somewhere in her ordering of things.

You hold her gaze without flinching. She is silent for a long moment.

'Ah,' she says finally, and uncoils. She seems, somehow, pleased. 'The quiet ones always know where they're going.'
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_patrol#t:
Four naga rise out of the channel in formation, coils turning slow circles to hold position against the current. The lead wears a collar of hammered silver and carries no weapon — she does not appear to think she needs one.

"You are walking on the roof of someone's house," she says. "State whose permission you carry."
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_patrol/c: The honesty surprises her into stillness. "No one says that." She considers you for a long moment, then flicks her tail and the formation opens. "Walk quickly. Someone less patient holds the next channel."
Say you carry no one's permission and ask for hers
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_patrol/s: The lead's head turns before you have taken four steps. "They always try the tide," she says, almost bored.
The tide changes and their formation drifts three lengths downstream to compensate. You are across the open water before it closes.
Wait for the current to turn and slip through behind them
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_patrol/w: You shape the greeting the way the current shapes stone — slowly, with the vowels drowned. Her whole posture changes. "You were taught properly. By whom?" You do not answer, and she decides not to press. She gives you the safe line through the reef and the name of a tidal pool worth visiting.
Greet her in the old water-tongue
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_temple#t:
The temple was built on dry land. That was a long time ago. Now the sea comes in through the doorway at every tide and goes out again, and the carvings on the inner walls have been polished featureless from the waist down and remain razor-sharp above.

The upper registers show naga teaching. The lower, worn away, presumably showed who they were teaching.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_temple/e: Salt, silence, and a stone box someone left behind in a hurry a very long time ago.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_temple/l: You leave it to the tide, which has been more patient with it than any worshipper.
This is not yours to enter
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_temple/m: The water comes to your chest and goes away again and comes back. Somewhere in the fourth hour the distinction between the tide's patience and your own stops being useful. You get up when it is over without any clear sense of having decided to.
Sit through a full tide in the flooded nave
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_temple/p:
You go down and do the circuit, which underwater takes longer and hurts more and is in every other respect identical.

The naga who find you doing it are so thoroughly disarmed that the conversation afterwards starts from a position no negotiation would have reached.
It is a temple. The water is a detail.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_naga_temple/r: The sequence is a commentary on desire, carved by people who lived where the water always took things back. The final panel is worn to nothing, but the panel before it shows the teacher's hands open and empty, and you find you do not need the last one.
Read what remains of the teaching registers
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_pearl_merchan:
She has set out her stock on a square of blue cloth weighted at the corners with stones: pearls, mostly, but also polished shell, sea-glass, and a few things that are clearly older than her trade and probably not hers to sell.

"Everything here came out of something living," she says cheerfully. "Prices reflect that."

She goes very still, then picks up the bead and turns it over twice. "Sold to me as a deep-water pearl. Three years ago." She is not angry with you. She is calculating something. Then she hands you a genuine one — small, flawed, real. "For the education. I have an appointment to keep with a man in the shallows."
Point out that one of her 'pearls' is a carved bone bead
She names prices without haggling and watches your hands the entire time.
The pressure turns you back twice, and the third time something large moves past you in the dark and you surface with nothing but a great deal of respect for her profession.

She tells you, laughing, certain the depth will beat you. It nearly does. You come up grey-lipped and shaking with three good ones in your fist, and she buys two on the spot at a price that suggests she has revised her opinion.
Ask which bed the good ones come from, and go get your own
"Come back when the tide's out," she says. "Better stock, worse prices."

You go through the stock stone by stone, noting the flaws out loud in a tone of mild regret.

By the end she has halved two prices to stop you doing it to the rest, which is exactly the mechanism you were relying on.
Pearls have a price and it is not the one on the cloth.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_sunken_ship#t:
A trading vessel lies on her side in four fathoms, close enough to shore that her upper rail breaks the surface at low tide. She has been down long enough to grow a garden and not long enough for the cargo to have rotted.

Something has been at the hull. The tear in her side is not from rock.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_sunken_ship/g:
There is, and it is, and the water in it is black and the angle is wrong and you go down anyway.

You come up with more than the upper decks would have given and rather less breath than you went down with.
There is a hold. Everything good is in the hold.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_sunken_ship/h: A hatch swings shut above you in the dark and it takes a very bad half-minute to find the other way out. You surface with nothing, and stay sat on the rocks for a while.
Three trips down, lungs burning each time. The hold's manifest was accurate: bolts of oiled cloth still dry inside their wrapping, a strongbox, and a case of somebody's carefully packed instruments.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_sunken_ship/l: You walk the shoreline past her. At the low point of the tide the rail shows for a moment, like something surfacing to look.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_sunken_ship/r: You say the words over the water. Nothing visible happens, which is how it usually goes. But the hold, when you enter it afterwards, is simply a room full of goods rather than the other thing it had been — and the tear in the hull, you notice, is on the inside. Something got out. Whatever it was, it is long gone.
Speak the rites for the crew before touching anything
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_sunken_ship/s: The upper cabins are stripped — someone has been here — but the deck fittings are bronze and nobody bothered with them.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_teahouse#text: A structure built into a sea cliff, half-submerged at high tide and bone-dry at low. A fire burns in a sealed alcove. Along the benches: naga, karka, and silhouettes you don't immediately place. The keeper is a broad and unhurried makara current who settled down forty years ago and has been pouring the same tea blend since. Nobody asks the recipe.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_teahouse/leav: You keep going. The smell of salt and smoke follows you out of the cliff.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_teahouse/sit#: You take a seat. The current sets down a cup without asking.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_thermal_vents:
Where the seabed cracks, the water boils. A forest of pale chimneys vents black smoke into cold water, and around each one lives a whole crowded world that has never seen the sun and would die within sight of it.

The karka farm these. There are tool-marks on the nearest chimney.

You take from the seam where the boiling water meets the cold, which is where the interesting compounds precipitate and where a careless hand gets scalded to the bone. It takes hours. What you bring up is worth the hours.
Work the hot vents properly, with a chemist's care
The growth comes away in sheets, strange and rubbery and — according to every alchemist you have ever met — extremely valuable.
Harvest what grows on the cooler chimneys
The water shimmers behind you for a long way.
Give the vents a wide berth
A vent you had judged steady surges as you pass. The water is instantly, unsurvivably hot for about a second and a half, and you are only at the edge of it.
You read the plumes — which vent is steady, which is about to surge — and thread between them to the seam floor, where the good material has been collecting since before anyone was counting.
Dive between the chimneys to reach the deep seam
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_town_magic#te: A settlement built around a thermal vent, where the rising current brings strange minerals and stranger ideas. Water mages and naga sorcerers work from alcoves along the main tunnel. The air smells of sulfur and concentration. Someone is always arguing about the nature of current.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_town_supplies: A market platform on stilts above the tidal flat. Everything needed to survive the reef and deep water — preserved food, medicine, rope, breathing equipment. The sign reads: WHAT YOU NEED. NO QUESTIONS. The price is printed underneath, which saves time.
The shopkeeper nods without looking up.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_town_weapons#: A trading post built into a sea cliff and expanded outward on platform structures above the tideline. Karka shell-wrights and naga-forged spear merchants dominate the market. The clang of metalwork reaches out into open water. Most things for sale here were made to puncture something.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_town_weapons/: You push through to the main stalls.
You skirt the settlement along the reef.
fields.events:animal:animal_ocean_training_camp: A reef plateau where naga warriors train daily — the drills are ancient and precise. They accept outsiders who show genuine commitment. The water here slows everything and makes every technique twice as demanding, which is the point.
A senior naga warrior looks you over once. 'Two sessions. Choose carefully.'
fields.events:animal:animal_ridge_predator#text:
The pass through the thorn ridge narrows to a ledge barely wide enough to walk single file. At its midpoint, something large sits very still.

A marjara — a leopard of immense size, pale as the rock, watching you from exactly the spot the path must cross. His tail moves once, slowly. He does not rise.

He is neither blocking nor permitting. He is simply here, as he has been here many times before, watching what comes through.
fields.events:animal:animal_ridge_predator/figh: He rises from the rock in one fluid motion. His ears flatten. He has done this before.
fields.events:animal:animal_ridge_predator/offe:
You set a portion of food on the rock and retreat two steps. He looks at the offering, looks at you, and then — with the total lack of embarrassment of something that does not require gratitude — takes it.

The path is yours.
Set down some food and step back
fields.events:animal:animal_ridge_predator/pet_:
You want to. Everything in you wants to, and the part of you that knows better is losing the argument until somebody takes your elbow.

You cross without incident and spend the rest of the day defending the impulse, badly.
He is enormous and beautiful and you want to say hello.
fields.events:animal:animal_ridge_predator/proc:
Halfway across, someone's foot finds the one loose stone on the ridge.

It is a small sound. It is enough. He is up and moving before the stone has finished falling, and the crossing becomes a run, and the run becomes a scramble down the scree on the far side with a good deal less dignity than anyone intended.

He does not follow past the ridgeline. He does not need to — he has made his point, and you are bleeding from the places the scree found.

You walk forward with the deliberate calm of something that does not consider itself prey. Each step measured. Gaze steady.

He watches the whole crossing. When you reach the other side, he blinks once — slowly — and looks away. You have been assessed and found unremarkable. In predator terms, this is the best outcome.
Proceed slowly, making no threatening gesture
fields.events:animal:animal_ridge_predator/ritu:
You lower your gaze, expose your throat briefly, and then meet his eyes again without aggression — the grammar of predator recognition. It takes composure you didn't know you had.

He considers this for a long moment. Then he stands, turns, and walks to the edge of the ledge, leaving the path clear. He watches you cross without looking away.
Make the formal greeting between predator-kin
fields.events:animal:animal_sacred_grove#text: Yaksha-marked trees and colored ropes wound around ancient root systems indicate the boundaries of this place. The grove has been tended so long it breathes on its own — the leaves move when nothing else does. Yaksha and Yakshini commune with followers here in the old way: no temples, no intermediaries, just the practitioners and the inhabited earth beneath their feet.
fields.events:animal:animal_sacred_grove/approa: A Yakshini turns and regards you without surprise. Earth magic has a price — she names it.
fields.events:animal:animal_sacred_grove/leave#: You walk on. The light here filters differently than the rest of the forest — warmer, somehow, as though the sun is paying attention.
fields.events:animal:animal_sigh_of_relief#text:
In a forest clearing — or on an open hillside, or at the edge of the reef where the light reaches — you find a great stag standing alone. His rack is hung with orchids. Around him, smaller creatures have gathered: a rabbit, two kapota pigeons, a young vanara sitting cross-legged. The stag is lowering his head, letting them feed from the flowers and mosses growing between his antlers.

No one has asked him to do this. He simply knows it is time.
fields.events:animal:animal_sigh_of_relief/give:
You set down what you can spare and step back. The vanara reaches it first, then shares without being asked.

The stag watches. He has seen this before — the chain of giving. It always surprises him a little.
Leave some of your food for those gathered
fields.events:animal:animal_sigh_of_relief/medi:
You settle into stillness. The stag's attention moves over you once, and then returns to the gathered creatures. That moment of attention is enough — something clear passes through you and keeps going.

You remember that generosity is not sacrifice. It is just knowing it is time.
Meditate in the presence of this
fields.events:animal:animal_sigh_of_relief/take:
You walk into the clearing. The gathered creatures scatter. The stag raises his head and looks at you with amber eyes.

He does not move. He does not attack. He simply regards you until you leave.

You feel, for a long time afterward, that you have been recognized.
Approach and take from what is being offered
fields.events:animal:animal_sigh_of_relief/watc:
You stay at the edge of the clearing and watch until the stag lifts his head and the gathered creatures drift away. Then the clearing is just a clearing again.

You carry the image of it for a long time.
fields.events:animal:animal_temple_of_the_naga#: Offerings of saffron-milk and wild flowers line the path to the shrine — fresh, which means someone was here recently. The naga temple here is older than the settlements that surround it, and the naga who receive worship here are older still. Their presence is felt as a weight in the air, like the moment before rain.
fields.events:animal:animal_temple_of_the_naga/: A practitioner rises smoothly and names the spells they can teach. The price is gold. The naga do not haggle.
You don't touch the flowers. The scent of saffron and something older follows you for a while.
Move on without disturbing the offerings
fields.events:animal:animal_yogini_circle#text: A ring of standing stones in a forest clearing or on a meadow hill — no ceiling, built that way intentionally so the witches can land when they fly in from the sky. The sixty-four forms are inscribed on the inner face of each stone in a script that predates the current tradition of inscription. Practitioners who come here have traveled a long way to reach this circle.
fields.events:animal:animal_yogini_circle/enter: One of the practitioners turns and gestures. No words needed.
fields.events:animal:animal_yogini_circle/pass#: You back away slowly. The air around the circle hums for a long time after.
fields.events:animal:birds_congress#text:
The great assembly tree rises alone on a ridge where forest meets meadow — visible from both territories, which is why it was chosen. Every bird of the realm comes here when the season is right. Kapota and shyena roost three branches apart in a truce older than memory.

A kapota elder calls the session to order with a chant that names every species present. You recognize the structure: a congress, a parliament. They are looking for something. They are, in the old story, always looking for the Simurgh. And, in the old story, they are the Simurgh — but they haven't arrived at that part yet.
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/attend#resu: A kapota messenger escorts you to an observer's perch. Air magic, space magic, and the white traditions of the sky practitioners — all available. The price is a story you haven't told anyone else.
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/attend#titl: Attend the congress and learn from the teachings
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/bird_lover_:
You can, and you do, quietly, and the naming turns out to be the credential — the congress has been addressed by a great many people who did not know a shyena from a garuda.

You are given a place at the lower branches, which is further in than visitors go.
You can name most of the delegations from here.
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/leave#resul: You descend from the ridge. The chant continues behind you, diminishing into the wind.
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/leave#title: Leave the birds to their congress
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/listen#resu:
You sit at the base of the tree for the full congress — hours, perhaps longer. The birds speak in twenty overlapping languages and you understand almost none of it.

But near the end, when the elder names the purpose of the journey, you understand that part. Not the words — the shape of it. The search that finds itself.
fields.events:animal:birds_congress/listen#titl: Listen to the full session without speaking
fields.events:animal:bone_forest#text:
The bones are organized, not scattered. Skulls face east, spines curve north, limb bones arranged radially from the center as though following a diagram. Something has been doing this for a very long time. In the center of the clearing, a practitioner in dark robes performs a slow ritual over a fresh death — a khadga, enormous, at peace.

They don't look up when you approach.

'Looking for death lessons,' they say. 'Or life ones. They're the same here.'
fields.events:animal:bone_forest/assist#result:
You take your position across the body from the practitioner and mirror their movements as best you can. The ritual has its own grammar; you improvise where you don't know the words.

The khadga's presence, enormous even in death, seems to hold still for a moment. Then it passes, as presences do.
fields.events:animal:bone_forest/mourner_reads_:
Somebody decided it, and kept deciding it, for what must be generations — the arrangement is maintained, not merely made.

You find the current keeper by looking for who has been walking here recently, and they are glad to be found.
The skulls face east. Somebody decided that.
fields.events:animal:bone_forest/respect#result: You bow toward the center of the bone arrangement and leave without disturbing anything. The practitioner has already returned to their work.
fields.events:animal:bone_forest/study#result: The practitioner rises, unhurried. Black magic and summoning — the traditions that work with what remains. They name the spells and the prices without ceremony.
fields.events:animal:naga_palace#text: A coral arch rises from the reef, inscribed with naga glyphs marking territorial sovereignty. Two naga warriors flank the entrance but do not move to stop you. Beyond the arch, chambers of living coral lit by bioluminescent algae descend into the deep. Water magic and enchantment traditions have been practiced here without interruption since before the reef was reef.
fields.events:animal:naga_palace/beauty_struck_:
The arch alone would have done it. You stand in front of it for some time with the specific helplessness of somebody who knows exactly what is happening to them and cannot speed it up.

The naga are used to this. One of them waits with you.
You have been ambushed by this before.
fields.events:animal:naga_palace/leave#result: You turn and leave the arch behind. The two warriors watch you go without expression.
fields.events:animal:naga_palace/observe#result:
You bow in the naga manner — low, without breaking eye contact — and withdraw. The court watches. A minor official nods very slightly.

You have not been insulted. In naga terms, this is an achievement.
fields.events:animal:naga_palace/observe#title: Observe the court protocol and withdraw respectfully
fields.events:animal:naga_palace/study#result: A court official receives you with formal courtesy. They have everything the ocean's magic traditions offer. The price is calibrated to what you can pay, which means they already know.
fields.events:animal:termite_cathedral#text: The mound rises fifteen feet, engineered with an architect's precision for temperature and airflow. Carved archways mark the entrance in a script older than any living tradition. Inside, something hums at a frequency felt in the chest rather than heard by the ear. Yaksha practitioners and bhramara allies have used this place as a center of earth-consciousness work for as long as the mound has stood.
fields.events:animal:termite_cathedral/curious_:
You spend the afternoon working out the ventilation, which is the part that should not be possible, and by evening you have it: the mound breathes on a temperature differential and the whole structure is a lung.

You will be thinking about this for weeks.
Fifteen feet of engineering and nobody drew the plans.
fields.events:animal:termite_cathedral/leave#re: The hum follows you for longer than the mound is visible.
fields.events:animal:termite_cathedral/offering: You set your offering at the carved archway and stand back. The hum shifts frequency very slightly — just once. You take that as acknowledgement.
Leave an offering at the base of the mound
fields.events:animal:termite_cathedral/study#re: A yaksha practitioner emerges from the main chamber. Earth magic, summoning, and the basics of alchemy — the cathedral has all three. She names the prices plainly.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor#text: A figure in a creditor's sash steps into the firelight. It looks like no one in particular. It knows exactly who you are.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/debtor_knows:
You know the form: never deny the debt, never accept the figure, and always counter-propose a schedule.

It works on the dead as well as it works on the living, which is either reassuring or extremely bleak.
You have had this conversation before, with worse.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/negotiate#re: Three rounds of negotiation in the cold air. You emerge with an arrangement no one is happy with, which is the mark of a good deal. The creditor departs without incident. The ledger, as far as you can tell, now balances.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/negotiate#ti: Enter into negotiation — there is always a way to restructure.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/pay#result: It accepts payment. It looks faintly disappointed that there was nothing to argue about. It leaves. The camp feels lighter.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/pay#title: Pay what it asks without argument.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/refuse#resul: It notes this down in a ledger you cannot see. It does not argue. It leaves, which is somehow worse than if it had.
fields.events:domain:camp_creditor/refuse#title: Tell it you don't recognise the debt.
fields.events:domain:camp_ember_voices#text: Deep in the night, the campfire rises without reason. Between the popping of burning wood, something close to words — close enough that three people heard three different things.
fields.events:domain:camp_ember_voices/ignore#r: By morning the fire is cold ash. Whether anything was there or not, it is settled now.
fields.events:domain:camp_ember_voices/ignore#t: It's the heat. Go back to sleep.
fields.events:domain:camp_ember_voices/listen#r: The words aren't in any language, but the meaning arrives whole: a route, a danger, a name that matters. Whether this realm is warning you or baiting you, the information feels true.
fields.events:domain:camp_ember_voices/listen#t: Sit quietly and listen for meaning.
fields.events:domain:camp_ember_voices/speak_ba: The fire goes out. All of it, without smoke or cooling, just gone. It takes a long time to relight. No one speaks much after.
The fire brightens, then settles. Something received your address. The embers arrange and rearrange in patterns that suggest approval. You feel, briefly, observed and acknowledged.
Answer it — ask what it wants.
fields.events:domain:camp_fire_omen#text: The campfire flares without fuel. In the smoke, shapes coil and reform — faces, or something like faces — watching.
fields.events:domain:camp_fire_omen/extinguish#: The smoke curls and dissipates into the dark. The camp is cold for the rest of the night. Nothing comes of it, but nothing was risked either.
Smother the fire. You don't want to see.
fields.events:domain:camp_fire_omen/read_omen#f: The shapes shift too fast. By the time anything resolves, the fire has died back to coals. You saw something, but cannot say what.
fields.events:domain:camp_fire_omen/read_omen#s: The smoke forms something unmistakable — a path you haven't taken, a face you'll encounter, a moment of decision that has not yet arrived. The fire dims and the vision closes.
fields.events:domain:camp_fire_omen/read_omen#t: Watch the smoke and try to read it.
fields.events:domain:camp_guardian_threshold#te: Something stands at the very limit of the firelight. It has been there for some time. It is not threatening — it simply waits, in the particular way that a very old grievance waits.
fields.events:domain:camp_guardian_threshold#ti: At the Edge of the Light
fields.events:domain:camp_guardian_threshold/he: It speaks, or something like speaking happens. The story is circular and old — a wrong done long before any of you were born, compounding through each retelling. You acknowledge it without agreeing. The presence recedes satisfied, or at least finished.
Invite it to speak. A grievance aired is one less thing blocking the path.
fields.events:domain:camp_guardian_threshold/wa: It does leave with the light. One of the party barely slept. The camp breaks in an uneasy silence that no one names.
Watch it until dawn. It has to leave with the light.
The ritual is imperfect but sincere. The presence retreats from the boundary you've established. By morning it is gone, and the camp feels marginally warmer for it.
Perform a brief warding. Give it a boundary rather than an audience.
fields.events:domain:camp_night_vision#text: In the deep hours of the night, one of the party stirs from sleep with something vivid and strange behind their eyes.
fields.events:domain:camp_night_vision/ignore#r: By morning it is gone. Just a dream, probably. The camp breaks in ordinary silence.
fields.events:domain:camp_night_vision/ignore#t: Let it fade — dreams are just noise.
fields.events:domain:camp_night_vision/remember: The image is clear: a path, a figure, a moment yet to come. Whether prophecy or fancy, it burns itself into memory. The dreamer rises feeling purposeful.
Hold onto the vision — it felt like a warning.
fields.events:domain:camp_shared_dream#text: In the morning it becomes clear that every member of the party dreamed the same thing. The details vary — but the place, the light, the unspoken pressure of it — identical.
fields.events:domain:camp_shared_dream/compare_: The point where all accounts agree is a detail no one remarked on individually — a mark, a position, a quality of attention. When you locate it, something like recognition moves through the group. A shared dream properly examined becomes a kind of preparation.
Sit together and map the differences. There's something in the overlap.
fields.events:domain:camp_shared_dream/dreamer_:
The others describe a dream. You describe the *shape* of one, which turns out to be the thing they were all failing to say.

Once it has a shape, the differences between the four accounts become the interesting part.
You dream like this most nights. Take the lead.
fields.events:domain:camp_shared_dream/move_on#: The camp breaks in ordinary silence. Whatever the dream was trying to say, it did not say it.
Say nothing. Dreams are not decisions.
fields.events:domain:camp_shared_dream/write_it: Committed to paper, the dream becomes a document. Whether it's useful or not, it's no longer just a feeling in the air between you — it's a record, and records have a way of meaning something eventually.
Record what you remember before it fades.
fields.events:domain:camp_stranger_fire#text: A light on the hillside — too steady and too warm to be a spirit. Another camp. They haven't signalled, but they haven't hidden either.
fields.events:domain:camp_stranger_fire/approac: They receive you with flat unfriendliness. Not hostile — but by the time you've returned to your own fire, you've gained nothing and spent an awkward hour.
Traders, or something close to traders — three of them, neutral in disposition, willing to part with supplies at a fair price. You part on workmanlike terms.
fields.events:domain:camp_stranger_fire/gossip_:
They are three traders, badly lost, and delighted to see anyone at all.

By the time you go back to your own fire you have their route, their prices, and an unflattering account of a guard captain two days ahead.
Of course you are going to go and find out who they are.
fields.events:domain:camp_stranger_fire/signal#: They signal back — a single lamp moved twice. Then nothing more. Whoever they are, they're occupied or cautious. You sleep well enough anyway.
Signal peacefully and wait to see if they respond.
fields.events:domain:camp_stranger_fire/watch#r: Their fire goes out before yours. Two of them — moving efficiently, no wasted motion. Scouts or couriers, from their routine. Nothing threatening. The knowledge costs you some sleep but not much.
fields.events:domain:camp_stranger_fire/watch#t: Keep watch and observe without contact.
fields.events:domain:camp_wandering_spirit#text: The fire has burned low. In the outer dark, something moves — not threatening, not quite gone. A presence lingers at the edge of the light.
fields.events:domain:camp_wandering_spirit/mour:
You do it the way it is done at home: a place, not an offering. Somewhere to sit rather than something to take.

It sits. That appears to have been the whole request, and in the morning the fire has burned down more slowly than it should have.
Set out a place for it. Properly.
fields.events:domain:camp_wandering_spirit/offe: In the morning, the offering is gone. The camp feels lighter somehow. Something difficult has passed through and moved on.
Leave a small offering of food at the fire's edge.
fields.events:domain:camp_wandering_spirit/spea: It does not answer with words, but it turns toward the sound of your voice and then recedes, as if the acknowledgement itself was enough. A small thing done well.
Speak to it — ask what it wants.
fields.events:domain:camp_wandering_spirit/ward: It retreats into the dark. The camp is quiet after, but something about the night feels heavier.
Drive it off with noise and light.
fields.events:domain:camp_whispered_offering#te: You wake to find the camp's food supplies disturbed. Nothing taken — but arranged. Placed. A small portion of each item separated from the rest, set near the fire's edge, as if left for someone who didn't eat.
fields.events:domain:camp_whispered_offering/le: You set it out with care. By the next morning, the portion is gone, and whatever sorted your supplies has not returned.
Leave a proper offering — deliberately, this time.
fields.events:domain:camp_whispered_offering/ri: Consecrated food reaches further in this realm than it has any right to. The arrangement disappears, and for a moment you catch something at the periphery of the firelight that might have been gratitude.
Consecrate the offering properly with a brief ritual.
fields.events:domain:camp_whispered_offering/se: Nothing more is disturbed that night. In the morning the small arranged portion is still there, untouched.
Secure the supplies and post a watch.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace#text:
A palace materialises before you — or perhaps you have drifted into it without noticing. Its halls are open to the sky, its floors are cloud made solid underfoot. Through gaps in the floor, far below, you can see the tops of mountains. Through gaps in the ceiling, open sky.

Slithering through the amber light, singing to one another in voices like slow rain on stone, are nagas — a rare breed that rules the clouds and weather. Vast and iridescent, utterly absorbed in their song. They have not yet noticed you.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/attack#result: The song stops. The nagas uncoil.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/join_chorus#r: You find the thread of the melody and follow it in. One naga turns a great head toward you — eyes like water, expression unreadable — and then returns to the song. You have been included. When the chorus ends, the nagas coil and settle, regarding you with something that might be warmth. There are things they are willing to teach.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/join_chorus#t: Listen carefully and join their chorus.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/offerings#res: The song does not stop, but it shifts — a new note braided in, low and enquiring. One naga descends to inspect the offerings. It touches each item with the tip of its tongue. A long pause. Then it looks at you with those water-coloured eyes and the song shifts again, opening a space for you to enter. You have been acknowledged. They are willing to share something of what they know.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/offerings#tit: Listen in, then step forward and set out offerings: fruits, perfumed water, their favourite herbs and spices.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/pocket_jewels:
Your hand closes around something that feels like a frozen raindrop cut into a gem the size of a fist. The song stops.

They are not slow.
Walk inside and try to pocket some of their jewels while they are distracted.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace/talk_to_them#: You step through into the heart of the palace. The song reverberates in your chest. The nagas slither in vast arcs around the pillars, absorbed completely in their chorus — and then, one by one, they notice you.
Walk inside and try to talk to them.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace_inner#text:
The song stops. Every naga in the palace has turned to regard you. The silence is the silence of held weather.

The largest — coiled around a pillar of frozen cloud, scales catching the amber light like hammered silver — opens its mouth.

"Who daresss interrupt the sssong?"
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace_inner/back_ta:
There is a pause that contains weather systems.

"A guesssst," the large naga says, very softly, "isss invited."

What comes next is not words. When you come back to yourself you are standing outside. The palace is gone. The sky above is the particular grey of something that has already decided to rain.
"Is that any way to treat a guest?"
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace_inner/charm_r:
The naga stares at you for a long, terrible moment. Then it opens its mouth, and what comes out is not words. It is weather.

When you come back to yourself you are standing outside, alone. The palace is gone. Your bones ache with a deep cold.

You have spent years learning how to walk into rooms that do not want you and leave them differently. The large naga blinks — a slow, contemplative gesture — and something shifts in its posture.

"You," it says, "are either very brave or very foolish." It sounds like a compliment. They are willing to teach.
Smile, open your hands, and try to win them over on pure charm.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace_inner/persuad:
You speak carefully and at length. The nagas listen with the patience of creatures that measure time in rainstorms. The large one's tail shifts — once, then again. At last it makes a sound like distant thunder and the others settle.

"Ssso. You have a tongue worth hearing." They are willing to teach.
Bow low and explain, with all the words you have, why you have come and what you offer.
fields.events:domain:cloud_palace_inner/yoga_ha: You close your eyes and stop resisting the sound. The song fills you and passes through you, using you briefly as an instrument. The nagas relax — one by one, they return to their spiralling. The largest turns those water-coloured eyes on you and inclines its head. You have not interrupted the song. You have become, briefly, a part of it. They are willing to teach.
Breathe, settle, and let the song you were interrupting continue through you.
fields.events:domain:court_of_the_musician_prin:
A lavish building rises before you, its doors open to the warm air. Inside, a half-naked man sits in a carved chair, eyes closed, strumming a sitar with total absorption. He does not appear to notice your arrival.

A servant materializes at your elbow, inclining his head politely. 'Welcome. How may I serve you?'
The Court of the Musician Prince

'My lord always had the soul of an artist first, and ruler only second,' the servant says, with unmistakable pride. 'Some years ago, an itinerant yogi came to court and taught him that the path to awakening need not pass through renunciation — that music itself, heard rightly, is a door. The yogi has since moved on, as such men do. My lord has not moved at all.'

He glances toward the prince with something between concern and devotion. 'We manage.'
Ask about the prince and the state of his court.

The servant blinks, as if the question has surprised him from a great distance. He produces a few coins from somewhere about his person and presses them into your hand with the vague goodwill of someone performing a gesture they have been taught. You find yourself outside. The door closes quietly.
Ask if they could spare anything for travelers.
'I'm afraid my lord has very little in the way of worldly affairs to attend to anymore,' the servant says, pleasantly but with a finality that suggests the topic is closed.
Ask if they need any hired hands.

The court is composed entirely of people who do this professionally, and they recognise a colleague.

You are given a seat, a drink, and a reputation you will have to spend the rest of the evening defending.
Tell the court who has just arrived.
You step back into the open air. Inside, the music continues without interruption.

You find a place to sit and simply listen. The music is complex past comprehension — and then, quite suddenly, it isn't. You hear through it to something else: the source of the sound, the silence inside each note. After some time, the prince opens one eye. He looks at you with faint surprise, then nods curtly, as if settling a question he had been asking himself.

'Yes,' he says. 'Come.'
Sit and listen. Not to the notes — to what is between them.

The servant hesitates, then steps aside. You take a seat near the prince and begin to play. A long moment passes. Then, without opening his eyes, the prince adjusts his melody to harmonize with yours — a conversation with no words in it. When you finally stop, he opens his eyes and looks at you directly for the first time.

'Stay a while,' he says. 'I have something to show you.'
Take out your instrument and play alongside him.

You do not have his hands. You do have the shape of the thing, and you give him back the second half of a line he had left open — badly, in the wrong metre, and unmistakably the right line.

He stops playing. Then he starts again, from your version.
He is playing a form. Answer it in the form.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave#text:
The cave mouth is unremarkable — a crack in a hillside. Inside, it opens into something else entirely. Formations of crystal the height of houses catch what little light enters and multiply it into thousands of beams, filling the space with cold, sourceless radiance.

At the centre, seated in perfect stillness on bare stone, is a man. He is old. He is completely naked. He is meditating, and does not appear to notice you at all.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/ask_secrets#r:
He opens one eye. He looks you over slowly. Then he smiles — not warmly, exactly, but as if amused by something he's been waiting to see.

'You speak the right language,' he says. 'Then you will understand what I am about to tell you.'
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/ask_secrets#t: Ask him about the secrets of this cave.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/attack#result:
You raise your weapon. He opens his eyes.

The cave is gone. You are standing on the hillside in the open air. There is no crack in the rock, no crystal, no yogi. Only a very faint impression of sadness that may be yours or may be his — it is difficult to tell.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/meditate#resu:
You sit. The cave does the rest. After some time — minutes or hours, it is impossible to say — the yogi opens his eyes. He looks at you the way people look at someone they recognise from a long time ago.

'You already know some of this,' he says. 'Let me show you the rest.'
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/meditate#titl: Sit down and meditate alongside him.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/offerings#res:
You set down what you have brought — a little gold, a little food — and bow. The yogi does not open his eyes. But something in the cave shifts. The light settles differently on you.

You feel cleaner, somehow. Sharper. You carry the blessing forward.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/offerings#tit: Leave him offerings and ask for a blessing.
fields.events:domain:crystal_cave/pilgrim_offer:
You set it out in the correct order, which takes a while and which he watches without comment.

When you finally do ask, he answers as though you had been introduced, rather than as though you had arrived.
Do the offering properly before asking for anything.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave#text:
No light reaches the depths of this cave. The darkness is not empty — it has a quality to it, a density that suggests something is happening inside it.

At the back wall, barely visible, is a small opening the size of a fist. Beside it, a shallow bowl, worn smooth.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/ask_teachings#re:
A voice comes from the other side of the wall — unhurried, neither welcoming nor unwelcoming.

'The dark will teach you, if you sit with it long enough.'

Silence.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/leave#result: You step back into the light. The cave says nothing. The darkness continues its practice without you.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/push_food#result:
'Thank you, child.'

The bowl on your side is already empty. On the other side, the sound of something being received with care.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/push_food#title: Push some food through the opening in the wall.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/push_money#resul:
A pause.

'I don't need this, child.'

The coins reappear in the bowl on your side, one by one.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/push_money#title: Push some money through the opening in the wall.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/secret_bearer_wa:
You wait. You do not fill the silence, which is apparently the examination.

What comes through the wall eventually is four words long. You will be thinking about it for some time.
She has not spoken in thirty years. You can manage an hour.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/space_perception:
You let your perception settle and expand. The stone is there — cold, dense, indifferent. And then, not through it but somehow alongside it: a quality of light that is not light, sourceless, neither warm nor cold, bleeding outward through the rock without diminishing.

A pause from the other side of the wall. Then, quietly: 'I see you have some eyes of your own.' The sound of something being moved. 'Come then. Let's compare notes.'
Still your perception. Not the stone — the quality of what is in the stone.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/yoga_sit#result:
You sit. The dark settles around you. Visions begin — first muddled and confused, images and sounds without coherence, then gradually clarifying, like sediment falling through still water.

After some hours, a quiet laugh from the other side of the wall.

'You've shown the purity of your intent. I'll teach you a little — but keep practicing on your own.'
fields.events:domain:dark_cave/yoga_sit#title: Sit on this side of the wall and wait. Without expectation.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave_interior#text: The silence continues. The darkness has the same quality as before — dense, inhabited. The small opening in the wall. The worn bowl.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave_interior/leave#r: You step back into the light. The cave says nothing. The darkness continues its practice without you.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave_interior/push_fo:
'Thank you, child.'

The bowl on your side is already empty. On the other side, the sound of something being received with care.
Push some food through the opening in the wall.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave_interior/push_mo:
A pause.

'I don't need this, child.'

The coins reappear in the bowl on your side, one by one.
Push some money through the opening in the wall.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave_interior/space_p:
You let your perception settle and expand. The stone is there — cold, dense, indifferent. And then, not through it but somehow alongside it: a quality of light that is not light, sourceless, neither warm nor cold, bleeding outward through the rock without diminishing.

A pause from the other side of the wall. Then, quietly: 'I see you have some eyes of your own.' The sound of something being moved. 'Come then. Let's compare notes.'
Still your perception. Not the stone — the quality of what is in the stone.
fields.events:domain:dark_cave_interior/yoga_si:
You sit. The dark settles around you. Visions begin — first muddled and confused, images and sounds without coherence, then gradually clarifying, like sediment falling through still water.

After some hours, a quiet laugh from the other side of the wall.

'You've shown the purity of your intent. I'll teach you a little — but keep practicing on your own.'
Sit on this side of the wall and wait. Without expectation.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain#text:
A mountain of glass rises from the plain — not metaphor, not illusion. Pure fused silica, facets the size of houses catching the light and throwing it in every direction. The surface is perfectly smooth and perfectly vertical. There is no path up. There is no grip.

At the summit, something moves.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/admire#resu: You stand at the base of the mountain and look up. The light changes as you watch — slowly, the way a day changes, but condensed. Somewhere in the complexity of the refracted surface is something you cannot name but will not forget.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/admire#titl: Stand and look at it for a while. Some things teach by being looked at.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/air_ascent#: You step off the ground and let the wind take you — drifting upward along the face of the mountain, close enough to see your own distorted reflection in every facet. At the summit, glass spirits dance in slow, glitching loops, throwing light in directions that make no sense. One drifts close and holds the shape of something familiar — your face, perhaps, or the memory of one. Then it disperses, chiming softly.
Let the air carry you up.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/beauty_stru:
You have seen something like this before — that is the trouble with having been struck once. You know what it is you are looking at.

You stay until the light moves off it. Nobody hurries you.
Stop. Do not climb it, do not speak to it. Look at it.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/earth_speec: You press your hands to the surface and speak to what it used to be. There is a long moment. Then the glass does not open exactly — it simply stops being a wall in the way that it was. You walk through and up, the mountain permitting. At the summit, glass spirits spiral in their slow broken arcs. They feel very old. They feel like they have been waiting.
Speak to the glass as stone. It was sand once — and before that, it was earth.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/incurious_w: You go around. It takes an extra day and involves no revelation of any kind, which is precisely the outcome you were after.
It is a mountain made of glass. Note it and go around.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/meditate_at: You sit. The mountain does not move. You stop expecting it to. At some point — you cannot say when — you are at the summit, seated in the same posture, and the glass spirits are circling you in their glitching arcs, throwing light across your closed eyelids in patterns that carry meaning. You have not climbed the mountain. You have stopped being someone who needed to.
Sit at the base and meditate. Stop trying to climb.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/scale#failu: You slip. The glass offers nothing to hold and less to forgive — you slide and tumble, cutting yourself on the way down. The mountain stands unchanged.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/scale#succe: Your fingers find edges too fine to see, your weight shifts by instinct rather than thought. Slowly, impossibly, you climb. At the summit: glass spirits drifting in slow, glitching arcs — each movement a fraction out of time with the last, refracting light into cascades that should not be possible. They do not speak. They seem to notice you the way light notices a prism. Something passes between you.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/scale#title: Attempt to scale the glass face.
fields.events:domain:glass_mountain/sing_to_it#: You begin to sing — nothing composed, just what comes. The mountain answers. A harmonic rises from somewhere inside the glass, and then another, and footholds crystallise along the face as if the mountain is remembering how to be climbed. At the summit the glass spirits dance faster for a moment, producing tones you can almost hear. A faint luck settles on you like dust: the mountain was pleased.
fields.events:domain:rel_cool_thaw#text:
{a} and {b} are not fighting. They are doing the other thing — the scrupulous politeness, the passing of the water skin at arm's length.

It has been four days of this and the whole camp is tired of it.
fields.events:domain:rel_cool_thaw#title: Neither of Them Will Say It
fields.events:domain:rel_cool_thaw/force_it#res:
It takes them most of the morning, mostly in silence.

They come back having not discussed it at all, and having somehow discussed it entirely.
fields.events:domain:rel_cool_thaw/force_it#tit: Give them a job that needs both of them and walk away.
fields.events:domain:rel_cool_thaw/ignore#resul: They are adults, and it does not improve. The politeness gets a little more scrupulous.
fields.events:domain:rel_cool_thaw/talk_to_each: It is, as it usually is, one remark made two weeks ago that one of them does not remember making and the other has not stopped hearing.
Talk to each of them separately. Find out what it actually is.
fields.events:domain:rel_rivals_flashpoint#text:
{a} and {b} have been circling something for days, and tonight it arrives — over nothing, over a pot and whose turn it was, in the way these things always arrive over nothing.

The rest of the camp has gone very quiet.
fields.events:domain:rel_rivals_flashpoint/let_:
It is ugly and thorough and it takes about twenty minutes.

At the end of it they are not friends, but the thing that was under the surface is now above it, where everyone can see it, which is safer.
Let them have it out. Words only.
fields.events:domain:rel_rivals_flashpoint/medi:
You make them do it properly, one at a time, no interruptions.

It emerges that they are angry about two entirely different things, and have each spent a week being furious about the wrong one.
Get between them and make them each say the actual grievance.
fields.events:domain:rel_rivals_flashpoint/shut:
They obey, because of how you said it.

Nothing is resolved. Nothing gets worse tonight either, which was the immediate problem.
End it. Both of you, opposite sides of the fire, now.
fields.events:domain:rel_sworn_watch#text:
{a} takes second watch, which is {b}'s. No discussion, no announcement — they simply do not wake them.

In the morning {b} works it out from the burn-down of the fire and says nothing about it, which is its own kind of answer.
fields.events:domain:rel_sworn_watch/leave_it#r: Whatever the two of them have built, it does not require your supervision. The party moves a little easier for the rest of the week.
fields.events:domain:rel_sworn_watch/use_it#res:
You put them on the same flank and spend an evening on what each of them is going to assume the other is doing.

It shows almost immediately.
fields.events:domain:rel_sworn_watch/use_it#tit: Two who trust each other that far should be fighting together.
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa#text: On the open terrace of a small gompa, a yogi sits gazing single-pointedly at the sky. A soft rainbow shimmer is reflected in their eyes. As you approach, they smile and greet you with a gesture.
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/bless_us#r: The yogi's eyes soften. They place their hands together and murmur a mantra, then touch each of you lightly on the crown of the head. A warmth radiates outward.
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/bless_us#t: "Please bless us for this life and the next, master."
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/bow_and_le: You place what you can afford at the foot of the yogi's seat. They incline their head in acknowledgment. A faint warmth accompanies you as you descend the terrace steps.
Bow, place some offerings, and leave.
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/lapsed_ask:
It comes out badly. It comes out, which is more than it has done in a long while.

The answer does not resolve anything. It does establish, quite gently, that the question was always allowed.
Ask the question you stopped asking years ago.
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/source_of_: The yogi just laughs — a clear, boundless sound — and gestures you inside. There, arranged on low tables, are things you have never seen offered anywhere else.
"What is the source of the shimmer in your eyes I can't help but notice, master?"
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/teach_perf: Gladly, the yogi explains the workings of the mind as swirling reflections of rainbow light in a crystalline prism. The teaching opens doors you did not know were closed.
"Please teach us about the Great Perfection."
fields.events:domain:skygazing_gompa/what_are_y: "Observing the unceasing movement of the stream of the sky, friend." The yogi says nothing more, but the simplicity of the answer lingers with you long after you leave.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage#text:
On an exposed ridge, in full sight of the howling wind, a group of yogis sit cross-legged in the snow. They wear nothing but thin white linen. Steam rises from their bodies in visible wisps, melting the snow in a circle around each of them.

The oldest sits at the centre, utterly still, eyes open but seeing elsewhere. Slightly apart, the youngest shivers — barely perceptibly, but his toes have gone the faint blue of someone fighting a losing battle with the cold.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/ascet:
You sit. The cold does what cold does and you let it, and at some point the distinction between enduring it and not minding it stops being available.

One of them opens their eyes at the end and gives you a single nod, which appears to be the local currency.
You have sat in worse for less reason.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/ask_t:
The eldest yogi opens his eyes and regards you for a long moment. He nods once. The youngest, still shivering, looks up at you with something like relief — perhaps he will learn more if you are here too.

The teachings begin.
Approach, bow deeply, and ask for teachings.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/circu:
You walk the circle three times, quietly, and place what you have brought at the edge of their warmth. None of them acknowledge this directly. But as you turn to leave, the youngest yogi's shivering has stopped.

Something of their steadiness travels with you.
Circumambulate the group, set out small offerings, and leave them in peace.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/fire_:
The warmth flickers and goes out. The eldest yogi watches, patient and kind.

'The fire is there,' he says. 'But it needs tending before it can burn steadily. The doors of this hermitage will be open to you when you return, more mature in your practice, young sadhaka.'

Something in his words leaves a warmth in you that your technique could not produce.

You let it rise — the warmth from the secret place below the navel, imperfect but real. The youngest yogi's eyes go wide. The eldest smiles: not at the technique, which is rough, but at the unmistakable sincerity behind it.

'You have found the door,' he says. 'Come, let us show you what is behind it.'
You have some knowledge of inner heat yourself. Show them — not as a challenge, because you cannot help it.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/leave: You walk on. The sound of the wind returns. The steam rising from their circle diminishes behind you.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/sit_i:
The cold defeats you. You last longer than seems reasonable, but it defeats you. The youngest yogi — still shivering himself, toes still blue — gives you a small, sympathetic look as you scramble to your feet.

You carry the cold in your bones for a while after.

You have no technique. You have only stubbornness and the refusal to move. Minutes pass. The cold becomes a presence, then a voice, then a kind of silence. When you open your eyes, the eldest is looking at you.

'No technique,' he says, 'but something that technique cannot give. Sit closer. There is something we can show you.'
Say nothing. Sit down in the snow beside them and see how long you last.
fields.events:domain:snowcapped_hermitage/water:
The cold defeats you well before it touches them. The eldest yogi says nothing for a long time. When he speaks, there is no cruelty in it.

'You are not ready for the dharma taught in this place. Return once your merit grows.'

Your mastery of water is formidable — the cold bends to your will, and the youngest yogi has gone very still watching you. The eldest meets your eyes throughout, unshaken.

'Impressive,' he says at last. 'But your attitude is poisoned by arrogance. What you sought was not knowledge — it was victory. We will teach you anyway, because the fire does not care why you came, only that you did. But you will pay more for what arrogance has cost.'
Challenge them to a contest of cold resistance. They seem so untouchable — surely it cannot hurt to test them.
fields.events:domain:the_pit#text:
The path descends into a vast muddy hollow. Dozens of mudlings — squat, glistening figures of animated muck — mill about in the thick brown sludge below. They have a crude camp of sorts: stacked bones, offerings of rusted metal, a clumsily drawn circle of wet earth in the center.

One large mudling turns its featureless face toward you. A sound like bubbling tar rises from its throat. The others still.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/beast_tender_reads:
They are arranged the way a nesting colony is arranged — the small ones inward, the big ones facing out, and the whole thing pointed away from something rather than toward you.

You back out along the line they are not watching, and nothing follows.
They are not a mob. Look at how they are arranged.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/bribe#result: The large mudling reaches out a dripping limb and takes the sacks. One by one they are passed back through the colony and buried reverently in the central circle — seeds going into the earth, the way things are supposed to go. The mudlings make a sound like a long satisfied exhale of thick air. The elder turns back to you, willing to share what it knows.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/bribe#title: Offer most of your food stores as tribute — seeds, grain, everything you can carry forward.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/earth_magic#result: You call stone and soil to your hands and let the deep vibration speak. The mudlings go utterly still. Then, one by one, they prostrate themselves in the mud. The elder rises and presses both palms against your chest — it recognises a peer, and is willing to teach.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/earth_magic#title: Demonstrate mastery of earth. Let them see what the deep stone knows.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/mud_puppet_play#fa: Your puppet stumbles. Your plot collapses. The mudlings watch politely for a moment, then begin pelting you with clods. You flee the pit covered head to toe — but oddly, not harmed.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/mud_puppet_play#su: You give them heroes. You give them tragedy. You give them a protagonist who is unmistakably the large elder mudling, whose courage is legendary, whose mud is the finest mud in all the realms. The colony erupts into a sound like a dozen geysers firing at once. Applause. The elder mudling — visibly moved, perhaps slightly embarrassed — gestures toward the central circle. You are welcome to learn.
fields.events:domain:the_pit/mud_puppet_play#ti: Stage an impromptu mud puppet play — a heroic epic specifically about the mudlings. Their ancient glories. Their terrible battles. The beauty of their mud.
fields.events:domain:the_smoking_mirror#text:
