fields.events:hell:hell_the_invitation/ignore#r:
You set the envelope back on the rock and continue on your way.

Behind you, the envelope waits. A faint sense of disappointment from a specific direction — calm, professional, patient. The kind of disappointment that is already adjusting its timeline.

Someday, you think, you will want to know what was in that letter.
fields.events:hell:hell_the_invitation/ignore#t: Set it back on the rock and walk on
fields.events:hell:hell_the_invitation/read_sce: A new lava flow has already covered whatever marks were here. The ash tells you nothing. You're left exactly as uncertain as before.

The ash around the rock is undisturbed except for one set of prints — small, deliberate, placed and then retreated. No ambush position. No disturbance in the lava flow. Whoever left this came alone and didn't wait to watch. The invitation might be genuine.
Look for signs of who placed this — tracks, timing, intent written in the ash
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul#text:
A ghostly figure sits amid the frost, weeping silently. Unlike the mindless lost souls, this one retains its form — the shape of an old woman in tattered robes.

"Can you see me? Truly see me? So few can anymore..."
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/exorcise: You write a mandala of liberation by sight around her. She dissolves into light, leaving a piece of turquoise behind.
Perform a ritual to release her spirit
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/haunted_:
You do not offer advice, because there is none, and you do not tell them it passes, because you would be lying.

What you do is stay until the worst of the current one is over. It is apparently not something anyone has done for them before.
You know what it is like when the memory arrives uninvited.
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/help#res: She dissolves into light with a sigh. In life, she was a healer who once turned away a sick wanderer for a lack of payment.
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/help#tit: Use white magic to ease her suffering
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/ignore#r: The weeping grows quieter, then stops. The cold deepens.
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/ignore#t: Walk past — you have enough of your own problems
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/listen#r: She speaks of small cruelties compounded until her breath grows a little longer and slower.
fields.events:hell:hell_tormented_soul/summon_g:
You call a guide spirit — one of the patient ones, without agenda — and ask it to wait with her. It settles beside the old woman with the quality of something that has done this before.

She looks at it for a long moment. Then at you. 'You can see me.' Not a question anymore. A fact, confirmed.

The guide spirit takes her hand. Her form steadies. Something releases in her posture.

You leave them together.
Summon a guide spirit to show her the way forward
fields.events:hell:hell_town_magic#text: A settlement where more windows glow than can be explained by candlelight. Strange smells drift from the apothecary. A scholar argues with a demon outside the library.
fields.events:hell:hell_town_magic/#1#result: You leave the scholars to their arguments.
fields.events:hell:hell_town_supplies#text: A trading post that survives on practicality. The sign reads: FOOD. TOOLS. NO CREDIT. It is the most honest thing you have seen in hell.
fields.events:hell:hell_town_supplies/#0#result: The shopkeeper nods without looking up.
fields.events:hell:hell_town_weapons#text: A settlement built from salvaged iron and spite. The biggest building is the armoury. Someone is always selling something in the street, and half of it is sharp.
fields.events:hell:hell_town_weapons/#1#result: You skirt the settlement and keep moving.
fields.events:hell:hell_veterans_camp#text: A sparse camp around a fire. The people here are old — old for hell, which means they have survived something most haven't. One of them watches you approach with calculating eyes.
fields.events:hell:hell_veterans_camp/#0#result: "We can teach two things. Once each. Make your choices."
fields.events:hell:hell_veterans_camp/#3#result: The veteran returns to staring into the fire.
fields.events:hell:hell_veterans_camp/sole_surv:
She does not say anything about it. She moves along the log to make room, and later, when the fire is low, she says: 'It doesn't get quieter. You just get better at the noise.'

It is not comfort. It is better than comfort, which is accuracy.
One of them looks at you and knows.
fields.events:hell:hell_veterans_camp/war_harde:
They do not mind. Nobody asks where you served, because the question is not interesting to anyone here — what is interesting is whether you know how to sit at a fire without talking.

You do. By morning you have been told three things about the road ahead that are not on any map.
Sit down without being invited. They will not mind.
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave#text:
A cave entrance glows red with the heat of magma flowing within. The walls pulse with veins of liquid fire, casting dancing shadows. Deep within, you can hear a rhythmic sound — like a heartbeat, or the slow breathing of something enormous.

The heat is nearly unbearable, but you can see the glint of valuables deeper inside.
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/enter#fai: The heat is too much. You stagger back, skin blistered, gasping for cooler air. You manage to grab a few things near the entrance before retreating, but the deeper treasures remain beyond your endurance.
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/enter#suc:
You push through the searing heat, your body screaming in protest. The cave opens into a magma chamber where ancient demon forges still glow with purpose.

Among the abandoned tools, you find fire-forged equipment of remarkable quality and a cache of supplies left by the last smith to work here.
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/enter#tit: Brave the heat and explore the cave
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/fire_resi:
You weave a barrier of controlled flame around yourself, turning the cave's heat aside like water off oiled cloth. The magma parts before you as you walk deeper.

The cave holds wonders — natural formations of crystallized fire magic, and at its heart, a forge still burning with the flames that were lit when Naraka was young. You take what you can carry.
Use fire magic to protect yourself from the heat
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/grace_ven: Uncomfortable, but nevertheless doable — like so many things in life. You thread between the vents with quick, precise movements and find what you came for.
Move quickly and lightly between the thermal vents
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/leave#res: You back away from the cave entrance. The glow within seems to pulse with disappointment, but sometimes survival is its own reward.
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/leave#tit: The heat is too dangerous — move on
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/listen#re:
You close your eyes and listen. The rhythm is too regular for a creature, too purposeful for nature. After long study, you realize — it's the pulse of the realm itself. Naraka has a heartbeat, and this cave is one of its arteries.

The knowledge fills you with a deeper understanding of how the hell realm works. The suffering here isn't random — it has structure, purpose, even a kind of terrible beauty.
fields.events:hell:hell_volcanic_cave/listen#ti: Listen to the heartbeat sound from the entrance
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler#text:
A hunched figure dragging a heavy sack waves you down.

"Psst! Traveler! You look like you could use some supplies. I've got just the things — all cleaned up nice."
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/attac: The peddler drops the sack. From the shadows, his associates — desperate, hollow-eyed souls — close in. He was never alone.
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/brows: See what the peddler has to offer
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/direc: He starts talking a lot but making little sense. You catch bits and pieces about frozen ghosts on the lake, wandering monks and torture chambers.
Ask for directions and local knowledge
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/haggl: The trader seems amused, and after a short back-and-forth, grants you a discount. "Fine, fine. A fair deal." You walk away having spent less than expected.
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/move_: "Your loss! If you change your mind, I'll be around. I'm always around."
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/scrim:
It takes eleven minutes and involves a detailed excursion into the condition of his sack.

He settles well below where he started, calls you something unrepeatable, and shakes your hand.
He has told you the price. Tell him the real one.
fields.events:hell:hell_wandering_peddler/steal: Your foot catches on a frozen rut. The peddler watches you sprawl, unmoved. "Not the first time," he says, gathering his bag. "Not the worst, either." He trudges on without another word. You are left with bruised dignity and nothing else.
You snatch the pack and sprint. Behind you, the peddler's shouts fade into confused silence. The bag contains more than you expected — and something that rattles like it's alive.
fields.events:hell:hell_warden_strongroom#text:
A door of blue iron set into the ice, and behind it a room the cold has kept exactly as it was left: a desk, a ledger, a rack of seals on hooks.

One hook is labelled and empty. The rest hold the authority to open every lock in the cold hells, and nobody has been in to count them for a very long time.
fields.events:hell:hell_warden_strongroom/leave: You close the blue iron door behind you. The rack of seals stays on its hooks, and every lock in the cold hells stays shut.
fields.events:hell:hell_warden_strongroom/ledge:
Every seal is signed out against a prisoner's name and a sentence length. The empty hook belongs to a seal signed out four hundred years ago against a sentence of ninety days, never returned. Somebody is still in a box out there on a warrant that expired before this ice formed.

You take a seal, and you take the ledger page too, because a name will matter more than a key.
Read the ledger before you touch anything
fields.events:hell:hell_warden_strongroom/strip: Seals, desk fittings, the good inkwell, and a strongbox that has clearly not been opened since the last audit.
Take everything that is not nailed down
fields.events:hell:hell_warden_strongroom/take_: Cold blue iron, heavier than it looks, stamped with a sigil that makes your thumb ache where it rests. Whatever this opens, it opens with authority.
Take a warden's seal from the rack
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit#text:
A fortified post around a deep pit, guards drilling in formation on the parade ground. The warden — a scarred devil in heavy armor — watches them from the parapet.

"Outsiders," she says, not looking at you. "You want something. They always do."
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/attack#resu: The warden doesn't raise her voice. She just raises one finger. The drilling stops. The soldiers turn. "Show me what you've got," she says.
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/attack#titl: Challenge the warden's authority — by force
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/browse#resu: She jerks her chin toward the supply depot.
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/leave#resul: The drilling continues. You are not relevant to it.
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/steal#failu: The warden's voice carries across the entire pit: "I SAW THAT." She has not moved from the parapet. She does not need to.
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/steal#succe: The drilling formations create a predictable rhythm. You match it — moving only when boots hit the ground, stopping when they stop. The supply depot yields a spear and some armor before the rotation changes. You are back outside before anyone notices the count is off.
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/steal#title: Slip into the supply depot while everyone is drilling
fields.events:hell:hell_wardens_pit/training#re: She looks you over slowly. "You know how to hold a spear. The rest is discipline. Discipline costs coin."
fields.events:hell:hell_water_lily#text:
At the edge of a frozen river in the cold hell wastes, a blue-skinned woman stands alone. She is looking down at the ice. The water beneath it is visible, dark and still.

She does not move when you approach. She has been here a while.
fields.events:hell:hell_water_lily/leave_her#re: You walk on. The frozen river does not change. Neither does she.
fields.events:hell:hell_water_lily/leave_her#ti: Leave her to her silence. Not every stillness wants company.
fields.events:hell:hell_water_lily/reach_throug:
The cold travels up your arm. You let it. Something underneath the surface stirs — not the water, but her attention.

She looks at your hand on the ice, then at you. "You're not afraid of it," she says.

"No."

She steps back from the river's edge for the first time in a long while. "Where are you going?"
Place your hand on the ice. Commune through it.
fields.events:hell:hell_water_lily/sit_in_silen:
You sit. You do not speak. The cold hell wind moves across the ice.

After a long time — long enough that most people would have given up — she turns and looks at you properly for the first time.

"You stayed."

"Yes."

She does not ask why. She seems to already understand. When you stand to leave, she stands with you.
Sit beside her. Say nothing. Wait.
fields.events:hell:hell_water_lily/speak_plainl: She looks at you briefly, then back at the ice. The words weren't wrong, exactly — they just weren't right. She doesn't respond. The river holds her attention more completely than you do.

What you say is simple. Honest. Not an offer to fix anything — just acknowledgment of what she is looking at and why.

She is quiet for a moment. Then: "You didn't try to talk me out of it."

"No."

She turns from the river. "I'll come with you."
Say something to her — something real, not reassurance.
fields.events:hell:hell_waystation#text: A fortified waystation rises from the volcanic plain, its walls scorched black by centuries of eruptions. Smoke vents line the roof, and a battered sign reads 'ALL TRADES WELCOME — NO SOULS ACCEPTED AS PAYMENT.' Inside, merchants, healers, and weapon-smiths carve out a livelihood amid the suffering.
fields.events:hell:hell_yogini_circle#text: The inward-facing side of this circular stone wall is carved with the bizarre forms of sixty four Yoginis. There is no ceiling, so the witches can land when they come flying from vast space to meet their earthly sisters.
fields.events:hell:hell_yogini_circle/#0#result: One of the earthly sisters turns and gestures. No words needed.
fields.events:hell:hell_yogini_circle/#1#result: You back away slowly. The air around the circle hums for a long time.
fields.events:hell:hell_yogini_circle/circle_me: The combined power of sixty-four Yoginis is too much to hold. You lose your center within minutes and have to stumble out, disoriented, the carved faces still spinning. You sit outside until the world steadies.

The sixty-four faces hold your attention without pulling it apart. Something passes through you — not comfortable, but clarifying. The energies here are immense and indifferent, but they don't consume you. You emerge with a clean, bright quality to your awareness.
Sit at the center and meditate — open yourself to whatever the circle holds
fields.events:hell:hell_yogini_circle/correct_r: You move clockwise, make the right offerings at the right points, and step through the gap with the correct orientation. The carved faces seem to relax. The circle activates around you in spiraling light. One Yogini's form peels slightly from the stone and places something cold in your hand — a small charm of compressed power.
Perform the correct entry rites — approach the circle as it demands
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_alchemist_camp#te:
A dré — a bodiless ghost inhabiting a suit of robes stuffed with dried herbs — floats above a bubbling cauldron. Jars of questionable substances line makeshift shelves carved from bone. It turns as you approach.

"Customer or ingredient?" it asks cheerfully.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_alchemist_camp/as: The ingredients are unusual — some things that work differently in this realm than in the living world. The dré explains patiently, and you come away with a recipe that shouldn't work but does.
The dré is delighted to have a competent hand. You work together for an hour over the cauldron, and what emerges is something neither of you could have made alone.
Offer to help with the brewing
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_alchemist_camp/bu: Browse what it has for sale
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_alchemist_camp/kn: The cauldron hits the ground with a sound like a scream. The dré's cheerful demeanor evaporates instantly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancestor_spirit#t:
The shrine is small and very old and somebody has been maintaining it — swept, the offering-bowl clean, fresh dust patterns raked around the base. Above it hangs a presence rather than a shape.

"You are not of my line," it says. It does not sound disappointed. It sounds like it is checking.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancestor_spirit/a:
There is a rite for this — adoption across the line of death, so a family that has run out of living can be continued by someone willing to take the observance on. It is not a small thing to accept. You do it properly, with the responses, and the presence at the shrine becomes something with a stake in whether you live.

It gives you what it has: its name, its protection, and the contents of a grave nobody else knows about.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancestor_spirit/l: "Go well," it says, and the presence settles back into the raked dust.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancestor_spirit/m:
The offerings are recent and the cloth has been changed within the month, which means somebody is walking a long way to do this and will not always be able to.

You do what they have been doing, and you leave the shrine better stocked than you found it.
Somebody has been maintaining this. Take a turn.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancestor_spirit/o: "Not of my line," it observes again, differently this time. The offering is accepted. Something eases in the air around the shrine that had been held for a long time.
Leave something in the bowl anyway
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancestor_spirit/w: Silence. Then: "I do." An ancestor spirit with no descendants left, maintaining its own shrine, raking its own dust, keeping up the observances for a family that ended. It has not admitted this out loud before. You spend an hour helping with the raking and it talks the entire time, about people eight hundred years dead, and you listen.
Ask who has been sweeping the shrine
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancient_battlefie: Weapons jut from the earth like iron flowers — spears, swords, shafts of arrows, all corroded past use but too numerous to count. The ground is more bone than dirt. Some of the fallen still twitch between the weapons, trapped between death and something worse, unable to move on.

"The ocean of samsara is itself a battlefield. I vow to end the battle — first inside, and eventually everywhere." The field is very quiet. The twitching figures slow. You sit with them until you feel the weight of the vow settle into something real.

You walk the length of the field, speaking the words, touching each fallen fighter with blessing. The twitching slows. Stills. The field goes quiet for the first time since before either of your lifetimes.
Consecrate the field and put the fallen to rest
The words come up from somewhere old. Three fighters rise — ragged, half-formed, but battle-ready. They follow behind you with the patience of the dead, ready for the next fight.
Raise some of the fallen to fight beside you
You find something worth taking — and something finds you.
Search the field for salvageable equipment
Nothing here should have survived. One thing has, under a shield that fell the right way up, and it is in the condition it was in on the day.
Something in that jumble is not corroded.

You walk the field reading armor the way others read books — construction methods, battle damage, repairs, the wear patterns of years of use. Three factions, at minimum, all fighting each other. The oldest armor is local; the other two came from somewhere else.

One piece near the center shows signs of combat on all sides simultaneously. Whoever wore it died surrounded — held their ground far longer than the math suggested was possible.
Survey the fallen armor — read who these were
The field is a library of killing techniques if you know how to read it. You practice forms between the weapons for two hours, learning from the preserved evidence of old fighters.

A line held, then folded from the left. The reserve went in late and went in wrong. Everything after that was arithmetic.

You walk the field explaining it to nobody in particular, and the party is very quiet, and at the end of it you are more of a veteran than you were that morning.
You can read what happened here from where you are standing.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancient_crypt#tex:
The crypt door is stone, and it is ajar — about a hand's width, which is both an invitation and a warning depending on which side of it opened.

Dry air comes out. It smells of dust and cold iron and nothing organic at all.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancient_crypt/ent: Two of them are standing just inside the door, one to each side, in the dark. They have been standing there since the door was last closed.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancient_crypt/lea: The stone grinds shut. It takes both hands and most of your weight, and it feels like the right thing to have done.
Pull the door to and walk away
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancient_crypt/lis: Nothing breathes in there, but something *shifts* — twice, at an interval, the way a person shifts weight when they have been standing a long time. Two of them, flanking the door. You open it wide instead of squeezing through, and take them from outside with the light behind you, which turns a bad fight into a short one.
Listen at the gap before you open it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ancient_crypt/sea: The inscription is a service contract. The two inside are not guardians in any hostile sense — they are staff, on a term of duty that expired four hundred years ago because the family that hired them stopped existing. You go in and tell them so. There is a pause you would describe as stunned. Then they hand over the keys, formally, and lie down in the alcoves they were meant to occupy in the first place.
Read the door before touching it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_black_lodge#text: A mound of bones marks the entrance, a khatvanga hung with a skull and streaming black silk. As you enter, the darkness swallows sound. Something in the corner shifts — it may not be fully alive. A slow turn. A waiting smile.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_black_lodge/#0#re: The movement stills. A bony hand gestures to a list scratched into the wall. Spells. Prices. No explanation offered.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_black_lodge/#2#re: You step back into the pale light. The khatvanga watches you leave.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_black_lodge/secre: It is. You are inside before you have decided whether you wanted to be, and what is discussed there is not written down anywhere, including here.
Say nothing at the door. That is the password.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_body_possession#t:
One of your party stops walking. Turns around. Smiles.

It is not their smile. The face is doing something faces do not do, and when it speaks the voice is right and the cadence is entirely wrong: "Oh, this is a *good* one. Strong legs. Do you know how long I've been on foot?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_body_possession/b: It wants passage, not the body specifically — it is simply tired of walking. You pay it off. It leaves without argument and with genuine thanks, and your companion drops to their knees swearing in a language nobody knew they spoke.
It abandons the body the instant real damage starts — vetala are pragmatists — and comes out fighting in its own shape, furious about the inconvenience.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_body_possession/e: The rite is short and extremely unpleasant for everyone in the room. It comes out backwards, complaining bitterly about professional courtesy, and is gone before it hits the ground. Your companion is fine. Your companion is going to want to talk about this later.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_body_possession/g:
You do not let go. This is the one circumstance in which the thing that is wrong with you is exactly the thing required.

It tries several exits. You are still holding the arm at the end of it, and the face that comes back is the right one.
Whatever is in there is in one of yours. Do not let go.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_body_possession/q: A possessing spirit is, briefly, a captive audience — it cannot leave without giving up the body, and it does not want to give up the body. You spend a fascinating and deeply unethical twenty minutes interrogating it about the charnel grounds, the courts, and who exactly rules here. Then you let it out. Your companion is going to want to talk about this too, and rather more loudly.
It is in there. Ask it things while it is
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bog_hermit#text:
A gaunt figure crouches in the reed beds, sorting through bundles of grey-green herbs with practiced hands. It is alive — or near enough to count. It looks up without alarm.

"You find herbs growing in the shade," it says by way of greeting, as if this explains everything. It holds up a sprig of something. "Helps with the rot. Mostly."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bog_hermit/ask_he: "Keep the living alive. Slow the dead down. Somewhere in between there's a tea that tastes almost good." It hands you a bundle without ceremony. You take it.
Ask what the herbs are for
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bog_hermit/medici: You name what you recognise. The hermit corrects you once, with precision, then settles into a real conversation — the first, you suspect, it has had in some time. You leave knowing more than you arrived with.
Discuss the pharmacopoeia of the dead realm
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bog_hermit/trade#: "I trade in knowledge, mostly. I already have everything else I need." It gestures at the grey sky, the toxic water, the rustling reeds. It seems to mean it. You move on.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bog_hermit/yoga_m: You sit. The hermit works. The bog makes its sounds. After a long silence it says: "Most people run through here." Another silence. "Thank you for not running."
Sit with it a while — you have nowhere better to be
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_arena_event#: A circular pit ringed with skull-topped posts. Skeletons sit in the stands, clicking their jaws in anticipation. A skeleton announcer with an elaborate wig of woven hair calls out over the crowd: "Fresh meat! Who wants to test the newcomer?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_arena_event/:
The announcer considers with a long click of its jaw. 'Unusual. We have never done that.' A pause. 'We will try it.'

Targets are assembled from spare ribs and skulls with remarkable speed. The contest draws a crowd intrigued by novelty. You hit every target cleanly. The skeletons are not sure if they like this more or less than combat — but they are watching.

The gold reflects the attendance.
Propose an archery contest as an alternative spectacle
The favorite wins. Of course it does.
The underdog wins in a way no one predicted. You collect double.

You were never going to sit in the tiers. You are over the rail before the current bout has finished and the crowd's noise changes shape.

It is close. You win it, barely, and the barely is what they will remember.
You are not going to sit in the tiers.
The announcer's wig falls off from excitement. The crowd goes silent.
Demand to fight the champion directly

There is, and the odds are being set by someone who has not watched the third fighter closely enough.

You have. You bet accordingly and collect with a straight face.
There is money moving in those tiers.
Booing. A rib bone bounces off your head. The announcer wags a finger: "Not what they came for, friend."
You become the entertainment. The skeletons appreciate variety. Tips rain down from the stands — mostly coins, occasionally something that used to be a coin.
Work the crowd as an entertainer instead
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_bridge#text: A bridge of interlocking bones spans a chasm of howling darkness. Halfway across, a figure blocks the way — a massive bone horror, assembled from dozens of skeletons, looming in perfect silence. It does not speak. It does not need to.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_bridge/brave:
You go. The bridge says things while you are on it, in several voices, and you keep walking through all of them.

On the far side you find you have to sit down for a moment before waving the others over.
Somebody crosses first or nobody crosses.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_bridge/colla: You both go over. You catch the edge. It does not.
You trigger the collapse and run. The bridge drops away beneath you and you catch the far edge with both hands, hauling yourself over as the horror falls into the dark below.
Collapse the bridge behind you and leap
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_bridge/find_: There — the keystone bone, the one the spell anchors to. If that goes, the rest follows.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_bridge/sing_: You sing something simple, something that belonged to someone once. The horror shudders. The assembled bones tremble against each other. One by one, the fragments that were people hear something they recognize. The thing steps aside, shaking. You cross in silence.
Sing to the people inside it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_bridge/timid:
It is, and you cannot, and the party has to spend an hour finding a way that does not involve it.

The hour costs supplies. Nobody says anything about it, which somehow does not help.
It is made of people and it is over a hole that howls.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_collector#te:
He works the graveyard with a handcart and a system, and he is extremely particular: he takes only certain bones, only from certain graves, and he is keeping a tally on a wax tablet.

"Femurs," he says, before you can ask. "Matched pairs. You would be amazed how hard that is."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_collector/as: "A bridge," he says, with the patience of a man who gets asked a lot. "Over the chasm on the north road. Been at it eleven years." He shows you the plans. They are competent. He is entirely serious.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_collector/et: He stops the cart. It is clear nobody has ever put it to him and equally clear he has put it to himself, many times, at night. "They're not using them," he says, and then, after a while: "I ask. Every one. If it feels wrong I put it back." He shows you the reject pile. It is much larger than the cart.
Ask whether the dead consented to being a bridge
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_collector/he: You know what he does not: matched femurs are far easier to find if you stop opening random graves and start reading the markers for age at death. Inside an hour you have found him six pairs, which is better than his last two months. He is so pleased he gives you his spare tools and a genuinely useful map of the graveyard's dry routes.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_collector/le: The handcart creaks away between the mounds. He is whistling.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_gate_keeper#:
The pass through the ossuary wall runs beneath an arch of ten thousand fused skulls. Before it stands a skeleton formation in ancient parade order — warriors, archers, and at their center a bone horror wearing the rusted regalia of a gate captain.

Its jaw grinds open: "State. Your. Dead."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_gate_keeper/: Your word of command cracks across the pass like a whip. The formation snaps to attention — and holds it, rigid, as you walk through their ranks. The captain's eye sockets track you the whole way.
Command them in the tongue of the dead
You walk the line like a visiting general. Halfway down the rank, the captain decides you are worth testing — but formation discipline binds most of its troops to their posts.
Return the salute and inspect the honor guard

You speak the names — companions lost, enemies slain, the lives that ended so you could stand here. The captain's skull tilts with each one, counting. When you finish, the formation parts with a sound like dry applause.
Name your dead, honestly, one by one
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library#text:
Shelves of bone hold scrolls of dried skin. A bespectacled silver skeleton moves between them, filing and organizing with tireless precision. It turns at your approach.

"Knowledge doesn't decay. My work today may help somebody in a thousand years. What can I do for you?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library/ask_: The librarian settles into it with obvious pleasure. The history of the hungry ghost realm is longer than you expected and stranger. You come away with the sense that this place has its own logic, older than any of the beings currently living in it.
"Well, I suppose. Why not." It pulls a selection of relevant scrolls and begins.
Ask if they'd teach you a few things
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library/curi:
The silver skeleton adjusts its spectacles and produces, from somewhere, a second chair.

What you find in four hours is not what you were looking for and is considerably better: a name, an obligation, and where the obligation was last recorded.
You are not leaving a library. Be reasonable.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library/offe: The librarian takes it with both hands, holding it carefully away from the bone shelves as if it might be infectious in the best possible way. "I have nothing like this. Nothing written after the living left." It opens the rare section.
Offer a book from the living world
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library/rese: The librarian pulls scrolls without hesitation, knowing exactly where everything is. What you find goes beyond what you expected to find.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library/shar:
You go through the shelf-marks rather than the scrolls, which the librarian watches with mounting professional respect.

By evening you hold the shape of the whole collection, and the shape has a gap in it exactly where something was removed.
Do not read them. Index them.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_library/stea: The librarian looks at you. Then at the scroll. Then at you again — not angry, just deeply, genuinely sad. You put it back.
You find what you want and leave with it. The librarian doesn't notice.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_merchant_eve:
A skeleton in a tattered merchant's robe sits behind a blanket of wares laid on the dry earth — wrapped bundles, clay jars, glinting objects of uncertain purpose. It clicks its jaw merrily as you approach.

"Ah! Customers! Or at least, beings capable of carrying things away! Welcome, welcome — the overhead is low and the bones are FREE."
The merchant stares at you with hollow sockets. "Was that... a joke? Was it supposed to be funny?" Uncomfortable silence. You browse its wares.

"...and the skeleton said, 'I just don't have the guts for it!'" The merchant clacks its jaw so hard a tooth falls out. "HA! Oh — oh, that's GOOD. I haven't laughed like that since — well, since I had muscles to laugh with. Here, take this. Consider it payment for services rendered."
The skeleton's eye sockets swivel with unsettling precision. "I may be dead, but I am not BLIND." It produces a weapon from somewhere in its robes.
The skeleton turns to argue with a passing rolang. Your hand moves before you've quite decided to move it. By the time it looks back, you're innocently studying the sky.
Wait for its attention to wander and pocket something

You counter its opening price with calm authority, citing comparable goods in the living world. The skeleton clacks its teeth together in what might be admiration. "You know your market. Fine — take it for less."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_raft#text: A crude raft of lashed femurs floats slowly past on the current. Something wrapped in waxed cloth sits in the middle. It's addressed to someone.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_raft/grab_it: You lean too far. You get wet. The raft keeps going.
You snag it. The cloth is still dry inside.
Grab it before it floats out of reach
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_raft/let_dri: Whoever it's for, it's not you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_raft/read_ad: You can't retrieve it. But you read the name. It means something, even if you're not sure what yet.
Notice the name on the address — read it before it's gone
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_shrine#text:
Skulls set into a cairn in a spiral, each one facing outward, each one with a small offering wedged into the eye socket — a coin, a bead, a folded scrap.

It is either a place of great devotion or a place of great warning, and the two are not always different.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_shrine/leave: Every socket you pass is looking somewhere else. That is the intended effect and it works.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_shrine/offer: There is exactly one empty socket, at the centre of the spiral, and it takes your coin as though it had been waiting for that specific denomination. The air over the cairn goes briefly warm.
Add your own offering to an empty socket
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_shrine/read_: It is a containment, wound outward, and the offerings are the seal — each one a small debt paid on behalf of whatever is under the cairn. It has been maintained by passing strangers for centuries without any of them knowing what they were maintaining. You pay your share, tighten the two sockets that had gone loose, and leave it in better repair than you found it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_shrine/rob#f: The spiral is a ward and the offerings are what holds it closed. The third socket you empty opens it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_shrine/rob#s: Forty-odd offerings, some of them very old and one of them gold. You are three miles away before you stop feeling watched, and you never entirely stop.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_tower#text:
Nine storeys of fused bone, tapering, with a stair spiralling up the outside and no rail. It serves no obvious purpose. Nothing lives in it. It simply goes up.

At the base, cut into the lowest course, one word in an old script: HIGHER.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_tower/climb#: Somewhere around the sixth storey the wind gets under the party and everyone's nerve goes at once. Coming down is worse than going up. Somebody is sick over the side from a great height.

Nine storeys of no rail. At the top there is a flat platform, a stone bench, and a view of the entire charnel grounds — every fire, every court, every road — laid out like a map somebody drew for you. You sit on the bench for an hour and learn more about this realm than in all the walking that got you here.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_tower/leave#: It is visible from a very long way off, in every direction, for the rest of the day.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_tower/practi: Up without a rail, sit facing west, and do the thing the structure is asking for — which becomes obvious the moment you are seated, because the whole tower has been shaped to make one particular state of mind the easiest thing available. Whoever built this was extremely good. You come down at dusk not entirely the same.
Climb it and do what it was built for
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_bone_tower/read_t: It is a practice structure. The bench at the top faces west; the whole thing is oriented for a specific meditation done at a specific hour, and the climb without a rail is not an obstacle but the first part of the exercise. Somebody built a nine-storey teaching aid out of bones and then, presumably, used it.
Work out what it is for
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_boss_insatiable_k:
He sits on a throne of fused bone before the Realm Gate, a mountain of a preta — belly vast as a granary, throat thin as a needle. A thousand offering bowls lie scattered around him, every one licked clean and none of them enough.

"More," he says, and the word carries the weight of centuries. "Everything that passes this gate feeds me first. Wealth. Blood. Memory. What have you brought the King of Hunger?"
He devours everything in moments — and for one heartbeat his eyes close, almost peaceful. When they open, the hunger is back, but slower. Heavier. He rises to fight without his court.
Lay out a feast from your own stores before the fight
Give him nothing — draw your weapon

The question stops him like a blade. Slowly, haltingly, he remembers: a rich man who buried grain while his village starved, who died counting. You sit with the memory until he can hold it himself.

When he finally weeps, the tears are ordinary and human. The throne of bone crumbles. Where the King sat there is only an old man's shadow, bowing once before it fades. The gate stands open.
Sit with him. Ask what he was, before the hunger

The words land like rain on a fire that has burned for ten thousand years. His courtiers dissolve, wailing. The King alone remains, diminished, weeping — and still he attacks, because he no longer knows how to do anything else.
Speak the sutra of the open hand — hunger ends where giving begins
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_burial_mound#text: An ancient mound rises from the swamp, its entrance marked with faded symbols carved into standing stones. Cold air breathes from the opening — not the damp cold of the swamp, but the dry cold of sealed places.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_burial_mound/call: The offering is correct. The incantation is correct. A shape emerges from the mound's dark — a dralha, a warrior-chieftain, still bearing the weapons of a kingdom that has not existed in centuries. It looks at you with eyes that have not looked at anything for a very long time.
Call the spirit within to your side
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_burial_mound/coll: You bring the entrance stones down. Whatever is inside stays there.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_burial_mound/ente: Something ancient is waiting in the dark.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_burial_mound/read: The symbols are warnings — and instructions. You understand what is inside, what it guards, and how to approach it without waking the worst of it. You go in, find what you came for, and leave intact.
Study the carved symbols before entering
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_burial_mound/ritu: You don't take anything. You leave offerings instead — a little food, some incense, a prayer for the dead. The cold air stills. Somewhere inside, something ancient settles into proper rest.
Perform a ritual for the entombed
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_feast#tex: A long table laid out in the open, covered in a feast that looks perfect and smells wrong. Seated pretas reach for food endlessly — it passes through without satisfying anything. The table is infinite. The hunger is infinite. Neither notices you standing at the edge.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_feast/asc:
You look at the table the way you look at any table, which is to say briefly.

Whatever laid it was counting on the wanting, and there is not enough of that in you to work with. The hall loses interest and the food stops being convincing halfway down the table.
You have been hungrier than this on purpose.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_feast/eat: You understand, briefly and completely, what it is like to need something and have it provide nothing at all.
It's real enough. Strange but real. It sits wrong for an hour, then doesn't.
Eat anyway — you're hungry, and it looks real enough
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_feast/gou:
You can. That is the trouble — it is not a general temptation, it is a specific and extremely well-observed one, and something went to the effort of knowing what you would want.

You eat one mouthful before the party gets you away from the table. One is enough to be unwell for a day.
You can tell from here that the lamb is done properly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_feast/ste: They are real. Everything solid about this table is real.
Pocket the gold candleholders — they look real
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_feast/yog: You observe the feast without hunger. The pretas slow, one by one, and watch you — the strange creature at the edge of the table who is not reaching. Something about this interests them.
Sit with the nature of what you're seeing
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_ground_en:
Smoke rises from ritual pyres. Human bones are arranged in geometric patterns on the ground — too deliberate to be accidental, not quite like anything you recognize. A vetala perches on a skull-pile, watching you with amused curiosity.

"Another living one. How delightful. We don't get many."

"Passage costs breath," it says. "Not much. Just a little. You have plenty to spare." There's a brief cold sensation, as if something has been lifted from you. You feel slightly less alive than you did. The vetala waves you through with its too-long fingers.

You show it something that makes its eyes go wide with professional appreciation. "Oh, you ARE interesting," it says. "Someone actually worth talking to." It grants passage and, before you leave, whispers the shape of a spell you hadn't known before.

It is not fear, which would at least be respectable. It is that everything here is *touching* everything else, and you spend the whole passage moving in a way the vetala find frankly hilarious.

They let you through specifically to see how far you will get.
You cannot help it. You simply cannot help it.

Vetalas prize novelty above most things, and living stories are rarest of all. You sit together on the skull-pile for an hour, trading tales. It laughs often. When you leave, it waves with something approaching fondness.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_hermit#te:
She has built a hut against the wall of the burning ground and lives in it, alive, by choice, among the smoke and the offerings and the vetala. She is boiling something over a small fire.

"Sit," she says. "You'll want to hear this before you go further in. Most don't. Then most don't come out."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_hermit/le: "Mm," she says, and stirs the pot. She does not seem surprised, which is worse than if she had argued.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_hermit/li: An hour of extremely practical advice about the charnel grounds: which fires to walk upwind of, what the courts consider an insult, why you never accept food, and how to tell an illusion by the smell. It is the single most useful hour of your time in this realm.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_hermit/pr: She takes you out among the bodies at the hour when the fires are low and sits you down facing one, and gives you no instruction whatsoever, because there is none. It goes on for a long time. Twice you want to leave. Around the third hour the thing the practice is for happens, briefly, and then you are just a person sitting near a corpse in the cold, which turns out to be the same thing.
Ask to sit the corpse-ground practice with her
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_hermit/st:
She looks at you for slightly too long and then moves over on the mat.

No instruction is given. None is needed and both of you know it, and the afternoon goes by in a burning ground in complete silence and is one of the better afternoons.
Ask to sit with her. You will not need it explained.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_hermit/wh: "Because it is the only honest place I have ever lived." She has been here nineteen years. She came to do the corpse-ground meditation for a season and found she had no further use for anywhere else. She is not mad, and she is not enlightened, and she is entirely at ease, which in this realm is the rarest thing you have seen.
Ask why a living woman lives in a burning ground
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_charnel_sorcerer_:
In a cave hung with bones and dried entrails, a vetala sorcerer works rituals by the light of candles made from human fat. It turns at your footstep with an expression of genuine pleasure.

"I don't get many visitors. Most find the décor off-putting. Can't imagine why."
The vetala's pleasant expression disappears. What's underneath is considerably less friendly.
Disrupt the ritual — shut this down
It tells you things that are not in the books. Things about what persists after death, what can be moved and where, what the dead remember that the living cannot access. You come away changed.
Browse what it has to offer
You lay out your reagents. It picks through them with practiced fingers, setting things aside, weighing others. What you receive in exchange is stranger and more potent.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_choki#text: At the edge of a bog with no wind and no movement, a girl sits watching the water. She does not look up. She has been here long enough that moss has grown around where she sits. She is holding a bundle of forest plants that dried to nothing long ago.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_choki/ask_what_sh: She finally looks up. Something in the question — the specificity of it, the acknowledgment of what she was doing when she left — gets through where comfort never would. She tells you everything she was carrying. She asks if you need a guide.
Ask her what she was gathering when the flood came
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_choki/leave_her#r: The bog is silent as you walk away. You don't hear her move.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_choki/sit_in_sile: She doesn't acknowledge you. The waiting becomes its own kind of grief. You eventually stand and go.
The silence stretches to an hour. Then two. Then she says: 'You're still here.' After another long while: 'Most people leave.' She looks at you sideways. 'Where are you going?'
Sit beside her without speaking — wait for her to acknowledge you
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_choki/touch_the_w: The water stirs slightly under your hand. She watches it. 'It was like that,' she says. 'One moment there was nothing. Then—' She trails off. Then: 'You are going somewhere. Can I come?'
Touch the water beside her — let it speak for you
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror#tex:
A copper skeleton sits polishing an enormous mirror of burnished copper. The mirror shows not reflections but truths — the viewer sees themselves as they truly are.

"Most can't bear it," the skeleton says, without looking up. "Can you?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror/ask: "I was a judge. In life, I showed people their crimes. In death, I show them themselves. It is the same work." It resumes polishing.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror/cle:
Nobody asks that. Everybody asks what it shows.

He stops polishing. 'For the King,' he says, and then, after a pause that goes on rather too long, 'He has not asked for it in some time.'
Ask what he is polishing it for.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror/loo: You look. What you see is too much. You look away after a moment, unsettled in a way that takes time to settle back.
You look. What you see is not flattering and not damning — it is accurate. You stand with it until the accuracy becomes useful.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror/pol: You work in companionable silence. The mirror grows brighter. The skeleton nods when you finish.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror/rea:
The enchantment is elegant — a truth-compulsion layered over a reflection spell, calibrated not to lie but not to flatter either. It shows what is, precisely and without context.

You study the structure for a while. The skeleton watches you study it.

'Most people just look in,' it says.

'Most people aren't trying to understand it.'

The skeleton polishes in silence. 'You just did both,' it says. 'You looked in when you read it.'
Study the enchantment behind the mirror
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_copper_mirror/sma: The skeleton sets down its cloth. The mirror reforms before the fight is over.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_flower#tex: An enormous flower blooms in the swamp, its petals the color of bruised flesh. Its scent is overpowering — sweetly wrong, like incense covering something that should not be sweetened. Dead insects litter the ground around it in concentric rings.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_flower/bur: The smell, briefly, is terrible. Then it's gone. Whatever the flower was attracting, it won't attract anymore.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_flower/har: You cut carefully, taking the useful parts without triggering the aromatic glands. The reagents are worth having — the flower's strange chemistry has properties you've never seen elsewhere.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_flower/med: Disgust is a judgment. You sit with the smell and the wrongness until they stop being wrong and start being simply what they are. The flower is a flower. It does what it does. Something in you loosens.
Meditate on it — find the beauty in the strange
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_flower/res: The scent overwhelms you — you stumble, and the stumbling draws things from the mire.
The smell hooks something in you and pulls. You keep moving. It takes more will than you expected.
Walk past without being drawn in
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_flower/stu: Medicinal — in the right doses. The same compound that overwhelms at close range becomes a useful palliative in small quantities. You harvest a bundle carefully.
Study it from a safe distance
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_merchant#t:
A broad figure in a waxed coat stands over a cart heaped with cloth-wrapped bundles, sealed jars, and objects you decline to examine closely. Its face is partially masked. It does not smell good, but it has clearly made peace with this.

"Everything recovered in good condition," it says. "Relative condition. Relative good."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_merchant/a: "The dead leave things behind. I collect them. Consider it a service." A pause. "To commerce. Also arguably to the dead. They weren't using it."
Ask where the goods come from
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_merchant/r: The merchant doesn't turn around. "I can smell the living," it says. "I can smell them reaching." It produces a heavy implement from the cart.
The merchant turns to re-tie a bundle. In the gap, your hand moves. You're three paces gone before it straightens up. It doesn't seem to notice — or doesn't care. Possibly both.
Pocket something while it looks away
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_merchant/t: You explain the theory of salvage pricing. The merchant listens with professional attention and adjusts its margins. "Fair. You know the trade." The discount is modest but genuine.
Haggle — this is salvage, not retail
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle#tex:
A body has been arranged on a platform with its mouth propped open, and a queue of the dead is waiting patiently for their turn to lean in and listen. The corpse itself is quite ordinary and thoroughly deceased.

"It says true things," explains the vetala managing the queue. "Not helpful things. True ones."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle/ask: An oracle that only says true things is useless if you ask it what you should do. You ask it something checkable instead — where the horizontal pass lies, what holds the bone bridge together, who the King's messenger reports to. Three answers, all verifiable, all worth having. The vetala managing the queue watches you do this and takes notes.
Frame a question the truth can actually answer
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle/cle: Half of it is the propped jaw and the wind. A quarter is what any dead mouth says. The remaining quarter is specific, and specific is the only part that can be wrong, which is what makes it worth having.
Sort the prophecy from the plumbing.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle/lea: The line shuffles forward by one. Somebody at the front leans in, listens, and walks away looking much worse.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle/lis: You lean over the open mouth. What you hear is one sentence, in your own voice, about something you did before you came to this realm. It is entirely accurate. It is not advice and there is nothing to be done about it. You give up your place in the queue.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle/rel: Nobody in the queue has thought to ask whether the corpse consented to being an amenity. You perform the closing, and the truth-telling stops, and there is a small ugly moment where the queue considers being angry with you. Then the vetala at the head of it says, "Well. It never said anything good anyway," and the crowd disperses, and the body is allowed to be a body.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_corpse_oracle/sup:
You take it down complete, including the parts that are clearly the mechanism rather than the message.

One line of it will turn out to matter enormously, and you will not know which until it does, which is precisely the arrangement you have always found bearable.
It is an oracle. Write down every word.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crossroads_stupa#: At the intersection of the ancient paths, a stupa rises from layers of offerings — skulls, prayer flags, bones wrapped in cloth. Juniper smoke and the smell of old offerings drift on the wind. A practitioner crouches behind the stupa, neither fully alive nor fully dead.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crossroads_stupa/: The figure looks up. The crossroads is the right place for calling back what is lost. The price is gold.
You watch the butter lamps flicker in the wind, then walk on. Some things are better left undisturbed.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crumbling_mausole:
It was grand once and it is coming apart now — the roof half in, one wall bowed outward, the whole structure held up mostly by the habit of standing. Inside, the sarcophagi are visible through the gaps.

Something moves in there when the wind does. It may only be the wind.

Eleven names, four generations, one family line that ended here. You say each name aloud in the ruin of their house. Nothing dramatic happens. But the movement in the back of the mausoleum stops, and stays stopped, and when you leave the grave-goods are simply objects rather than the other thing they had been.
Read the family names and give them their rites
You give it a wide berth. Behind you, a stone comes off the parapet and lands where nobody is standing.
It will fall on someone. Not you.
The lid you are levering is load-bearing, which is not a sentence anyone wants to discover from underneath. You get out. Most of the building does not.
In through the gap in the bowed wall, two sarcophagi levered open, out before the dust settles. The roof comes down about ten minutes later. Nobody was under it.
Get in, get what is reachable, get out

Two hours of bracing with timber cut from grave-markers, which is grim but effective. With the wall held you can work the whole interior properly instead of snatching at what is nearest, and there is a great deal more in the back than there was in the front.
Prop the wall before anyone goes in
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crying_river#text: A river of black water flows silently through the wasteland. The surface ripples with faces — the crying dead, trapped in the current. A ferryman waits on the bank, pole in hand. He is enormous. He is silent. He has been waiting here for a very long time.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crying_river/help: The ferryman looks at you for the first time — properly looks, as if assessing something. Then steps aside and hands you the pole. You work in silence side by side. When you reach the far bank, he nods once. You have the sense this will be remembered.
Offer to help pole the raft
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crying_river/mela:
The faces are not saying anything. That is what everyone gets wrong — they assume the sound is speech.

It is not. You know exactly what it is, and you sit on the bank with it for a while, and the ferryman waits without complaint, because he has seen this before too.
You have heard this note before, from the inside.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crying_river/pay_: The ferryman accepts without looking at you and poles across in silence. The faces in the water follow your progress with eyes that remember hope.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crying_river/spea: You reach into the current with dark working and the faces turn toward you, speaking in voices like water over stone. They tell you things about this realm that aren't written anywhere. The lore is old and the weight of it stays with you.
Speak to the faces in the water
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_crying_river/swim: The faces pull at you, curious or desperate. You go under twice before the current spits you out downstream, bruised and shaking.
The current is strong and the water thick. You make it across with teeth clenched and nothing left.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_cursed_well#text:
A well, in a swamp — which is absurd, because there is water everywhere. Somebody dug down through all this wet ground looking for something cleaner, and found something else.

The rope is still on the winch. It is taut. Something is hanging on the other end of it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_cursed_well/cut#r: You can feel it up the rope like a pulse — patient, attentive, entirely aware that someone has come. You cut the rope near the winch and the tension goes out of it, and something a long way down makes a sound of what is unmistakably disappointment. Then nothing. You fill the shaft with stones for an hour to be certain.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_cursed_well/cut#t: Cut the rope and let whatever it is go back down
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_cursed_well/leave: The rope stays taut behind you for as long as you can see the well.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_cursed_well/purif: You work the rite down the shaft in stages, and what is on the rope comes apart quietly on the way up — not destroyed, released, the way a knot is released. What finally reaches the top is a bucket. In the bucket is clean water, the first you have seen in this realm, and it tastes of nothing at all, which is extraordinary.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_cursed_well/wind#: It comes up easily. It comes up much too easily, in fact, for the weight that was on the rope.
Turn the winch and see what comes up
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dancing_dead#text: A ring of corpses dances in perfect silence around an empty throne. Their movements are stiff but coordinated, as if memory persists where intention does not. They do not appear to notice you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dancing_dead/cele:
They are dancing around an absence and they are doing it in total silence and they have clearly been doing it a long time.

You watch it through rather than past, which nobody has done, and at the end one of them bows to you specifically.
Let them have it. Watch properly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dancing_dead/comp: This is a specific ceremony. You've seen fragments of it. You take the empty throne, perform your part. When you rise, the dance resolves — the figures slow, then still, with something like satisfaction.
Recognize the ceremony and complete your part
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dancing_dead/join: You misstep. The ring shifts. They look at you all at once. Then, somehow worse, they resume — leaving you outside it.
Your body finds the rhythm. For a moment you are part of something very old and very strange. When the dance ends, you are on the other side of the ring.
Join the ring — dance with them
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dancing_dead/slip: Whatever they are celebrating, or mourning, continues without you.
Slip past the outer edge carefully
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_death_meditation#: A flat stone among the bones, worn smooth by sitting. This is a practice site — you can feel it in the quality of the stillness around it. Confronting death directly. Not abstractly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_death_meditation/:
The stone is worn smooth in the shape of people who have done exactly this, and you fit the shape.

What comes up is not fear, because that was dealt with some time ago. What comes up is the ordinary and much harder question of what to do tomorrow.
You have sat in places like this before.
You tie it to a bone and leave it fluttering. A small mark that someone was here and paid attention.
A few minutes on the stone. The reality of the place presses in. You let it. Something small shifts.

You sit and let the smell and the reality and the inevitability be present without distance. It is not pleasant and it is not supposed to be. When you rise, something has been processed that had been waiting to be processed for some time.
The collection here is unusual — varied, old, well-preserved by the dry air. You learn something about anatomy and something else, harder to name, about impermanence.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_desperate_mother#:
A rolang woman crouches in the grey dust, clutching a bundle to her chest, rocking back and forth. The bundle is empty — just rags shaped by a mother's hands. She doesn't seem to know. Her eyes are elsewhere, in a time this realm cannot reach.

"Have you seen my child? I just need to feed them. Just once more."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_desperate_mother/: She doesn't fully notice you. But your presence seems to register somewhere, some warmth in the grey. She rocks more slowly.
Sit with her gently — offer what comfort you can
You back away without disturbing her. She doesn't notice you leave. She was somewhere else already.

You speak softly about attachment, about the nature of what she holds. She listens with the partial attention of someone dreaming. A long pause. She looks at the bundle. "There's nothing here, is there." It isn't a question. She sets it down. Her hands are empty.
Guide her gently toward understanding her condition
The words come out wrong. Something in her breaks in the wrong direction. The grief becomes rage and the rage becomes something else entirely.

You choose your words with great care. She goes still. Looks at you. Looks at the bundle. "I know," she says, very quietly. After a long moment: "I know." She rocks more slowly. She seems, in some way, relieved.
Tell her plainly that her child is gone
She looks through you and resumes rocking, babbling softly to the empty rags. The dream is too strong.

"If there is no child, how can there be a mother?" She looks at you with sudden, piercing clarity. Her eyes sharpen. Then, very slowly, the clarity passes into something like peace. Her form grows transparent. She smiles — genuinely — and fades. She is not here anymore.
Try to wake her from the dream entirely
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband#te:
A dralha — an undead warrior-king — rides at the head of a column of skeleton soldiers. Banners of a forgotten kingdom snap in the memory of a wind that doesn't blow anymore. The dralha raises a gauntleted fist and the column halts.

"You. You have the look of a fighter."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband/ac: "Against the rolang horde to the east. Standard terms." It pays.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband/ch: The column watches in absolute silence. This is going to be talked about.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband/de: "Different roads," you say. The dralha studies you for a moment, then lowers its fist. "Fair enough. Ride on."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband/in: You fall in with the column, spear at the correct angle, march at the correct pace. The column incorporates you without ceremony. The brief engagement at the far side of the patrol route goes quickly with the warband behind you.
Fall in with the column — present yourself as infantry
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband/of: You share what you know about the terrain ahead and the rolang movements you've observed. The dralha listens with the attention of someone who has fought a thousand battles and knows useful information when it hears it.
Offer tactical intelligence instead of service
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dralha_warband/pe:
You don't ask permission and you don't defer — you address it the way one field commander addresses another, with the specific confidence of someone who has made the same decisions under worse conditions.

The dralha reads this immediately. Its posture shifts — not submission, but respect.

'Where are you headed?' You tell it. 'The southern route is safer. We cleared it two days ago.' It turns the column without further words.

You have, without planning to, just exchanged tactical intelligence with an undead warlord. Both parties leave better informed.
Speak to it as a peer commander
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_drowned_temple#te: Half-sunken in the black swamp, a temple's upper spire still rises above the waterline. Faded murals of bodhisattvas peer out from beneath the surface, their serene faces distorted by the water. From inside comes a sound that should not survive in this realm: the turning of a prayer wheel, still spinning after all this time.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_drowned_temple/pr: You kneel in the grey mud and offer what you have. The prayer wheel turns inside its sunken room. Somehow, in this realm, the gesture feels heard.
Pray from the bank — don't enter
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_drowned_temple/sa: The upper stonework is solid — old construction, well-made. You extract what you can carry without disturbing the structure below the waterline.
Salvage building materials from the accessible sections
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_drowned_temple/sw: In the tight darkness under the water, something cold wraps around your arm.

You find a chamber still half above water. The prayer wheel turns in a current you cannot feel. The murals inside are extraordinary — preserved perfectly by the dark water. You study them until you understand something new.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_drowned_temple/wa: The water pulls back. The temple mouth opens before you, still and reverent. Inside, the murals are perfect — the water preserved them. The offerings are intact. You spend a proper hour within, taking what is offered and leaving what is owed.
Part the waters and enter dry
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_durvasa#text: In a hollow beneath a collapsed stupa, a gyelpo sits within a circle of his own making — binding signs carved into the stone, faintly active. He is maintaining a careful stillness. Whatever is bound is inside him. He watches you approach with eyes that are doing a great deal of work to remain calm.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_durvasa/disperse_: It takes time. It takes all the steadiness you have. Gradually the sigils stop glowing. He slumps, then straightens. He looks at his hands, then at you. 'You have done this before,' he says. 'No,' you say. He considers this. 'Hm. I owe you a debt. How are you traveling?'
Diffuse the bound energy through the air — disperse it gradually
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_durvasa/leave_him: You feel his eyes on your back as you leave. The sigils continue to glow.
Leave him to it — this is his problem
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_durvasa/perform_r: The curse unwrites itself, step by step. He exhales for the first time in what sounds like a very long time. 'Thorough,' he says. 'Methodical. I appreciate methodical.' He stands slowly. 'Whoever taught you that taught you well. I find myself without current employment. Are you taking work?'
Perform a proper reversal — unmake the binding through ceremony
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_durvasa/read_the_: You can see something is deeply wrong but not what. He watches you fail to understand with the patience of someone who has been sitting very still for a very long time.

A death-curse, reflected and internalized. He has been holding it in containment since it returned to him. 'How long?' you ask. He answers. You do not ask again. You sit across from him and begin talking through options. By the time the sigils fade, you are colleagues.
Try to read the binding — understand what you are dealing with
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dust_storm#text: A wall of bone-dry grit sweeps across the graveyard with no warning. There's nowhere to shelter. You're going to take this one.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dust_storm/brace_: You turn your back, cover your face, wait it out. It passes.
Brace against it — or dodge the worst of it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dust_storm/earth_: A low ridge of packed earth takes the worst of it. You emerge into clear air already reforming your thoughts about dry graveyards.
Raise a wind-break with earth magic
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dust_storm/push_t: You bow your head and walk. It gets in everywhere.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dusty_library#tex:
A reading room, intact, under a collapsed roof that fell in such a way as to shelter rather than crush it. Shelves of scroll-cases, a desk, a chair pushed back as though someone stood up mid-sentence.

On the desk, a document is still weighted flat, half-copied, the ink long dry.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dusty_library/cat: It is not a general library. Every text is on one subject, approached from every possible angle over what must have been decades: how to die correctly. Somebody in this realm spent a lifetime studying the thing they were about to fail at. The final shelf is practical instructions, and they are good ones.
Work out what the collection was *for*
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dusty_library/inc: You move on. The roof comes down the rest of the way about an hour later, which you hear from some distance and do not go back to investigate.
A collapsed roof over wet paper. Move on.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dusty_library/lea: You put the weight back on the corner of the document on your way out, which is a small courtesy to nobody in particular.
Leave the room as you found it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dusty_library/loo: Scroll-cases of good bronze, a silver inkwell, and three documents that look important enough to sell to somebody.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_dusty_library/rea: It is a commentary on a sutra you know, and the copyist was arguing with it in the margins — sharp, funny, occasionally wrong, entirely alive. The hand stops mid-word. You finish the sentence yourself, in your own hand, underneath, because it is obvious how it was going to end and it seems a shame to leave it hanging.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_feasting_hall_tra:
Long tables, laid for a hundred, in a hall with the roof still on. Food on every platter. Every chair occupied by something that was a guest once and has not left the table since.

At the head, one chair is empty, and a place is set at it. The setting is clean. It has been kept clean.
Nothing at the tables moves. The empty chair stays empty. You are extremely aware of the clean place-setting for a long time afterwards.
Back out the way you came

The guests are arranged by precedence and the empty chair is not the host's — it is the *guest of honour's*, and it is set for someone who never came. This entire hall has been holding a place at a party for a person who declined the invitation, for four hundred years, out of spite. You do not sit down. You do steal the silver, which is superb, and nothing at the tables has any protocol for that.
Work out what the seating means

You go to the head of the table, take the clean place-setting, and clear it — which is, in the grammar of the hall, the host announcing that the last guest is not coming and the meal is over. A hundred bound guests are released from a dinner party at once. Several of them weep. Most simply come apart with an air of enormous relief.
A hundred heads turn as one. The host has been waiting a very long time for the last guest to arrive, and you have just accepted the invitation.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_flooded_crypt#tex:
Stone steps go down into standing water. Whatever this was built to hold has been below the waterline for centuries, and the swamp has been patiently filling it the entire time.

The first two feet of the stair are slick with something that is not algae.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_flooded_crypt/dra: You push the water back down the stair and hold it there, and walk into a crypt that has not been dry since its builders sealed it. The sentinel in the third chamber is standing exactly where it was posted. It does not attack. It looks at the dry floor for a long moment and then, apparently satisfied that its watch is finally over, sits down and stops.
Part the water and walk in dry
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_flooded_crypt/lea: You go back up into the grey daylight, which is not much, but is more than what is down there.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_flooded_crypt/rea: The seals are not protective. They are a *containment*, and the water is part of it — whoever flooded this crypt did it on purpose and did it well. You take what is in the entry chamber, which is generous, and you leave the inner door alone, which is wisdom.
Read the seals on the doorway before opening anything
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_flooded_crypt/wad: The torch goes out in the second chamber. In the dark, something that has been standing in this water for four hundred years turns to face the sound of you.
Chest-deep, torch held over your head, through three chambers of grave-goods that nobody has been able to reach since the water came. Cold beyond describing. Worth it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_king#te:
The tomb is the largest thing in the graveyard and every inscription on it has been chiselled out — thoroughly, deliberately, by people who wanted this specific man erased and had the time to do it properly.

Inside, on a throne, he is still sitting. He turns his head as you enter. "Do you know my name?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_king/fi: He rises with the enormous unhurried dignity of a man who has been waiting a long time for something to happen.
Whatever he was, he is a corpse on a chair now
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_king/no: "No," he agrees. "Nobody does. That was the sentence." He sits back. He does not attack, does not threaten, does not ask for anything. After a while it becomes clear the audience is simply over, and you leave him in the dark he has been sitting in for eight hundred years.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_king/re:
They were thorough on the walls and careless underneath — the mason's setting-out marks are still there, cut deep and never intended to be read. You work it letter by letter and then say it out loud.

The effect is not gratitude. He goes very still, and then he begins, quietly and with great precision, to come apart, because being named was the only thing still holding the shape together. What is left on the throne is a crown and a considerable quantity of dust.
Reconstruct the name from what the chisels missed
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_king/si: You do not ask him anything and you do not tell him anything. You sit on the tomb step for a couple of hours in the company of a man whose entire punishment was to be alone with himself indefinitely. Eventually he says, "Thank you," in a voice that has clearly not been used for that before. He is still there when you go. But he is sitting differently.
