Sit down on the step and keep him company a while
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_shrine#: A small roadside shrine, half-buried in grey dust. The offering bowl is empty. The carved face of the deity has worn smooth — you cannot tell who it once depicted. It could be anyone. It could be no one.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_forgotten_shrine/: You place coins in the bowl and press your palms together. Whoever this was, someone carved this stone and set it here. That deserves acknowledgment.

You settle into stillness and the shrine's history comes in fragments. Among them: a vision of the bodhisattva once depicted here — the one whose name means Womb of the Earth, who comes to this bleak realm to patiently teach and feed the ever-hungry dead. The face that has worn away is still present somehow.
You dig it out. It takes an hour and ruins a pair of gloves and reveals that the offering bowl is not empty — it was buried full, which means somebody left in a hurry and meant to come back.
Half-buried is not the same as finished.
You re-level the base, clear the dust from the carvings, and shore up the crumbling back. You can't recover the face, but the structure stands again with purpose. Someone will see it.
Finely carved stone, old work. It fits in your pack. The shrine looks wrong without it.
Take the offering bowl — it's well-made
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_funeral_rites#tex: A skeleton sits beside a crumbling grave, methodically arranging offerings — flowers long since turned to dust, fruit that is only the shape of fruit. It works without hurry, with complete attention.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_funeral_rites/don: Some things should be left alone. You pass at a respectful distance.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_funeral_rites/hel: It turns to look at you when you kneel. A long pause. Then it extends a handful of dust-flowers toward you, and together you finish the ceremony.
Kneel and help perform the rites correctly
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_funeral_rites/wat: You shift your weight. A branch snaps. The skeleton freezes. You hold your breath. Then it continues, ignoring you entirely.
You recognize the pattern. Old funeral rites, obscure but correct. Someone taught this skeleton well.
Watch what it is arranging — try to understand
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_fungal_grove#text: Enormous mushrooms grow from the bodies of the dead, some taller than trees. The air is thick with spores. There is a sound underneath the silence — soft, irregular, buzzing — and when you listen closely you seem to hear melodies within it. Call and response, echoing somewhere in the mycelium.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_fungal_grove/burn: The mushrooms burn poorly and smell terrible. You get through. The melodies stop.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_fungal_grove/harv: Unusual reagents — things with properties you haven't seen in living-world fungi. This place grows something new.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_fungal_grove/list: You sit very still and let the sound find you. The fungi are sharing memories of the dead they grow from — and their own nature as something new, a collective being beyond ego and egolessness, not just the dead and not just the fungus, but an amalgam that has grown past both. Something in this troubles the assumptions you arrived with.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_fungal_grove/push: The spores get in. The world becomes very interesting for a while.
You make it through without breathing more than necessary. The buzzing fades behind you.
Move through quickly, hold your breath
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ghost_light#text: Pale blue flames dance above the swamp surface, drifting slowly deeper into the mire. They're beautiful, and clearly a trap. Yet they seem to be leading somewhere specific, with unusual purpose.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ghost_light/extin: You reach out with the spell and the lights go out one by one. Not dramatically — gently, like candles at the end of a long evening. Whatever they were, they are done now.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ghost_light/fire_: The lights pause, then pulse in response. They're souls, not traps — trapped here by the same forces that trap all things in this realm. They show you a safe path through the mire in gratitude for being seen.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ghost_light/follo: The lights lead you off solid ground. You sink to your waist in mire before managing to haul yourself free, filthy, somewhat injured, and deeply unimpressed.
The lights lead you on a winding path through the mire and stop above a half-sunken object — a cache, wrapped in oilcloth, wedged between the roots of a dead tree.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ghost_light/ignor: You watch them drift away into the dark. Wise, probably.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_golden_skeleton_s:
A skeleton of gleaming gold sits beneath a withered bodhi tree, radiating calm. Other skeletons give it a wide berth — not from fear, but from reverence. It does not speak first. It waits.

"You carry the weight of many lives. Would you like to set some of it down?"
The teaching is brief and exact. It goes directly to something you have been carrying and shows you how you've been carrying it wrong.
"Compassion doesn't disappear when the body does. It goes somewhere." It gestures at itself. "Here, apparently."
It teaches without preamble. What it shows you is not complex — simplicity is the whole point of it.
It places a hand on you without ceremony. The damage recedes. The exhaustion behind it recedes too, which is rarer.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gomchen#text: In a monastery that has somehow persisted in the charnel grounds — crumbling but still standing, its prayer flags bleached to grey — a gyelpo meditates in the central hall. Carved into every surface around him: contracts. Obligation clauses. Reciprocal bindings. The accumulated leverage of a long political career, frozen in stone. He sits in the center of it with his eyes slightly open.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gomchen/dissolve_: The stone cracks. The inscription flakes. He exhales slowly. 'I felt that.' The rest of the web loosens by degrees. He opens his eyes fully. 'You have just made me more dangerous. I hope you know what you are doing.' He stands, after effort. 'I owe you a debt. I prefer to pay them personally.'
Dissolve the primary binding — force the keystone obligation apart
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gomchen/find_the_: The web is too complex. Everything connects to everything else. He watches you fail to find the thread without expression.

You find it — a debt of precedence, buried under thirty layers of mutual obligation. You point to it without speaking. His eyes focus for the first time. 'You see it,' he says. 'No one has seen it.' A long pause. 'Then you are someone worth traveling with. Come.'
Study the contract web — try to find the obligation everything else depends on
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gomchen/leave_him: The hall is silent except for the slow erosion of stone.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gomchen/oath_keep:
You take one obligation off the web — the smallest, and even the smallest is heavier than it looks — and the gomchen watches you accept it with an expression that has not been used in a long time.

You will keep it. That was never in question, which is precisely why it could be offered.
Offer to hold one of them. You are good for it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gomchen/read_obli: You read them back slowly. Each one. He is very still. When you finish, the hall is quiet. 'I know,' he says. 'Say it again. Slower.' You do. When you finish the second time, something changes in his face. 'I have been very foolish,' he says quietly. 'Will you walk with me? I need to think outside these walls.'
Read the obligations back to him — enumerate the full cost of what he is holding
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_goods#text:
A grave has opened itself — the earth has subsided rather than been dug, and the contents are simply lying there in the depression, exposed to the grey daylight.

Someone was buried well. Bronze, worked cloth, a sword still in a scabbard, all of it a hand's reach away and nobody's.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_goods/ask_f: She is still in there and she is entirely lucid and she has been listening to people discuss her possessions for two hundred years without once being consulted. Being asked improves her mood immeasurably. She grants you the sword, declines to part with the cloth, and asks — as her condition — that you push the earth back afterwards, which you do.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_goods/greed:
You have the reasoning worked out before your hand arrives, which is the sign of a well-practised reasoning.

The goods are real, valuable, and will be missed by something that is still nearby.
It is in the open. That makes it nobody's.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_goods/rebur: An hour with your hands and a broken marker for a spade. When you have finished you cannot tell there was ever a subsidence, which is the point.
Push the earth back over it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_goods/take#: It is good gear and it is on the surface and there is no argument to be had with a hole in the ground. You take it and you do not linger.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_goods/why_o: There is a void under this whole section of the graveyard — something hollowed it out from below, recently, and this grave is simply the first to notice. You mark the extent of it, which takes an afternoon, and the map you make of where not to walk is worth more than the grave goods. You take those too, since the occupant is about to have a much worse problem.
Work out why the ground gave way
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_hound_pack#: A pack of grave hounds — skeletal dogs with eyes of green flame — circles you. They're not attacking. They're sniffing. Curious. One tilts its skull and whines.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_hound_pack/:
You identify the pack leader — the one the others keep watching — and put a shot between its shoulder blades at range. Clean drop. The pack scatters immediately, the hierarchy dissolved in one shot. No further engagement required.

Somewhere behind you, a green flame flickers once and goes out.
Drop the alpha at distance — scatter the pack

Third from the left, smaller than the rest, standing slightly apart.

Everything the pack does routes through her. You do not have to fight seven grave hounds; you have to convince one, in front of six witnesses.
Find the one the others keep glancing at.
You hold your ground and meet the eyes of the largest one. It blinks first. The pack loses interest and drifts away.
They eat with the focused joy of dogs everywhere. One stays close to your heel afterward, green eyes glowing up at you.
Something in your tone reaches the part of them that was once a dog. They settle. The one that whined leads you, with clear purpose, to a hollow in the ground.
The binding fails. The hound in question is offended and snaps at you. The pack loses interest and trots away.
The binding takes. One hound sits and tilts its skull at you with what you decide to read as acceptance.
Attempt to bind one as a familiar
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_robbers#tex: Two skeletons are prying open a stone sarcophagus with iron bars. They freeze when they see you — a guilty, comedic tableau. One slowly puts the crowbar behind its back.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_robbers/dem: You plant yourself between them and the tomb and fold your arms. They exchange a glance — or the skeleton equivalent — and reluctantly extend a share. Good bones know when they're outmatched.
Demand a cut for your silence
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_robbers/hel: Three sets of hands make short work of the lid. Inside: some aged valuables, a corroded weapon, a few coins. You divide the take by unspoken agreement.
Help them open it — split the loot
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_grave_robbers/rep: The grave robbers see you look around for a patrol, decide their odds are better now, and attack.
You locate a patrol two streets over and lead them back. The grave robbers are hauled away clacking in protest. The patrol sergeant presses a coin into your hand — the King's reward for civic virtue.
Find a skeleton patrol and report them
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gravedigger#text:
A living man — actually alive — digs graves in the realm of the dead. He's been here so long he's forgotten how he arrived. He looks up as you approach without stopping his work.

"Someone's got to do it. The dead keep coming and the holes don't dig themselves."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gravedigger/ask_l: "Couldn't tell you. Been trying myself." He leans on his shovel. "What I can tell you is: don't eat anything they offer. Don't go near the river after dark. And the Skeleton King's patrols are mostly reasonable, as long as you're doing something they can categorize."
Ask how to leave this realm
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gravedigger/help_: You work side by side in companionable quiet. At the end of it, he shares what he has — some food, some stories, a practical warmth that is rare in this realm.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gravedigger/offer: He stops digging. Considers it for a long moment. "Who'd dig the graves?" He goes back to work. But something about him looks lighter after the question was asked.
Offer to help him find his way home
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gravedigger/trade: He digs through a sack he keeps by the graveside. Things accumulate around graves. He has more than you'd expect, and most of it is in good condition.
Offer to trade — he's had interesting finds
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gravedigger/warm_:
Nobody has asked him that. He gets asked what he is doing here, and how he got here, and whether he can be bought.

He leans on the spade for a while before answering, and the answer takes most of an hour and is worth the hour.
He is alive. Ask him how he is, before anything else.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_graveyard_dog#tex:
It is standing on a grave mound with its head down and its green eyes fixed on you, and it has not decided yet. A grave hound alone is a guard; a grave hound in a pack is a problem. This one is alone.

Behind it, the mound has been dug at. Not by the hound.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_graveyard_dog/cal: Low voice, no eye contact, hand held out flat and still. Whatever it is now, it was a dog once, and something in the shape of the address gets through. It comes down off the mound and walks you a quarter mile to the graveyard's edge, and turns back at the boundary of what it considers its ground.
Speak to it the way you would to a working dog
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_graveyard_dog/fee: It takes the meat back onto the mound and eats there, watching you the whole time, guarding even while it chews.
Throw it food and go around
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_graveyard_dog/pet:
It is a dog in the way that a burnt-out house is a house, and you go toward it anyway with your hand out, and the party makes noises.

It lets you. It has apparently been standing on that grave for a very long time and nobody has offered it anything since.
It is a dog. You are going to do this whatever anyone says.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_graveyard_dog/rea: Tool marks, not claws — somebody came for this grave with a spade and left in a hurry. The hound is not guarding the grave from you; it is guarding it from whoever is coming back. You reset the turf and stack stones over it while the hound watches, and when you finish it lies down. It is still lying there when you look back.
Look at what dug the mound
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gyelpo_court#text:
A ruined palace, still grand in its decay. A gyelpo — a dead sorcerer of terrible power — holds court here, attended by bound spirits drifting in slow orbits. He turns as you enter without being told you'd arrived.

"I ruled then and I rule now. What makes you think I'd stop for something as trivial as dying?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gyelpo_court/attr:
It does, and the gyelpo — dead some centuries and still vain about his hall — decides that you improve the room.

You are seated well above where a traveller is seated, which is useful, and watched throughout, which is not.
The court notices you before you have said anything.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gyelpo_court/chal: The bound spirits stop their orbiting and turn inward.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gyelpo_court/offe: He leans forward for the first time. What you offer genuinely interests him — not for its power but because it is new, and almost nothing is new to him anymore. He gives back more than you gave.
Offer him magical knowledge in exchange
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gyelpo_court/pay_: The gyelpo is pleased by the form, if not the visitor. He waves a hand and the bound spirits clear a path. "You may pass. Tell no one what you saw here."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_gyelpo_court/requ: He grants it. The negotiation takes time — he thinks in decades, not minutes — but eventually yields something valuable. A name, a technique, a piece of knowledge that should not have survived him.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_hidden_gompa#text: A small monastery sits undisturbed between the burial grounds, its walls marked with painted eyes that seem to follow you. The monks here practice for the benefit of all beings caught between lives. The ground vibrates faintly with their prayers.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_hidden_gompa/#0#r: After a long pause, the door opens. A monk gestures you inside and names what can be taught here — and the price.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_hidden_gompa/#1#r: You walk past without knocking. The painted eyes seem to close behind you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace#t:
A palace stands where there was nothing an hour ago: lit windows, music, the smell of food, a door standing open onto warm light.

Everything in this realm is grey and cold and starving. This is none of those things, which tells you everything you need to know and does not make it one bit easier to walk past.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace/d: It is an excellent working — layered, self-repairing, with the smell built in, which is the part most illusionists skip. You unpick it from the outside like a knitted seam. Underneath is a pit with fourteen vetala in it looking extremely startled and, for the moment, extremely visible.
Take the illusion apart from outside
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace/e: The warmth lasts about as long as it takes for the door to close. Then the hall is a charnel pit with a very good acoustic, and the hosts are already seated.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace/p: It takes more out of the party than the last three fights combined. Half a mile on, the music stops abruptly, mid-phrase.
Walk past without looking in the windows
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace/s:
A palace was not here an hour ago, and you say so, repeatedly, until the party stops arguing about it.

You make camp at a distance and watch. At some point in the small hours the lit windows go out one row at a time, which settles the matter.
A palace was not here an hour ago.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace/t:
It is. You are three rooms in and being handed something warm before anyone else has crossed the threshold.

What saves you is that you are genuinely, transparently pleased to be there, and whatever runs the palace finds it has nothing to work with. It lets you go, baffled.
It is a warm building with the door open.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_palace/w: You walk the whole length of the hall through the music and the light and the smell of roast lamb, decline everything offered with perfect courtesy, and go out the far door. The hosts cannot touch a guest who accepts no hospitality; that is the entire rule the illusion is built to exploit, and you have simply not broken it. Behind you somebody throws a plate.
Go in, take nothing, eat nothing, leave
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_illusory_treasure:
A hoard, unattended, in the open: coin and plate and gemwork heaped against the base of a bone-wall, glittering in a realm that does not glitter.

There are no tracks around it. There is no reason for it to be here. It is, objectively, the single most suspicious object any of you has ever seen.

You rig the hoard — a tripline, a deadfall of bone-wall masonry, and a very convincing set of fresh footprints leading up to it. Then you wait uphill. What comes to collect the next victim collects a quarter ton of wall instead. Its own hoard, it turns out, is somewhere much better hidden and now unguarded.
Use the bait against whatever set it

Light does not do that. It takes about four seconds once you are looking at the right thing, and the right thing is never the treasure.

You can see where whatever laid it is waiting, too, which is more useful than the hoard would have been.
Look at the light on it. Light does not do that.

You have. Someone catches your arm and you shake it off, and the arm-catcher lets you go because there is a limit to how much you can save a person from themselves.

What you come back with is worthless and you carry it for two days before admitting that.
You have already started walking toward it.
The moment your hands close on it the hoard is a hand's-breadth of gravel and something that has been lying underneath it for a long time is sitting up.
You keep walking. The party discusses it for the next hour in the tone of people reassuring themselves.

You throw a stone into it. The stone does not clink; it lands with the soft sound of gravel. Everything above the third layer is glamour over grit — but the bottom layer, interestingly, is real, and the thing guarding it is asleep. You take the real part slowly and leave the glitter for the next fool.
Test it from a safe distance first
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_iron_skeleton_due: An iron skeleton stands at a crossroads, sword driven into the ground before it. A sign reads: DEFEAT ME AND PASS. LOSE AND SERVE. It has clearly been here a very long time. The paint on the sign is old. The skeleton is patient.
It pulls the sword from the ground and takes its stance.

You draw before it has finished standing up, which it takes as the courtesy it was intended to be.

The iron skeleton is better than you in three respects and worse in one, and the one is enough.
A sword in the ground at a crossroads is a sentence with one ending.
You cross your arms over your chest and bow, empty-handed. The iron skeleton looks at you for a long moment. Then it accepts the terms. What follows is not a sword fight.
Fight unarmed — use joint locks and throws
The iron skeleton has a short sword. You have a spear. The reach disparity matters more than the skill gap. You manage distance and let it exhaust itself against your range.
Fight at reach — keep it off its blade advantage

"I'll stand here. You've done enough." The iron skeleton goes very still. Then, slowly, it pulls the sword from the ground and holds it out to you. Its posture as it walks away is the lightest you've seen anything move in this realm.

You point out the ambiguity in the oath's wording — technically, the requirement is already fulfilled by the act of being challenged. The skeleton freezes mid-reach for its sword. You can hear it processing. You walk past at a measured pace.
Find the logical flaw in its oath
"My oath is not a matter for debate." It draws.

You speak to it about the nature of oaths — not their letter but their purpose. What was it protecting? Is the thing it was protecting still here? The iron skeleton stands for a long time. Then it lowers its sword. Something releases in its posture.
Persuade it that the oath no longer serves
Your first move is not a block — it's a strike at the wrist holding the sword. Iron on iron. The skeleton stumbles back, sword arm compromised. The duel continues, but on your terms now.
Smash its sword arm — end the fight before it starts
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_khedrup#text: On a flat rock carved with auspicious symbols, a preserved rolang sits in full meditation posture, counting beads with extraordinary precision. His lips move with sub-vocalized counts. Beside him, a pile of tally marks in the stone suggests he has been at this particular session for a very long time. He has the focused look of a man who is almost sure his formula is right.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_khedrup/examine_p: 'Copper oxide as the fixative?' He looks up sharply. 'How did you—' He examines his own hand, then back at you. 'What else can you tell?' The conversation goes on for some time. By the end he is standing. 'I should like to continue this. If you're traveling, I'll accompany you as far as convenient.'
Examine his preserved state — make a technical observation
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_khedrup/leave_him: The counting continues. The tally marks accumulate.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_khedrup/spot_the_: His hand stops on the beads. He looks up for the first time. 'Show me.' You do. He studies it. Studies you. Then: 'I may need to revise my methodology. I would welcome a second opinion — going forward.'
Point out a flaw in his formula — you can see where the multiplier breaks down
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_khedrup/wait_for_: You shift at the wrong moment. He loses count, closes his eyes, and begins again from the beginning without acknowledging you.

Three hours. Four. He reaches the end of his calculation, opens his eyes, and finds you there. 'You waited.' A pause. 'Most don't.' He consults his tallies. 'This is inconvenient. I will need to adjust for your presence in the calculation. Sit down. What is your birth star?'
Wait for him to complete his count — do not interrupt
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_king_messenger#te:
A skeleton in the Skeleton King's copper livery reins in a bone horse beside you, unrolls a scroll, and reads without preamble:

"To the living party currently trespassing in the charnel grounds: the King of the Setting Sun requires your attendance. Or your absence. He is flexible. He requires you to choose, in writing, today."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_king_messenger/ab: "Sensible," says the messenger, entirely off the record, and stamps it. "Between us: the ones who attend are usually still there." It gives you a route that avoids the bone city and will not accept payment for the favour.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_king_messenger/am: You add two clauses in the margin: attendance at a time of your choosing, and safe conduct both ways. The messenger reads them, reads them again, and gets down off the horse to do so properly. Nobody has ever amended one of these. It counter-signs — because the document does not actually forbid it — and rides off looking like a functionary who is going to have an interesting conversation with its superior.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_king_messenger/at: The messenger countersigns, stamps it, gives you the counterfoil, and departs at speed. You are now, formally, expected somewhere. It is oddly steadying to have an appointment.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_king_messenger/go:
He has orders and a schedule and neither of them survive twenty minutes of being asked, with evident interest, about places he has recently been.

By the time he remembers the schedule you know the state of three roads and one court.
A messenger has been everywhere. Keep him talking.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_king_messenger/re: The messenger sighs, rolls the scroll, and raises one hand. The escort you had not noticed comes out of the bone-scrub on three sides.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites#text: A half-completed funeral pyre. The body hasn't been burned — the rites were interrupted. A dré circles the pyre, keening. Without proper rites, neither body nor spirit can move on.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/ask_dr: It takes a long time to understand the dré — its grief interrupts its speech constantly. Eventually you piece it together: the ritual was interrupted by a fight, the practitioners fled, and no one came back. It tells you where the practitioners went.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/build_:
The existing pyre was assembled wrong — too loose, wrong timber arrangement, no heat concentration. You break it down and rebuild it properly in forty minutes, using the scavenged materials as they should be used.

The dré watches you work in silence. When you light it, the fire catches cleanly and burns hot. Not the same as the proper rites — the spirit knows the difference — but the dré settles at the fire's edge with something that is almost quiet.
Build a proper pyre from what's available
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/comple: The ceremony takes time and every word must be right. When the pyre catches, the dré's keening softens and then stops. It drifts upward and is gone.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/mourne:
You know the order. You have done this often enough that your hands know the order, which is the part nobody warns you about.

When the pyre takes, the thing that has been waiting at the edge of the clearing goes wherever such things go, without any fuss at all.
Somebody started this and did not finish it. Finish it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/pray#r: You cannot complete the rites, but you can witness. You sit and pray for a while. The dré calms, marginally. It is not enough but it is something.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/pray#t: Pray for the dead — what you can offer
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_last_rites/take_o: The dré notices. Its keening changes pitch.
You work quickly and quietly. The dré doesn't notice.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_lost_caravan#text: Overturned carts and scattered goods. The caravan guards are dead — properly so. Something attacked them recently. Tracks lead into the swamp. The goods are still here, undisturbed by the local dead.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_lost_caravan/bury: You leave the goods untouched and dig. It takes time. When you finish, the site looks less like a disaster and more like a grave. You say what should be said.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_lost_caravan/sear: There — breathing, barely, under an overturned crate. The wound is serious but survivable if treated now. You work fast.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_lost_caravan/take: You work quickly, taking the most valuable things. The dead guards don't object.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_lost_caravan/trac: The tracks are fresh. You follow them into the swamp and find the attackers still circling their kill.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_lost_traveler_swa:
He is sitting on his pack in six inches of water, and he is alive — properly alive, breathing, shivering, sunburnt on one side of his face from a sun that does not shine here.

"I've been walking in a circle," he says, with the terrible calm of someone who worked this out some time ago. "I keep finding my own footprints. I've stopped following them."

The loop is real and it is thin — a fold in the swamp about a mile across that returns everything to its own footprints. You cut it. The change is not visible; it is simply that the horizon means something now. He starts crying, which he seems as surprised by as you are.
Break whatever is turning him in a circle

He talks for the first hour and then stops, and the silence afterwards is better. At the treeline he shakes everyone's hand formally, one at a time, and walks off south. You do not find out whether he makes it.
Take him with you as far as the next dry ground

Lost is a thing you can fix with directions. This is the other thing, and you recognise it because you are carrying a version of it yourself.

You do not give him directions. You sit in the water next to him for a while, and then you both get up.
He is not lost. He is somewhere he does not want to be.
He eats too fast and apologises for it. The directions he repeats back to you three times, getting them right on the third.

He does not know, and the not-knowing is the whole horror of it. But in the telling he mentions a doorway in a hillside, a smell of jasmine, and a woman who asked him to carry something. You write down everything he says. Some of it will matter later.
Ask how a living man got into the realm of the dead
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mass_grave#text: The ground sinks under your feet. You realize you're standing on a mass burial site — hundreds, maybe thousands of dead from some forgotten catastrophe. The earth pulses with dark energy.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mass_grave/channe: You open yourself to it and let it move through you. It is vast and old and full of a specific kind of knowledge. What you learn cannot be unlearned.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mass_grave/consec: The undertaking takes everything you have. The pulse of dark energy fights you for an hour before it yields. When it's done, the ground is quiet for the first time since the catastrophe that filled it. This will matter to someone, somewhere, even if you never know who.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mass_grave/grief_:
It is not the same, and you know it is not the same, and you kneel anyway because the difference is not the point.

Something in the ground eases. Not much. The amount you would expect one person's attention to be worth.
You are already carrying one. What is a thousand more.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mass_grave/invest: Your foot goes through the soil into something that moves. Then several things move.
You move slowly, reading the ground. There — a corner of something preserved, protected by the sheer density of death around it. Burial goods from someone important.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mass_grave/leave#: Some places don't want to be investigated. You respect that.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_medicinal_garden#:
Something is growing here on purpose. Beds of herbs in ordered rows, staked and labelled, tended in a place where nothing should tend anything — and the labels are in a careful hand, in a language you half-recognise.

A preserved one straightens up from the weeding and regards you without alarm. "Patients or customers?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_medicinal_garden/: She sets you thinning the third bed and does not explain why it matters until you have done it correctly, at which point she explains at length and with real pleasure. Nothing grows well in this realm; everything here grows because she made it. You leave with your kit restocked and an open invitation.
Offer your hands for the afternoon

She has not mentioned them because most people do not ask, and most people who do ask are not asking about medicine.

She establishes which you are with one question, and appears satisfied with the answer.
Ask about the beds she has not mentioned.

The gardener stops what she is doing. It is, apparently, a much rarer request than the other one and a considerably easier one to fulfil.

What she gives you will not fix anything. It makes tomorrow's walking possible, which is the whole of what you asked for.
Ask for the thing that helps rather than the thing that cures.

"It doesn't," she says. "I feed it." She shows you the trench at the garden's edge, where she has been composting her own substance — a little at a time, for a very long time, into the soil. She is markedly less than she was when she started. She considers this an entirely reasonable arrangement and will not be argued with.
Ask how anything grows in the realm of hunger
"Mm," she says, and goes back to the weeding. "Mind the third bed."
She lays out what is dried and ready, and prices it fairly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mehr#text: Something catches the thin light of the charnel grounds and throws it back — gold, steady, unblinking. Not an insect. Not a torch. An eye. Set in the face of a preserved woman standing knee-deep in black water, watching you with the patience of someone who has been here a long time.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mehr/call_out#res: She answers. Dry, measured, without warmth or hostility. She answers your questions the way a stone does if you press your ear to it. She is not interested in traveling. You are not sufficiently interesting.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mehr/read_the_sig: Her good eye narrows. The gold one does not move. 'That is the first intelligent question anyone has asked me in a very long time.' A pause. 'Come. Walk with me while I explain what it actually said.'
Ask about the prophecy — you have enough to read what she was reading
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mehr/ritual_flame: The flame catches her attention in a way nothing else would. She straightens. Her golden eye moves before the other one does. 'Where did you learn that form?' She is already wading toward you before you finish answering.
Light a ritual flame — the old greeting of the Sun priesthood
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mehr/speak_as_equ: She looks at you the way she must have looked at the court before they threw her in the tar pit. 'I have heard every manner of introduction,' she says. 'Go.'
She studies you for a long moment. 'You have the manner of someone who has survived things,' she says. 'I find that more persuasive than credentials.' She wades toward you.
Speak to her as an equal — not with reverence, not with wariness
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_memory_echo#text: A shimmer in the graveyard air, like heat haze — but it's cold here. For a moment you see a family at a meal. Vivid, fully real. Then gone, leaving only the smell of food that isn't there.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_memory_echo/hold_: The hunger in the image reaches you before the meaning does. You feel it in your chest for an hour.
A life becomes briefly comprehensible. The attachment, the warmth, and what happened to it.
Hold the vision — try to understand who they were
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_memory_echo/move_: Some things are just residue of lives. You don't need to understand every one.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_memory_echo/study: A well-preserved echo. Whoever imprinted it was powerful in life, and thoroughly unresolved.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_guild#t: A walled compound marked with the crossed-bone sigil of the guild. Skeletal warriors and half-dead fighters linger between contracts, sharpening weapons they barely need to use anymore.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_guild/#: The guildmaster looks you over without interest. Weapons, armor, contracts — name what you need.
You leave the compound to its dead-eyed inhabitants.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_lodge#t: A squat building of stacked bones, its door marked with crossed shovels. Inside, undead mercenaries sit sharpening weapons and arguing about pay rates with the vigor of the professionally disgruntled. A notice board covers one wall, bristling with jobs and wanted notices.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_lodge/e: "Do you think it's a circus, stranger? Do your business or leave before I lose patience." The lodge master points at the door. You can still browse, but everything is priced 25% higher.

It takes a few minutes of material to break through the professional sullenness. Then one skeleton starts laughing. Then another. By the end, the lodge is rowdy and welcoming. One of the mercenaries pulls you aside afterward. "That was good. I could use a change of scene. You taking on crew?"
Try to entertain the mercenaries — loosen them up
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_lodge/n: Wanted: rolang herders to redirect a mob from the eastern fields. Reward posted by the Skeleton King's chamberlain. Two other notices offer bounties on a rogue dré that's been impersonating officials. The third is just a skeleton complaining about a debt.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_lodge/o: The lodge master hands you a contract without ceremony. "Rolang infestation, two miles east. Standard terms." You go.
Offer your fighting services — take a contract
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_lodge/s: You lose solidly. The mercenary is professional about it. "Not bad. Keep practicing. Costs you a round though." You pay for drinks you cannot drink.
You hold your own — better than hold your own. The watching mercenaries go quiet in a way that means something. The sparring partner extends a hand. "Not bad for a warmie. We'll call it a draw."
Challenge a mercenary to a practice spar
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mercenary_lodge/u:
You find a cleared space and run through a form — not showing off, just working. The lodge goes quiet in the particular way it gets when something unexpected is happening.

A mercenary with no visible weapons walks over and watches carefully. 'Who trained you?' You talk for an hour. She introduces you to three people who turn out to be worth knowing.
Demonstrate unarmed technique — get their attention
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_lake#text: The surface of the lake is perfectly still, reflecting not the sky above but something else — other realms, other moments, faces that do not look back when you stare. Practitioners sit at its edge, meditating on what the water reveals.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_lake/#0#re: A practitioner meets your eyes in the reflection before turning around. They can teach what the lake teaches. The water makes everything a fair price.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_lake/#1#re: You step back from the water's edge. The reflection holds your shape a moment longer, then dissolves.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_pool#text: A pool of perfectly still, perfectly clear water in the middle of the wasteland. Impossible here. It shows not your reflection but something else — a past life, a death, something that might be a future.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_pool/drink: The visions come faster than you can process them. You sit by the pool for a long time before you can stand again.
The water tastes like memory. Something sharpens in you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_pool/look_: The vision comes without asking for it. You see the realms ordered by what you've built — the highest first, the lowest last. No numbers. Just the weight of things.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_pool/medit: You sit with the visions rather than fighting them. The pool shows you the cycle — not as horror, but as mechanism. Something in the understanding frees a knot you didn't know was there.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_pool/shatt: You throw a stone. The vision breaks into ripples. Something lifts. Something else wonders if you were ready to stop looking.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_mirror_pool/vain_:
You look. It shows you accurately, which is the cruelty of it — not distorted, not aged, simply seen from outside for the first time.

You are quiet for some hours afterwards and decline to say why.
Of course you are going to look.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nangwa#text: In the collapsed shell of what was once a library — shelves of ash, scrolls of smoke — a barely-visible figure moves between the ruins. It is picking up nothing, reading nothing, but its lips are moving. Occasionally it stops, gestures at empty air, shakes its head, and starts again from the beginning.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nangwa/complete_h: He stops. Turns toward you with the most attention he has given anything in centuries. He seems to become slightly more present in the physical world as he focuses. 'Walk with me,' he says. 'I think better when I walk. Tell me if I have this right.'
Complete his sentence — you can see where the argument is going
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nangwa/follow_the: Your interjection breaks his concentration entirely. He dissipates for a moment, then reforms, looking confused and irritated. You have cost him hours of work.

You catch the flaw and name it. He stops mid-gesture. 'Say that again.' You do. He is silent for a full minute. Then: 'I hadn't considered that approach.' A longer silence. 'Come with me while I think it through. I need a sounding board.'
Follow the argument — interrupt at the right moment
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nangwa/reach_thro: For a moment, genuine contact. He startles. Looks at his hands as if seeing them for the first time in a while. 'Oh,' he says. 'I have been quite far away.' He looks at you with new attention. 'Would you stay nearby? I find I concentrate better when someone is present.'
Reach toward him through space — make contact with the part of him that is still here
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nangwa/watch_and_: He doesn't notice you leave. The argument continues.
Watch him for a while, then leave
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nyingje#text: Among the ruins of a catacomb, a silver skeleton moves methodically from form to form — rolangs, dré, the occasional barely-present ghost. It is tending them. Binding wounds that will not heal, offering a hand to things that won't take it, reciting something under its breath to creatures that cannot hear. It does not seem to need an audience.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nyingje/ask_direc: 'I am needed here.' She returns to her work without hostility. It is simply true.

She pauses in her work. Studies you with empty eye sockets that somehow convey careful attention. 'You are going further than here,' she says. 'There will be beings who need tending there too.' She finishes with her current patient, then stands. 'I will come.'
Ask her directly: will you travel with us?
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nyingje/help_with: You work in silence for a while. She watches your technique without comment. Then: 'You have been taught properly.' A pause. 'By whom?' By the time you finish answering, you are both walking. You realize later you agreed to travel together without either of you saying so directly.
Help her with her round — tend alongside her
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nyingje/leave_wit: She doesn't look up as you go. The recitation continues.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_nyingje/meditate_: She completes her round and comes back to where you are sitting. Waits. When you open your eyes, she is very close. 'You practice,' she says. It is not a question. A pause. 'I will walk with you for a while.'
Sit in meditation nearby — make yourself a point of stillness in this place
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ossuary_bargain#t:
Bones stacked to the vaulted ceiling, sorted by type, in a building constructed entirely for that purpose. At a counter near the door, a skeleton in a clerk's visor is doing sums in a ledger.

"Buying, selling, or storing?" it asks. "We do all three. Storage is where the money is."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ossuary_bargain/a: The storage business is running at a loss and has been for eighty years — the clerk has been discounting long-term contracts against a currency that stopped existing. You show it the error. It goes very quiet, recalculates two centuries of accounts in about four minutes, and then, being fundamentally honest, insists on paying you a consultant's fee out of the correction.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ossuary_bargain/l: "Everyone says that," the clerk says, and goes back to the sums.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ossuary_bargain/o:
You read all of it. You are not agreeing to something you have not read; you have never been able to, and it has cost you opportunities.

This time it costs the ossuary keeper an hour and you the clause on the fourth page, which was going to be the expensive one.
Read all of it before agreeing to any of it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ossuary_bargain/s: The clerk produces a second ledger and a surprisingly good selection.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_ossuary_bargain/w: The contracts are prepaid, in perpetuity, by the deceased themselves — every skeleton in this building is a client who arranged its own indefinite safekeeping rather than risk being scattered. It is not a warehouse. It is a very long-term hotel, and the clerk is the concierge, and it takes the duty extremely seriously.
Ask who is paying for all this storage
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_peddler_graveyard: A preta wanders between the grave markers, its distended belly dragging, desperate hands clutching bundles of goods. It will trade anything for food — though it can never eat enough to be satisfied.
The preta's needle-thin neck cranes toward you, eyes fixed on your pack. It lays its goods on a grave marker and waits.
You give the preta a wide berth. It watches you go with hollow, hungry eyes.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_peddler_swamp#tex: A preta rises from the mist at the water's edge, its needle-thin neck craning as it senses your approach. Desperate hands clutch wares salvaged from the swamp floor. It will trade anything for food.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_peddler_swamp/#0#: The preta spreads its goods on a half-submerged log and regards you with hollow, hopeful eyes.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_peddler_swamp/#1#: You leave it to the mist. Its eyes follow you until the fog closes in.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog#text: Green mist clings to the surface of a bubbling swamp, hanging low and still. The water hisses faintly where it touches exposed stone. The smell is thick enough to feel.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog/air_ma: You push a wind through the bog. The mist tears and scatters. A clean path opens.
Disperse the mist with air magic
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog/find_s: A raised ridge of firmer ground runs along the bog's western edge — not obvious, but there. You cross clean.
Look for a path above the mist line
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog/iron_s:
Everyone else is retching before the halfway point and you are not, which means you are the one still capable of pulling people forward.

It is not a heroic contribution. It is the whole crossing, as it turns out.
Green mist. You have kept worse down than this.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog/neutra: You scatter reagents into the water upstream. The reaction takes ten minutes and smells worse before it smells better. But the mist clears, and the exposed bog yields unusual materials.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog/push_t: The mist gets into you. By the time you reach the other side your hands are shaking and your vision has gone green at the edges.
You cross at a run, holding your breath until your lungs burn. On the far bank you spit twice and keep moving.
Move fast and hold your breath
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_poison_bog/sealed: You know exactly where the mist gets in — the seams, the collar gap, the wrist joints. You seal them all before you step off solid ground. The crossing is still unpleasant but the mist finds no purchase. You arrive on the far bank clean.
Seal your joints against the mist before crossing
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_prashan#text: A vetala perches on a crumbling milestone, its mismatched layers of stolen cloth draped over a body it wears like a borrowed coat. It turns its head at your approach with the particular alertness of someone who has been waiting for exactly this. 'Ah,' it says. 'A traveler. I have a question for you.'
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_prashan/answer_th: 'No. That is the obvious answer. Everyone says that.' It gestures dismissively. 'Go away. Come back when you have thought more carefully.'

It tilts its head. Then further. Then further still, nearly upside down. 'Hmm.' A long pause. 'That is either a very good answer or a very bad one, and I cannot immediately tell which.' It straightens. 'I need to follow this further. Come with me.'
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_prashan/ask_a_bet: It goes very still. This has not happened before — or not for a very long time. 'You—' It stops. 'Where did you—' Stops again. Slowly, a smile spreads across a face not quite designed for it. 'All right. This is excellent. You will come with me. I insist.'
Ask it a better question instead of answering
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_prashan/refuse#re: 'As you like. You will be back. They always come back when they have had time to think of an answer.' It settles in to wait.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_prashan/tell_a_jo: It blinks. Then, despite itself, makes a sound. Then another. 'That is — oh, that is terrible. That is genuinely terrible.' Its head is listing sideways with laughter. 'Come, I'll show you something better. I promise.'
Tell it a joke instead of answering
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_feast_charn:
The offerings left for the dead are heaped at the edge of the burning ground — rice, cakes, fruit, poured milk — and the pretas are around them in a ring, on their knees, faces inches from the food.

None of it goes in. Their throats will not pass it. They stay anyway, because being near it is the closest thing available.

It is the oldest solution and the reason the offerings get burnt in the first place: a preta cannot swallow rice but it can take the smoke. You build the fire properly and feed everything into it. The ring closes around the smoke and breathes, and for a while the sound they make is not the sound they were making.
Burn the food — smoke, they can take
You go quietly. It is the second-worst thing you have seen in this realm and you are aware you will not remember which was first.

Burnt offering with the dedication spoken over it is a different order of thing from a bonfire — the words are what turn smoke into food. You perform the whole sequence. The ring of pretas eats, properly, for the first time in however long, and one of them thanks you in a language that died before the offerings were stacked.
Do it as the rite prescribes, with the words

Feeding them once is an afternoon's work. You spend three days instead, teaching the ring to build and dedicate the fire without you — which is harder, because they have to stop clinging to the heap long enough to learn. Two of them get it. Those two will teach the others. You leave a functioning arrangement behind rather than a full stomach, which is the difference between charity and something better.
Teach them to make the smoke themselves
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_feast_swamp:
They have laid a table in the marsh. A real table, on real trestles, in eight inches of standing water — and on it, a banquet: rice, fruit, roast meat, all of it steaming.

The pretas are seated around it. None of them is eating. They are all just looking at it, and have been for a long time.

It is real, and it is good, and it is the best meal you have had in weeks. Every preta at the table watches every mouthful. Nobody stops you. Nobody says anything. You finish because stopping halfway would somehow be worse.

The throat is the width of a straw and the swallowing has to be taught — small, slow, wait, again. It takes twenty minutes to get four mouthfuls into her. She keeps them down. The others watch this happen with an attention that is difficult to be the subject of. When you leave, three of them have moved their chairs closer to hers.
Take a bowl and feed the nearest one by hand
Nobody at the table looks up as you go. The food is still steaming when you lose sight of it.

You look, and having looked you decline, and the declining is easy in a way it has not been easy for years.

The pretas cannot make you want it. They have nothing else to offer and drift off to find someone who can be worked with.
Look at what is actually on the table first.

"Because it will end," says the one at the head of the table, without looking away from the rice. "While we do not begin, it is still whole." You sit with that for a while. Then you point out, gently, that the food is going cold, and that this is also an ending, and that it is happening whether or not anyone begins. There is a very long silence. Then somebody picks up a spoon.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_feeding_gro: A hollow where pretas gather around a spring of water that turns to pus in their mouths, fruit trees whose apples become ash when touched. The pretas wail and claw at sustenance that perpetually escapes them. It is one of the worst things you have ever seen.
The water runs clear. The pretas drink with expressions that have no analog in the living world. It reverts after an hour. But for that hour it is something.
Bless the spring with white magic
You can't help everyone. You keep moving. The sound follows you for a while before the wind takes it.
It works, briefly. Your food is not cursed, and for a moment they eat — actually eat. The crying slows. It doesn't last. But for a moment it was real.
You understand it now — how the curse works, where it originates, why the simple solutions fail. What to do with this understanding is a separate and harder question.
Study the mechanics of the curse
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_pack#text: A pack of pretas surrounds you — a dozen, maybe more — moaning and reaching with skeletal hands. Their eyes are cavernous and desperate. They don't attack. They beg. The sound is almost worse than violence.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_pack/intimi: The hunger is stronger than the fear. They surge forward.
You spread your arms wide and roar. For a moment, the part of them that remembers fear overrides the hunger. They scatter into the grey mist.
Drive them back with presence and force of will
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_pack/lead_t: You speak calmly and point the way — there's a trickle of clean water half a mile east, something most denizens here cannot find or would not think to look for. They turn. Whether the water helps is uncertain. But they turn.
Lead them toward a water source
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_pack/share_: The food vanishes in their hands — the curse takes it before it reaches their mouths. But the act itself seems to do something. The desperate reaching slows. They let you pass.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_wail#text: A chorus of voices rises from just beneath the waterline — hungry ghosts calling out in a language that is not quite sound. The words, if words they are, convey only need.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_wail/listen: The need fills your mind for a moment. Hollow.
One voice becomes distinct. A name. Something that mattered, once, somewhere.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_wail/press_: Nothing reaches you. The voices fade behind you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_preta_wail/yoga_m: The voices quiet, one by one. It doesn't solve anything. It might help anyway.
Chant a mantra of compassion for them
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rasabhava#text: In a low-ceilinged catacomb chamber, a preserved zombie works steadily at a cluttered bench. Phials, powders, a bellows made of preserved lung. The formula on the stone tablet before him is enormously complex. He is at the part he always reaches before noticing something is wrong and starting over. He has not looked up.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rasabhava/identif: 'The stabilization phase — your catalyst ratio shifts at temperature.' He goes absolutely still. 'Say that again.' You do. He checks it three times. 'I have been wrong for forty-three years.' He closes his eyes. Opens them. 'I believe I need a different sort of problem. Will you have me?'
Identify the phase where the formula breaks down
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rasabhava/leave_h: He doesn't notice you leave. He's found something to check.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rasabhava/read_th: You can follow the general outline but the specifics are beyond you. He doesn't look up.

You see it — a small error in the stabilization phase, invisible in isolation but fatal in combination. 'There,' you say. He looks. Silence. 'That can't be right. I've checked it six—' He checks it again. 'Oh.' The smallest, most deflated sound. Then: 'Are you traveling? I may want to get out of this room.'
Read the formula over his shoulder — try to spot what keeps going wrong
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rasabhava/suggest: He looks up for the first time. 'You're suggesting — instead of physical fixation, a binding of—' He sets down his tools. 'That would require a collaborator.' A pause. He looks at you properly. 'Come in. Close the door. I want to try something.'
Ask what he is trying to preserve and whether it can be summoned instead
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_realm_exit#text: The air changes. Ahead, the grey wasteland of the hungry ghost realm gives way to something else. A boundary marker — a stone carved with the Wheel of Life — stands at the transition point. Behind you, the realm of craving. Ahead, the unknown.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_realm_exit/cross#: You step through. The grey lifts.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_realm_exit/dedica: You stand at the boundary and give it all away — every good thing earned in this realm, offered outward to those who couldn't earn it for themselves. The gesture costs you nothing you can measure. What it does is harder to name.
Dedicate all merit gained here to the beings still suffering
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_realm_exit/leave_: For those still inside. You leave what you can spare and cross.
Leave an offering at the boundary stone
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_realm_exit/look_b: You turn. The realm reveals itself — not as horror, not as punishment, but as consequence. Everything here follows from something. The craving was always going somewhere. It came here. That clarity stays with you as you cross.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_choki#tex:
A dré stands at the edge of a still pool with her feet in the shallows, facing the water. She has been standing there long enough that reeds have grown around her ankles.

"It came down the valley in the afternoon," she says, to nobody. "There was no sound. That's the part I keep coming back to. There should have been a sound."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_choki/hir: She looks at the coin without much interest, and then at you. "You want me to come." That part seems to land. She comes.
Ask her to come along and offer to pay
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_choki/lea: "There should have been a sound," she says again, behind you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_choki/lis:
It takes two hours and she has clearly never got to the end of it before — she stops three times and each time you wait, and each time she starts again slightly further on. When she reaches the part where she went into the river herself, she stops for a long while.

Then she says, "That's all of it," with enormous surprise, and steps out of the reeds for the first time in however long.
Let her finish the whole account
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_choki/wat:
You put your hand in the pool and let her feel it the way you feel it: not a thing that took her village, just water, doing what water does, without intent and without memory of having done it. It is not comfort. It is accuracy, and she has been waiting for accuracy.

"Oh," she says. And then, after a while: "Where are you going?"
Show her what the water is actually doing
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_durvasa#t:
The gyelpo is pinned in the air about a foot above the ground, arms out, held there by something that is visibly still working — a curse coming back the way it went, and arriving continuously.

"Contract work," he says, through his teeth, with considerable dignity. "Final commission. The client's target had a *practice*. Would you consider — this is embarrassing — would you consider stabilising the field?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_durvasa/h: He accepts the retainer with the professionalism of a man who has never in his life worked without one, and remains, technically, still being cursed.
Cut him down and put him on retainer
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_durvasa/l: "Fair," he calls after you, entirely without rancour. "Genuinely — that is fair."
He is a professional curse-caster. Leave him hanging.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_durvasa/s:
The curse is not attacking him; it is *returning*, endlessly, along a channel that never closed. You cannot break it. You can widen it until the flow is survivable, which takes about twenty minutes of extremely careful work.

He comes down onto his feet, straightens his robes, and says: "That is still happening, you understand. It will be happening in a hundred years." Then, with real courtesy: "Where are we going?"
Take the pressure off the field

A returned curse runs on an open contract. You do not fight it — you settle it: name the commission, name the client, mark the invoice paid, and close the instrument with the correct forms. It takes an hour and a great deal of chalk.

He lands hard, on his knees, silent for the first time. "Nobody," he says eventually, "has ever thought to *pay it off*."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_gomchen#t:
A gyelpo sits in perfect meditation posture in the middle of a room knee-deep in paper. Contracts, deeds, letters of appointment — thousands of them, all bearing his seal, all still legally in force.

He opens one eye. "I am told this is the practice now. Sitting in it." He does not sound convinced. He does sound like a man who has been trying for a long time.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_gomchen/d:
Every document bearing his seal is a binding he is still party to, and there are, at a rough count, eleven thousand of them. You cannot read them all. You can dissolve the seal itself, which voids the lot at once, and takes most of a day and everything you have.

The paper goes to ash in a single soft rush. He sits in the middle of it with his eyes shut. "A master of ten thousand sutras," he says. "And what got me out was somebody else's paperwork."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_gomchen/h: The phrase "no paperwork whatsoever" does more work than the coin. He is on his feet before you have finished the offer.
Offer him a position with no paperwork whatsoever
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_gomchen/l: He closes the eye again. The paper does not move.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_gomchen/r:
You read for two hours. The contracts are not corrupt — that is the thing. Every one is defensible, procedurally sound, and in the interest of the institution. He never once did anything indefensible. He simply did ten thousand defensible things and ended up here.

You tell him so. It is not absolution and he does not take it as any. But he stops sitting in the paper as though it were a punishment and starts going through it as though it were a problem.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_khedrup#t:
A preserved one sits cross-legged on a flat rock, reciting at speed, with a tally-board propped beside him and a set of tables weighted down under a stone.

He holds up one finger without breaking the recitation — *wait* — finishes a count, marks the board, and only then looks up. "Auspicious day," he explains. "Triple merit. I am not going to waste it being sociable."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_khedrup/a:
The tables are internally consistent and beautifully kept and rest on one bad assumption made four hundred years ago, which he has been compounding ever since. You show him. He recalculates. It takes eleven minutes and the colour, such as it is, goes out of him.

"So the entire ledger," he says.

"The entire ledger."

He sits with it. Then he picks up the tally-board, considers throwing it, and puts it in his bag instead. "I should like to see how other people are doing this," he says.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_khedrup/h: He checks the tables. Pilgrimage does in fact carry a multiplier. He accepts on those grounds and only those grounds, and brings the tally-board.
Point out that travel accrues merit too, and pay him
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_khedrup/l: The recitation resumes before you are out of earshot, at the same impossible pace.
Leave him to the triple merit
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_khedrup/p:
You do not argue with the system. You just sit down and do the practice properly beside him for three hours, at the pace it is meant to be done at, which is about a fifth of his.

He speeds up for the first hour out of competitiveness. In the second he slows down. In the third he stops counting altogether, and afterwards he sits very still for a while and does not mark the board.

"That was slower," he says eventually. "Why was that better?"
Sit down and recite with him
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_mehr#text:
Something catches the light at the bottom of a tar seep — a single gold glint, deep down in the black.

It blinks.

"Yes," says a voice from under the tar, quite calmly. "I can see you too. Only the one eye, mind. Would you mind terribly?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_mehr/haul: It takes both arms and most of an hour and she comes out of the tar in one long appalling motion, tall and black-lacquered and entirely composed. She thanks you, wipes the good eye clear, and says: "You are going to want to hear the last prophecy. Nobody ever does. It was the accurate one."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_mehr/hire: "A commercial arrangement. Very sensible." She takes the coin with a tar-black hand and does not mention that she would have come for nothing.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_mehr/leav: "Quite all right," the voice says, receding. "It is not an urgent situation. It has not been urgent for some time."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_mehr/prop:
She recites it from under the tar, in the dark, unhurried. It is not a failed prophecy. It is a correct one that arrived at a court that had already decided, and the court's response is why she is in a tar pit.

When you pull her out afterwards, she has already decided you are worth attaching to.
Ask her for the failed prophecy first
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nangwa#te:
The library is three walls and a floor of wet scroll-pulp. In the middle of it a dré is pacing a tight circle, talking rapidly, gesturing at a diagram that is not there.

"—and therefore, if the third term holds, which it does, which I have shown, then—" He stops. Frowns. Starts again. "—and therefore, if the third term holds—"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nangwa/fi:
You listen through two full cycles, work out where he is going, and say the next line out loud.

He stops dead. Turns around. Looks at you as though you have appeared out of nothing, which from his perspective you have. "Yes," he says. "Yes — that's it — and then the corollary—" and he is off again, but forward this time, and he does not stop for an hour, and at the end of it he is somebody who has finished a thought and needs a new one.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nangwa/hi: The interruption works where nothing else has. He accepts the terms distractedly, still gesturing at the diagram, and follows you out still talking.
Interrupt and make him an offer
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nangwa/sa: Three scroll-cases from a high shelf, dry inside. He does not notice you take them. He does not notice you at all.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nangwa/sp:
He is not haunting the library. He is caught in about four seconds of it, running them over and over, and the loop is thin enough to see the seam. You cut it. He arrives in the present mid-gesture, extremely disoriented and — once he works out how long it has been — extremely embarrassed.

"Right," he says. "Well. I shall need to see what's been published."
Look at what is holding him in the loop
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nyingje#t:
A silver skeleton is working its way along a row of pretas laid out on mats, doing for each one whatever can be done — water it cannot swallow, a cloth on a forehead that feels nothing, a hand held.

It does not look up. "There are forty-one today. Yesterday there were thirty-nine. I am not gaining."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nyingje/h:
You work the row from the far end and meet in the middle after four hours. Neither of you says anything useful in that time. At the end it straightens up, looks at the mats, and then at you.

"I vowed to remain until every being here found its way out," it says. "I have been assuming that meant standing still." It picks up its bowl and comes with you, and does not look back at the forty-one, which costs it something.
Take the other end of the row
It accepts the coin on behalf of the forty-one, arranges for their care with a neighbouring dré, and comes. The arrangement is meticulous. It takes most of the afternoon.
Offer to fund the work if it comes with you
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nyingje/s: It accepts without fuss and immediately begins distributing. "Forty-one," it says. "That is better than it was an hour ago."
Leave what supplies you can spare
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_nyingje/v:
It recites the vow. You point out — carefully, because this is somebody's life's work — that it says *until every being finds its way out*, not *until every being here is comfortable*, and that one of those is a task that can be advanced by leaving this row of mats.

The silence is long. "I have been reading it wrong for eight hundred years," it says, without any bitterness at all. "Well. Shall we go?"
Ask what the vow actually said
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_prashan#t:
The vetala at the crossroads does not block the road. He simply says, as you pass:

"What is it that you carry everywhere, cannot put down, did not choose, and will lose entirely at the moment you most need it?"

Then he waits, with the air of someone who has waited a very long time and expects to wait longer.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_prashan/a:
"Your name," you say.

The silence goes on for some time. "...That is not the answer I have," he says at last. "It is better than the answer I have." He gets up off the milestone he has been sitting on for four centuries, dusts himself off, and falls in beside you without being invited. "I shall need considerably more material. You appear to be going somewhere interesting."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_prashan/c:
"What are you going to do," you ask, "if someone answers it?"

He opens his mouth. Closes it. You watch four hundred years of a very good defensive position collapse in about six seconds. "I had not," he says slowly, "considered that as a live possibility." He is, it turns out, delighted rather than wounded — which is what makes him worth having.
Ask him one he cannot answer
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_prashan/h: "A commercial answer. Disappointing but valid." He pockets the coin and comes, and asks the riddle again three miles later in case you have improved.
Skip the riddle; offer him employment
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_prashan/w: "Take your time," he calls after you. "I have some."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_recruit_rasabhava:
A workshop cut into the rock: benches, glassware, a cold-vault, everything labelled in a small exact hand. On the central bench a vessel of clear liquid sits exactly where it was set down, beside a notebook open to a finished page.

The preserved one on the stool beside it inclines his head. "Mixed it the night before. You will notice the date."

"You would have been preserved," you say. "You would not have been finished."

He considers this for a long time — he is a careful man and does not accept propositions quickly. "An unfalsifiable consolation," he says at last. "But not, I think, a false one." He caps the vessel, labels it with the date and the word UNTESTED, and leaves it on the bench for whoever comes next.
Say the only useful thing there is to say about the timing
"A travelling practice." He is packing before you finish the sentence. The glassware is wrapped in eleven minutes; he has clearly rehearsed this.
Offer him a laboratory that moves

The formula is correct. You check it three times because you do not believe a formula for eternal preservation can be correct, and it is. He watches you check it, entirely composed, and you understand that he has been waiting a very long time for somebody who could tell whether it was right.

"It works," you say.

"It works," he agrees. "By eleven hours." And then, after a moment: "I should like to be somewhere else now."
"Take it. It is no use to me at this end." He watches it go with the mildest possible expression.
Ask whether you might have the vessel
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_restless_grave#te: The earth shifts. A hand pushes through the soil — five fingers, then a second hand. Something is clawing its way up from below. The ground heaves.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_restless_grave/di: You get both hands under the soil and heave. The earth gives. The rolang sits up, dazed and blinking. It looks at you for a long moment, then slowly nods. It will follow you.
Force the earth open with brute strength
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_restless_grave/he: It comes up snarling — whatever consciousness it had is buried under panic and hunger. It goes straight for you.

You haul it clear of the earth — a confused rolang, blinking in the grey light. It looks at its hands, then at you. Something surfaces in its eyes. Not a full mind, but enough. It stays close to your heel like a dog that's found someone.
Grab its hands and pull it free
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_restless_grave/la: You press your palm to the churning soil and recite the words. The hands slow, relax, and slip back into the earth. The ground settles. The air is lighter.
Perform last rites — put whatever's down there to rest
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_restless_grave/le: A low groan follows you from beneath the trembling ground. It fades as you move on. This realm is full of things trying to surface.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rolang_horde#text: The ground trembles. Over the ridge, a mass of rolangs shuffles forward — dozens, maybe hundreds. Not aggressive, just moving. A tide of the mindless dead flowing toward something far away, unfortunately seemingly unaware of a village lying directly in their path.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rolang_horde/foll: You trail them at a distance. Hours pass. They converge on a vast pit, an old mass grave, and begin to circle it in an endless loop. Something in the earth is pulling them home. You watch for a long time, learning more about this realm than you wanted to know.
Follow them — see where they're going
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rolang_horde/get_: You press yourself against a rock wall and wait. The tide takes ten minutes to pass. The village on the far side of the hill has no idea what's coming.
Get out of the way and let them pass
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rolang_horde/guid:
You work the edges of the horde with your spear horizontal, using reach and presence to deflect the outermost rolangs. The mindless dead respond to obstacle and pressure — they don't fight back, they just redirect. Your leverage at the flank shifts the whole column gradually, like guiding a slow river.

It takes two hours and the spear gets heavy. But the horde turns, and the village is no longer in its path.
Guide the horde with your spear — use reach to steer them
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rolang_horde/redi: You work the edges of the horde, using presence and sound to nudge the direction of hundreds of shuffling dead. It takes an hour and every ounce of focus you have. But the horde turns, flowing away from the village and into empty wasteland.
Herd them away from the village
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rotting_bridge#te:
The bridge is the only crossing for miles and it has been rotting for longer than that. Half the planks are gone; the rest are the colour of old cheese. Beneath it, the channel runs deep and black and busy.

Someone has scratched a warning into the post. The scratching is also rotten.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rotting_bridge/ba: Most of a day added to the journey and every member of the party privately relieved.
Not worth it — go the long way
