fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rotting_bridge/cr: The board does not creak first. One moment there is a bridge and the next there is black water and a great deal of movement in it.
Four crossings, four held breaths, one plank that goes into the water without you. Everyone across.
Cross one at a time, testing every board
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rotting_bridge/fo: Bridges exist where the crossing is hard. Two hundred paces upstream the channel spreads over a gravel bar and is thigh-deep and boring. You get wet to the hip and nothing tries to eat anyone.
Find where the channel shallows and ford it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_rotting_bridge/re: You cut and set new stringers, deck it in salvaged planks, and lash the whole thing to the surviving piles. It takes four hours and a quantity of scrap. When you finish, it is the only sound structure you have seen in this realm — and it will still be here for whoever comes next, which is a strange thing to care about in a place like this.
Rebuild the span properly before anyone sets foot on it
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacred_grove#text: A stand of ancient trees whose roots grow through charnel earth. The branches are hung with offerings of food — the hungry ghosts who press at the edge of the grove can smell them but cannot eat. Practitioners move among the roots, speaking to both the living and the dead.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacred_grove/#0#r: One of the practitioners turns. She names what can be taught here, and then the price. Gold is gold in every realm.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacred_grove/#1#r: You walk on. The smell of offerings follows you through the trees.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacrifice_post#te: A wooden post driven into the mud, hung with trinkets, cloth strips, dried flowers. The offerings are from multiple eras — some ancient, some recent. Whatever this appeases, it is still being appeased.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacrifice_post/id: Folk magic doesn't always leave notes. You make a small offering anyway.
You piece it together from the nature of the offerings. The swamp has teeth, and this is how the locals have been keeping them dull.
Try to identify what this protects against
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacrifice_post/sm: Add something small to the post
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sacrifice_post/ta: They're not yours to take, but they're functional.
Take several of the more potent-looking charms
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shadow_market#tex: A market that appears only between the grave stones, visible only to those who know how to look. The stalls are draped in dark cloth and the merchants keep their faces in shadow. Everything here was obtained quietly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shadow_market/#0#: A shadowed hand gestures you deeper into the market. No questions asked, no names given.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shadow_market/#1#: You step back. The market seems to thin and vanish between blinks.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shadow_peddler#te: A hunched figure steps from behind a grave marker, face obscured beneath a ragged hood. Its voice is barely a whisper but its goods are real enough — things it has acquired in ways it declines to explain.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shadow_peddler/#0: The figure spreads its goods on the grave stone between you. It wants food more than gold.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shadow_peddler/#1: You walk past without stopping. The figure watches you go, then is gone.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush#text: A shaza pack has been tracking you — body-snatching predators that crave living flesh above all else. You spot them circling at the same moment they realize you've noticed. The circling tightens.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/clim: Not fast enough. They hit you from behind as you climb.
You scramble up a bone-pile before they close the distance. From up here you're outside their preferred engagement range. They mill about below, and eventually give up.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/pick:
You wait for the lead shaza to enter knife range, drop it cleanly, and move through the pack targeting vital points. The rest of them scatter when they realize what's happening — they hunt in groups because they have to, and a group suddenly three smaller is no longer a group with confidence.

You walk on. The survivors do not follow.
Pick off the hunters as they close — surgical precision
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/play: They're not fooled. And they go for you first because you're already on the ground.
You go down convincingly and stay down. They sniff around you, confused. Their hunger is for living flesh — and yours, for the moment, doesn't smell like it. They drift on.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/set_: You choose your ground carefully, then let them come to you on your terms.
Lure them into a kill zone
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/syst: You back up to maintain distance and start shooting — not panicked, but methodical, picking the ones moving to flank first. The shaza are confident close-in hunters and terrible at range. You stay outside their distance and well within yours. They figure this out on the third volley and decide you are not worth the cost.
Keep them at range — shoot them down before they close
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/vent: You produce a small doll from your pack and throw your voice into it, sending the shaza into baffled circles trying to locate the sound. While they mill in confusion, you walk briskly in the other direction.
Confuse them with a quick act of ventriloquism
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_shaza_ambush/war_:
You picked it up two hundred paces back — not a sound, a shape of silence in the wrong place — and you have spent the walk since arranging where everyone is standing.

When it comes, it comes into a formation rather than a column.
You heard them a while ago. You have been waiting.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sigh_of_relief#te: A small cairn with a folded cloth on top. Written in a careful hand: "You are not as lost as you feel."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sigh_of_relief/re: You are not as lost as you feel.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_singing_skull#tex: A skull sits atop a cairn of stones, humming a melody. When you approach, its jaw opens wider: "Oh! A listener! I used to be a bard, you know. Died mid-song. Very embarrassing. Would you like to hear how it ends?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_singing_skull/ask: "Mid-performance. Big crowd. I was just getting to the good bit." A pause. "I've had time to work out whether it was tragic or funny. I've decided it was both."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_singing_skull/car: The skull goes very still. Then: "You're serious." Then: "YES." It settles into your pack with enormous dignity, humming quietly. Its commentary on your journey turns out to be worth hearing.
Offer to carry it to an audience
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_singing_skull/lis: It's actually beautiful. The skull has had a long time to get the ending right. Something about the melody lingers with you long after you leave.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_singing_skull/sin: Off-key. The skull is politely disappointed but thanks you for trying. "Not everyone has it. That's what makes it special."

You find the harmony. The skull stops mid-phrase and stares. "Oh," it says softly. "Oh, that's exactly it. That's exactly what was missing." The duet locks together and the song completes. Something resonates.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_singing_skull/sto:
You give it something long with a good middle, and it listens the whole way through without humming over you, which for a skull on a cairn is close to reverence.

What it gives back is not a song. It is directions, sung, and they are accurate.
It has a song. Trade it one.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_army#tex:
They are drawn up in ranks across the whole width of the dry valley, and they are not moving. Rank on rank of skeleton infantry in the armour of an army that lost — you can tell it lost, because it is all still here.

They are facing an enemy that is no longer present. They have been facing it for a very long time.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_army/com:
You walk down the middle at an even pace with your hands where they can be seen, and you do not speed up at any point, including the point at which the second rank turns its head.

They close behind you. Nothing else happens.
Ranks do not attack what walks through them like it belongs.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_army/dis: You walk to the front, face the ranks, and dismiss them — properly, with the form and the cadence, the way it is done at the end of a campaign. It takes a moment. Then ten thousand skeletons ground their arms in one enormous rattling crash and the formation simply ceases to be a formation. Some of them sit down. Most of them come apart. What is left is a valley full of bones and a great deal of abandoned equipment.
Give the order to stand down
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_army/rea: The line is anchored on high ground at both ends and refused on the left — a textbook defensive deployment against cavalry that would have come from the north. There is no north army. There has not been for centuries. But there is a supply train behind the line, unlooted, because nobody has ever gotten past the ranks to it.
Work out what they are still facing
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_army/ski: Two hours of picking along the valley wall while ten thousand skulls face resolutely the other way. Not one of them turns.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_army/thr: You are six ranks deep when the nearest one registers that something has entered the formation, and the correction ripples outward.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king#tex:
A city of bone — towers of fused ribcages, walls of skulls, gates of pelvis and shoulder blade. On a throne of vertebrae sits the Skeleton King, crowned with a circlet of hammered copper. His eye sockets burn with cold intelligence. Rings of copper, gold, and ruby decorate his fingers and exposed ribs.

"All the dead pass through my kingdom eventually."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king#tit: The Skeleton King of the Setting Sun
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king/bow: No shame in discretion. He watches you go with what might be respect.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king/cha: He rises from his throne for the first time in years. The court goes absolutely still. "Then let us see." The battle ends when he reaches ten percent — he stops it himself. "Enough. You have proven your right."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king/kne: He's amused. "Clear the infestation to the east and you may pass freely." Simple enough.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king/off: He listens with unexpected patience. What you offer is genuinely rare. He gives back something equally rare.

You set up the offering with care — the correct order, the correct words, nothing improvised. The Skeleton King watches every detail. When you finish, something in his bearing has shifted. He teaches you something from his own practice.
Offer a puja in his honor

"I am a poor traveler. But I will offer my only treasure — my voice." He leans back. The court goes still. You sing. When it's over, he reaches into his robes and extends a trinket and a small purse. "An unusual currency. But acceptable."
Offer a song of praise in lieu of tribute
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_king_her:
A copper skeleton in ceremonial armor — turquoise beads strung between its ribs, feathers wired to its shoulder plates — plants itself in the middle of the road. Its voice is enormous for its frame.

"His Ruby-like Majesty, the Skeleton King of the Setting Sun, demands tribute from all who traverse his domain. Pay, serve, or be added to the collection."

You produce a very official-looking nothing and speak with great certainty. The herald stares at the empty air where your credentials should be. "...very well. I shall note your passage as diplomatic in nature." You walk past with a straight face.

"I am a poor traveler, but I will offer my only treasure — my voice." The herald goes still as you begin. By the second verse, it has lowered its halberd. By the third, it has produced a small donation from its own coin pouch. "His Majesty would approve," it says. "Pass freely."
Offer a hymn of praise in lieu of gold
"A fighting force! The King can always use those." It leads you to a trouble spot — rolang incursion, needs clearing. You earn safe passage and the patrol's grudging respect.
Offer military service instead of tribute

The herald accepts the gold with practiced dignity. "For your patient compliance, receive a sparkle of the King's unceasing glow." It touches your brow with a copper finger. Something warm passes through you — and for the next few encounters, your words carry unusual weight.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_musician: A skeleton sits on a gravestone, playing a two-stringed instrument with surprising skill. The music is slow and strange and not entirely unpleasant. It stops when it notices you.
It makes no sound. But the jaw moves, and the ribcage shakes, and the instrument ends up upright and the musician hunched over it in a posture that can only be described as helpless.
It watches you go. When you're far enough away, the music resumes.
Your contribution is not musically interesting. The skeleton watches you politely until you stop.
It tilts its head at you, then picks up the tempo. You manage to follow. For a few minutes, in a graveyard in the hungry ghost realm, something like music happens.
Play along, or try to match the melody

You put words to what it is playing, roughly and out of metre, and it stops dead for the length of a breath before picking the line back up underneath your voice.

You get through four verses. It has not had a singer in a very long time.
It is playing a form. Give it words.
It tilts its head at you, then picks up the tempo to match your voice. For a few minutes, in a graveyard in the hungry ghost realm, something like music happens.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_patrol#t: Four skeletons in mismatched armor march in tight formation down a grey road. Their sergeant — distinguishable only by a dented helmet someone has polished to a painful shine — holds up a bony hand. "Halt. State your business in the King's domain."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_patrol/c: The sergeant's empty sockets narrow. "We have no record of any emissary today. Seize them."

You speak with sufficient authority and sufficient vagueness. The sergeant salutes. "Very well. The King's emissaries have right of passage." You are escorted, somewhat against your will, all the way to the next waypoint.
Claim to be a royal emissary
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_patrol/s: "Traveler. Moving through." The sergeant looks you up and down. Nods. "Move through, then. Stay on the road." The patrol resumes its march.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_patrol/t: Merchants of standing move freely in the Skeleton King's domain. The sergeant examines your credentials with unexpected care, nods, and waves you on. "Nearest market town is north. The road is clear today."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_skeleton_patrol/y: "Don't try messing with my head, stranger."
The sergeant goes still. The others exchange glances. A long pause. "Go on your way, yogi." They step aside.
"Who truly knows their business in this world of dreams?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_smuggler_tunnel#t: A narrow tunnel entrance hidden behind a collapsed wall. Scratch marks on the stone suggest frequent use. From inside: voices, the clink of coin, the smell of something cooking.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_smuggler_tunnel/a: "A spy." They don't wait to find out.
A pause. Then: "Come in, then. Leave your paranoia at the door." Better prices for a customer who didn't sneak.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_smuggler_tunnel/o: You know the right words. They let you into the back room.
Present yourself as a potential partner
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_smuggler_tunnel/r: You find the nearest patrol and bring them back. The tunnel is raided. The Skeleton King's forces are grudgingly grateful.
Report them to the bone patrol
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_smuggler_tunnel/s:
They are a message, in the sense that anything kept from most people is a message to the rest.

You read it: a count, a direction, and a warning about the third turning. All three prove accurate.
Those scratches are not damage. They are a message.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sorcerer_of_corps:
He is working on a body laid out on a stone bench, and the work is precise — thread, needle, small silver instruments, a diagram weighted at the corners.

"Don't jog the table," he says without looking up. "I have been at this since the moon was somewhere else."

He accepts instantly and without surprise, which tells you how long it has been since he had help. Four hours of surgery on a corpse, conducted with total professional courtesy in a place that smells the way this place smells. What he is building turns out to be a body for a friend who lost theirs. He pays you in reagents and technique.
Whatever he is making, stop him making it

It is a binding, and it is beautiful work, and it is also — you check twice — inverted at the third node, which means when he finishes, the thing on the table will not be bound to him. It will be bound to nobody, and it will be very strong. You point at the node. There is a long silence while he traces it himself. Then he sits down heavily on the floor and says a word you have not heard before.
Read the diagram he is working from
The needle goes in and out. He does not notice you go.
Do not jog the table. Leave.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_fire#text: Three fires burn without fuel at the edge of the charnel grounds. One is pale blue, one is deep green, one is a colour that doesn't have a name. None of them give off heat.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_fire/eleme: Three elements, one process. You spend time with each one, and each one teaches you something.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_fire/study: The nameless-coloured one flares. The heat is not physical. You step back.
Each one is a distinct consciousness, in the earliest stage of what might become a ghost or might become something else. You learn something from how they burn.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_fire/walk_: They seem to watch you go — or seem to.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns#t: A line of ghostly lanterns floats through the darkness, each carried by an invisible hand. They move with purpose — a funeral procession of pure spirit, honoring someone important who died long ago. The procession repeats every night, endlessly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/b: The pattern resists you. The procession blurs and stutters for a moment, then resumes its course as if nothing happened.
You reach into the pattern of it and find where the loop closes. You open it. The lanterns flicker, then go still. The procession ends — truly ends. The darkness is darker for a moment, then easier.
Try to end the eternal repetition
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/i:
The enchantment is a grief-loop — a mourning spell that has outlasted its caster by centuries, still running because no one cancelled it. The procession is real; the love in it is real. It just doesn't know it's allowed to stop.

You cannot dissolve it with enchantment alone, but now you understand its structure. The next person who walks beside these lanterns might be able to give it the permission it's been missing.
Study the enchantment — understand what drives the loop
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/j: A lantern drifts into your hands. As you carry it, visions come — fragments of the honored dead's life, their work, their love for whatever is being mourned here. The procession ends at a marker stone. The lanterns settle. A long peace.
Join the procession — carry a lantern
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/l:
You always are. It means you see the procession from its first lantern to its last, which nobody else in the party does, and you count them.

The number matters later.
You were awake before the light reached the camp.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/n:
Everyone else is asleep or nearly. You are at your best, and you fall in at the back of the procession and walk with it for a mile before it notices you.

When it notices, it does not object. It makes room.
It is the middle of the night and you are wide awake.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/s: The invisible hand does not let go. What was carrying the lantern turns its attention to you.
The lantern comes away in your hands, warm and surprisingly heavy.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_spirit_lanterns/w: You fall into step with the procession. The light is warm despite the cold. Something solemn and beautiful moves through you with it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta#te:
An emaciated figure blocks the path — belly swollen like a gourd, throat thin as a reed. Its hands are skeletal claws reaching toward you. The voice that comes out is barely a whisper.

"Please. Anything. I haven't eaten in — I can't remember how long. Please."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta/at: Cut it down — put it out of its misery
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta/ge:
It is not enough. Nothing would be — the throat is a needle and the belly is a room.

But it stops, for a moment, being a thing that is starving and becomes a thing that is being fed, and it looks at you differently for the length of that moment.
Give it something. It will not be enough and give it anyway.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta/gi: The food dissolves the moment it touches its lips, transformed to ash by the curse it carries. But it weeps, grateful for the gesture. "You... tried. That's more than most."

"There is no meal that ends hunger. There is no object that ends want. The relief you seek cannot be found in a bowl." The preta goes still. Its eyes, desperate a moment ago, grow strangely clear. It doesn't answer. But something in its posture changes.
Teach it about the nature of craving
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta/me: You recognize the curse of the hungry ghost — every craving fed only deepens the hunger. You describe this to the creature gently, guiding it to eat slowly, deliberately. It seems to find some fragile relief in understanding its own condition.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta/sc:
The answer is: nothing will, so the correct expenditure is the smallest amount that buys passage.

You are right. You are right in a way that sits badly on the walk afterwards, and the party does not discuss it.
Work out exactly how little will satisfy it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_starving_preta/tu: The whisper fades behind you. You tell yourself it's not your problem. The realm of hungry ghosts is full of such creatures. You can't save them all.
Turn your eyes away and walk past
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sunken_village#te:
Roof-ridges break the water in rows. A whole village went under here and did not go anywhere else — the water simply arrived and stayed, and the village kept its shape beneath it.

In the shallows at the edge, a cooking pot sits on its stones, upright, full of black water.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sunken_village/de: Something in the rafters is not a rafter, and it has been waiting in the dark of that room for a very long time.
Three dives. The third one gets the box out of the rafters where somebody put it when the water was already at the door.
Dive the headman's house at the centre
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sunken_village/le: The roof-ridges are still visible a long way down the road, whenever you look back.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sunken_village/ri: You stand in the shallows and name the village — you do not know its name, so you name it by what it was: a place where people cooked and argued and slept. The water does not change. But when you go through the houses afterwards nothing objects, and in the headman's rafters you find what was hidden there, and it comes away easily.
Say the water-rites over the whole village
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_sunken_village/sa: Waist-deep through what used to be doorways. Cookware, tools, a strongbox nobody had time for.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing#te: A wide stretch of black, stinking water blocks the path. Shapes move beneath the surface — too large to be debris, too slow to be fish. The only bridge is half-rotted wood on crumbling stone. It might hold. Might.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing/fi: There — a line of flat stones barely visible below the surface, an old ford hidden by the murk. You pick your way across with dry boots.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing/fr:
You are not. You make it across and you make it across badly, and you spend the next day with something in your lungs that should not be in them.

The party slows for you, which you would rather they did not.
Black water to the chest, and you are not built for this.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing/st:
You go in with the line and the current is exactly as bad as it looks and you stand in it anyway while everyone else comes over hand by hand.

Your legs are unhappy for a day. Nobody else gets wet above the waist.
Take the rope across first. You are the one who can.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing/sw: Within three strokes something grabs your ankle.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing/us: The board snaps. You go in. The water is cold and thick as tar — and something in it is already moving toward you.
You move fast and light, skipping over the worst boards. The bridge shudders but holds. On the far bank, you look back — a plank falls into the water the moment your foot leaves it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_crossing/wa: You take the damage. The water burns where it touches skin, and something bumps against your leg in the darkness. You push through on will alone and drag yourself up the far bank, filthy and hurting. But through.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_hermit#text: Deep in the swamp, a rolang sits on a rock, fishing in toxic water with a line made of hair. It's the most peaceful undead you've ever seen. It has achieved something rare here — contentment.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_hermit/ask_: It doesn't look up from the water. "I stopped wanting." A long pause. "That's it. That's all there is."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_hermit/dist: You consider it. Then the thought seems so ridiculous — there is so little peace in this realm and so much to disturb — that you simply leave. The faintest hint of hell clings to the idea.
Disturb its peace — just to see
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_hermit/offe: It shakes its head gently. "I have everything I need." It gestures at the toxic water, the dead fish, the grey sky. It means it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_hermit/sit_: You sit in silence for a long time. Nothing bites. It doesn't seem to matter to either of you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_spirit#text: A translucent figure stands ankle-deep in still water across a narrow channel. It watches you with the expression of someone who has forgotten where they were going.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_spirit/offe: You know the practice for this. It takes most of an hour. The spirit becomes more present, then less, then gone — in the right direction.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_spirit/spea: It stares at you for a long moment, then sinks slowly into the water. You're not sure what you said wrong.
It doesn't answer in words, but something shifts. It presses a cold hand briefly to your forehead, then walks away into the mist.
Speak to it gently — ask if it needs help
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_spirit/wave: It raises a hand in response. You don't look back.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_toll#text:
The causeway is the only dry ground for a mile, and four bog zombies stand across it in a row. They are not shambling. They are *waiting* — arranged, deliberate, with the stillness of a posted guard.

One of them holds out a swollen hand, palm up. It has been taught to do this.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_toll/counte: You press a flat river stone into the swollen palm with great ceremony. The fingers close on it. Whatever instruction these four are running does not include an assay step. They step aside. You cross the causeway feeling both clever and slightly cheap.
Pay with something that is not money
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_toll/pay#re: The fingers close. The four of them step aside in unison and resume waiting, facing the way you came. Somewhere in this swamp is whoever trained them, and you find you would rather not meet them.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_toll/scrimp:
You establish, at length, that the causeway is not theirs, that no work has been done to maintain it, and that the toll has no basis of any kind.

The zombies are not equipped for this argument. Two of them wander off during it.
Four zombies and a causeway. Do the arithmetic out loud.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_toll/who_ta: The zombies are facing the causeway, but their heels are aligned to a stand of dead willow forty paces off. There is a rolang in it, very old, very still, running a toll booth in a swamp with four corpses and infinite patience. You negotiate directly. It turns out to be reasonable, and lonely, and it waives the fee for conversation.
Follow the training back to whoever set this up
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_warden#text:
The only dry crossing through the wall of thorn and mire is watched. A rolang ancient stands waist-deep in the black water, preserved by centuries of swamp tannin, carrion worms moving beneath its skin like slow thoughts.

It raises one dripping arm and points — not at you, but at the toll stone beside the path, hollowed like a begging bowl.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_warden/figh: Cut it down and force the crossing
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_warden/last: You speak the old words and the warden goes very still. The worms leave it, one by one, sliding into the water. What remains is only a dead man, finally allowed to be dead, toppling softly into the reeds. The crossing is yours.
Perform the rites that should have been spoken over this corpse
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_warden/toll: The worms boil out of the warden's body to swarm the offering. While the ancient stands hollowed and swaying, you walk the causeway unopposed.
Fill the toll stone with food and pass
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_swamp_warden/wade: The mud holds you fast — and the warden comes wading.
Chest-deep in rot, leeches at your ankles, you haul yourselves through the mire and up the far bank, shaking but past.
Wade through the deep mire, out of its reach
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_charnel#: A lantern glows faintly above a low doorway carved into a wall of stacked bone. Inside, a quiet figure brews tea from dried flowers that grow only on graves. The dead do not drink, but the living are welcome.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_charnel/: The figure pours without looking up. You can rest here — if you can afford it.
You leave the lantern light behind. The scent of grave-flowers follows you a while.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_event#te: In an impossible pocket of warmth among the grey wastes, a skeletal figure in fine robes serves tea to the dead. The smell is real — jasmine and wood smoke, somehow surviving in this realm. Dead patrons sit quietly at low tables. A hand-painted sign above the door reads: ALL ARE WELCOME. PAYMENT EXPECTED.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_event/as: The teamaster pours without looking up. "The one by the window was a judge. That one a merchant. The two arguing in the corner have been arguing about a land dispute for two hundred years. The tea helps. Not much, but some."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_event/he: You spend an hour moving through the tables, refilling cups with the careful attention the work demands. The teamaster watches you from across the room. At the end, it sets before you a full meal and refuses payment. "Well done," is all it says.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_event/pe: Silence. Then an awkward clicking of bones. The teamaster sets a cup of tea gently in front of you. "Sit," they say. "Drink. We all have bad days."

The dead crowd goes quiet as you begin. Then something stirs in them — the memory of being moved by something beautiful. Coins appear on tables. The teamaster nods at you with something like approval.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_event/te:
There is, and you do it — the whole form, in a bone teahouse at the edge of the grey.

The skeleton proprietor watches every movement. When you finish it turns the cup over, which you understand at once to mean that the house will not be serving anyone else today.
There is a right way to take a last cup.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_graveyar: A small dwelling built into the side of an old burial mound, its entrance marked with a hanging lantern and a painted sign no longer legible. Someone has been serving tea here for a very long time.
The host gestures to a low table. The tea is bitter and dark. You can rest here — if you can afford it.
You leave the mound behind. The lantern swings in a wind you can't feel.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_swamp#te: A teahouse built on stilts above the swamp water, its light the only warmth for miles. A rope bridge leads to the door. Someone is already watching you from the window.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_swamp/#0: The host sets a cup on the table before you sit. You can rest here — if you can afford it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_teahouse_swamp/#1: You leave the light behind. The swamp closes around you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_temple_of_the_nag: A low temple built around a black-water pool. The nagas who dwell in such pools are guardians of the dead, and their human followers leave milk offerings at the water's edge. A practitioner sits cross-legged on the stone, eyes closed, lips moving.
The practitioner opens her eyes. She names the spells the nagas have permitted to be taught here, and the price. It is not cheap.
You leave the offerings undisturbed. The pool surface ripples once as you go.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_toll_bridge#text: Two massive skeletons in heavy armor flank a stone bridge. A sign lists prices that escalate from the merely unreasonable to the openly delusional. The skeletons seem bored.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_toll_bridge/comed: You hit something genuinely funny. One skeleton laughs so hard it falls apart at the waist, and is still clicking on the ground when you walk past.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_toll_bridge/debto:
There is a clause. There is always a clause, and you have spent enough of your life on the wrong side of one to find it inside a minute.

The toll applies to the living. Two of your party, on a technicality that the skeletons accept with visible irritation, are not paying it.
Read the sign properly. Signs like this always have a clause.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_toll_bridge/haggl: They hold the line. The price goes up.
You work down through the price list methodically. They concede ground slowly, then all at once.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_toll_bridge/logis: You explain, briefly and with specific examples, why their pricing model is destroying long-term traffic revenue and creating a structural deficit. The skeletons stand very still for a long time. You walk past during this.
Point out the economic flaws in the toll structure
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_toll_bridge/pay#r: They accept the coins without enthusiasm and step aside. Professional.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_event#text: A settlement of the dead — bone-walled buildings, skeleton merchants, ghostly lanterns in permanent vigil. It functions. That's the remarkable thing. Guards at the gate eye you without hostility. "Weapons peace inside the walls. Break it and we break you, warmie."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_event/look_f: You spend a few hours moving crates for a bone merchant, delivering a message for a skeleton official who turns out to be three levels underground, and locating a mislaid femur for a very upset skeleton. You are paid in coin and the particular satisfaction of a task well done.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_event/sing_i: The dead gather slowly at first, then in numbers. They stand very still in the way that means they are listening hard. When you finish, coins appear on the ground before you — more than you expected. A skeleton merchant nearby leans over: "Come back. You're good for business."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_event/teach_: Nobody likes an uninvited preacher. The locals glance at you, then go back to their business. A skeleton child — or at least, a small skeleton — throws a pebble at you. You pack up.

The locals circle slowly, then stop. A crowd of skulls tips attentively as you speak. These beings know more about impermanence than most — and something in your framing reaches them. Offerings appear when you finish: food, a small pouch of coin, a health potion pressed into your hands by a skeleton with no face left to show its expression.
Set up at the shrine and teach about impermanence
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_magic#text: A settlement where more windows glow than can be explained by candlelight. Strange smells drift from the apothecary. A practitioner argues with a vetala outside the library, and neither seems to have the better of it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_magic/#0#res: You find the market square. The odd merchants eye you with professional interest.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_magic/#1#res: You leave the scholars to their arguments. The strange lights fade behind you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_supplies#tex: A trading post built among the graves, supplies scavenged from the dead and traded among the half-living. The market is quiet but well-stocked — necessity makes practical merchants of everyone here.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_supplies/#0#: You push through to the market. Traders call out their wares in dry, patient voices.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_supplies/#1#: You skirt the settlement and keep moving.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_weapons#text: A fortified compound where warriors trade blades and bones. The biggest building is an armory. Someone is always sharpening something, and the sound of whetstones never stops.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_weapons/#0#r: You push through the gate. The armorer looks up from their work.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_town_weapons/#1#r: You skirt the compound and keep moving.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_turquoise_dancers:
A troupe of turquoise skeletons in rainbow skirts and flower headdresses dances in a circle, rattling and clacking in joyful rhythm. They notice you and beckon.

"Dance with us! What is the use of worrying here?"
The nearest dancer stops and looks at you with an expression that somehow works without a face. "Why don't you?"

You are terrible at it. This turns out to be entirely beside the point — the troupe's delight is not in the standard of the dancing but in the fact of somebody dancing.

You come away with flowers in your hair and, for some hours, the inability to be gloomy about the hungry ghost realm.
They are enjoying themselves. Join in.

You throw yourself in completely — dancing, mugging, making art of your own clumsiness. The troupe loves every second of it. When you finally stop, breathless, they press a trinket into your hands with both skeletal fists.
Join them fully — dance and make them laugh
You trip over your own feet. The dancers catch you, clacking with laughter. They dance around your embarrassment until it becomes part of the performance.
You find the rhythm and it carries you. When the song ends, a turquoise hand presses something into yours — a trinket worn smooth by dancing fingers.
The dance transforms around your music. Skeleton audience members appear from nowhere, clacking appreciatively. Coins rain down.
They wave goodbye with genuine warmth. The music follows you for a while.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_undead_caravan#te:
A line of skeletons carrying bundles marches along a dusty road. Pack animals made of bone and binding-wire bear crates of indeterminate goods. A skeleton with an extravagant feathered hat rides at the front on a skeletal horse.

"Traders of the dead! We go between the cities of this realm and ask no questions of the living. Care to travel with us for a stretch?"
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_undead_caravan/am: The feathered hat turns. The guards reach for weapons. The trading life has made them careful.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_undead_caravan/gu: The hat bobs appreciatively. "A living fighter! Excellent — rolang packs have been troublesome this season." Three miles on, the packs appear. You earn your pay.
Offer your services as a guard
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_undead_caravan/tr: Safe company across a bleak stretch of road. The caravan guards watch the wasteland for threats. The feathered hat bobs ahead. You part ways at a crossroads.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_arena#text:
A pit, ringed by tiered seating cut from bone, and it is full — several hundred vetala in their finery, watching two of their own tear at each other on the sand below for entertainment.

The crowd notices you at the entrance tunnel. A chant starts. It is not a friendly chant, but it is unmistakably an invitation.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_arena/book: There is always a bookmaker. His odds are set for a crowd that bets on style rather than outcome, which means the outcome is badly mispriced, which means an afternoon's careful work at the rail is worth more than any purse from the sand. You leave rich and entirely uninjured, which nobody in this building considers a victory except you.
Find the bookmaker instead of the sand
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_arena/figh: The crowd noise when a living thing steps onto the sand is something you will hear in your sleep.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_arena/leav: The chant follows you up the tunnel and turns to booing, which is somehow more humiliating than being chased.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_arena/stop: You go down and get between them, which is insane, and then talk — not to the fighters, who are past hearing, but to the crowd, about how much more interesting it would be if they *didn't*. It takes everything you have. The crowd, which above all fears being bored, decides that this is the novel thing and stops the fight itself. The two on the sand look at each other, baffled, and are led away by friends.
Get the two on the sand to stop
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_bargain#te:
It is sitting on a wall, swinging its heels, and it has clearly been waiting for someone specifically your size.

"A trade," it says. "Your body for a day and a night. I have errands. You get everything I know — and I know a great deal — and I give it back exactly as I found it. I have never once failed to give it back."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_bargain/ac: You wake a day and a night later exactly where you lay down, with everything where you left it and a head full of somebody else's knowledge — genuinely useful, precisely as promised. Your hands smell faintly of smoke. Nobody in the party will tell you what they saw you doing, and you decide, on balance, not to press.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_bargain/oa:
It wants a promise. It does not much care what the promise is about — the value is in the breaking, later, when it can be collected on.

You recognise the shape because you have been on the other side of it, and you decline in terms it finds genuinely disappointing.
You know what it is going to ask for, because you have given it before.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_bargain/re: "Worth asking," it says, unoffended, and goes back to swinging its heels. "Someone always says yes eventually."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_bargain/se: "Returned. Every one." True, and not the answer. You keep asking, and eventually get the rest: returned, yes — but a body worn by a vetala for a day and a night is a body that has been *somewhere*, and the ones who said yes have all, without exception, come back a little easier to persuade the second time. It admits this freely. It considers it a feature.
Ask what happened to the ones who said yes
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_bargain/te: Four hours of hard bargaining. You get: a witness, a fixed return time, a prohibition on violence while wearing you, and the knowledge transferred up front. It agrees to all of it, with increasing respect, and then keeps every clause to the letter — because a vetala that breaks terms in front of a witness stops being able to make bargains, and bargains are what it eats.
Accept — but negotiate the terms first
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_court#text:
They have taken over what was once a hall and turned it into something between a salon and a slaughterhouse. Perhaps thirty vetala, beautifully dressed, holding a conversation of extraordinary wit across a floor that has not been cleaned in living memory.

The talk stops. Thirty faces turn with the same expression: delight.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_court/etiq: There is a protocol for a living guest and almost nobody alive has ever known it. You give the greeting, present the required token, and take the low seat without being told to. The effect is roughly that of a peasant walking into a royal audience and getting every bow right. They are charmed, scandalised, and obliged — the forms bind both ways, and now they cannot touch you.
Observe the forms of a vetala court exactly
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_court/figh: You are not going to talk your way out of thirty
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_court/join: The rule of the court, you work out fast, is that dullness is the only capital offence. You are interesting for two hours — genuinely, exhaustingly interesting — and at the end of it a vetala in green raises her glass and says, "We shall not eat this one," and the matter is settled by acclamation. They send you off with gifts and directions and an open invitation you will never use.
Take a seat and hold your own
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_court/with: The courtesy is so unexpected that it works. Somebody laughs; somebody else says "oh, let it go"; the conversation resumes behind you as though you had been a draught from an open door.
Bow, apologise for interrupting, and back out
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_elder#text:
Deep in the charnel grounds, where the bone-fires burn highest, you find her — a vetala so old her skin has turned to parchment, her eyes like oil lamps. She sits on a throne of piled corpses, surrounded by offerings brought by lesser vetalas.

"I have eaten the memories of ten thousand dead. Ask me anything. And remember — everything has a price."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_elder#titl: The Elder of the Charnel Grounds
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_elder/ask_: "Death is a trick of perception. There was never a separate, singular body that lived and then died. The minuscule creatures in your gut have not noticed any change." She pauses. "There was never a separate person. Nobody was born and nobody died."
Ask about the nature of death
She is quiet for a long time. Then: "Who will be liberated? From where? To where?" Another pause. "Keep dreaming, child. As long as you want."

She smiles for the first time. "Now that is the honest question." She names a price: something permanent, something significant, and something that will follow you across lives. Whether the exchange is worth it is entirely up to you.
"All worlds are the same. They arise out of the potential of the void, driven by the expectations of sentient beings. Here, you see a world of thirst. A Buddha sees a garden ripe with possibility."
Ask about the nature of the world
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_elder/atta: She does not look up. "I wondered when you'd try that." The court rises.
Strike while her attention is elsewhere
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_elder/offe: She goes still as you speak. Something behind the oil-lamp eyes flickers — surprise, perhaps, or something that was once longing. "I have not tasted a living memory in centuries." She gives you something in return that only she could give.
Offer her a memory from the living world
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_riddler#te:
A vetala hangs upside-down from a dead tree by its knees, grinning. Its arms are folded. It seems completely comfortable.

"Answer my riddle, traveler, and I'll let you pass with a gift. Fail, and I take something of yours."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_riddler/ac: You guess wrong. The vetala drops to the ground with a long, satisfied smile. "Mine, I think." Your coin purse is lighter when you walk away.

"What is it — a shoal of silver fish jumps up and down in a blue net?" You think. Then: "The stars in the night sky." The vetala blinks, rights itself, and drops to the ground. "Hm. Correct. I haven't heard that from someone in decades." It tosses you something valuable.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_riddler/co: You pose a riddle back at it. The vetala's grin falters. It answers wrong. You collect the reward twice over — once for accepting the challenge, once for winning it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_riddler/cu:
You are, and the vetala can tell, and it is so pleased to have a genuine participant that it gives you the second riddle for free.

You get one of the two. It considers this a good afternoon's work for both of you.
A riddle. Obviously you are going to try the riddle.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_riddler/fo:
You heard the riddle and it has gone, entirely, in the time it took to start thinking about it.

The vetala repeats it once, with visible enjoyment, and then declines to repeat it again.
It said the riddle. You heard the riddle.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_riddler/tr: The vetala's smile disappears. It drops to the ground and three more drop from the branches. "Let's try a different game."
While the vetala is busy posing dramatically, you've already located the cache behind the tree roots and lifted it. You wave cheerfully as you leave. The vetala is still explaining the rules.
Try to steal its treasure without engaging the riddle at all
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_trickster#:
"Thank the gods, another living soul! This place is absolutely horrible! I've been lost for days — do you know the way to the eastern road?"

The smile is wrong. Too many teeth. Held a fraction too long.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_vetala_trickster/:
You compliment it extensively on its meatsuit. You ask about the tailor. You admire the not-quite-living-flesh color — very fashionable this season. You wonder aloud if it ever gets the seams adjusted.

The vetala laughs until it has to sit down. When it recovers, it presses a ring into your hand. "That's the funniest thing I've been subjected to in forty years. You're terrible. Here."
Turn the whole thing into a bit
Your counter-play is good but not quite good enough. The smile widens into something real and dangerous.

You match its performance beat for beat, leading it along a route that ends with its own ambush companions confused and its stash located and emptied. It stares at you. "I... you..." A long pause. "I respect that enormously."
It leads you cheerfully around a corner, down a path, through a narrow gap — and straight into three of its friends. The smile is back. "I DID say thank the gods."

"You're a vetala." A pause. Then it laughs — genuine, delighted, not the performance from before. "Oh, finally. You have no idea how boring this is when no one notices." It drops the pretense entirely and offers you a trade. Something real, as a reward for paying attention.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_veterans_camp#tex: A camp of battle-scarred fighters who never left the ghost realm. Their fire has been burning since they arrived — they stopped counting how long ago. They still trade in the tools of their old trade.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_veterans_camp/#0#: A veteran looks up from the fire. Old fighters make fair merchants — they know what things are worth.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_veterans_camp/#1#: You leave the veterans to their fire. It will still be burning when you pass this way again.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_veterans_camp_eve:
A fortified camp — real fortifications, not the improvised sort. These undead soldiers maintain discipline, run drills, keep watch rotations. A grizzled skeleton missing half its ribcage sits by the fire cleaning a weapon it will probably never use again.

"We remember what we were. That's more than most here can say."
You lose solidly. The camp watches in respectful silence. The grizzled skeleton helps you up. "Come back when you're ready."
You win. Narrowly. The grizzled skeleton nods once — the highest praise available in this camp — and hands you a weapon from its own collection.

You study the camp's layout and defensive positioning before saying anything. Then you lay out a redeployment — one that accounts for the patterns you've observed in this realm, the cover the terrain offers, the direction of the usual threats.

The grizzled skeleton is quiet for a long time.

'Show me on the map.'

You work together for an hour. Their defensive position improves considerably. They give you something from the supply cache in recognition — not payment, but acknowledgment.
Assert field command — suggest a redeployment

They gather around you. You tell them about roads and cities and the way the light looks in the morning. They listen with the complete attention of beings who have been starved of new information for a very long time.
Share news from the living world
They train you the way they trained soldiers — without ceremony, without encouragement, with complete focus. You come out of it tired and considerably more capable.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wailing_well#text: A stone well stands alone in a dead field. No village, no path to it — it was simply placed here and has been here a long time. Wailing rises from its depths. Not wind. Voices, dozens of them, calling from somewhere far below. Something glints at the bottom.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wailing_well/list: You close your eyes and let the wailing wash over you. Under it — patterns, repetitions. These aren't screams of pain. They're warnings. Specific ones, about specific places in this realm. You listen until you have what you need.
Be very still and listen to the voices
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wailing_well/lowe: The rope slips at the worst moment. You take the fall hard on cold stone and have to drag yourself back up, bruised and empty-handed.
Hand over hand in the dark, the voices growing louder. Your feet touch the bottom — wet stone, a narrow chamber. And there: a cache, sealed in oilcloth. Someone threw it in a long time ago.
Lower yourself down on a rope
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wailing_well/seal: You bring stone up from below and cap the well properly. The voices stop with finality. Something is over.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wailing_well/sing: You add your voice to theirs — not mocking, but joining. For a moment the dissonance is jarring. Then something shifts. The voices find a new shape around yours, a resolution they hadn't been able to reach alone. One by one, they stop. The field is quiet.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wailing_well/thro: Coins fall into the dark. The wailing pauses — as if something has been surprised. Then, slowly, it stills. The field is quiet for the first time in what feels like a long age.
Throw an offering into the depths
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wandering_monk#te:
A skeleton in saffron robes sits in perfect lotus position on a flat stone. Prayer beads still wrapped around its bony fingers. Intact, somehow — no rot, no damage, as if it simply sat down and stopped one day.

As you approach, its jaw opens: "I have been waiting. Not for you specifically. Just... waiting."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wandering_monk/as: "This realm is the shape of want," it says. "Every being here is caught in the moment they decided their craving was more important than everything else. They are still in that moment. They will be until they aren't." It resumes its stillness.
Ask about the hungry ghost realm
It accepts the coin without looking at it and begins. The teaching is brief, precise, and aimed exactly at something you've been struggling with. You aren't sure how it knew.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wandering_monk/me: You sit across from it in the grey dust. For a long time, neither of you speaks. Then the skeleton begins, in a voice like wind through empty rooms, to talk about impermanence — not as tragedy, but as relief. You listen. When you open your eyes, hours have passed and you feel lighter than you have in some time.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wandering_monk/st: "Well," the skeleton says softly, without opening its eyes, "what can I expect from beings in this realm if not demented hijinks like that?" It sounds more tired than angry. You retreat with your dignity in tatters.
Your hand moves. The beads slide free. The skeleton sits perfectly still. Maybe it didn't notice. Maybe it chose not to.
Take the prayer beads while it's distracted
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_wandering_preta_e:
A preta merchant dragging an enormous sack materializes from the grey. Despite being a hungry ghost, this one has channeled its craving into commerce with evident satisfaction.

"I can't eat, I can't drink, I can't sleep — but I CAN make a profit! Browse my wares?"

"The margins are incredible since I no longer need to eat into them." A pause. "That's a joke. I can still make jokes." It delivers a ten-minute monologue on the economics of not needing to sleep, eat, or maintain any quality of life while operating a commercial enterprise.
Ask what merchant life is like as a preta
A wheeze that might be laughter. "Oh, that one's good. That one's actually good." It waves you toward the sack. "Take what you want. I'll give you the suffering-colleague discount."
Make a joke about hunger for money
It stares at the food for a long time. Then at you. "Nobody has done that in... a long time." It waves you away. "Take ten percent off whatever you buy. Consider it a professional courtesy."
Offer it some of your food
It screams loud enough to be heard across the wasteland. Apparently it has regulars.
Fast hands, fast feet. You're gone before it counts its stock.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weary_pilgrim#tex:
A skeleton in a pilgrim's robe sits at the roadside with its staff across its knees, facing the direction it was going. Prayer-flags, long since bleached white, are tied to the staff head.

"Is it much further?" it asks. It does not say to where.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weary_pilgrim/pil:
It is not the walking. It is never the walking — it is the arithmetic of how much road is left against how much of you there is.

You sit down at the roadside with it and do not offer any encouragement, which is what it needed and what nobody else has managed.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weary_pilgrim/sit: Neither of you says anything for a long time. It is restful in a way very little in this realm is. When you stand up to go it lifts the staff an inch off its knees in farewell.
Sit down beside it for a while
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weary_pilgrim/wal: Six miles of shared road, in step, in silence, with a dead pilgrim who has been walking since before your language existed. Around the fourth mile you stop being someone accompanying it and start simply being on a pilgrimage, and the difference is not subtle. At the crossroads it goes one way and you go the other and both of you are, briefly, going somewhere.
Walk with it as far as you are going
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weary_pilgrim/whe: It cannot remember the destination, only the walking, and it is not distressed by this — it stopped needing the destination somewhere around the fourth century. "The road was the observance," it says. "I just liked to have somewhere to point it." It gives you its spare flags, which it has been carrying for no reason it can name.
Ask where the pilgrimage was going
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weary_pilgrim/yes: "Good," it says, and gets up, and sets off in the direction it was facing at a pace that suggests it believes you. You watch it go. You have no idea whether you told it the truth.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weeping_shrine#te: A small shrine on a mud-island, half-sunk. Water seeps continuously from the cracks in the stone — it has been weeping so long the ground beneath is stained dark.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weeping_shrine/me: Grief doesn't always explain itself. You sit with it anyway.
The grief becomes specific. A name, a cause, an old loss. Understanding doesn't fix it, but understanding tends to be useful.
Meditate on what the shrine mourns
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weeping_shrine/of: The shrine accepts. The weeping continues.
Make an offering and move on
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weeping_shrine/pi:
You wade out to it. This is unpleasant and takes some time and the party makes remarks.

What you find on the far side, above the waterline, is a carved instruction — brief, practical, and clearly meant for whoever cared enough to get that close.
It is half-sunk and it is still a shrine.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_weeping_shrine/pu: The weeping slows, then stops — for the first time in however long. The shrine feels lighter. So do you.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_whispering_bones#: Scattered bones on the ground begin to whisper as you pass. Each one holds a fragment of memory — a name, a regret, a last wish. The whispers grow louder the longer you stay.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_whispering_bones/: The whispers find the gaps in your concentration and settle in. Something heavy lingers in your mind.
You hold the silence inside yourself and walk through the noise. It doesn't touch you.
Block out the sound and push through

The ceremony takes an hour. You arrange the bones with care, speak the names as you collect them, give the fragments the dignity they were denied. The whispering quiets into something that might be gratitude.
You sit for a long time. The stories come in fragments — none complete, all real. You learn the names of people no one else remembers.
Sit and listen to all of them
As you speak each name, something answers. The bones whisper back differently — with direction, with purpose. There is something hidden nearby that they want you to find.
Speak their names aloud — give them voice
The bones rise. But whatever you called, it is not taking orders.
The bones rise and coalesce — dozens of fragments assembling into something massive. It looks at you with eyes made of hollow sockets and memory. Then, slowly, it kneels.
Call them back — all of them at once
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_will_o_wisp#text: A faint light dances ahead, moving just fast enough to stay out of reach. It has no face — just a glow, and an implied direction.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_will_o_wisp/follo: You step wrong. Bog, not ground. You pull yourself out soaked.
It leads you to a dry patch of ground, then vanishes. Something is buried just beneath the surface.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_will_o_wisp/let_d: You watch it go. It doesn't look back.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_will_o_wisp/recog: You know this pattern. A soul caught between awareness and dissolution. You speak the syllable that releases it. It brightens, briefly, then goes out.
Recognize it as a trapped spirit
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yidag_encounter#t:
A yidag — the truest form of the hungry ghost, belly swollen to bursting, throat thin as a needle — blocks the road. Not threateningly. It simply can't move. It wheezes:

"Please. Anything. Even a drop."
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yidag_encounter/a:
You sit down in front of it, which nobody does, and you do not offer it anything, which everybody does and which has never once worked.

What you offer instead is the observation that the wanting does not have to be obeyed. It is not cured. It is, for the first time in a very long while, spoken to.
You know what it is to want and not take.

A story of accumulated small greeds, none of them spectacular. It builds a picture of a life structured entirely around taking without giving — not evil, just narrow, for a very long time. The warning in the story is precise.
Ask how it came to this
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yidag_encounter/g: The water evaporates the moment it touches its throat. It weeps. You tried.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yidag_encounter/p: The suggestion that it could stop triggers something desperate. It attacks.

"There is nothing to drink here. There has never been anything to drink here. You can stop." It looks at you for a long time. Then, very slowly, it loosens its grip on existing. It dissolves, quietly.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yidag_encounter/w: You temporarily widen its throat — just enough. It drinks for the first time in centuries, slowly, with its eyes closed. When it opens them, they're wet in a way that has nothing to do with the water.
Use white magic to ease its suffering
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yogini_circle#tex: Sixty-four forms carved into standing bones form a perfect ring on the charnel ground. The earth inside is worn smooth by countless ritual footprints. A low humming comes from the center — women's voices, or something passing for them.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yogini_circle/#0#: One of the sisters turns. No words — a gesture toward the center of the ring. What do you need?
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_yogini_circle/#1#: You back away slowly. The humming follows you longer than it should.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_zombie_horde#text:
They come out of the reeds in ones and twos and then in dozens — bog zombies, waterlogged and patient, drawn by whatever it is the living give off that the dead can smell.

There is no line to hold. There is only the direction with fewest of them in it.
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_zombie_horde/fire: There is more methane over this bog than anyone should stand in. You touch it off from the far side and the whole flat goes up in a low blue sheet. The horde does not so much burn as simply stop, mid-step, and keep standing there while the fire takes them. You are well clear. You watch longer than you meant to.
Set the marsh gas alight behind you
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_zombie_horde/reed: Somebody's lungs give out. A head turns. Then all of them turn.

Face-down in black water breathing through a reed while a hundred waterlogged feet go past inches from your ribs. It takes forty minutes. Nobody coughs. That is the whole achievement and it is enormous.
Go low into the reeds and let them pass over you
fields.events:hungry_ghost:hg_zombie_horde/rele: Rolang are not animate by their own will — something keeps them walking, and it is thin here. You speak the release across the whole flat at once and the horde goes down in a long ragged wave, like a field of wheat. In the silence afterwards the swamp sounds almost ordinary.
Sever what is holding them upright
fields.items:acid_bomb#description: A corrosive splash that eats through armor.
fields.items:acid_flask#description: A flask of corrosive alchemical acid. Dissolves armor on impact.
fields.items:air_charm_common#description: A feather caught in a perpetual breeze. Reduces the mana cost of your next Air spell.
fields.items:air_charm_middling#description: A Garuda-feather charm tied with wind-knotted cord. The air around it never quite stills.
fields.items:air_charm_rare#description: A thunderstone from the peak of a holy mountain, smelling faintly of ozone.
fields.items:air_charm_unique#description: A lightning in a bottle, sealed safely with empowered silver wire.
fields.items:alchemists_pouch#description: A carefully prepared kit of distilled essences and reactive powders.
fields.items:amalaki#description: Dried Indian gooseberry — sour enough to water the eyes, rich in vital essence.
fields.items:apothecary_pouch#description: A leather pouch packed with carefully sorted remedies.
fields.items:ashwagandha#description: Withania root, dried and powdered. Steadies the humors under duress.
fields.items:backpack#description: More room for more things. Less room to move.
fields.items:barley_grain#description: A cloth pouch of raw barley. Needs cooking, but it keeps.
fields.items:black_charm_common#description: A bone token etched with dark sigils. Reduces the mana cost of your next Black magic spell.
fields.items:black_charm_middling#description: A tooth from a revenant, threaded on corpse-hair cord. It pulses faintly in dark places.
fields.items:black_charm_rare#description: A shard of a gyalpo sorcerer's magic mirror. Leaches light from nearby flames.
fields.items:black_charm_unique#description: A talismanic seal stripped from a dead rakshasa warlord. Heavier than it looks.
fields.items:blessed_air_ngakpa_crown#descripti: A light ornament of pale metal, worn low on the brow. Air practitioners note that it never seems to sit quite the same way twice.
fields.items:blessed_air_ngakpa_robe#descriptio: Green cotton, close-woven and lightweight. Air practitioners favor fewer layers and more movement. The color is said to invite the wind's attention.
fields.items:blessed_amethyst_mala#description: A hundred and eight beads of amethyst, worn smooth at the thumb. Counts the recitation so the mind need not.
fields.items:blessed_aquamarine_mala#descriptio: A hundred and eight beads of aquamarine, worn smooth at the thumb. Counts the recitation so the mind need not.
fields.items:blessed_black_mantra_hat#descripti: A black crown of lacquered bone and iron. The weight is real and the message is clear.
fields.items:blessed_black_mantra_robe#descript: Black wool heavily embroidered with bone-white thread, charnel ground symbols running hem to collar. Practitioners of the dark schools wear it as armor of a different kind — it communicates what you are before you have to prove it.
fields.items:blessed_bone_bead_mala#description: A hundred and eight beads of bone, worn smooth at the thumb. Counts the recitation so the mind need not.
fields.items:blessed_bone_damaru#description: A small double-headed drum shaken by a cord. Three spells cast while holding it and the rhythm reaches its peak — the next spell costs 40% less mana. Bone is the wrathful material — it has already been through death. Black magic practices find their anchor here naturally.
fields.items:blessed_bone_dorje#description: A ritual sceptre, the symbol of indestructible method. Weak as a weapon. In the right hand of a trained practitioner, it amplifies every spell cast. Bone is the wrathful material — it has already been through death. Black magic practices find their anchor here naturally.
fields.items:blessed_bone_drilbu#description: A ritual bell, held in the left hand. Its tone represents sunyata — emptiness. Rung in concert with the dorje, it opens the practitioner to a larger mana pool. Bone is the wrathful material — it has already been through death. Black magic practices find their anchor here naturally.
fields.items:blessed_bone_kangling#description: A thigh-bone trumpet. The sound calls what should not be called. Used in Chöd to offer the self — spend 25% of max mana to stack raw spellpower. When mana is gone, the cost comes from HP. Bone is the wrathful material — it has already been through death. Black magic practices find their anchor here naturally.
fields.items:blessed_bone_khatvanga#description: A trident staff topped with a skull, the emblem of wrathful practice. Enemies within melee range feel their composure — and initiative — erode. Bone is the wrathful material — it has already been through death. Black magic practices find their anchor here naturally.
fields.items:blessed_bone_melong#description: A disc of polished bone hung at the breast. It shows what approaches, and turns some of it away.
fields.items:blessed_bone_phurba#description: A three-bladed ritual dagger. The three blades cut through ignorance, attachment, and aversion. Can be used to physically strike, but its true power is thrown — a ranged attack that pins and subjugates. Bone is the wrathful material — it has already been through death. Black magic practices find their anchor here naturally.
fields.items:blessed_bronze_damaru#description: A small double-headed drum shaken by a cord. Three spells cast while holding it and the rhythm reaches its peak — the next spell costs 40% less mana. Bronze is a compromise — not the ideal metal for space-work, but workable. Practitioners who cannot find sky-iron use it and find it adequate.

fields.items:blessed_chodpa_eye_covering#descri: A blindfold of dark cloth. What is called does not need to be seen.
fields.items:blessed_chodpa_robe#description: The chodpa's robe, worn to the charnel ground and not washed after.
fields.items:blessed_citrine_mala#description: A hundred and eight beads of citrine, worn smooth at the thumb. Counts the recitation so the mind need not.
fields.items:blessed_conch_damaru#description: A small double-headed drum shaken by a cord. Three spells cast while holding it and the rhythm reaches its peak — the next spell costs 40% less mana. fields.items:blessed_dreamers_robe#description: Loose, and strangely quiet. Worn for the practices done while asleep.
fields.items:blessed_earth_ngakpa_crown#descrip: Gold-set amber, heavy, stable. Earth practitioners tend not to adjust it once it is on.
fields.items:blessed_earth_ngakpa_robe#descript: Yellow, the color of late-season grain and mountain clay. Earth practice is patient, and practitioners who favor earth magic tend to keep their robes in repair longer than most.
fields.items:blessed_fire_ngakpa_crown#descript: Copper ornament with a small flame-shaped finial. Warm to the touch even in cold, which practitioners find appropriate.
fields.items:blessed_fire_ngakpa_robe#descripti: Red with orange-bordered trim, the color of the hearth fire that is never fully extinguished. Fire tantra practitioners work with heat as both metaphor and fact. The robe holds warmth longer than the material seems to warrant.

Gold is earth's incorruptible face — abundance, permanence, and stability. Earth-working through gold tends to endure longer than the fight.

fields.items:blessed_healers_robe#description: White cotton with saffron-dyed borders and a medicine wheel embroidered at the hem. The sleeves roll back easily. Healers wear it not as display but as identification: you can call on this person.

fields.items:blessed_longlife_cap#description: A cap of long life. The wearer endures.
fields.items:blessed_pandita_cap#description: A tall brocade cap worn by scholars and translators, marking long years of study. The pandita tradition values accumulated learning over inspired guessing. So does this cap.
fields.items:blessed_pandita_robe#description: The scholar's robe. Debate is a kind of combat, and this is its armour.
fields.items:blessed_rosewood_mala#description: A hundred and eight beads of rosewood, worn smooth at the thumb. Counts the recitation so the mind need not.
fields.items:blessed_sages_robe#description: Plain and heavy. The sage mends and endures in equal measure.
fields.items:blessed_sandalwood_mala#descriptio: A hundred and eight beads of sandalwood, worn smooth at the thumb. Counts the recitation so the mind need not.
