fields.world:shop:animal_forest_training_camp#d: A gana training ground deep in the canopy — worn wooden practice posts, rope courses strung between trees, the smell of exertion and leaf-litter. The instructors are scarred veterans who have survived things that don't have names yet.
fields.world:shop:animal_garuda_roost#descripti: A great landing pole rises above the canopy, hung with wind-bells and sky-prayer flags. The Garudas who use it leave residual power in the ground below. Practitioners of air and space magic come here to feel the difference between flight and fall.
fields.world:shop:animal_healer_camp#descriptio: A canvas clinic strung between four trees, run by a grey-muzzled gana who does not hurry.
fields.world:shop:animal_hidden_gompa#descripti: A monastery that exists only insofar as the practice of its inhabitants sustains it. The walls are older than memory and the silence deeper than the forest. The practitioners here have been undisturbed for long enough that the ground itself has opinions.
fields.world:shop:animal_meadow_merchant#descri: An enormous cart drawn by a harnessed khadga, worked by a yaksha who has run this route for decades.
fields.world:shop:animal_meadow_teahouse#descri: A circular tent-structure at a major watering hole, serving travelers and migrants and the occasional khadga who has learned to sit still long enough to drink something warm. The yaksha proprietor brews from the seasonal grass-flowers and charges exactly what the market will bear.
fields.world:shop:animal_meadow_training_camp#d: An open-air training ground where the wind comes from every direction at once. The dura instructors here believe that there is no better teacher than exposure, and schedule sparring sessions during the hour before the bhramara cloud arrives.
fields.world:shop:animal_medicinal_garden#descr: A cultivated clearing tended by practitioners who have studied the relationship between plant, body, and suffering for generations. The herbs here grow things that have no equivalent elsewhere. Knowledge is shared freely; materials cost what they cost.
fields.world:shop:animal_mercenary_guild#descri: Animals who have figured out that their skills have cash value and have the good sense to organize. Better equipment than you might expect. The guild master keeps the contracts brief and the payment terms clear.
fields.world:shop:animal_mirror_lake#descriptio: The surface shows things that aren't there — or rather, things that are there but not yet. Followers of the Goddess of Illusion use this as a training ground: if you can hold your mind still enough to see clearly in a place that specializes in confusion, you can do it anywhere.
fields.world:shop:animal_naga_palace#descriptio: The seat of a naga court that remembers when this ocean was fresh water. Trading access: the naga have long memories and are interested in what traveling parties have seen. Their price for advanced teaching is always information — specific, verifiable, and something they don't already know.
fields.world:shop:animal_ocean_teahouse#descrip: A structure built into a sea cliff, half-submerged at high tide and bone-dry at low. A fire burns in a sealed alcove. The keeper is a broad and unhurried makara current who settled down forty years ago and has been pouring the same tea blend since. Nobody asks the recipe.
fields.world:shop:animal_ocean_training_camp#de: A karka war-school built into the coral. Sessions alternate between fighting in the shallows and fighting in open water, on the grounds that you will never get to choose. The instructors communicate primarily by demonstration.
fields.world:shop:animal_pearl_merchant#descrip: Pearls, polished shell, sea-glass, and a few things older than her trade.
fields.world:shop:animal_sacred_grove#descripti: The oldest trees in the realm gather here as if in council. Bark-sigils accumulate on the trunks over centuries — offerings pressed into the wood, prayers absorbed by the roots. The Yakshas and Yakshinis who maintain this grove are older than the realm's current configuration.
fields.world:shop:animal_shell_wright#descripti: A karka craftsman working in moulted shell, chitin, and salvaged metal.
fields.world:shop:animal_temple_of_the_naga#des: An old structure where those born with naga-affinity come to train under the great serpents' direct guidance. The water here has properties that don't exist anywhere else in the realm. Offerings of saffron milk and river-flowers are accepted at the outer shrine.
fields.world:shop:animal_termite_cathedral#desc: A structure ten meters high, built over centuries by beings each the size of a thumbnail, with architectural precision that confounds engineers. The collective intelligence that designed and maintains it doesn't communicate in any language known to surface beings, but it does teach — by implication and exposure.
fields.world:shop:animal_town_magic#description: A settlement that has drawn its share of hedge-mages, ritual practitioners, and wandering herbalists. The apothecary smells of bark, fungal spores, and something resinous that's been burning for days.
fields.world:shop:animal_town_supplies#descript: A clearing settlement where four game trails meet. Sounder matrons and herb-walkers tend most of the stalls. Food preserved in bark and clay, medicines extracted from things most travelers walk past without recognizing, tools for the deep wild. It is honest trade in a place that doesn't demand credentials.
fields.world:shop:animal_town_weapons#descripti: A market where different territories agree, briefly, to exchange. Dura shell-wright craftsmanship, vanara jugaad improvisation, marjara-claw handles on daggers sold by gana traders who got them somewhere no one is explaining. The weapons here are practical and tell stories.
fields.world:shop:animal_yogini_circle#descript: Sixty-four Yoginis carved in relief on an inward-facing ring of stone, no ceiling, no door. The practitioners who gather here are a rougher assembly than the hidden gompa — interested in results more than elegance, and willing to discuss the dangerous schools.
fields.world:shop:bone_archer_camp#description: A fortified camp of skeleton archers who've been here long enough to start trading. Their fletching is excellent. Their interpersonal skills are not.
fields.world:shop:brimstone_lab#description: A rickety structure of cracked glass and boiling tubes. The alchemist here has survived seventeen explosions. This gives them a certain confidence.
fields.world:shop:cloud_domain_shop#description: The gandharvas and apsaras of the Cloud Palace teach the sky arts — what it means to move like weather, to see from altitude, to become the medium through which lightning travels. These arts cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:crystal_domain_shop#descripti: The elder yogi has been here long enough to have grown into the crystals themselves — or the crystals have grown into him. Either way, what he knows about resonance, focus, and geometric mind cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:demon_sorcerer#description: A powerful demon who teaches the dark arts... for a price.
fields.world:shop:ember_merchant#description: Fire-forged goods from the burning half of Naraka. Everything radiates warmth.
fields.world:shop:frozen_merchant#description: Frost-covered wares from a resilient trader in the frozen wastes.
fields.world:shop:general_store#description: A well-stocked shop with a bit of everything.
fields.world:shop:glass_domain_shop#description: The mountain teaches through its own nature — perfect transparency, perfect hardness, perfect memory of having once been scattered sand. What it knows about clarity and cutting cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:hell_black_lodge#description: The entrance is half-buried in the earth, marked only with a crooked khatvanga topped with a skull and streaming black ribbons reeking of smoke and poison. As you enter, the darkness overwhelms you - until you notice the glint of a sneering smile.
fields.world:shop:hell_circle_of_yoginis#descri: The inward-facing side of this circular stone wall is carved with the bizarre forms of sixty four Yoginis. There is no ceiling, so the witches can land when they come flying from vast space to meet their earthly sisters.
fields.world:shop:hell_crossroads_stupa#descrip: The wind carries the smell of sacred juniper smoke and sacrificial wine far from this place. As you come closer, you see little heaps of tormas and butter lamps, some still burning.
fields.world:shop:hell_eternal_fire#description: Priests clad in white robes have been guarding the sacred fire since time immemorial. Many come to pay their respects and seek visions in the dancing flames.
fields.world:shop:hell_garuda_roost#description: A tall pole with a horned symbol at the top rises from the ground, sacred stones and offerings heaped at its base, colorful ribbons fluttering in the wind. The worshippers say the Garudas come to perch at the top during their long travels.
fields.world:shop:hell_hidden_gompa#description: Practitioners come to this place seeking solitude and peace. The ground itself vibrates with the power of their meditation, mantric syllables appearing spontaneously in the rock.
fields.world:shop:hell_medicinal_garden#descrip: The air is vibrant with the aroma of medicinal herbs and flowers. The healers cultivating them are happy to share some of their knowledge for the benefit of all suffering beings.
fields.world:shop:hell_mercenary_guild#descript: A fortified post where demonic soldiers hire out between assignments. Their equipment is functional, their prices are fair, their loyalty is negotiable.
fields.world:shop:hell_merchant#description: A twisted soul who trades in suffering... and useful goods.
fields.world:shop:hell_mirror_lake#description: Mirages flicker over the mercurial surface of the lake. Followers of the Goddess of Illusion gather around, meditating on the fleeting nature of phenomena and exchanging stories of their dreams.
fields.world:shop:hell_sacred_grove#description: The dappled light streaming through the dense canopy seems like living gold. The Yakshas and Yakshinis come to commune with their followers in this place, marked with colored ropes on the tree trunks and prayer flags hanging from the branches.
fields.world:shop:hell_tavern#description: A dim roadhouse where the desperate gather. Someone at the bar looks like they're between allegiances.
fields.world:shop:hell_teahouse_cold#descriptio: A dim waystation where the desperate catch their breath. The barkeeper keeps a pot of Lapsang Souchong going — its smoke is the closest thing to warmth in the frozen wastes.
fields.world:shop:hell_teahouse_fire#descriptio: The tea here is brewed in volcanic water. It tastes like char and smoke and something almost familiar. The barkeeper doesn't ask where you've been.
fields.world:shop:hell_temple_of_the_naga#descr: In every world some beings are born innately attuned to the mindstreams of the Naga. Temples arise where they practice, communing with their reptilian friends and patrons through offerings of saffron milk, fruits and flowers.
fields.world:shop:hell_town_magic#description: A settlement that has drawn more than its share of sorcerers and wandering scholars. The apothecary is always busy.
fields.world:shop:hell_town_supplies#descriptio: A trading post that survives on practicality. The sign reads: FOOD. TOOLS. NO CREDIT. It is the most honest thing you have seen in hell.
fields.world:shop:hell_town_weapons#description: A cluster of hovels that qualifies as a settlement. The main trade here is war.
fields.world:shop:hell_veterans_camp#descriptio: A camp of soldiers who survived long enough to have something to teach. They charge for lessons — nothing is free in hell.
fields.world:shop:hell_yogini_circle#descriptio: A circle of Dakinis — fierce, half-wild tantric practitioners. They trade knowledge for gold and ask no questions about what you plan to do with it.
fields.world:shop:hg_alchemist#description: A dré ghost crouches behind a folding table heaped with dried herbs, stoppered gourds, and bundles of something that smells like incense and rot. Its robes are stuffed so full of plant matter that it looks like a walking thicket. It speaks in a dry rasp and seems to genuinely enjoy its trade.
fields.world:shop:hg_black_lodge#description: A mound of bones marks the entrance, a khatvanga hung with a skull and black silk. Inside, something moves that may not be fully alive. It knows what you want.
fields.world:shop:hg_black_market#description: A low tunnel behind a false wall, lit by a single floating ember. The figure inside won't show its face. It trades in things that shouldn't have made it into the hungry ghost realm — quality ironwork, foreign medicines, a few items with the smell of other worlds still on them. Prices reflect the difficulty of getting anything here at all.
fields.world:shop:hg_bone_merchant#description: A skeleton trader squats among the dry graves, its jaw clicking as it counts coins with bony fingers. The wares are crude but functional — carved from the bones of those who no longer need them.
fields.world:shop:hg_charnel_sorcerer#descripti: A vetala perches atop a crumbling funerary monument, its stolen body draped in rotting silk. It trades in dark knowledge — curses, poisons, and the thin art of pulling life from the dying.
fields.world:shop:hg_circle_of_yoginis#descript: Sixty-four forms carved into standing bones, forming a ring on the charnel ground. The earth inside is worn smooth by countless ritual footprints. The witches still come.
fields.world:shop:hg_crossroads_stupa#descripti: At the intersection of the ancient paths, a stupa rises from layers of offerings — skulls, prayer flags, bones wrapped in cloth. The practitioners here call back what has been lost.
fields.world:shop:hg_hidden_gompa#description: A small monastery sits undisturbed between the burial grounds, its walls marked with painted eyes. The monks here practice for the benefit of all beings caught between lives.
fields.world:shop:hg_mercenary_guild#descriptio: A fortified charnel house where the realm's hired fighters gather between jobs. They call themselves undertakers — they put things in the ground, one way or another.
fields.world:shop:hg_mirror_lake#description: The surface of the lake reflects not the sky but something else — other realms, other moments. Practitioners sit at its edge, learning to bend what is seen.
fields.world:shop:hg_sacred_grove#description: A stand of ancient trees whose roots grow through charnel earth. Offerings of food hang from the branches — the hungry ghosts can smell them but cannot eat. Practitioners here speak to both the living and the dead.
fields.world:shop:hg_spell_shop#description: A sorcerer-ghost has assembled a collection of sutras and grimoires, most of them water-stained or singed at the edges, all of them legible to those with the patience to study. It charges for access by the session — a small candle's worth of time per spell — and answers no questions that aren't paid for.
fields.world:shop:hg_teahouse#description: A lantern glows faintly above a low doorway carved into a burial mound. Inside, a quiet figure brews tea from dried flowers that grow only on graves. The dead do not drink, but the living are welcome to rest.
fields.world:shop:hg_temple_of_the_naga#descrip: A low temple built around a black-water pool. The nagas who dwell in such pools are guardians of the dead. Their human followers leave milk offerings at the water's edge and learn what the serpents are willing to teach.
fields.world:shop:hg_town_magic#description: Faded prayer flags hang from a cracked shrine where the boundary between the living and dead has worn thin. The priests here teach what they remember of the old arts — healing and hexing in equal measure.
fields.world:shop:hg_town_supplies#description: A practical establishment run by those who tend to the dead for a living. The shelves are well stocked — people always need supplies in a land where nothing grows.
fields.world:shop:hg_town_weapons#description: A squat stone building marked with crossed femurs above the door. The smith inside is alive — barely — and forges weapons from scavenged iron and whatever the gravediggers bring in.
fields.world:shop:hg_veterans_camp#description: A ring of tents around a guttering fire, where warriors who have survived the hungry ghost realm long enough gather to share what they know. Their eyes have the hollow look of those who have seen too much decay.
fields.world:shop:hg_wandering_preta#descriptio: A gaunt, distended figure with a neck like a needle and a belly like a drum. It clutches its wares with desperate hands, willing to trade food for almost anything — though it can never eat enough to be satisfied.
fields.world:shop:infernal_forge#description: Heat-warped iron, a bone-white anvil, and a demon who hasn't slept in three hundred years. The weapons here are ugly and they work.
fields.world:shop:luminosity_domain_shop#descri: The unseen teacher shares what they know of the clear light. These practices cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:mercy_ward#description: A tent with clean bandages, a smell of herbs, and a medic who patches up anyone who can pay — no questions, no karma, no judgment. In hell this is rare enough to be miraculous.
fields.world:shop:mud_domain_shop#description: The mudlings share what they know of deep earth — the patience of silt, the memory of clay, the slow power of things that have been compressed for a very long time. These arts cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:rainbow_domain_shop#descripti: The yogi shares what they know of the rainbow body and the prismatic nature of mind. These spells cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:smoke_domain_shop#description: The mirror teaches, in the way mirrors do — by showing rather than telling. What it shows about smoke, shadow, and the nature of reflected things cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:sound_domain_shop#description: The gandharva prince teaches the art of sound — mantra, resonance, and the spaces between notes. These arts cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:steam_domain_shop#description: The old frog settles onto the edge of the pool, pours two cups of tea, and begins to talk. What it knows about steam and the place where water meets fire cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:tummo_domain_shop#description: The hermit teaches the inner fire — the heat that blazes upward from the secret chakra and melts the crown. These practices cannot be found in any guild.
fields.world:shop:wandering_peddler#description: Eclectic trinkets and supplies scavenged from the frozen wastes.
fields.world:shop:wandering_sage#description: A mysterious figure who can unlock your hidden potential.
fields.world:shop:wardens_pit#description: The pit warden runs the eastern patrols and teaches her soldiers to fight. For coin she'll train outsiders too — up to a point. She has standards.
fields.world:shop:weapon_master#description: A grizzled veteran who teaches combat techniques.
fields.world:terrain:ice#description: Frozen surface. Slightly fast but treacherous.
fields.world:terrain:water#description: Deep water. Cannot cross without a boat.
fields.world:zone:animal:coastal_wall#design: Horizontal wall separating the ocean from the inland zones. A coral barrier ridge — impassable except at tidal passes where the reef breaks. The karka hold these choke-points.
fields.world:zone:animal:forest#design: Upper-left section. Dense canopy — dark, layered, territorial. The forest floor is never quiet. Every fallen log is a claim, every fruiting tree a war. The portal to the Human Realm is hidden in the oldest part, near the northwestern corner.
fields.world:zone:animal:meadow#design: Upper-right section. Open sky-brushed plains, termite cathedrals, migration routes, watering holes. Exposure is the currency here — the khadga charge, the yaksha mark territory, the bhramara darken the midday sun. More dangerous than the forest because there is nowhere to hide.
fields.world:zone:animal:ocean#design: Bottom section. Entry zone — player arrives from the Hungry Ghost Realm. Vast coastal shelf and open ocean: deep water channels, coral reef flats, rocky islets, sandy shallows. The naga rule here and they remember everything.
fields.world:zone:animal:ridge#design: Vertical wall between forest and meadow. A ridgeline of tumbled boulders, thorn scrub, and dry ravines. Hard to cross but not impossible — the passes tend to be where the old game trails are.
fields.world:zone:hungry_ghost:charnel_grounds#: Top-right section. Final zone — reached by going UP through the horizontal wall from the graveyard.
fields.world:zone:hungry_ghost:dry_graveyards#d: Bottom-right section. First zone entered after the vertical wall pass.
fields.world:zone:hungry_ghost:fetid_swamps#des: Left third of the map, full height. Start zone.
fields.world:zone:hungry_ghost:horizontal_divid: Horizontal wall within the right section. Pass biased to the right so the player must explore the graveyard before finding it.
fields.world:zone:hungry_ghost:vertical_divider: Vertical wall separating swamp from the right half. Pass biased to lower area so the player must travel south before crossing.

notes.births:race:khadga: Known issue (from the Meadow workbook): **Khadga is two animals.** The birth, its body plan (`mantis`), its backgrounds and its enemy archetypes are the mantis. Its naming lore is a rhinoceros — wallows, horns, *The Good Mud*, *Where the Horn Broke*, "May your horn be long" — and so are both its companions: Tikshnashringa means *sharp horn* and charges in straight lines, and Nirvikalpa weighs two thousand pounds. *Khadga* is Sanskrit for both a sword and a rhinoceros, which is probably how it happened. Pick one — or split it into two births, as gana and mriga were split.
notes.companions:amlamarjari:
Meaning: "Sour Cat" (Sanskrit: *amla* = sour/acidic, *mārjārī* = cat)

Why generous, night_drinker: Patches everyone up after the party; reliable at both
notes.companions:angulimala:
Meaning: "Garland of Fingers" (Sanskrit: *aṅguli* = finger, *māla* = garland/necklace) — a famous Buddhist outlaw who collected the fingers of his victims

Why fastidious, sharp_memory: Professional precision with a "particular habit" involving fingers — exact and unforgettable
notes.companions:ayurmangala:
Meaning: "Auspicious Life" / "Blessed Lifespan" (Sanskrit: *āyur* = life/lifespan, *maṅgala* = auspicious/fortunate)

Why curious, fastidious: Studies anatomy with botanical thoroughness — fascinated, precise
notes.companions:choki:
Meaning: "Dharma Joy" / "Joyful in the Teaching" (Tibetan: *chos skyid*)

Why grief_struck, melancholic: Lost her entire village to a flash flood; still not sure what she is waiting for
notes.companions:coolhead_hotblood:
Meaning: English — a contradiction; the calm exterior over the boiling interior

Why hot_tempered, sharp_memory: Pent-up frustration building like a retort — remembered every slight, every frustration, until the seal broke
notes.companions:drupchen:
Meaning: "Great Achiever" / "Great Practice" (Tibetan: *sgrub chen*)

Why lapsed, stubborn: Performed every ritual, recited every text; believed none of it. Finds his current situation philosophically interesting.
notes.companions:durvasa:
Meaning: "Hard to Live With" (Sanskrit: *dur* = difficult, *vāsas* = dwelling/abiding) — the name of a legendarily wrathful sage in Hindu mythology

Why blood_handed, stubborn: Professional curse work; final commission backfired. The invoice was never collected.
notes.companions:dvijihva:
Meaning: "Two-Tongued" (Sanskrit: *dvi* = two, *jihvā* = tongue) — the forked tongue of a snake; a liar

Why greedy, stubborn: Worked two rivals simultaneously and was shocked it went wrong — greedy and absolutely certain it would work
notes.companions:dyutapati:
Meaning: "Lord of Gambling" (Sanskrit: *dyūta* = game of dice/gambling, *pati* = lord/master)

Why greedy, patient: Casino owner, odds always in his favour — calculating and willing to wait as long as it takes
notes.companions:gomchen:
Meaning: "Great Meditator" (Tibetan: *sgom chen*)

Why lapsed, vain: Mastered ten thousand sutras and used them for monastery politics — form without substance, prestige without faith
notes.companions:hustle_bones:
Meaning: English — a trader who never stops dealing, even after death

Why greedy, gambler: Traded finger joints, ribs, and one femur for better deals; still in profit
notes.companions:iron_oath:
Meaning: English — a vow made in iron; unbreakable and unyielding

Why stubborn, war_hardened: Kept his post for three hundred years. The order to stand down was never transmitted.
notes.companions:jawbreaker:
Meaning: English nickname — one who breaks jaws

Why quick, gambler: Fast, reckless, pocket-picking mid-fight — natural reflexes and high-risk instincts
notes.companions:kanjus:
Meaning: "Miser" (Hindi/Urdu: *kanjūs* = penny-pincher, tightwad)

Why greedy, stubborn: Maximum profit, minimum worker wellbeing — inflexible efficiency maximiser
notes.companions:karnak:
Meaning: Karnak — "fortified village" (ancient Egyptian place name)

Why devout, brave: Showed mercy at great personal cost — faith-driven act, genuine courage
notes.companions:khedrup:
Meaning: "Accomplished Scholar" (Tibetan: *mkhas grub* = learned one who has achieved)

Why stubborn, superstitious: Treated dharma as a system to optimise; found every shortcut, every auspicious day. Still reviewing the calculations.
notes.companions:kripana:
Meaning: "Miser" / "The Wretched One" (Sanskrit: *kṛpaṇa* = miser, pitiable person)

Why greedy, addiction: Died sitting on his gold. The gold is gone. The hunger is not.
notes.companions:leraya:
Meaning: Possibly Tibetan for "swift one" or a regional name meaning "the pursuer"

Why curious, stubborn: Switched from animals to people for the challenge; relentless once he picks a target
notes.companions:marmajna:
Meaning: "Knower of Vital Points" (Sanskrit: *marma* = vital point/vulnerable spot, *jña* = one who knows)

Why curious, stubborn: Followed the logic past the line; still insists the reasoning is impeccable
notes.companions:mehr:
Meaning: "Sun" / "Love" (Persian: *mehr*)

Why sharp_eyed, brave: One-eyed prophet who told the truth the court didn't want to hear
notes.companions:nangwa:
Meaning: "Light" / "Appearance" / "Clarity" (Tibetan: *snang ba*)

Why curious, stubborn: Died mid-proof, mid-thought; just needs one more moment — has needed it for quite some time
notes.companions:niyamendra:
Meaning: "Lord of Rules" (Sanskrit: *niyama* = rule/regulation, *indra* = lord)

Why fastidious, patient: Invented regulations and let bureaucracy grind — meticulous and unhurried
notes.companions:nurse_bones:
Meaning: English — a healer reduced to her most literal form

Why generous, devout: Non-violent by principle; patches enemies if they need it — principled care
notes.companions:nyingje:
Meaning: "Compassion" (Tibetan: *snying rje*)

Why patient, devout: Vowed to remain until every being in this realm found its way out. Still here. Still trying.
notes.companions:peldon:
Meaning: "Glorious Lamp" (Tibetan: *dpal sgron*)

Why generous, patient: Ran the village market for forty years; knew every price, every family — indispensable and invisible
notes.companions:prashan:
Meaning: "The Question" (Sanskrit: *praśna* = question, riddle)

Why curious, sharp_memory: Centuries of riddles at crossroads; still looking for the one no one can answer
notes.companions:princess_spiderface:
Meaning: English — a noble title paired with a bluntly descriptive epithet

Why generous, trusting: Actually rather nice; calls spirits by name, asks how they've been
notes.companions:raktamatta:
Meaning: "Blood-Mad" / "Drunk on Blood" (Sanskrit: *rakta* = blood, *matta* = intoxicated)

Why fastidious, stubborn: Every permit filed, every regulation followed — meticulous, inflexible
notes.companions:rasabhava:
Meaning: "Essence of Being" / "Becoming of Mercury" (Sanskrit: *rasa* = essence/juice/mercury in alchemy, *bhava* = being/existence)

Why curious, composed: Formula was perfect; timing was not. Still reviewing it calmly.
notes.companions:red_peony:
Meaning: The red peony — a flower associated with passion and fierceness

Why strong, hot_tempered: Enormous physical presence, moves like she owns the space
notes.companions:saka:
Meaning: "Arrow" (Tibetan) — also the name of an ancient steppe people

Why patient, stubborn: Desiccated but still carrying the bow; still knows which way the game runs
notes.companions:samvibrahmi:
Meaning: "Perfectly Bewildered" (Sanskrit: *sam* = completely, *vibhrāmī* = one who is confused/erring)

Why paranoid, suspicious: Obsessively prepared for every threat; died to a cabbage cart
notes.companions:sarpatailaka:
Meaning: "Snake Oil" (Sanskrit: *sarpa* = snake, *tailaka* = oil/unguent) — literally

Why greedy, gambler: Snake oil merchant — high-margin, high-risk operation
notes.companions:serji:
Meaning: "Golden" (Tibetan)

Why war_hardened, composed: Left the gym when winning stopped meaning anything — violence-desensitised but at peace with that
notes.companions:shantipala:

notes.perks:cross_perks:dual_discipline:
Cross-skill perks (from PERKS.md): Cross-skill perks reward characters who invest across multiple disciplines. They require minimum levels in two or more skills, which may be from the same or different elements. Any character meeting the requirements can unlock the perk.

**Design note:** These are tuning targets for alpha. Requirements and numbers will shift based on playtesting.
notes.perks:cross_perks:void_adept: Elemental mastery (from PERKS.md): These unlock based on total element affinity — the sum of all your skill levels in that element's 7 skills. Reaching **40 affinity** requires deep specialization across multiple skills in that element (e.g., four skills at 7+, or a broad spread reaching 40 total). These are late-game capstones.
notes.skills:alchemy: Consumable Power affects all potions, bombs, oils, and elixirs. Crafting Yield is a % chance to produce an extra item when crafting.
notes.skills:comedy: Nothing evades disaster like someone who doesn't take it seriously.
notes.skills:maces: Stun Chance is a flat addition to the chance of triggering a Constitution save vs Stun (1 turn) on each hit.
notes.skills:performance: Morale effects include inspiration, fear, panic, confusion, and confidence-related bonuses and penalties.
notes.skills:ritual: The following perks use **ritual objects** tied to schools: charms, gems, fetishes, seals. Objects are consumed or exhausted on use.
notes.skills:smithing: Crafting Quality improves stats on crafted items. Repair Efficiency reduces material cost and improves restoration.
notes.skills:summoning: Summon HP applies to all summoned creatures regardless of school.
notes.world:realm:hungry_ghost:
From the hungry ghost events plan (all 60 planned events are built):

Realm themes:
- **Insatiable hunger and craving** — the defining trait of pretas
- **Decay, rot, and impermanence** — everything is falling apart
- **Attachment to the past** — ghosts clinging to former lives
- **Three zones**: Fetid Swamps (rolang/zombies), Dry Graveyards (skeletons), Charnel Grounds (vetalas)

Karma guidelines:
- Feeding/sharing → god, human karma
- Greed/hoarding → hungry_ghost karma
- Violence against undead → hell, asura karma
- Compassion/release → god karma
- Trickery/theft → animal, hungry_ghost karma
- Buddhist practice (yoga, ritual) → god karma

    - Samaptika `#7`
      - meaning: the completer; the one who finishes

- **Place names** `kapota.place_names`
  - place_names:
    - The Assembly Tree `#0`
      - meaning: The conference location — both a specific tree and a category
    - The Safe Roost `#1`
      - meaning: Reliable overnight stop on a long route; evaluated by predator pressure, not comfort
    - Where the News Came From `#2`
      - meaning: Origin point of an important piece of information — used as coordinates
    - The Welcome Branch `#3`
      - meaning: Where returning pilgrims are greeted; a specific branch of the Assembly Tree
    - The First Waypoint `#4`
      - meaning: The start of the established route; most pilgrims begin here
    - The Long Route `#5`
      - meaning: The difficult migratory path — named for its character, not its length

- **Named places** `landscape.named_places`
  - named_places:
    - The Good Thermal `#0`
      - meaning: A reliable rising air column — different birds name different thermals; same name, different location
    - The Assembly Tree `#1`
      - meaning: The conference tree on the ridge between forest and meadow — visible from both territories
    - The High Seat `#2`
      - meaning: Any primary nesting site — shyena use this as a proper noun; kapota use it as a category
    - The Migration Flyway `#3`
      - meaning: The aerial corridor used by all migrating species; everyone knows it, no one owns it
    - The Storm Approach `#4`
      - meaning: The direction from which weather comes — all bird cultures orient by this

- **How this region is experienced** `region`
  - design:
    > Sky births live across all three zones but share a vertical orientation — they measure the world in altitude, thermal quality, and wind. Their place names are mostly aerial; their ground-level place names are functional minimums.

- **Shyena** `shyena`
  - philosophy:
    > Shyena measure the world in height and angle. Their territory is not the ground below but the airspace above it — measured in altitude bands, thermal columns, and sight lines. A name should describe either a quality of speed or a quality of vision. Children are named at first flight: what the parent saw in the first stoop tells them the name.
  - parent_wishes: May the stoop be clean, May the thermal hold you, May the sky be loyal, May you arrive first, May your eye be exact

- **Personal names** `shyena.personal_names`
  - personal_names:
    - Shyeni `#0`
      - meaning: hawk-born; the pure kind
    - Pratapin `#1`
      - meaning: burning swift; speed as fire
    - Drishtara `#2`
      - meaning: far-seeing; the eye that reaches
    - Kshepa `#3`
      - meaning: the hurler; released downward at speed
    - Drutaka `#4`
      - meaning: swift one; first in every moment
    - Urdhvaka `#5`
      - meaning: the upward one; always gaining altitude
    - Antariksha `#6`
      - meaning: sky-space; not in the sky but of it
    - Vegaka `#7`
      - meaning: velocity; the state before impact

- **Place names** `shyena.place_names`
  - place_names:
    - The Good Thermal `#0`
      - meaning: A reliable rising column — named per location, this is the best one in range
    - The High Seat `#1`
      - meaning: Main nesting site; a cliff ledge with unobstructed approach and retreat
    - The Stooping Ground `#2`
      - meaning: Hunting territory below — named from the air, looking down
    - The Ridge Wind `#3`
      - meaning: A reliable updraft on a cliff face — used for gaining altitude without effort
    - The First Light `#4`
      - meaning: The position where the morning hunt begins — a compass direction more than a place
    - The Wrong Altitude `#5`
      - meaning: An airspace controlled by another — acknowledged without confrontation

- **Uluka** `uluka`
  - philosophy:
    > Uluka are the most deliberate namers of all births. They watch a child for a full season before naming. What is observed in that season becomes the name — not what is hoped, but what is seen. 'You cannot name what you haven't watched,' they say. Place names are named for specific events of perception: what was heard there, what was seen from there, what was understood in that location for the first time.
  - parent_wishes: May you see what others miss, May the night be generous, May you carry the knowledge, May silence serve you, May you understand before you act

- **Personal names** `uluka.personal_names`
  - personal_names:

    - Nishaka `#1`

    - Jnanaka `#2`
      - meaning: knowledge-bearer; carries it as identity
    - Drishti `#3`
      - meaning: sight; vision as the whole self
    - Munika `#4`
      - meaning: the silent sage; speaks rarely, nothing lost in the silence
    - Ratriki `#5`
      - meaning: night-child; the dark is home
    - Viveka `#6`
      - meaning: discernment; the exact quality that distinguishes the uluka
    - Nishadaka `#7`
      - meaning: night-dweller; fully inhabited in darkness

- **Place names** `uluka.place_names`
  - place_names:
    - The Silent Rock `#0`
      - meaning: Primary perch — chosen for the quality of the surrounding silence
    - The Hunting Dark `#1`
      - meaning: Night territory — not a place but a time-within-place
    - The Hollow Where I Heard `#2`

    - The Old Tree `#3`

    - The Dreaming Point `#4`

rendered.Events › animal › ancient_banyan:
- **The Ancient Banyan** `ancient_banyan` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > No one told you the tree existed, but you found it anyway. The banyan's aerial roots form a labyrinth; its canopy covers a quarter mile in every direction. The Vanara Elder sits in the first great fork, weaving something from spider silk and what you eventually realize is solidified starlight.
    >
    > The tree has the attention of something older than itself. Earth magic and summoning traditions have always known about this place.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Approach the Elder and ask to study `study`
      - result: The Elder looks down from the fork with unhurried eyes. She names a price for her teaching. It is not small.
    - [blue] Sit beneath the roots in silence `meditate` — requires yoga 2 · result: xp: 25 · add_trait: beauty_struck
      - result:
        > You sit with your back against a root as wide as a wall and close your eyes. The tree breathes. You breathe. After a time — you cannot say how long — something shifts: a sense of patience that is not your own, accumulated over centuries, seeping in through the bark.
    - [grey] Walk away from the ancient tree `leave`
      - result: You leave the labyrinth of roots behind. The canopy covers you until you are out of the grove, and then the light returns all at once.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_black_lodge:
- **Black Lodge** `animal_black_lodge` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The entrance is low, partially hidden by undergrowth. You would miss it if you were not looking. Inside: incense so thick it stings, a khatvanga propped against the wall streaming black ribbons. The practitioner here works alone, without students, without oversight — the animal realm affords the privacy that the human realm did not. They turn when you enter, without surprise.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask to learn `learn`
      - result: A hand gestures to a list scratched into the bark of the wall. Spells. Prices. No preamble.
    - [grey] Back out `leave`
      - result: You step back into the daylight. The khatvanga watches you leave.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_boss_simha_king:
- **The King of Beasts** `animal_boss_simha_king` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The oldest part of the forest is where he sits — where the trees are so wide you could sleep in their roots and the canopy blocks all direct sun. The simha king does not rise when you approach.
    >
    > He is the largest lion you have ever imagined possible. His mane is the color of old wood. He is already ancient in legends that are themselves old. The portal to the Human Realm shimmers behind him in the roots of the oldest tree.
    >
    > He is not blocking it, exactly. He is simply here, as he has always been here — at the threshold, at the end of the animal realm, where the path changes.
    >
    > His gaze crosses your party without hurry, taking careful measure.
  - choices:
    - [blue] Approach peacefully and bow `bow` — requires yoga 2 · result: xp: 50
      - result:
        > You approach slowly and bow — low and long. When you rise, he has not moved, but something in his posture has changed: the calculation has left it.
        >
        > 'You have learned something here,' he says, in a voice like the ground settling. 'Go forward. Don't waste it.'
        >
        > He stands and walks aside. The portal is clear.
    - [yellow] Offer tribute worthy of a king `tribute` — requires roll charm vs 16 · success: xp: 30 · failure: pressure: earth-12
      - success:
        > You present what you have with the ceremony the moment deserves. He examines it without touching it — not the goods, but the gesture.
        >
        > 'Adequate,' he says. He steps aside without further ceremony. 'The realm of humans is expecting something. Try not to disappoint it.'
      - failure:
        > He looks at what you have brought for a long, unhurried moment.
        >
        > 'You have given me,' he says, 'what you could spare.' There is no anger in it. That is the difficulty — there is nothing in it at all. 'Tribute is what you cannot spare. Otherwise it is only tidying.'
        >
        > He returns it. The goods are yours again and worth rather less than they were.
    - [grey] Prove your worth in combat `fight`
      - result:
        > He rises slowly — no urgency, no anger. He has simply agreed to your terms. His voice carries one last note before the charge:
        >
        > 'Good. I wanted to see if you could.'
    - [yellow] Attempt to find another way through `circle` — requires roll finesse vs 18 · success: xp: 20 · failure: pressure: space-10
      - success:
        > You study the roots, the shadows, the angles. There is a gap — not much of one, but enough.
        >
        > As you slip through, his voice reaches you from the center of the clearing: 'Clever. But you'll find cleverness has limits, further on.'
        >
        > He does not pursue.
      - failure:
        > The gap is there. It is exactly where you judged it to be, and it closes while you are still committed to it.
        >
        > He has not moved quickly. He has simply been in the place you were going to be, for some time, waiting to see whether you had understood the ground as well as you believed.
        >
        > 'No,' he says, almost kindly. 'Again, or not at all.'
rendered.Events › animal › animal_crossroads_shri:
- **Crossroads Shrine** `animal_crossroads_shrine` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > Where three animal trails cross, someone built a cairn of stones. Prayer flags, thread, feathers pressed flat between layers of bark, bones arranged with obvious care — offerings that don't specify any particular tradition but cover their bases. A single butter lamp burns in a notch in the topmost stone.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave an offering `offering` — result: xp: 8
      - result: You add something of yours to the cairn. The butter lamp flickers once in still air.
    - [blue] Sit for a moment and breathe `meditate` — requires yoga 2 · result: xp: 12
      - result: You sit at the base of the cairn. At a crossroads, all directions are valid — this is what makes them sacred. For a moment you remember all of them.
    - [blue] Somebody built this where the animals cross, not where people do. `pilgrim_animal_trails` — requires trait: pilgrim · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > That is the whole point of it and almost nobody notices. The cairn faces the trails, the offerings are the kind an animal would take, and the person who built it was making an argument.
        >
        > You add to it in the same spirit.
    - [grey] Pass without disturbing anything `pass`
      - result: You leave the lamp to its burning.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_crossroads_stup:
- **Crossroads Stupa** `animal_crossroads_stupa` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > Where the old game trails intersect, someone built a stupa centuries ago. The mortar between the stones includes offerings pressed in during construction — seeds, feathers, a cracked egg. Butter lamps burn at the base. The place smells of juniper smoke and something that has been burning for a very long time.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Approach the stupa `approach`
      - result: A practitioner emerges from behind the stupa. Summoning magic — the crossroads is the right place for it. Gold is the price.
    - [grey] Observe from a distance `observe`
      - result: You watch the butter lamps in the wind. Some things are better left undisturbed.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_eternal_fire:
- **Temple of the Eternal Fire** `animal_eternal_fire` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The fire burns at the entrance to a cave, or near a volcanic vent, or at the base of an ancient tree struck by lightning and somehow still alive — wherever the ground produces heat that can be consecrated. The priests who tend it wear white and speak rarely. Creatures of many species come to pay respects. The fire does not discriminate.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Approach the priests `approach`
      - result: A priest turns from the flame and regards you. He names the spells, and then the prices.
    - [grey] Pay your respects and leave `respect`
      - result: You bow before the flame and step back. The fire reflected in your eyes for some time after.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_banyan_h:
- **Ancient Banyan** `animal_forest_banyan_hollow` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The banyan has been walking for a thousand years — dropping roots, standing on them, letting the original trunk rot away — and what is left is a hollow cathedral of living wood a hundred paces across, with a floor of soft mast and a roof you cannot see.
    >
    > Things have been left here. Not hidden. Left.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Take nothing, disturb nothing `leave` — result: xp: 6 · pressure: earth+10
      - result: You walk through and out the other side. The quality of the silence stays with you for days.
    - [grey] Take what has been left `take_offerings` — result: xp: 8 · gold: 130 · items: ['item_random']
      - result: Coins, tools, a folded cloth with something heavy inside. Nobody stops you. Nothing happens at all, which somehow makes it worse.
    - [grey] Leave something of your own and take something in exchange `trade_offering` — result: xp: 12 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > You set down coin and lift a small carved thing in its place, and the exchange feels correct in a way you could not defend to anyone. The banyan does not comment.
    - [blue] Address the tree properly `ask_the_tree` — requires summoning 4 · result: xp: 24 · learn_spell: {'school': 'summoning'} · pressure: earth+30, space+20
      - result:
        > You call, and something enormous and extremely slow turns a fraction of its attention toward you. It is not a spirit inhabiting the banyan; it is the banyan, thinking, at a speed that makes a human life look like a spark. It permits you one question. You are still deciding whether you asked the right one.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_cliff_ae:
- **Cliff Aerie** `animal_forest_cliff_aerie` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The nest is a cartload of branches wedged into a fissure two hundred feet up a limestone face, and it has been in continuous use for generations — the bones of a great many meals are cemented into its base by weather.
    >
    > The adults are out. Something in the nest is not.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave the aerie alone `leave`
      - result: You are a mile off when two shapes cross the sun on their way home. Good timing, you reflect.
    - [yellow] Climb and take what the nest has collected `climb_raid` — requires roll finesse vs very_difficult · success: xp: 20 · gold: 190 · items: ['item_random']
      - success:
        > Two hundred feet of limestone and then a nest full of two generations of shiny things nobody has ever come to reclaim. You are down and gone before the adults return. Your hands will not stop shaking for an hour.
      - failure: You are eighty feet up and fully committed when the shadow crosses you, and shyena do not need to land to fight.
    - [blue] The chick is tangled — free it `chick` — requires medicine 3 · result: xp: 22 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > It has gotten a leg through a gap in the branch weave and has been there long enough to be past panic. Freeing it takes an hour of very careful work at a height that does not bear thinking about. The adults arrive while you are doing it, and hang in the air twenty feet out, watching, and do not attack. When you finish, one of them escorts you down — pacing your descent, ledge by ledge, the whole way.
    - [blue] Look at what is in the nest, not at the nest. `bird_lover_reads_nest` — requires trait: bird_lover · result: xp: 20 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > Bone, wool, a length of dyed cord that did not come from anywhere nearby, and — under all of it — the thing the cord was tied to.
        >
        > The aerie's owner has been collecting from a settlement that is not on your map, and the direction it must lie in is now obvious.
    - [blue] Read the face for the updraught and go up on it `wind_read` — requires air_magic 4 · result: xp: 18 · gold: 120
      - result:
        > There is a standing column against the rock that will take a light body most of the way if it is not fought. You ride it up, take what is loose, and step off into it again on the way down. Whether the shyena saw you is unclear. If they did, they seem to have approved of the method.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_gana_cer:
- **Gana Ceremony** `animal_forest_gana_ceremony` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The clearing is full of gana, arranged in concentric rings, and every one of them is dancing — not chaotically, but in a slow interlocking pattern that has clearly been going on for hours and shows no sign of ending.
    >
    > Nobody is watching. That is not what it is for.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Watch from the treeline `watch` — result: xp: 8 · pressure: earth+10
      - result: You stay for an hour, understanding none of it, moved anyway. When you leave nobody has acknowledged you, and it does not feel like a slight.
    - [grey] Go around the clearing without disturbing it `skirt`
      - result: You add an hour to the day's walk and disturb nothing. The drumming follows you for a long way.
    - [blue] Join the outer ring `join` — requires grace 4 · result: xp: 20 · add_trait: celebrant · pressure: earth+25, water+20
      - result:
        > You step in on the beat and the ring absorbs you without breaking stride. It is harder than it looks and then, abruptly, much easier — the pattern does the thinking if you let it. Somewhere in the third hour you stop being a visitor. At dawn the eldest presses her forehead to yours and says nothing at all.
    - [blue] Whatever it is for, they are glad about it. Be glad too. `celebrant_joins_ring` — requires trait: celebrant · result: xp: 20 · pressure: air+12, fire+8
      - result:
        > You do not know the steps and you join the outer ring anyway, and the outer ring is precisely where people who do not know the steps are supposed to be.
        >
        > By the third round you have most of it. By the fifth you are being corrected, kindly, by a gana half your height.
    - [blue] Work out what the ceremony is for `read_rite` — requires ritual 4 · result: xp: 18 · skill_up: {'skill': 'ritual', 'amount': 1, 'cap': 8}
      - result:
        > The rings are moving at different rates — outer fast, inner slow, the centre almost still. It is a calendar. They are dancing a year, and the still figure at the centre is the year that has ended. It is a funeral. You take your hat off and stay until it finishes.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_gana_pac:
- **Gana Pack** `animal_forest_gana_pack` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > They do not surround you so much as *arrive around* you — six gana, drifting out of the undergrowth at intervals, each one taking a position that closes an option you had not yet realised you were relying on.
    >
    > The last to appear is the smallest, and she is the one the others keep glancing at.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Fight the pack `fight`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Put meat on the ground and keep walking `feed` — result: xp: 6
      - result: They let the food sit until you are forty paces on. Behind you there is a brief, businesslike scuffle over shares, and then nothing. You are not followed.
    - [blue] Speak to the small one — the others already are `address_leader` — requires leadership 4 · result: xp: 18
      - result:
        > You ignore the big males entirely and address the small female directly, which is both correct and clearly unexpected. She holds your eye for an uncomfortably long time. Then she yawns — enormous, deliberate, a gesture of dismissal that is also a gesture of safe-conduct — and the whole pack loses interest at once. One of them walks you to the ridge, for reasons of its own.
    - [blue] This is not an ambush. This is a working formation. `hunter_recognises_work` — requires trait: hunter · result: xp: 20 · pressure: air+8
      - result:
        > It is the shape you would use yourself, if you had six people and needed them to arrive around something at once.
        >
        > You say so, out loud, with the technical terms. The gana stop what they are doing and reconsider you from the beginning.
    - [yellow] Stand absolutely still and let them lose interest `hold_ground` — requires roll constitution vs difficult · success: xp: 12
      - success: Twenty minutes. Nobody moves; nobody blinks first, exactly, but the pack's attention frays the way attention does, and one by one they are simply elsewhere.
      - failure: Someone's nerve goes. A foot shifts. That is all it takes.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_healer_c:
- **Healer's Camp** `animal_forest_healer_camp` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > Someone has strung a canvas between four trees and turned the space under it into a clinic. There is a queue: a gana with a bad leg, two vanara holding a third between them, a varaha piglet being extremely brave about something.
    >
    > The healer — a gana, grey-muzzled, working fast — glances at your party and evidently sees nothing urgent. "Back of the line."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Take your place in the queue `wait`
      - result: It takes two hours. When she gets to you she is thorough, blunt, and charges exactly what the work is worth.
    - [grey] Leave the queue to those who need it `leave` — result: xp: 4
      - result: You go. Behind you the piglet is informed it has been very brave, which it clearly already knew.
    - [blue] Roll up your sleeves and work the queue with her `assist` — requires medicine 3 · result: xp: 18 · supplies: {'herbs': 12} · restore: {'hp_percent': 60, 'stamina_percent': 100} · add_trait: merciful
      - result:
        > She hands you the gana's leg without discussion and watches your first two minutes out of the corner of her eye. After that she stops watching. You work until the light goes. When the last patient limps off she treats your party for free, restocks your kit from hers, and says "come back" in a tone that means it.
    - [blue] You know how to wait in a queue like this. `chronic_pain_in_the_queue` — requires trait: chronic_pain · result: xp: 15 · restore: {'hp_percent': 25}
      - result:
        > You do, and you do it without complaining, which the healer notices from the other end of the line and files away.
        >
        > When your turn comes she spends longer on you than the queue can really afford, and does not mention why.
    - [blue] Somebody here is worse off. You have had worse than this. `scarred_gives_place` — requires trait: scarred · result: xp: 20 · restore: {'hp_percent': 20}
      - result:
        > You give up your place, and then the next one, and by the end of the afternoon you have not been treated at all and have carried four people to the front of the line.
        >
        > The healer finds you at dusk and treats you without being asked.
    - [grey] Pay for the queue's treatment and move on `donate` — result: xp: 12 · supplies: {'herbs': 8} · add_trait: generous
      - result:
        > You settle the whole line's account and leave before anyone can make it into a moment. The healer catches you at the treeline anyway and presses herbs into your hand, scowling, as though you had done something inconvenient.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_hedonist:
- **Hedonist's Camp** `animal_forest_hedonist_camp` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > Someone has been living extremely well out here. There is a fire, a great deal of fermented something in gourds, the remains of a genuinely impressive meal, and a marjara lying on his back in the middle of it all, utterly at peace.
    >
    > "You look," he says, "like people who have been walking."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Decline and keep walking `decline` — result: xp: 3
      - result: "Suit yourselves," he says, wounded on your behalf rather than his own, and pours another.
    - [grey] Stay the night `stay` — result: xp: 8 · restore: {'hp_percent': 40, 'stamina_percent': 60} · add_trait: gourmand · pressure: fire+20, water+15
      - result:
        > It is a very good night. It is a considerably less good morning. You lose most of a day and some indeterminate amount of money, and the party is in a better mood than it has been in weeks.
    - [yellow] Match him gourd for gourd `out_drink` — requires roll constitution vs very_difficult · success: xp: 16 · items: ['item_random'] · supplies: {'reagents': 6} · add_trait: night_drinker · failure: xp: 5 · pressure: earth-15
      - success:
        > At some point around the fourth gourd he stops treating it as a joke. At the sixth he concedes with enormous grace, declares you a person of substance, and gives you the good stuff — the sealed one he had not been intending to open for anybody.
      - failure: You do not remember the end of the contest. He does, and tells everyone in the forest about it for the next several years.
    - [blue] You have opinions about this camp and you keep them to yourself. `ascetic_declines` — requires trait: ascetic · result: xp: 20 · pressure: fire+12
      - result:
        > You decline everything — the gourd, the cushions, the extremely good food — politely and without comment, and your host finds this so novel that he follows you to the edge of the clearing asking questions.
        >
        > He is, under all of it, lonely. You had guessed that from the size of the camp.
    - [blue] He is pouring and you are not going anywhere. `drunk_stays` — requires trait: drunk · result: xp: 30 · gold: -30 · pressure: fire-12, space-8
      - result:
        > You are not. The evening is genuinely excellent and the following day is not, and somewhere in the middle you agreed to something you cannot reconstruct.
        >
        > Your host, when you leave, looks briefly like someone watching a colleague go.
    - [blue] He has more than drink out here and you can smell it. `bhang_shares` — requires trait: bhang_enjoyer · result: xp: 20 · supplies: {'herbs': 5} · pressure: water+8
      - result:
        > He does. The two of you spend an hour agreeing about a number of things that will not survive contact with morning, and one thing that will: he tells you where the good stands are, and he is not wrong.
    - [blue] Ask what he is drinking away `see_through` — requires yoga 4 · result: xp: 20 · add_trait: composed · pressure: fire+15, space+15
      - result:
        > The question lands like a dropped plate. For a moment the whole performance is visible from the inside — the fire, the gourds, the impressive meal, all of it built nightly against a silence he cannot sit in. He does not answer. But he stops pouring, and after a while he asks you how one learns to sit still, and you tell him, and he listens.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_high_can:
- **High Canopy Perch** `animal_forest_high_canopy_perch` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > A shyena is perched at the very top of the tallest tree in sight, motionless, looking out over the whole forest canopy. She has clearly been there for hours.
    >
    > When she notices you at the base she does not startle. She simply looks down, once, and returns to looking out — which somehow communicates, precisely, that you are welcome to climb if you think you can.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave her to her watch `leave`
      - result: She does not look down again.
    - [grey] Call up and ask what she can see `call_up` — result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > "Everything," she calls back, unhelpfully. Then, relenting: the smoke to the north-east, the migration two days out, the gap in the ridge that the maps do not have. She gives it freely and goes back to watching.
    - [yellow] Climb up and join her `climb` — requires roll finesse vs difficult · success: xp: 18 · pressure: air+25, space+15 · failure: xp: 5 · hp_loss: {'amount': 'moderate', 'target': 'random'}
      - success:
        > Forty minutes of climbing to sit beside something that got there in nine seconds. She says nothing about it, which is its own kind of courtesy. From up here the forest is not trees; it is one continuous green surface with weather moving over it, and you can see the ridge, the meadow, the sea. You stay until the light goes.
      - failure:
        > You get two-thirds up before a branch you had committed to informs you it is dead. The fall is survivable, mostly because of the branches you hit on the way. From above, faintly, comes what is unmistakably laughter.
    - [blue] Do not call up to it. Wait until it comes down. `bird_lover_waits` — requires trait: bird_lover · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > Everyone calls up. That is why the shyena is at the top of the tallest tree and not talking to anyone.
        >
        > You sit at the base for two hours. It comes down in its own time, which is the only time it was ever going to come down in.
    - [blue] Ask her what the sky-people make of the ground-people `sky_talk` — requires air_magic 4 · result: xp: 18 · learn_spell: {'school': 'air_magic'}
      - result:
        > "That you live in a tunnel and call it a world." She says it without cruelty — it is simply the view from up there. Then she describes the wind-roads: the thermals, the standing waves off the ridge, the column over the meadow that will lift a body a thousand feet if it is patient. You will never use them. You are glad to know they are there.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_jungle_m:
- **Forest Merchant** `animal_forest_jungle_merchant` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > His entire stock is on his back and his back is enormous. A varaha trader, three days out from anywhere, working a circuit that he clearly holds entirely in his head.
    >
    > "You're the second party this month," he says, delighted. "Business is booming."
  - choices:
    - [grey] See what he is carrying `browse`
      - result: He unpacks with practiced speed, laying everything out on a groundsheet in an order that makes his own sense.
    - [grey] Wish him luck and move on `leave`
      - result: "Tell people I'm out here!" he calls after you. "Nobody knows I'm out here!"
    - [blue] Trade him route information for stock `route_trade` — requires trade 4 · result: xp: 16 · gold: 50 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > You give him the state of the ridge crossings and where the marjara boundary now runs; he gives you a price no one else in this forest will ever see, and adds two items to the pile that were not for sale. Both of you leave convinced you got the better end of it, which is the mark of a good trade.
    - [grey] Walk with him as far as your roads agree `escort` — result: xp: 10 · supplies: {'food': 10, 'herbs': 4}
      - result:
        > Half a day of company. He talks the entire time — prices, gossip, a long involved grievance about a vanara bridge toll — and when your roads part he presses supplies on you and refuses payment on the grounds that conversation is worth more than goods out here.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_marjara_:
- **Marked Territory** `animal_forest_marjara_territory` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > Claw-marks at head height on every fourth trunk, running as far as you can see in both directions. The marks are fresh, deliberate, and evenly spaced — this is not an animal scratching. It is a boundary, maintained.
    >
    > The forest beyond the line is very quiet.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Cross the line `cross`
      - result: You are forty paces past the marks when the pale shape detaches from a trunk that it had, until that moment, appeared to be part of.
    - [grey] Follow the boundary until it ends `go_around` — result: xp: 6
      - result:
        > It takes most of a day. The line ends at a river, and something pale watches you from the far bank the whole time you are fording — but the marks stop at the water, and so does she.
    - [blue] Add your own mark beside hers and wait `mark_own` — requires might 3 · result: xp: 16
      - result:
        > You cut your mark at the same height, the same depth, and sit down with your back to it. She comes within the hour. For a long time she just looks at the two marks side by side. Then she cuts a third — above both — and withdraws. You have been given passage and put in your place simultaneously, which is, you gather, the marjara way of being generous.
    - [blue] Cross without leaving a trace `quiet_passage` — requires guile 4 · result: xp: 18
      - result:
        > Downwind, on stone and root, never breaking a stem. You are through her range and out the other side and she never knows — which is worth more than her permission would have been, and cost more to earn.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_mercenar:
- **Mercenary Guild** `animal_forest_mercenary_guild` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > A fortified outpost at the forest edge, flying a plain black banner between two old trees. The figures inside are armoured in hide and shell-plate — practical for the terrain. They look up when you enter with the universal expression of people who do this professionally.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Browse their services `browse`
      - result: The quartermaster opens a case and waits.
    - [grey] Move on `leave`
      - result: You leave the mercenaries to their sharpening.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_mushroom:
- **Mushroom Maze** `animal_forest_mushroom_maze` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The fruiting bodies here are the size of buildings, and they have grown close enough together to make corridors. The light under them is the colour of weak tea, the air is thick with spores, and sound does not carry the way it should.
    >
    > After twenty minutes you pass the same distinctively split cap for the second time.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Retrace your steps and go around `backtrack` — result: xp: 5 · pressure: space-10
      - result: It takes an unnerving amount of time to find the edge again, but you find it. The party is quiet for a while afterwards.
    - [yellow] Push on and trust your sense of direction `push_through` — requires roll awareness vs difficult · success: xp: 14 · supplies: {'reagents': 10, 'herbs': 6} · failure: xp: 6 · hp_loss: {'amount': 'light', 'target': 'all'} · pressure: space-20
      - success:
        > You keep the slope on your left and refuse to be argued out of it, and the corridors eventually run out of ways to disagree with you. You come out the far side having crossed in a third of the time the detour would have taken — and having gathered a great deal on the way.
      - failure:
        > Hours. The spores get into everything, and by the end at least two of you are seeing things in the corridors that the others are not. You come out somewhere you did not intend to be, tired and rattled.
    - [blue] Work the maze deliberately for what grows here `harvest` — requires alchemy 4 · result: xp: 18 · supplies: {'reagents': 18, 'herbs': 10}
      - result:
        > You stop trying to get out and start trying to get value, which turns out to be the correct relationship with the place. Half a day later you leave by the entrance you came in, loaded, having mapped the good stands by the smell of the air in each corridor.
    - [blue] There is something to be heard here and you are not going to hear it. `hard_of_hearing_misses_it` — requires trait: hard_of_hearing · result: xp: 22 · pressure: air-8
      - result:
        > The others stop and tilt their heads and go quiet, and you watch them do it and understand only that something has been heard.
        >
        > By the time it has been explained the thing that made the sound has moved, and the party's route with it.
    - [blue] Nobody is getting lost in here on your watch. `fastidious_marks_route` — requires trait: fastidious · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You mark every third turning, consistently, on the same side, at the same height.
        >
        > It is fussy and slow and the party complains about it right up until the point where you walk everyone back out in a fifth of the time it took to walk in.
    - [blue] Stop moving and listen to the maze `listen` — requires space_magic 4 · result: xp: 20 · pressure: space+25
      - result:
        > The corridors are not a maze. They are one organism's idea of a shape, and it is not trying to trap you — it has simply never had a reason to consider the concept of a straight line. Once you stop expecting corridors to behave like corridors, the way out is obvious, and always was.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_mycelium:
- **Mycelium Tender** `animal_forest_mycelium_tender` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The varaha is on her knees in the leaf-litter with her snout an inch from the ground, doing something that is unmistakably horticulture. Around her, over perhaps an acre, the forest floor has been coaxed into patterns — fruiting bodies in arcs and spirals, each species where it does best.
    >
    > "Don't step there," she says without looking up. "That one took nine years."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Step carefully back the way you came `leave`
      - result: "Good," she says, still not looking up. It is the warmest thing anyone has said to you all week.
    - [grey] Ask whether any of it is for trade `ask_trade` — result: xp: 6 · supplies: {'herbs': 8, 'reagents': 4}
      - result: "Some." She sells you the ones that fruit fast and refuses to discuss the others. The transaction takes ten minutes and eight words.
    - [blue] Offer to help with the nine-year patch `help` — requires medicine 4 · result: xp: 18 · supplies: {'herbs': 14, 'reagents': 8} · skill_up: {'skill': 'medicine', 'amount': 1, 'cap': 8}
      - result:
        > She tests you with one question about rot, decides you are not a fool, and puts you to work. You spend an afternoon thinning a fungal bed under instruction from a boar with better hands than yours. At the end she gives you a wrapped bundle and tells you what each one treats, twice, until you have it.
    - [blue] She is doing something specific. Get down and look. `curious_kneels_too` — requires trait: curious · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > The varaha does not stop or explain. She does move over slightly, which is permission.
        >
        > What she is doing is grafting — one network into another, at a join she has prepared over what must be months. Nobody in the party had known this was a thing that could be done.
    - [blue] Ask what the mycelium is connected to `network` — requires earth_magic 4 · result: xp: 20 · learn_spell: {'school': 'earth_magic'} · pressure: earth+25
      - result:
        > She looks up for the first time. "Everything. That is the whole point." And she shows you: hands flat on the soil, the slow enormous conversation running under the entire forest, older than the trees standing in it, patient beyond any possible use. You take your hands off the ground eventually. She lets you sit with it for as long as you need.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_rakshasa:
- **Rakshasa Ambush** `animal_forest_rakshasa_ambush` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The birds stopped a hundred paces back. You noticed, and kept walking, because there was nowhere else to walk.
    >
    > He drops out of the canopy directly into your path — a rakshasa, orange-eyed and unhurried, blocking the trail with the relaxed posture of something that has already counted you and likes the number.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Meet him `fight`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Back down the trail without turning around `back_away` — result: xp: 5
      - result:
        > You retreat facing him, slowly, for two hundred paces. He follows for one hundred and fifty of them and then simply stops, having established whatever he needed to establish. You go the long way.
    - [blue] Make yourself expensive — show him the arithmetic `not_worth_it` — requires might 4 · result: xp: 14
      - result:
        > You do not threaten him. You simply plant, shift your grip, and let him read what taking you would cost. Rakshasa are predators, not gamblers. He tilts his head, makes a sound that might be a laugh, and steps off the trail to let you pass — then follows at fifty paces for an hour, just to be sure you leave.
    - [blue] The birds stopped a hundred paces back. You stopped too. `hunter_heard_it_first` — requires trait: hunter · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > You stopped with them, which is why the party is already off the trail and in cover when the rakshasa commits to a charge at where you were going to be.
        >
        > It is very fast. It is not faster than being somewhere else.
    - [yellow] He is too relaxed — look for the other one `spot_the_second` — requires roll awareness vs difficult · success: xp: 16 · items: ['item_random'] · supplies: {'food': 10}
      - success:
        > There. Above and behind, flattened along a branch, the actual ambush. You point at her without looking away from him, and the whole shape of the encounter collapses. Caught out, they withdraw with what dignity they can — and leave the kill they had been guarding.
      - failure: You are still looking for the second one when she lands behind you.

- **Rakshasa Den** `animal_forest_rakshasa_den` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > The cave mouth is screened by hanging root and would be invisible from ten paces. Inside, the floor is dry sand, deliberately swept, and the walls are stacked with what a rakshasa considers worth keeping.
    >
    > The den is empty. The bedding is warm.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave now, quickly `leave` — result: xp: 5
      - result: You are a quarter-mile away before you let yourself breathe properly. It is, on reflection, the best decision you have made today.
    - [grey] Take what you can and go `loot` — result: xp: 10 · gold: 110 · items: ['item_random'] · add_trait: covetous
      - result: You grab from the nearest stack and are out in ninety seconds. Something calls, far off and unhurried, and you do not stop moving for an hour.
    - [yellow] Search it properly — the good things will be buried `thorough` — requires roll awareness vs very_difficult · success: xp: 20 · gold: 200 · items: ['item_random']
      - success:
        > Under the sand at the back, where the sweeping is most careful, there is a hollow lined with cloth. What is in it has nothing to do with hunting and everything to do with whatever this rakshasa was before it came out here to be a predator.
      - failure: You are elbow-deep in the sand at the back of the cave when the light from the entrance changes shape.
    - [blue] Prepare the den before its owner returns `set_trap` — requires guile 5 · result: xp: 24 · gold: 180 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > You do not steal anything. You rearrange: the bedding, the stacks, the sand, all of it shifted an inch or two out of true. Then you wait outside. The rakshasa comes home, stops dead in the entrance, and spends the next twenty minutes in a state of profound existential unease. It leaves the valley that night. You take the den at your leisure.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_sounder_:
- **The Sounder Matron** `animal_forest_sounder_matron` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > She is enormous, grey around the snout, and lying in a wallow with the contentment of someone who has nothing left to prove to anybody. Two dozen varaha of assorted sizes are arranged around her in the mud.
    >
    > One eye opens. "You are in my forest," she observes, without any particular concern about it.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Apologise and withdraw `leave`
      - result: "Mm," she says, and closes the eye. The audience is over.
    - [grey] Ask her the safe way through `ask_road` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > She tells you, in detail, with landmarks, and includes which stretches are contested and by whom and at what hours. It is the single most useful conversation you have had since arriving in this realm.
    - [blue] Sit down in the mud and stay a while `sit_with` — requires yoga 3 · result: xp: 16 · pressure: earth+30, fire+15
      - result:
        > You get into the wallow. It is warm and appalling and after ten minutes you understand it completely. Nobody says anything for two hours. Piglets walk over you. When you finally rise, the matron says: "You may come back," which from a varaha of her standing is close to adoption.
    - [blue] She is lying in a wallow, not guarding a pass. Approach accordingly. `beast_tender_approaches` — requires trait: beast_tender · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > You come in downwind, slowly, at an angle, and you stop at the distance she chooses rather than the one you would prefer.
        >
        > She lets you stop there. For a sounder matron with young in the trees behind her, this is an extraordinary concession, and both of you know it.
    - [blue] You know exactly how this goes if it goes wrong. `hunter_declines` — requires trait: hunter · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > You have seen what a sounder does to something that got between the matron and the young, and the memory is specific enough to be useful.
        >
        > You take the party the long way without arguing about it, and nobody finds out how it would have gone.
    - [blue] Ask her advice on leading people `counsel` — requires leadership 4 · result: xp: 18 · skill_up: {'skill': 'leadership', 'amount': 1, 'cap': 8}
      - result:
        > "Eat last," she says. "Sleep where they can see you. Never explain a decision twice — they stop believing the first one." She has run a sounder of forty for thirty years. You take notes, mentally, and use them for the rest of your life.
rendered.Events › animal › animal_forest_teahouse:
- **Forest Teahouse** `animal_forest_teahouse` — realm: animal
  - text:
    > A platform structure high in the canopy, reachable by rope bridges from three directions. The vanara who run it have been doing so since before any of them can remember. The tea is brewed from forest herbs you don't recognize and tastes like rain, bark, and something that is not quite spice. It is very good.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Sit down `sit`
      - result: You take a platform seat. A vanara sets down cups without ceremony.
    - [blue] A teahouse a hundred feet up. Do this properly. `tea_ritualist_canopy` — requires trait: tea_ritualist · result: xp: 20 · pressure: water+12
      - result:
