rendered.Events › domain › glass_mountain:
- **Glass Mountain** `glass_mountain` — realm: any · rarity: rare
  - text:
    > A mountain of glass rises from the plain — not metaphor, not illusion. Pure fused silica, facets the size of houses catching the light and throwing it in every direction. The surface is perfectly smooth and perfectly vertical. There is no path up. There is no grip.
    >
    > At the summit, something moves.
  - choices:
    - [yellow] Attempt to scale the glass face. `scale` — requires roll finesse vs difficult · failure: hp_loss: {'amount': 'moderate', 'target': 'random'}
      - success:
        > Your fingers find edges too fine to see, your weight shifts by instinct rather than thought. Slowly, impossibly, you climb. At the summit: glass spirits drifting in slow, glitching arcs — each movement a fraction out of time with the last, refracting light into cascades that should not be possible. They do not speak. They seem to notice you the way light notices a prism. Something passes between you.
      - failure: You slip. The glass offers nothing to hold and less to forgive — you slide and tumble, cutting yourself on the way down. The mountain stands unchanged.
    - [blue] Let the air carry you up. `air_ascent` — requires air_magic 5
      - result:
        > You step off the ground and let the wind take you — drifting upward along the face of the mountain, close enough to see your own distorted reflection in every facet. At the summit, glass spirits dance in slow, glitching loops, throwing light in directions that make no sense. One drifts close and holds the shape of something familiar — your face, perhaps, or the memory of one. Then it disperses, chiming softly.
    - [blue] Speak to the glass as stone. It was sand once — and before that, it was earth. `earth_speech` — requires earth_magic 5
      - result:
        > You press your hands to the surface and speak to what it used to be. There is a long moment. Then the glass does not open exactly — it simply stops being a wall in the way that it was. You walk through and up, the mountain permitting. At the summit, glass spirits spiral in their slow broken arcs. They feel very old. They feel like they have been waiting.
    - [blue] Sing to the mountain. `sing_to_it` — requires performance 6 · result: buffs: [{'stat': 'luck', 'amount': 1, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - result:
        > You begin to sing — nothing composed, just what comes. The mountain answers. A harmonic rises from somewhere inside the glass, and then another, and footholds crystallise along the face as if the mountain is remembering how to be climbed. At the summit the glass spirits dance faster for a moment, producing tones you can almost hear. A faint luck settles on you like dust: the mountain was pleased.
    - [blue] Sit at the base and meditate. Stop trying to climb. `meditate_at_base` — requires yoga 5 · result: add_trait: beauty_struck
      - result:
        > You sit. The mountain does not move. You stop expecting it to. At some point — you cannot say when — you are at the summit, seated in the same posture, and the glass spirits are circling you in their glitching arcs, throwing light across your closed eyelids in patterns that carry meaning. You have not climbed the mountain. You have stopped being someone who needed to.
    - [blue] It is a mountain made of glass. Note it and go around. `incurious_walks_on` — requires trait: incurious · result: xp: 22 · pressure: space-8
      - result: You go around. It takes an extra day and involves no revelation of any kind, which is precisely the outcome you were after.
    - [blue] Stop. Do not climb it, do not speak to it. Look at it. `beauty_struck_stops` — requires trait: beauty_struck · result: xp: 20 · pressure: space+12, fire+8
      - result:
        > You have seen something like this before — that is the trouble with having been struck once. You know what it is you are looking at.
        >
        > You stay until the light moves off it. Nobody hurries you.
    - [grey] Stand and look at it for a while. Some things teach by being looked at. `admire` — result: xp: 15 · add_trait: beauty_struck
      - result:
        > You stand at the base of the mountain and look up. The light changes as you watch — slowly, the way a day changes, but condensed. Somewhere in the complexity of the refracted surface is something you cannot name but will not forget.
rendered.Events › domain › rel_cool_thaw:
- **Neither of Them Will Say It** `rel_cool_thaw` — realm: any · trigger: relationship · requires_band: cool · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > {a} and {b} are not fighting. They are doing the other thing — the scrupulous politeness, the passing of the water skin at arm's length.
    >
    > It has been four days of this and the whole camp is tired of it.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Give them a job that needs both of them and walk away. `force_it` — result: xp: 15
      - result:
        > It takes them most of the morning, mostly in silence.
        >
        > They come back having not discussed it at all, and having somehow discussed it entirely.
    - [blue] Talk to each of them separately. Find out what it actually is. `talk_to_each` — requires persuasion 4 · result: xp: 25 · pressure: air+8
      - result: It is, as it usually is, one remark made two weeks ago that one of them does not remember making and the other has not stopped hearing.
    - [grey] They are adults. Leave it. `ignore` — result: pressure: water-5
      - result: They are adults, and it does not improve. The politeness gets a little more scrupulous.
rendered.Events › domain › rel_rivals_flashpoint:
- **It Has Been Building** `rel_rivals_flashpoint` — realm: any · trigger: relationship · requires_band: rival · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > {a} and {b} have been circling something for days, and tonight it arrives — over nothing, over a pot and whose turn it was, in the way these things always arrive over nothing.
    >
    > The rest of the camp has gone very quiet.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Let them have it out. Words only. `let_them` — result: pressure: fire-5
      - result:
        > It is ugly and thorough and it takes about twenty minutes.
        >
        > At the end of it they are not friends, but the thing that was under the surface is now above it, where everyone can see it, which is safer.
    - [blue] Get between them and make them each say the actual grievance. `mediate` — requires persuasion 5 · result: xp: 30 · pressure: air+10
      - result:
        > You make them do it properly, one at a time, no interruptions.
        >
        > It emerges that they are angry about two entirely different things, and have each spent a week being furious about the wrong one.
    - [blue] End it. Both of you, opposite sides of the fire, now. `shut_it_down` — requires leadership 4 · result: xp: 15
      - result:
        > They obey, because of how you said it.
        >
        > Nothing is resolved. Nothing gets worse tonight either, which was the immediate problem.
rendered.Events › domain › rel_sworn_watch:
- **Second Watch** `rel_sworn_watch` — realm: any · trigger: relationship · requires_band: sworn · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > {a} takes second watch, which is {b}'s. No discussion, no announcement — they simply do not wake them.
    >
    > In the morning {b} works it out from the burn-down of the fire and says nothing about it, which is its own kind of answer.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave them to it. `leave_it` — result: pressure: water+10, earth+5
      - result: Whatever the two of them have built, it does not require your supervision. The party moves a little easier for the rest of the week.
    - [blue] Two who trust each other that far should be fighting together. `use_it` — requires leadership 4 · result: xp: 30 · buffs: [{'stat': 'initiative', 'amount': 3}]
      - result:
        > You put them on the same flank and spend an evening on what each of them is going to assume the other is doing.
        >
        > It shows almost immediately.
rendered.Events › domain › skygazing_gompa:
- **Skygazing Gompa** `skygazing_gompa` — realm: any · rarity: rare
  - text:
    > On the open terrace of a small gompa, a yogi sits gazing single-pointedly at the sky. A soft rainbow shimmer is reflected in their eyes. As you approach, they smile and greet you with a gesture.
  - choices:
    - [blue] "Please teach us about the Great Perfection." `teach_perfection` — requires yoga 5 · result: add_trait: touched_by_grace
      - result:
        > Gladly, the yogi explains the workings of the mind as swirling reflections of rainbow light in a crystalline prism. The teaching opens doors you did not know were closed.
    - [grey] "Please bless us for this life and the next, master." `bless_us` — result: buffs: [{'stat': 'awareness', 'amount': 2, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - result: The yogi's eyes soften. They place their hands together and murmur a mantra, then touch each of you lightly on the crown of the head. A warmth radiates outward.
    - [blue] "What is the source of the shimmer in your eyes I can't help but notice, master?" `source_of_shimmer` — requires space_magic 5
      - result: The yogi just laughs — a clear, boundless sound — and gestures you inside. There, arranged on low tables, are things you have never seen offered anywhere else.
    - [grey] "What are you doing here?" `what_are_you_doing` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > "Observing the unceasing movement of the stream of the sky, friend." The yogi says nothing more, but the simplicity of the answer lingers with you long after you leave.
    - [blue] Ask the question you stopped asking years ago. `lapsed_asks` — requires trait: lapsed · result: xp: 15 · remove_trait: lapsed · pressure: space+15
      - result:
        > It comes out badly. It comes out, which is more than it has done in a long while.
        >
        > The answer does not resolve anything. It does establish, quite gently, that the question was always allowed.
    - [grey] Bow, place some offerings, and leave. `bow_and_leave` — result: buffs: [{'stat': 'luck', 'amount': 1, 'combats_remaining': 1}]
      - result:
        > You place what you can afford at the foot of the yogi's seat. They incline their head in acknowledgment. A faint warmth accompanies you as you descend the terrace steps.
rendered.Events › domain › snowcapped_hermitage:
- **Snow-Capped Hermitage** `snowcapped_hermitage` — realm: any · rarity: rare
  - text:
    > On an exposed ridge, in full sight of the howling wind, a group of yogis sit cross-legged in the snow. They wear nothing but thin white linen. Steam rises from their bodies in visible wisps, melting the snow in a circle around each of them.
    >
    > The oldest sits at the centre, utterly still, eyes open but seeing elsewhere. Slightly apart, the youngest shivers — barely perceptibly, but his toes have gone the faint blue of someone fighting a losing battle with the cold.
  - choices:
    - [blue] Approach, bow deeply, and ask for teachings. `ask_teachings` — requires yoga 5
      - result:
        > The eldest yogi opens his eyes and regards you for a long moment. He nods once. The youngest, still shivering, looks up at you with something like relief — perhaps he will learn more if you are here too.
        >
        > The teachings begin.
    - [yellow] You have some knowledge of inner heat yourself. Show them — not as a challenge, because you cannot help it. `fire_magic` — requires fire_magic 5, roll focus vs easy · failure: buffs: [{'stat': 'focus', 'amount': 2, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - success:
        > You let it rise — the warmth from the secret place below the navel, imperfect but real. The youngest yogi's eyes go wide. The eldest smiles: not at the technique, which is rough, but at the unmistakable sincerity behind it.
        >
        > 'You have found the door,' he says. 'Come, let us show you what is behind it.'
      - failure:
        > The warmth flickers and goes out. The eldest yogi watches, patient and kind.
        >
        > 'The fire is there,' he says. 'But it needs tending before it can burn steadily. The doors of this hermitage will be open to you when you return, more mature in your practice, young sadhaka.'
        >
        > Something in his words leaves a warmth in you that your technique could not produce.
    - [yellow] Challenge them to a contest of cold resistance. They seem so untouchable — surely it cannot hurt to test them. `water_challenge` — requires water_magic 5, roll focus vs difficult
      - success:
        > Your mastery of water is formidable — the cold bends to your will, and the youngest yogi has gone very still watching you. The eldest meets your eyes throughout, unshaken.
        >
        > 'Impressive,' he says at last. 'But your attitude is poisoned by arrogance. What you sought was not knowledge — it was victory. We will teach you anyway, because the fire does not care why you came, only that you did. But you will pay more for what arrogance has cost.'
      - failure:
        > The cold defeats you well before it touches them. The eldest yogi says nothing for a long time. When he speaks, there is no cruelty in it.
        >
        > 'You are not ready for the dharma taught in this place. Return once your merit grows.'
    - [yellow] Say nothing. Sit down in the snow beside them and see how long you last. `sit_in_snow` — requires roll constitution vs normal · failure: buffs: [{'stat': 'constitution', 'amount': -2, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - success:
        > You have no technique. You have only stubbornness and the refusal to move. Minutes pass. The cold becomes a presence, then a voice, then a kind of silence. When you open your eyes, the eldest is looking at you.
        >
        > 'No technique,' he says, 'but something that technique cannot give. Sit closer. There is something we can show you.'
      - failure:
        > The cold defeats you. You last longer than seems reasonable, but it defeats you. The youngest yogi — still shivering himself, toes still blue — gives you a small, sympathetic look as you scramble to your feet.
        >
        > You carry the cold in your bones for a while after.
    - [grey] Circumambulate the group, set out small offerings, and leave them in peace. `circumambulate` — result: buffs: [{'stat': 'constitution', 'amount': 2, 'combats_remaining': 2}, {'stat': 'focus', 'amount': 2, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - result:
        > You walk the circle three times, quietly, and place what you have brought at the edge of their warmth. None of them acknowledge this directly. But as you turn to leave, the youngest yogi's shivering has stopped.
        >
        > Something of their steadiness travels with you.
    - [blue] You have sat in worse for less reason. `ascetic_sits` — requires trait: ascetic · result: xp: 20 · pressure: fire+12, space+10
      - result:
        > You sit. The cold does what cold does and you let it, and at some point the distinction between enduring it and not minding it stops being available.
        >
        > One of them opens their eyes at the end and gives you a single nod, which appears to be the local currency.
    - [grey] Leave them to their practice. `leave`
      - result: You walk on. The sound of the wind returns. The steam rising from their circle diminishes behind you.
rendered.Events › domain › the_pit:
- **The Pit** `the_pit` — realm: any · rarity: rare
  - text:
    > The path descends into a vast muddy hollow. Dozens of mudlings — squat, glistening figures of animated muck — mill about in the thick brown sludge below. They have a crude camp of sorts: stacked bones, offerings of rusted metal, a clumsily drawn circle of wet earth in the center.
    >
    > One large mudling turns its featureless face toward you. A sound like bubbling tar rises from its throat. The others still.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Attack. Clear the pit. `fight`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Offer most of your food stores as tribute — seeds, grain, everything you can carry forward. `bribe`
      - result:
        > The large mudling reaches out a dripping limb and takes the sacks. One by one they are passed back through the colony and buried reverently in the central circle — seeds going into the earth, the way things are supposed to go. The mudlings make a sound like a long satisfied exhale of thick air. The elder turns back to you, willing to share what it knows.
    - [blue] Demonstrate mastery of earth. Let them see what the deep stone knows. `earth_magic` — requires earth_magic 7
      - result:
        > You call stone and soil to your hands and let the deep vibration speak. The mudlings go utterly still. Then, one by one, they prostrate themselves in the mud. The elder rises and presses both palms against your chest — it recognises a peer, and is willing to teach.
    - [blue] They are not a mob. Look at how they are arranged. `beast_tender_reads` — requires trait: beast_tender · result: xp: 20 · pressure: air+8
      - result:
        > They are arranged the way a nesting colony is arranged — the small ones inward, the big ones facing out, and the whole thing pointed away from something rather than toward you.
        >
        > You back out along the line they are not watching, and nothing follows.
    - [yellow] Stage an impromptu mud puppet play — a heroic epic specifically about the mudlings. Their ancient glories. Their terrible battles. The beauty of their mud. `mud_puppet_play` — requires performance 5, roll charm vs easy · failure: xp: 10
      - success:
        > You give them heroes. You give them tragedy. You give them a protagonist who is unmistakably the large elder mudling, whose courage is legendary, whose mud is the finest mud in all the realms. The colony erupts into a sound like a dozen geysers firing at once. Applause. The elder mudling — visibly moved, perhaps slightly embarrassed — gestures toward the central circle. You are welcome to learn.
      - failure:
        > Your puppet stumbles. Your plot collapses. The mudlings watch politely for a moment, then begin pelting you with clods. You flee the pit covered head to toe — but oddly, not harmed.
rendered.Events › domain › the_smoking_mirror:
- **The Smoking Mirror** `the_smoking_mirror` — realm: any · rarity: rare
  - text:
    > In a clearing where ash drifts like snow, a mirror stands alone — black obsidian framed in tarnished silver, taller than a person, tilted slightly as if to catch a sky it has no interest in showing you.
    >
    > The surface does not reflect. It smokes. Slow dark coils rise from the glass and dissipate without smell or warmth. Where your reflection should be, there is only depth — and somewhere in that depth, something moves.
  - choices:
    - [yellow] Look into the mirror. `look` — requires roll focus vs normal · success: add_trait: harrowed · failure: attribute_loss: {'which': 'random', 'amount': 1}
      - success:
        > You hold its gaze. The smoke parts. You see yourself — but wrong: every flaw given a face, every hidden thing laid bare. You do not flinch. Something dissolves, and something else rises in its place. When you look away you understand smoke in a way you did not before. The mirror has nothing more to show you.
      - failure:
        > You hold its gaze too long. The smoke parts and shows you something you were not ready to see — and a piece of yourself goes with it, drawn into the depth. The knowledge of smoke rises in you regardless. The price was a piece of yourself. The mirror does not seem to care.
    - [blue] Recognize the mirror for what it is. Hold up your own mirror to face it. `ritual_mirror` — requires ritual 5 · result: buffs: [{'stat': 'awareness', 'amount': 1, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - result:
        > You have seen this described in the old texts: a Tezcatlipoca-mirror, a devourer of reflections. You produce your own mirror — polished bronze, consecrated — and hold it to face the black glass.
        >
        > The two mirrors lock. The smoke rushes between them in a furious loop, finds no victim, and exhausts itself. The obsidian surface is still. In the silence, the knowledge of smoke rises in you like cooling ash.
    - [blue] Recognise the mirror for what it is. Don't look at the surface — look at what the surface is doing. `yoga_recognition` — requires yoga 5 · result: buffs: [{'stat': 'focus', 'amount': 1, 'combats_remaining': 2}] · add_trait: clear_eyed
      - result:
        > You see the mirror without seeing what it shows. The smoke coils and finds no purchase — there is no self presented to be consumed. The mirror continues smoking. You absorb its nature without being changed by its contents.
    - [grey] Strike the mirror. Whatever is in there, drag it out. `strike`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Turn away. Do not look. `turn_away`
      - result: You turn your back on it and walk. The smoke coils behind you. Whatever it wanted to show you, it keeps.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_ascetic_fast:
- **The Long Night** `trait_ascetic_fast` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: ascetic · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > {a} has not eaten since yesterday, and does not intend to eat today either. They have taken the far side of the fire and gone somewhere behind their own face.
    >
    > It is not clear whether this is discipline or something that has stopped being discipline a while ago.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Sit up with them. Say nothing. `sit_with_them` — result: xp: 15 · pressure: space+10
      - result:
        > You sit. The fire goes down. Around the fourth hour {a} says one sentence about their teacher, and then nothing else, and in the morning something between you has been settled without being discussed.
    - [blue] Give the fast a shape — make it a practice, not a punishment. `guide_it` — requires yoga 4 · result: xp: 30 · pressure: fire+15, space+10
      - result:
        > You give them the frame: the hours, the posture, what to do with the part of the mind that starts bargaining around midnight.
        >
        > By dawn {a} is hollow-eyed and unmistakably clearer.
    - [grey] Put food in their hands and stand there until it is gone. `make_them_eat` — result: restore: {'hp_percent': 10}
      - result: They eat, because you are standing there. They are steadier for it in the morning and quietly furious with you for three days.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_beast_tender_str:
- **It Has Decided** `trait_beast_tender_stray` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: beast_tender · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > Something has attached itself to the camp — thin, wary, and entirely certain about which member of the party it intends to belong to.
    >
    > {a} has already fed it, which settles the matter as far as it is concerned.
  - choices:
    - [grey] It can come. It eats what we can spare. `keep_it` — result: pressure: water+10, fire+5
      - result: It comes. It is useless in every way that can be measured and the camp is measurably better for it.
    - [grey] Drive it off before it starves with us. `send_it_off` — result: pressure: water-10
      - result: {a} does it themselves, which is the kindest way it can be done and does not appear to help.
    - [blue] Anything that eats can earn. `put_it_to_work` — requires logistics 3 · result: xp: 25
      - result: Within three days it is walking point, and doing it better than anyone you would have assigned.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_debtor_collector:
- **Someone Has Been Asking** `trait_debtor_collector` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: debtor · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > A traveller shares your fire for an hour, and mentions, without any particular emphasis, that a man has been asking after someone matching {a}'s description in every settlement between here and the pass.
    >
    > He is described as patient. That is the word the traveller uses. Patient.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Send the money ahead with the traveller. `pay_ahead` — result: pressure: air+15
      - result:
        > It is most of what you have. The traveller takes it with the blank courtesy of a man who has carried worse.
        >
        > Whether it arrives is another question, but {a} sleeps properly for the first time in a while.
    - [blue] Have {a} send word: terms, and a date. `send_word` — requires trade 4 · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > The letter is careful. It admits the debt, proposes a schedule, and contains one line that a certain kind of creditor will recognise as an offer rather than a plea.
        >
        > The asking stops for a while.
    - [grey] Let him ask. The world is large. `ignore_it` — result: pressure: air-12
      - result:
        > The world is large. {a} spends the rest of the night working out exactly how large, and how many roads there are through it, and how few of them a patient man would need to watch.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_gambler_game:
- **A Game at the Next Fire** `trait_gambler_game` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: gambler · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > There is another fire within sight of yours, and around it, the unmistakable rhythm of a game — the pause, the clatter, the noise people make when someone loses badly.
    >
    > {a} has been looking at it for some time now.
  - choices:
    - [blue] Let {a} play, but set a limit before they go. `play_it_safe` — requires persuasion 3 · result: xp: 15 · gold: small
      - result:
        > {a} agrees to the limit with the easy sincerity of someone who has agreed to limits before. This time, remarkably, they keep it — and come back with more than they left with, and with the name of a man who buys things quietly.
    - [yellow] Let it run. {a} knows what they are doing. `play_deep` — requires roll luck vs moderate · success: xp: 20 · gold: moderate · failure: pressure: earth-10
      - success:
        > It goes late. It goes badly, and then very well, and then the other fire goes quiet in the way fires do when the stranger is winning.
        >
        > {a} walks back before anyone decides to discuss it further.
      - failure:
        > The game turns. It turns the way games do when someone else at the fire has also been doing this for years.
        >
        > {a} comes back with empty hands and a story about the light being bad.
    - [grey] Nobody is playing anything. We move at dawn. `forbid` — result: pressure: fire-10
      - result: {a} does not argue, which is worse than arguing. They sit with their back to the other fire for the rest of the night, and are notably unrested in the morning.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_grudge_bearer_le:
- **The Ledger** `trait_grudge_bearer_ledger` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: grudge_bearer · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > {a} is awake, and has been for some time, going over something in the dark with the thoroughness of a clerk.
    >
    > You have seen this before. It is never nothing, and it is never recent.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask who it is. Let them say the name. `hear_it` — result: pressure: water+8
      - result:
        > They say it. Then they say it again, with the details, and the details have not softened by a single degree in however many years it has been.
        >
        > Saying it out loud does not fix it. It does make the night shorter.
    - [blue] Tell them plainly what carrying it is costing. `cut_it` — requires yoga 4 · result: xp: 25 · pressure: water+15
      - result:
        > It lands badly and then, some hours later, it lands properly.
        >
        > {a} does not forgive anyone. But they put the ledger down for the night, which is not nothing.
    - [grey] Let it sharpen. There will be a use for it. `sharpen_it` — result: pressure: water-10, fire+5
      - result: You leave them to it. In the morning {a} is rested in the specific way of someone who has spent the night deciding something.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_pilgrim_detour:
- **A Stone Off the Road** `trait_pilgrim_detour` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: pilgrim · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > {a} has noticed something the rest of you walked past: a marker stone, half-swallowed, with the remains of offerings at its base.
    >
    > Someone tended this within living memory. Nobody has for a while.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Clear it properly. It costs an hour. `tend_it` — result: xp: 15 · pressure: earth+10
      - result:
        > You clear the base, straighten the stone, leave what can be spared. {a} does the words from memory.
        >
        > The hour is gone and something about the party's footing is better for the rest of the day.
    - [blue] Read what is carved there. `read_it` — requires learning 4 · result: xp: 30
      - result:
        > The script is three languages old and mostly worn, but enough survives: a name, a direction, and a warning that was specific once.
        >
        > {a} copies it down. It will mean something later.
    - [grey] Note it and keep walking. `walk_on` — result: pressure: space-8
      - result: You keep walking. {a} looks back twice, and then makes a point of not looking back again.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_scarred_weather:
- **It Knows the Weather** `trait_scarred_weather` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: scarred · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > The cold has got into {a}'s old wound, the way it does, and they are pretending with some effort that it has not.
    >
    > It will pass by midday. It always passes by midday.
  - choices:
    - [blue] Work on it properly before it stiffens. `treat_it` — requires medicine 3 · result: xp: 15 · restore: {'hp_percent': 15}
      - result: Heat, pressure, and twenty patient minutes. {a} is functional by dawn instead of by noon, and says so in about four words.
    - [grey] Ask how they got it. `ask_about_it` — result: pressure: water+5
      - result:
        > They tell it flatly, which is how the bad ones get told. It is shorter than you expected and there is a second story underneath it that does not get told tonight.
    - [grey] Say nothing and set an easy pace tomorrow. `say_nothing` — result: pressure: earth+8
      - result: You set the pace without mentioning why. {a} notices, and does not mention that either. This is apparently how it is done.
rendered.Events › domain › trait_secret_bearer_sl:
- **Nearly Said** `trait_secret_bearer_slip` — realm: any · trigger: trait · requires_trait: secret_bearer · rarity: uncommon
  - text:
    > Late, with the fire low and everyone half-asleep, {a} begins a sentence.
    >
    > It is four words long and it stops. Whatever the fifth word was going to be, it has been put back.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Pretend not to have heard. `let_it_go`
      - result: You let it lie. {a} is grateful in the particular way of someone who has just been spared, and sits a little closer to the fire afterwards.
    - [yellow] Ask gently. Some things want carrying together. `draw_it_out` — requires roll charm vs moderate · success: xp: 25 · pressure: water+20 · failure: pressure: space-5
      - success:
        > It takes an hour and it costs them something.
        >
        > What comes out is smaller than you expected and much heavier than it looks, and {a} is a different kind of tired at the end of it — the kind that heals.
      - failure: They talk around it for a while, pleasantly, and tell you nothing at all. By the end you are not certain there was ever a sentence.
    - [grey] Push. Whatever it is, it is walking with us. `press_hard` — result: pressure: air-10
      - result: {a} closes like a door. Whatever was nearly said is now considerably further from being said than it was an hour ago.
rendered.Events › domain › waterworks:
- **The Waterworks** `waterworks` — realm: any · rarity: rare
  - text:
    > A low wooden building rises from the mist, every surface slick and steaming. Above the entry hangs a sign painted with a frog holding a cup of tea. Through the latticed panels you can see shapes moving in pale mineral water — people, perhaps, or creatures that resemble them. The smell of cardamom and sulfur drifts toward you.
    >
    > The door is open.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Pay the entry fee and use the baths `bathe` — result: restore: {'hp_percent': 100, 'mana_percent': 100, 'stamina_percent': 100}
      - result:
        > You hand over the coins, receive a worn linen towel, and are waved through. The water is exactly the right temperature. Somewhere, a flute plays a tune you almost recognize. When you finally climb out, you feel entirely new.
    - [blue] Ask whether they serve tea on the hot side. They will. `tea_bath` — requires trait: tea_ritualist · result: xp: 20 · pressure: water+12, fire+5
      - result:
        > They do, and it is served in the manner of a place that has been serving it to the same twelve people for three hundred years.
        >
        > You are, briefly, extremely comfortable. It is not an experience this realm offers often.
    - [grey] Leave without going in `leave`
      - result: You walk on. The sound of splashing water and low voices fades behind you.
rendered.Events › domain › waterworks_inner:
- **The Bathhouse Floor** `waterworks_inner` — realm: any · rarity: follow_up_only
  - text:
    > Clean, rested, and wrapped in borrowed linen, you survey the room. A pair of river spirits play dice in the corner. Two monks argue quietly over a plate of dumplings. A large toad in a silk robe sips tea with the focused air of someone who has been doing this for several centuries.
    >
    > On low tables between the pools: small plates of pickled plum, pale cakes, and pale green tea. Nobody looks at you with any particular suspicion.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Order tea and snacks for the whole room — your coin, your treat `treat_everyone`
      - result:
        > A small stir runs through the room. The toad in the silk robe sets down its cup, turns its enormous amber eyes toward you, and slowly crosses the floor.
        >
        > 'Generosity in a bathhouse,' it says, in a voice like water over smooth stone. 'That's rarer than you'd think.' It settles beside you. 'I know a trick or two. Buy something, and I'll show you.'
    - [blue] Hold the room with tall tales of your travels `tall_tales` — requires performance 5, comedy 5
      - result:
        > You begin with the time you crossed the frozen bridge over the River of Ash. By the second story, even the monks have stopped arguing. By the third, the toad in the silk robe is leaning forward with those great amber eyes half-closed in something like delight.
        >
        > 'You've been places,' it says, when you finish. 'I've been a few places myself. A trade seems fair.'
    - [blue] Say nothing and let the room talk over you. `gossip_floor` — requires trait: gossip · result: xp: 20 · gold: small
      - result:
        > A bathhouse is the most porous building ever devised. In ninety minutes you learn who is in debt to whom, which official is not returning, and one thing that is very obviously a lie and therefore worth more than the rest of it.
    - [blue] The entry fee is negotiable. It always is. `scrimper_fee` — requires trait: scrimper · result: xp: 20 · gold: small
      - result:
        > It is not negotiable, and you negotiate it anyway, on the grounds that you will not be using the oils, the towels, or the attendant.
        >
        > They take a third off to be rid of the conversation.
    - [yellow] Slip away and quietly go through the bags left unattended near the changing room `steal` — requires roll thievery vs easy · success: gold: 25 · items: ['water_charm_common']
      - success:
        > Everyone is very relaxed and nobody is watching the changing room closely. You move quickly and quietly. Coins, a small charm, and then you're back in your seat before anyone looks up. The dice players argue. The monks argue. The toad sips its tea.
      - failure:
        > You're doing well until a pale hand closes around your wrist. The room goes quiet. In short order you are dressed and deposited outside, the door clicking shut behind you. The painted frog on the sign stares at you with what might be disappointment.
rendered.Events › hell › cold › hell_frozen_trave:
- **Frozen Traveler** `hell_frozen_traveler` — realm: hell · zone: cold
  - text:
    > A shivering figure huddles by the roadside, barely conscious. Their robes are torn and frostbitten skin shows through the gaps.
    >
    > "Please... I've been wandering for so long. I can't feel my hands anymore. Is this... is this what I deserve?"
  - choices:
    - [blue] Tend to their wounds `heal` — requires medicine 1 · result: xp: 8 · items: ['prayer_beads']
      - result:
        > You work quickly. Color returns to their face — they look surprised, as if they'd forgotten warmth was possible. They press a trinket into your hands without words.
    - [grey] Give them some gold and food `give_gold` — result: xp: 4
      - result: They weep with gratitude and speak quietly of a lifetime spent hoarding while others starved. They understand now what they didn't then.
    - [blue] Offer them a small purification rite `purify` — requires ritual 2 · result: xp: 5
      - result: You bless a little water with mantras and wash their hands and forehead. It's not much — but it's something. They breathe a little easier.
    - [grey] Ask how they came to be here `ask` — result: xp: 3
      - result: They were a corrupt tax collector. They tell you plainly, without excuses. They understand now what their life cost others.
    - [grey] Walk past without stopping `pass`
      - result: They watch you go in silence. The cold feels a little sharper afterward.
    - [blue] Help, but count what it costs first. `scrimper_counts` — requires trait: scrimper · result: xp: 20 · pressure: earth+5
      - result:
        > Two rations, a blanket you were not using, and an hour. You total it as you go, out of habit, and find the total does not bother you as much as you expected.
        >
        > The traveller lives. The accounting is, you decide, still worth having done.
    - [blue] There is no decision here. Get them warm. `warm_hearted_no_question` — requires trait: warm_hearted · result: xp: 15 · pressure: water+12, fire+8
      - result:
        > You are already moving before the question has finished being asked, and the party follows because that is what happens when someone moves first.
        >
        > They live. They will tell someone about it, somewhere down the road.
    - [blue] You want to carry them and you cannot. `frail_cannot_carry` — requires trait: frail · result: xp: 22 · pressure: earth-10
      - result:
        > You get about forty paces before your legs make the decision for you, and somebody else takes the weight without comment, which is worse than comment.
        >
        > The traveller lives. You spend the evening being unhelpfully angry at your own arms.
    - [blue] Pick them up. Keep walking. `strong_carries` — requires trait: strong · result: xp: 15
      - result:
        > You pick them up and keep walking and the party rearranges itself around the fact without a word being spent on it.
        >
        > They are at the waystation an hour before they would otherwise have been, which is the whole difference between the two available outcomes.
    - [yellow] Sit with them without rushing — wait until the shock recedes enough for words `patient_presence` — requires roll charm vs easy · success: xp: 10 · items: ['random_common_talisman'] · failure: xp: 5
      - success:
        > Eventually they look up. Something surfaces from beneath the shock — a fragment of who they were. They press something into your hands as you leave: a small carved token from before. 'I won't need it here,' they say. It turns out to be worth something.
      - failure:
        > They are too far gone in shock for words yet. But they grip your hand for a long time. When you finally rise to leave, a little warmth has returned to their face. Perhaps that's enough.
rendered.Events › hell › devil_deserter:
- **A Familiar Face** `devil_deserter` — realm: any
  - text:
    > A red devil sits by the road, stripped of his armor. He looks up at you. 'I'm done with the Guard,' he says simply. 'Done with all of it. I just need somewhere to be.'
  - choices:
    - [grey] Take him with you. `recruit`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Not your problem. Walk on. `walk_on`
      - result: You leave him by the road. Some distances can't be closed.
    - [blue] Extract information about the Guard's patrol routes and weak points `probe_intel` — requires guile 1 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > He's grateful for someone who actually wants to listen. Between complaints, useful details slip out — patrol timings, which commanders take bribes, where the soft spots in the ring are. You leave better informed.
    - [yellow] Study him carefully — look past the performance to what's underneath `read_intent` — requires roll awareness vs easy · success: xp: 6
      - success:
        > He's genuine. Exhausted, frightened, and done. The despair in him isn't put on — no devil performs suffering this quietly. You feel something shift in your understanding of this place.
      - failure: Hellfire makes everyone's eyes the same — flat and red and unreadable. You can't tell. He might be desperate. He might be a trap. You move on uncertain.
    - [blue] You know what showing mercy in hell costs. Acknowledge it. `recognize_the_cost` — requires yoga 3
      - result:
        > He looks at you carefully. The recognition is mutual — you have both thought about the same thing. 'You understand it,' he says. It isn't a question. He stands and picks up his pack.
    - [blue] Offer him something worth serving — not just somewhere to be. `offer_purpose` — requires leadership 4
      - result: He listens to what you are doing and why. Something shifts behind his eyes for the first time in a while. 'That I could follow,' he says.
    - [blue] You know exactly what he is doing, because you did it. `oath_breaker_recognises` — requires trait: oath_breaker · result: xp: 20 · pressure: earth+8
      - result:
        > You do not tell him it gets easier. You tell him the specific practical things: which roads have checkpoints, what they ask, and how long before anyone stops looking.
        >
        > He listens like a man taking down an address.
    - [blue] A vow is a vow. Say so, plainly, and then help anyway. `oath_keeper_disapproves` — requires trait: oath_keeper · result: xp: 20 · pressure: earth+10, water+5
      - result:
        > You tell him what you think of it. He takes it without arguing, which is worse than arguing.
        >
        > Then you give him the water anyway, because the two positions turn out not to be in conflict, whatever you had assumed.
    - [blue] He has not finished. Let him finish. `patient_hears_him` — requires trait: patient · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > It takes him a long time to get to the actual sentence, and the actual sentence is not the one he opened with.
        >
        > What he is done with is not the Guard. Once that is out, the rest of the conversation is a different conversation entirely.
    - [yellow] Be someone worth following — just ask him. `just_ask` — requires roll charm vs easy
      - success: He looks at you for a long moment, then stands and rolls his shoulders. 'Alright. Can't be worse than this.'
      - failure: He shakes his head. 'No offense. I just need a sign it is worth it this time. Come back if things get interesting.'
rendered.Events › hell › hell_ancient_stupa:
- **Ancient Stupa** `hell_ancient_stupa` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A crumbling stupa rises from the snow, its dome still intact after countless ages. Tattered prayer flags still flutter from the crown, faded but unbroken. Mantras are carved into every stone.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Walk around it three times in devotion `circumambulate` — result: xp: 5
      - result: As you circle it clockwise three times; the cold seems to lessen. You place a small offering at the base and leave.
    - [blue] Meditate at the stupa's base `meditate` — requires yoga 2 · result: xp: 8
      - result: Seeing the work of so many hands towards creating a better tomorrow fills you with determination.
    - [blue] Study the carved mantras closely `study` — requires ritual 1 · result: xp: 8 · learn_spell: {'school': 'white_magic', 'level_range': [1, 2]}
      - result: You study the faded letters until they become clearer.
    - [blue] Study the prayer flags and what sustains them `prayer_flags` — requires air_magic 1 · result: xp: 8
      - result: Somehow kept together by their inner charge rather than outer weave, the flags can still teach you something about how intention outlasts form.
    - [blue] Walk the full circuit. Three times, the correct direction. `pilgrim_circuit` — requires trait: pilgrim · result: xp: 20 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > It takes the better part of an hour in cold that makes an hour expensive.
        >
        > On the third circuit you notice the thing the first two missed: a niche at the base, sheltered from the wind, with something still in it.
    - [blue] You are carrying something you have been meaning to put down. `renunciate_leaves_it` — requires trait: renunciate · result: xp: 20 · add_trait: renunciate · pressure: fire+15, earth+8
      - result:
        > You put it in the niche. It is not an offering exactly — nobody is being asked for anything — it is simply somewhere to leave a thing so that it stops being yours.
        >
        > You walk on lighter by an amount that has nothing to do with the weight.
    - [grey] Leave a small offering and move on `leave_offering` — result: xp: 4
      - result: You leave a few coins. The flags flutter in farewell.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_angulimala_pursuit:
- **The Garland** `hell_angulimala_pursuit` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > The road ahead is clear except for one figure, standing still. Behind him: several bodies. He watches you approach with the calm attention of someone who has made his peace with violence.
    >
    > Angulimāla. You know the name even here. He does not move to block you. He just watches — to see what you will do.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Give him a wide berth. Some problems aren't yours to solve. `walk_around`
      - result: He watches you go. You feel the weight of his attention until the road curves out of sight.
    - [blue] Walk toward him — not around him. Calmly. `walk_toward` — requires yoga 5 · result: add_trait: merciful
      - result:
        > He watches you walk toward him. The calm does not waver — you are not afraid of him, and it shows in every step. Something shifts behind his eyes. He has met this once before, in a different life, a different road, and it ended the same way it ended him.
        >
        > "You're not afraid," he says. It is not a compliment. It is recognition.
        >
        > He turns and falls into step beside you.
    - [blue] Acknowledge what you see — not what he's done with it, but the skill itself. `acknowledge_the_craft` — requires martial_arts 4
      - result:
        > He tilts his head slightly. Most people flinch or reach for a weapon. You are looking at the bodies the way a craftsperson looks at joinery — reading method, not grieving consequence.
        >
        > "You know the difference," he says.
        >
        > You do. So does he. That turns out to be enough.
    - [yellow] His stillness isn't threat — read what it actually is, and act on it. `read_the_stillness` — requires roll awareness vs normal · success: add_trait: clear_eyed
      - success:
        > You see it — the absolute composure of someone who is tired. Not of violence. Of the point of it.
        >
        > "You're done," you say. Not a question.
        >
        > A long silence. Then: "I need somewhere that isn't this."
        >
        > You offer that. He follows.
      - failure: Your movement reads wrong — a reach, a hesitation. He has spent a long time watching for exactly that. He moves before you finish the thought.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_black_lodge:
- **Black Lodge** `hell_black_lodge` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > The entrance is half-buried in the earth, marked only with a crooked khatvanga topped with a skull and streaming black ribbons reeking of smoke and poison. As you enter, the darkness overwhelms you - until you notice the glint of a sneering smile.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask to learn `#0`
      - result: The smile does not move. A hand gestures to a list scratched into the wall. Spells. Prices. No preamble.
    - [blue] You already know how to hold something. Say so. `secret_bearer_welcome` — requires trait: secret_bearer · result: xp: 20 · add_trait: secret_bearer
      - result:
        > The doorkeeper asks one question. Your answer is not the right one, but the way you decline to elaborate apparently is.
        >
        > You are shown further in than most, and what is discussed there stays where it was discussed.
    - [grey] Back out `#2`
      - result: You step back into the light. The khatvanga watches you leave.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_blisterfang:
- **Blisterfang** `hell_blisterfang` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > The red devil sprawled across three chairs outside a slag-side drinking house is enormous, cheerful, and entirely unbothered by the four separate people currently glaring at him from across the yard.
    >
    > "Blisterfang," he agrees, when you say the name. "Everyone's looking for me this season. It's flattering, honestly."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Tell him the ember merchant wants paying `collect` — result: xp: 12 · flags: {'blisterfang_found': True}
      - result:
        > "He does," Blisterfang says. "He absolutely does." He does not reach for a purse. He does, however, stop sprawling, which from a devil that size is a whole sentence.
        >
        > You have found him. Getting the money out of him is going to be a separate piece of work.
    - [grey] Take the payment off him `fight`
      - result:
        > "Ah," he says, delighted, getting up. "One of *those* collectors." The four people glaring from across the yard suddenly become extremely interested in the wall.

He is enormously relieved to be reminded and pays on the spot, in coin, counted out twice because he loses his place.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_bone_archer_camp:
- **Bone Archer Camp** `hell_bone_archer_camp` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A fortified camp of skeleton warriors — most armed with bows, some with knives. They regard you with hollow eyes. One of them, slightly larger than the rest, has set up a makeshift trading post.

    - [blue] Ask one of the archers to teach you `training` — requires ranged 1

    - [yellow] Lift something from the rack while no one is looking `steal` — requires roll finesse vs normal · success: items: ['hunting_bow', 'throwing_knife']
      - success:
        > Skeletons don't blink. What they do have is peripheral vision — but yours is better. You slip a bow from the rack while the trader skeleton is occupied. You are forty paces gone before anyone counts the inventory.

rendered.Events › hell › hell_bone_arena:
- **Bone Arena** `hell_bone_arena` — realm: hell
  - text:

  - choices:
    - [grey] Step into the arena and fight `fight` — result: gold: moderate
      - result: (empty)
    - [blue] Issue a formal challenge to the current champion `challenge` — requires strength 15 · result: xp: 12 · gold: moderate · items: ['good_iron_weapon']
      - result: The gatekeeper nods with respect and lets you in.
    - [blue] Narrate the fight dramatically for the crowd `narrate` — requires performance 3 · result: xp: 10
      - result: The crowd shifts from baying for blood to hanging on your words; gatekeeper laughs hard enough to let you through without charging.
    - [grey] Bet on one of the fighters `bet` — result: xp: 5 · gamble: {'type': 'gold', 'win_chance': 0.5, 'win_multiplier': 2}
      - result: "Sure, take a seat in the tiers."
    - [blue] Enter as a knife-fighter — blades against the arena's weapons `knife_fight` — requires daggers 3 · result: xp: 12 · gold: moderate
      - result: The crowd goes quiet as you draw blades instead of the expected weapon. Then louder.
    - [blue] Fight unarmed — no weapons, just technique `unarmed_fight` — requires unarmed 3 · result: xp: 12 · gold: moderate
      - result: The gatekeeper grins wider than usual. The crowd loses its mind.
    - [blue] You were always going to. Do not pretend otherwise. `duelist_cannot_refuse` — requires trait: duelist · result: xp: 20 · gold: small
      - result:
        > The gatekeeper sees it happen — the moment the decision stops being a decision — and grins with all the rows of teeth at once.
        >

    - [blue] Tell them who they are about to watch. At length. `braggart_works_crowd` — requires trait: braggart · result: xp: 20 · gold: small
      - result:
        > Very little of it is true. All of it is delivered well, and the tiers are chanting a name by the end that is only approximately yours.
        >

    - [blue] The crowd is not the fight. Do not spend anything on the crowd. `composed_before_fight` — requires trait: composed · result: xp: 12 · gold: small
      - result:
        > You do not. You go out flat, unhurried and entirely uninterested in the tiers, and your opponent — who has been playing to them for a living — cannot find the rhythm they were expecting.
        >

    - [blue] Pick up an arena bone-club — meet them on local terms `bone_mace` — requires maces 3 · result: xp: 10 · gold: moderate
      - result: You grab a femur from the ground and weigh it in your hand. The arena crowd approves of the improvisation.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_boss_yama_lt:

  - text:

rendered.Events › hell › hell_brimstone_lab:
- **Brimstone Lab** `hell_brimstone_lab` — realm: hell

rendered.Events › hell › hell_burning_library:
- **The Burning Library** `hell_burning_library` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A library is on fire.
    >
    > Not metaphorically — the entire building is actively burning, shelves collapsing, books falling in cascades of sparks. But at the center, visible through the inferno, an enormous bookshelf stands intact, its contents still whole.
    >
    > The fire has been burning long enough that the outer walls have almost collapsed. It will reach the center shelf soon.
  - choices:
    - [yellow] Dash through the flames to save what you can `brave` — requires roll constitution vs easy · success: xp: 10 · items: ['scroll_firebolt', 'scroll_lesser_heal'] · failure: xp: 5 · items: ['scroll_lesser_heal']
      - success:
        > You cover your head and run. The heat is enormous. You reach the center shelf, grab armfuls without looking, and sprint back as a beam comes down behind you.
        >
        > Singed, coughing, but standing. In your arms: books that are ancient and intact and unlike anything you have seen before. You have no idea what language they are in. That feels like a problem for later.
      - failure:
        > The heat drives you back before you reach the center. You grab one book from shelves near the entrance — old, smoke-damaged, but intact — before the entrance collapses.
        >
        > You stand outside, coughing, clutching a book you saved. The center shelf burns.
    - [blue] Command the flames to clear a path `fire_magic` — requires fire_magic 2 · result: xp: 14 · items: ['scroll_firebolt', 'mana_potion']
      - result:
        > You reach into the fire and speak to it. It takes a moment — the fire here is old and set in its ways — but it responds. A corridor of cooler air opens before you, the flames pulling back on either side.
        >
        > You walk to the center shelf calmly and take your time selecting. The books feel important in a way you cannot explain. You exit as the building finally collapses behind you in a controlled exhale.
    - [grey] Shout to see if anyone is still inside `rescue` — result: xp: 8 · items: ['demon_key']
      - result:
        > You cup your hands and call into the flames.
        >
        > Silence. Then: a cough. Then a small demon emerges from behind a burning pillar, clutching a ledger to its chest with both arms, absolutely refusing to put it down despite the circumstances.
        >
        > You pull it out by the collar. It stands outside looking humiliated — not by the rescue, but by the fact that it needed one.
        >
        > 'The accounts,' it says, still holding the ledger. 'I couldn't leave the accounts.' It presses a key into your hands. 'For an archive in the eastern quarter. Everything there is in order too. In case anyone asks.' It walks away with dignity it has not entirely earned.
    - [blue] Build a fireproof carry-container from materials at hand `construct_container` — requires smithing 3 · result: xp: 12 · items: ['scroll_firebolt', 'scroll_lesser_heal']
      - result:
        > You find fire-hardened bricks from the outer wall, a metal frame, hinges from a collapsed cabinet. The construction takes twenty minutes you don't quite have. But it works — a crude sealed box, clay-and-ash compound holding against the heat.
        >
        > You carry it in, load the best of the center shelf's contents methodically, and exit as the roof comes down behind you. The box is intact. The books inside are dusty but unburned.
    - [blue] It is a burning building. Leave the burning building. `incurious_leaves` — requires trait: incurious · result: xp: 22 · pressure: space-8
      - result:
        > You leave the burning building. This turns out to have been the correct structural assessment by a margin of about ninety seconds.
        >
        > Someone else will mourn the books.
    - [grey] Stand and witness the burning `witness` — result: xp: 3
      - result:
        > You stand in the heat and watch the library burn.
        >
        > At a certain point, the center shelf goes. The books go last — their pages lifting in the updraft, briefly bright, then dark.
        >
        > Something is lost. And yet, watching it, you also feel something like release — as though the books were finished being books and have become something else instead.
        >
        > You are not sure this is a useful thought. But it is the thought you have.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_burning_prisoner:
- **The Burning Prisoner** `hell_burning_prisoner` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A figure writhes in chains of molten metal, suspended above a pit of glowing coals. Their screams have long since faded to hoarse whispers. Despite their torment, their eyes are clear — filled with pain, but also a terrible awareness.
    >
    > 'Please,' they rasp. 'I know what I did. I know why I'm here. But I've suffered enough to understand. Please... if you can...'
  - choices:
    - [blue] Break the chains with your strength `free` — requires strength 14 · result: xp: 10 · items: ['demon_key']
      - result:
        > You grab the molten chains, gritting your teeth against the searing pain. With a mighty heave, the links shatter. The prisoner collapses, weeping.
        >
        > 'Thank you. I was a tyrant — I burned villages and tortured innocents. This was my punishment. But you... you showed mercy even to one who showed none.'
        >
        > They press something into your blistered hands — a key they'd been clutching all along.
    - [blue] Use healing magic to ease their suffering `heal` — requires white_magic 2 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You cannot break the chains, but you can mend what they've broken. Healing light flows from your hands, closing burns and numbing pain.
        >
        > The prisoner breathes freely for the first time in ages. 'You cannot free me — only I can do that, through true repentance. But this respite... it reminds me what kindness feels like. I had forgotten.' Tears trace clean lines through the soot on their face.
    - [blue] Offer a ritual purification to shorten their suffering `purification` — requires ritual 3 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > They nod somewhat absent-mindedly, numbed by the pain. You perform the rite as best you can under the circumstances. By the end they seem somewhat relieved — not freed, but perhaps a little less alone in their torment.
    - [grey] Ask what crime brought them here `talk` — result: xp: 4 · pressure: water-20, space-8
      - result:
        > 'I was a warlord,' they whisper. 'I burned a hundred homes. I thought fear was power. Now I know — fear is just fear. And cruelty is just cruelty dressed up as strength.'
        >
        > They look at you with haunted eyes. 'Don't make my mistakes, traveler. Power without compassion is just a longer chain.'
    - [blue] Use your gauntlets to grip the molten chain `armored_grip` — requires armor 3 · result: xp: 10 · items: ['demon_key']
      - result:
        > You know exactly where to grip through the gauntlets — the cooler sections, the fulcrum points. It takes strength and technique both. The chain holds long enough to matter, then a link gives way with a sound like a bell. The prisoner slides free and looks at their hands as if seeing them for the first time in a long while.
    - [blue] You are not going to be able to walk past this. `merciful_cannot_pass` — requires trait: merciful · result: xp: 30 · hp_loss: {'amount': 'light', 'target': 'random'} · add_trait: merciful · pressure: water+15
      - result:
        > You are not. Everyone in the party works this out at approximately the same moment you do, and the argument that follows is short.
        >
        > The chains are hot enough to cost you. The prisoner is down and breathing before you have finished deciding whether it was wise.
    - [grey] Turn away — this is their punishment `leave`
      - result: You walk on. Behind you, the prisoner's whispers fade back into the crackling of flames. The heat feels heavier on your shoulders.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_cold_hermit:

  - text:
    > He has dug himself into the lee of a boulder and built a wall of packed snow, and he is sitting in the shelter of it doing the only thing left to do, which is recite from memory and get it wrong.

rendered.Events › hell › hell_coolhead_aftermath:
- **Post-Clarity** `hell_coolhead_aftermath` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A black devil sits in the wreckage of what was recently a building. He is writing in a notebook. The walls around him are scorched. There is a crater behind him of impressive diameter.
    >
    > He looks up as you approach, expression neutral. He does not seem distressed. He seems, if anything, very calm — the particular calm of someone who has been through the seal-breaking and come out the other side of it.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Keep moving. Whatever happened here is between him and the building. `keep_moving`
      - result: He watches you go, then returns to his notes. The crater will be there long after both of you have moved on.
    - [blue] Look at what he's writing. Recognize what he's actually documenting. `recognize_the_documentation` — requires learning 4
      - result:
        > The notes are behavioral — not damage assessment but internal process, the phenomenology of the retort breaking. He is treating himself as a specimen.
        >
        > "You're cataloguing it," you say.
        >
        > "If I don't, who will?" He glances at the crater. "This is the third time. The interval is getting shorter. I should understand the mechanism."
        >
        > You talk for a while about mechanisms. By the end, he is walking with you.
    - [blue] Offer a different kind of stillness — not suppression, but actual peace. `offer_actual_calm` — requires yoga 3
      - result:
        > You settle beside him and demonstrate what you mean — not blocking the feeling but letting it move through without accumulating. He watches with the careful attention of someone encountering an unfamiliar technique.
        >
        > "I've been treating it like a pressure problem," he says slowly. "Structural."
        >
        > "It isn't."
        >
        > "No." He closes the notebook. "Show me that again, and I'll come with you."
    - [yellow] Ask how it felt. Without judgment — you are genuinely curious. `ask_how_it_felt` — requires roll charm vs easy
      - success:
        > He blinks. Most people, apparently, do not ask that.
        >
        > "Clarifying," he says, after a moment. Then, more slowly: "Like setting down something I'd been carrying so long I'd forgotten its weight."
        >
        > He looks at the crater again. "The building was empty. I made sure."
        >
        > "I didn't ask."
        >
        > "No." He stands, brushing ash from his robe. "You want a sorcerer who's done suppressing things?"
      - failure:
        > He looks at you with the polite wariness of someone who has heard that question before and found it a prelude to a lecture. He answers briefly and returns to his notes. The conversation does not develop.

rendered.Events › hell › hell_cursed_pilgrim:

      - result: A 40-minute forensic argument takes place. The bureaucrat is shaken and visibly tired. Finally, he waves you through, muttering to himself.
    - [blue] Point out that you cannot be subject to an official without a valid 16-F operating license `comedy_license` — requires comedy 2 · result: xp: 10
      - result: Stumped at first, the devil taps his quill against his chin, then nods slowly. Game recognizes game. He waves you through without another word.
    - [blue] Do not give your name. Do not give any name. `debtor_avoids` — requires trait: debtor · result: xp: 30 · pressure: air-8
      - result:
        > The clerk wants a name for the ledger and you supply one, fluently, along with a district and a plausible reason for travel.
        >
        > It is not your name. You have had a great deal of practice at this and it shows in all the wrong ways.
    - [blue] Talk. Keep talking. Do not stop talking. `braggart_talks_through` — requires trait: braggart · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > Forty minutes later the clerk has heard about three campaigns you were not in, a title you do not hold, and a mutual acquaintance who does not exist.
        >
        > He stamps the form to make it stop.
    - [blue] It is a clerk with a form. Let him have his form. `patient_waits_it_out` — requires trait: patient · result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > You answer every question in order, including the four that are the same question, and you do not once indicate that you have noticed.
        >
        > The clerk, who is braced for a fight the way clerks always are, has nothing to push against and stamps the thing in half the usual time.
    - [blue] You have been standing at this table for a very long time. `hot_tempered_snaps` — requires trait: hot_tempered · result: xp: 10 · gold: -15 · pressure: water-12
      - result:
        > You are two sentences into telling him what you think of the table, the quill and the entire apparatus before anyone can get a hand on your arm.
        >
        > The form is stamped eventually. It is stamped with an annotation, and the annotation will be waiting at the next checkpoint.
    - [blue] Lift the official seal and forge yourself a transit pass `forge_pass` — requires thievery 3 · result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > While arguing about Section 12, Subsection B, you palm the bureaucrat's official seal from the desk. A minute later you hand over a transit pass that is, technically, correct in every particular except that you wrote it yourself.
        >
        > The demon examines it at length. Stamps it. Files it. Waves you through.
        >
        > 'Everything in order. Move along.'
rendered.Events › hell › hell_demon_dojo:
- **The Demon Dojo** `hell_demon_dojo` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A stone courtyard surrounded by scorched walls, where a dozen demons practice combat forms with absolute precision. There is something almost beautiful about it — the focus, the discipline, the complete commitment to mastery.
    >
    > The sensei demon — larger than the others, covered in old scars — spots you and points with a clawed finger. Then gestures inward. An invitation.
  - choices:
    - [blue] Join the training session `train` — requires strength 12 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You strip off your pack and join the ranks. The sensei demon watches you critically, adjusting your stance twice without gentleness. The training is brutal but honest — no cruelty, just high standards.
        >
        > An hour later, bruised and exhausted, you bow. The sensei returns the bow — once, precisely. You have been accepted as a student, at least for today.
    - [yellow] Challenge one demon to a friendly bout `spar` — requires roll finesse vs easy · success: xp: 10 · failure: xp: 5
      - success:
        > You bow to your opponent and take your stance. It's a hard fight — the demon is fast and skilled — but you hold your own, forcing it back several times.
        >
        > The bout ends in a draw by mutual acknowledgment. The other demons stamp their feet in approval. You have earned something here that is not easily named.
      - failure:
        > You are put flat on your back within thirty seconds. The demon stands over you, then offers a hand up. The others are not unkind about it — they have all been put on their backs before.
        >
        > 'Again,' the sensei says. You last longer the second time.
    - [blue] Observe the forms carefully without participating `watch` — requires learning 1 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You find a wall to lean against and watch. These forms are old — older than you expected, derived from styles you half-recognize. The demons practice them with perfect fidelity, generation after generation.
        >
        > You learn more from watching than you could from participation. Certain sequences embed themselves in your muscle memory through pure observation.
    - [blue] Demonstrate your empty-hand technique `unarmed_technique` — requires unarmed 3 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You step onto the practice floor without a weapon. The training stops. The sensei crosses its arms and watches. You run through your forms — clean, deliberate, unflinching. When you finish, the demons exchange a look. The sensei inclines its head once.
        >
        > 'Not our style. But real.' You train alongside them for an hour. The forms absorb each other at the edges.
    - [blue] Assert yourself as a senior practitioner — take over the session `leadership_session` — requires leadership 4 · result: xp: 14
      - result:
        > You step in and redirect the group through a correction sequence — you've seen this error before, in better-equipped dojos. The sensei observes with narrowed eyes. Then steps back.
        >
        > You run the session for thirty minutes. The demons are better for it. The sensei says nothing at the end, which is the only acknowledgment available.
    - [blue] Ask to stand in the back row and do the forms with them. `ascetic_forms` — requires trait: ascetic · result: xp: 20 · skill_up: {'skill': 'martial_arts', 'amount': 1}
      - result:
        > Nobody objects. Nobody helps, either — you get the form wrong for two hours and are corrected exactly once, by a demon who does not break their own rhythm to do it.
        >
        > The correction is worth the two hours.
    - [grey] Decline the invitation and move on `leave`
      - result: You bow respectfully at the entrance and continue on your way. The sensei watches you leave without expression. The training continues without pause.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_demon_marketplace:
- **The Demon Marketplace** `hell_demon_marketplace` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A chaotic bazaar has assembled in the middle of the lava fields — dozens of stalls selling weapons, memories, bottled emotions, demon-forged equipment, and items you cannot categorize. The merchants are a mix of demons, damned souls, and creatures that do not appear to belong to any known category.
    >
    > A sign over the entrance reads: NO FIGHTING. NO UNAUTHORIZED FIRE (the sign is on fire). NO RETURNS.
    >
    > The noise is extraordinary.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Browse the marketplace stalls `browse` — result: xp: 2
      - result:
        > You move through the stalls, shoulder to shoulder with demons and the damned alike. It is, despite everything, a marketplace — and there is something almost comforting about the familiar rhythms of commerce.
    - [blue] Seek out the best deals with expert knowledge `trade_expert` — requires trade 2 · result: xp: 8 · items: ['fire_crystal']
      - result:
        > You spend an hour working the stalls with professional efficiency — checking quality, testing weights, haggling at the right moments. You find a stall in the back that others seem to avoid, its proprietor a very old demon sitting behind a display of items none of the other merchants will look at directly.
        >
        > 'Good eye,' the demon says. 'The things nobody wants are often the things someone needs.' The prices are fair. The goods are unusual.
    - [blue] Find the restricted goods in the back alleys `back_alley` — requires guile 2 · result: xp: 6 · items: ['scroll_firebolt']
      - result:
        > You find the alley behind the main stalls where the less official commerce happens. A hooded demon with careful eyes offers things the main market won't stock — items with complicated histories, scrolls from restricted collections, objects whose provenance cannot be confirmed.
        >
        > You leave with a scroll and a sense of mild unease.
    - [blue] Survey the market systematically — map what's actually here `systematic_survey` — requires logistics 2 · result: xp: 8 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > You work through the stalls in a pattern — quadrant by quadrant, comparing prices, noting quality, identifying which merchants specialize and which are generalists. By the end you have a clear picture of what this market contains and what it's worth.
        >
        > The most valuable stall turns out to be one you'd have walked past entirely: a narrow booth near the east exit, staffed by a demon with seven arms who handles bulk orders for things you didn't know you needed in quantity.
    - [grey] Watch the crowds instead of buying `watch` — result: xp: 4
      - result:
        > You find a good position and spend an hour simply watching.
        >
        > Three deals go wrong in interesting ways. Two go surprisingly right — a demon and a damned soul find they both want what the other has, and part looking pleased. A woman in grey robes stands before a stall selling memory-jars, reading the labels, and cries quietly in front of one that says: 'Tuesday, Age 7.'
        >
        > She doesn't buy it. Neither would you.
    - [blue] Every stall here is run by somebody bored. `flirt_works_the_stalls` — requires trait: flirt · result: xp: 20 · gold: small · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > They are, and boredom is the only currency you have never been short of.
        >
        > You do not buy anything at a discount. You are simply given three things over the course of an afternoon, by three different people, each of whom believes they started it.
    - [blue] You walk the whole market and want none of it. `content_buys_nothing` — requires trait: content · result: xp: 15 · pressure: earth+10, fire+8
      - result:
        > This is a strange sensation in a place engineered to produce the opposite, and one of the vendors follows you for a while trying to work out what is wrong with you.
        >
        > You leave with your purse intact and an unusual amount of goodwill from the one stallholder who understood.
    - [blue] The crowd noise here is total. `hard_of_hearing_misses` — requires trait: hard_of_hearing · result: xp: 22 · gold: -20 · pressure: air-8
      - result:
        > You catch about one word in four, and the one in four does not include the part where the vendor names the real price, or the part where somebody behind you says your description out loud.
        >
        > You find out about the second one later.
    - [yellow] Strike up conversation with vendors — gather market intelligence through friendly haggling `friendly_haggle` — requires roll charm vs easy · success: xp: 8 · failure: xp: 3
      - success:
        > Vendors talk more than they mean to when someone seems genuinely interested. By the time you've moved through half the market, you know which stalls are fronts, which goods are mislabeled, and where the real bargains are buried.
      - failure:
        > One vendor takes your interest as an insult to their pride and raises their prices to spite you. The word spreads faster than you'd like. You pay more for the same goods and leave resolving to be less obvious next time.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_demon_patrol:
- **Demon Patrol** `hell_demon_patrol` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > Three demons in frost-crusted armor block the path ahead. Their captain, a horned brute with blue-black skin, raises a jagged halberd.
    >
    > "No one passes without the Warden's permission. State your business or prepare to suffer."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Draw your weapon and attack `fight`
      - result: (empty)
    - [blue] Convince them you serve the Warden `negotiate` — requires charm 15 · result: xp: 8
      - result: "Well, if you say so."
    - [yellow] Throw a bag of gold and slip past while they argue amongst themselves `sneak` — requires roll finesse vs normal · success: xp: 6
      - success: Maybe sometimes it's true that greed is good.
      - failure: They look on you with confused pity and draw their weapons.
    - [grey] Offer them gold to look the other way `bribe` — result: xp: 3
      - result: They quickly pocket the gold and step aside.
    - [blue] Strike fast and precisely — take them down before they can sound the alarm `daggers_blitz` — requires daggers 3 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You move in fast, targeting the gaps in their armor. They barely have time to react before the first one goes down. The fight continues, but the terms are yours.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_dvijihva_chase:
- **Two Invoices** `hell_dvijihva_chase` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A blue devil is moving through the junction ahead with the practiced urgency of someone who has been in this exact situation before. He checks both approaches at every turn, tracks two separate routes in his head simultaneously, and is doing it with an air of irritated professionalism.
    >
    > You can hear the reason why from both directions. Two sets of footsteps. Two sets of clients who have recently compared notes.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Not your problem. Clear the junction before the clients arrive. `not_your_problem`
      - result:
        > You get out of the way. A few junctions later, you hear a brief commotion behind you. Then silence. Whether that means he escaped or didn't, you genuinely can't tell.
    - [blue] Help him play both clients — you take one side, he takes the other. `manage_both_pursuers` — requires guile 4
      - result:
        > You split without discussing it — instinct meeting instinct. Ten minutes later, both clients have been sent in wrong directions, each convinced the other one was dealt with.
