rendered.Events › hell › hell_samvibrahmi_fortres:
- **Security Theater** `hell_samvibrahmi_fortress` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A roadside ruin has been transformed. Tripwires — visible only if you know what to look for. Sight-lines from every approach accounted for. A small figure inside is crouched over what appears to be a very precise map, muttering assessments of approach vectors.
    >
    > He looks up when he realizes you've reached the interior of his perimeter without triggering a single countermeasure. His expression cycles through surprise, calculation, and something that might be professional offense.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Announce yourself calmly and give him time to collect himself. `announce_yourself`
      - result:
        > He accepts this with dignity and proceeds to document your entry vector in significant detail. You exchange brief pleasantries and move on. He returns to his map.
    - [blue] Walk him through exactly how you got past every single one of his defenses. `walk_him_through_it` — requires comedy 4
      - result:
        > You do it with affection — the way you'd point out a brilliant mistake to someone you respected. By the third countermeasure you breached without noticing, his expression has moved from offense to pained hilarity.
        >
        > By the seventh, he is laughing despite himself.
        >
        > "It's the cabbage cart problem," he says finally. "You plan for every threat you can imagine, and then—"
        >
        > "The one you didn't imagine."
        >
        > "Yes." He folds the map. "Traveling with you would be very bad for my threat assessments. I'll do it."
    - [blue] Identify the one gap in his defenses he hasn't thought of yet. `find_the_gap` — requires guile 5
      - result:
        > You point to a spot on his map. "From there. At this elevation, in rain. You've assumed flat-light approach vectors."
        >
        > He stares at the spot. His eye twitches once.
        >
        > "That's — " He stops. "I have been working on this for three weeks."
        >
        > "I know."
        >
        > Another pause. "Do you want a job? I mean — I assume you have a job. Can I have a job? The perimeter here is clearly inadequate."
    - [yellow] Invite him to redirect all this preparation into something that actually makes sense. `make_it_useful` — requires roll charm vs normal
      - success:
        > "You've put all this work into defending a ruin that no one was going to attack anyway," you say. "Travel with me and I can promise you: the threats will be real."
        >
        > He looks at you. Then at his map. Then at you again.
        >
        > "The threats will be real," he repeats slowly, as though tasting the words.
        >
        > "Genuinely dangerous. Multiple approaches. Poor visibility. Everything you've been preparing for."
        >
        > He rolls up the map with the energy of a man who has finally been understood.
      - failure:
        > He considers your offer carefully, then shakes his head. "The threats out there are speculative. The threat models in here are documented." He taps his map. "I will join you when I have finished mapping all approaches to this ruin."
        >
        > You look at the ruin. It has approximately forty approach vectors. You will not wait.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_scroll_in_the_drift:
- **Something in the Drift** `hell_scroll_in_the_drift` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A corner of oiled cloth shows above the snow at the base of a wind-scoured ridge — the kind of thing that has been buried and uncovered a dozen times by the same wind and will be buried again by evening.
    >
    > Something is wrapped in it.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Dig it out `dig` — result: xp: 14 · flags: {'mantra_scroll_found': True}
      - result:
        > A scroll case, sealed, dry inside. The scroll within is a sequence of protective mantras copied in a careful old hand, and the cold has not touched a single character of it.
    - [blue] Read the mantras before wrapping them back up `read` — requires ritual 3 · result: xp: 24 · learn_spell: {'school': 'white_magic'} · flags: {'mantra_scroll_found': True}
      - result:
        > They are cold-protection mantras, and they are a good set — the third one in particular is a variant you have not met, and you copy it into your own book before resealing the case. Whoever lost this lost something they will not survive the season without.
    - [blue] Read the ground — where did it come from? `tracks` — requires awareness 13 · result: xp: 20 · items: ['item_random'] · flags: {'mantra_scroll_found': True}
      - result:
        > The cloth did not blow here. It was dropped by someone moving north-east along the ridge line at a stumble, and there is a second set of prints behind the first, keeping pace and not closing. Somebody was being followed and shed weight to move faster.
        >
        > You take the scroll, and you take the bearing.
    - [grey] Leave it to the drift `leave`
      - result: By evening the wind has covered the corner of cloth again, as it has a dozen times before.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_serji_watching:
- **Old Habit** `hell_serji_watching` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A red devil stands apart from a pit fight, watching. He is the biggest person in the vicinity by a significant margin and the only one not involved. Arms crossed. Expression unreadable.
    >
    > The fighters below are working hard. He looks like he stopped caring about the outcome some time ago but cannot quite bring himself to walk away.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Walk past. Some people need to find their own door. `walk_past`
      - result: He doesn't look at you. The fight continues below. You leave him to his watching.
    - [blue] Stand beside him and watch. Let him see you understand what you're looking at. `stand_beside_him` — requires unarmed 4
      - result:
        > You stand beside him. You watch the same fight. After a while, he speaks without looking at you.
        >
        > "He's winning because the other one is afraid of his left hand. Doesn't know that himself yet."
        >
        > "I see it," you say.
        >
        > He looks at you sideways. A long pause. "You training anyone?"
        >
        > "I could use someone who knows what they're looking at."
    - [blue] Tell him what you're doing. Make it worth leaving this for. `offer_something_worth_following` — requires leadership 5
      - result:
        > He listens without interrupting. When you finish, the pit fight has ended below — neither of you noticed.
        >
        > "The gym stopped meaning anything when I got to the top of it," he says. "What you're describing hasn't got a top."
        >
        > He uncrosses his arms. "Alright."
    - [yellow] Ask him why he still watches, if he's done with it. `ask_why_he_still_watches` — requires roll charm vs normal
      - success:
        > He's quiet for a long moment. Then: "Habit. No other reason."
        >
        > "That's the saddest thing I've heard today."
        >
        > Something in his face shifts — surprise, maybe, that anyone would say that. Then something closer to a laugh.
        >
        > "Yeah," he says. "Probably is." He turns from the pit. "You going somewhere?"
      - failure: He looks at you once, the way you look at a bad technique — briefly, to catalogue what's wrong. Then back to the fight. He doesn't answer.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_sigh_of_relief:
- **A Sigh of Relief** `hell_sigh_of_relief` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > You feel strangely drawn towards a clearing, where among the bleakness a figure stands shining softly. A bodhisattva from the higher realms has come to the Hells to give offerings and teach the suffering shades.
    >
    > As you come closer you see piles of food, drink, and medicine manifesting from thin air, imps swarming around and swallowing mouthfuls.
  - choices:
    - [blue] Meditate in the presence of the Bodhisattva `meditate` — requires yoga 2 · result: xp: 12 · add_trait: touched_by_grace
      - result:
        > As you settle down and focus, you recognize there is no boundary between you. The teacher smiles and raises their hand to bless you.
        >
        > A warmth spreads through your body — not the burning heat of this realm, but something gentler. Something remembered.
    - [blue] Listen to the teachings `listen` — requires focus 14 · result: xp: 10 · add_trait: touched_by_grace
      - result:
        > Impermanence, compassion, joy. It seems like you have heard these words before, but long forgotten their meaning.
        >
        > The bodhisattva speaks without urgency, as though time here is different — and perhaps it is. When the teaching ends, the words continue to resonate somewhere you cannot quite locate.
    - [grey] Come and take your fill `partake` — result: xp: 8 · restore: {'hp_percent': 100, 'mana_percent': 100, 'stamina_percent': 100}
      - result:
        > For a moment, all your fears and hopes dissolve into the present moment. You are content.
        >
        > The food tastes like nothing you have eaten in this realm — clean, simple, nourishing. Your wounds close. Your mind clears. Your body remembers what it feels like to be whole.
    - [grey] Rush in and take as much as you can `grab` — result: xp: 0 · add_trait: covetous
      - result:
        > You shove past the imps and grab armfuls of food and medicine — but as your hands close around them, they dissolve like mist. The clearing shimmers. The bodhisattva regards you with an expression that is not disappointment but something closer to recognition.
        >
        > The scene vanishes as if it was never there.
    - [yellow] Open yourself precisely — ask without words for what your situation most needs `specific_teaching` — requires roll awareness vs normal · success: xp: 15 · add_trait: touched_by_grace · failure: xp: 6
      - success:
        > The Bodhisattva's attention focuses on you directly, gently, like sunlight through a small window. Nothing is said — but something specific passes, fitted exactly to the shape of what you carry. You know what it is without being able to say it.
      - failure:
        > The peace reaches you — warmth and light after long cold. But the specific teaching you reached for remains just out of grasp. You receive the general blessing, which is not nothing.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_sineater_encounter:
- **The Thirteenth Name** `hell_sineater_encounter` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > Something is wrong with the stretch of road ahead. Not visibly — the landmarks are where they should be. But the space between them feels occupied in a way that has nothing to do with sight.
    >
    > The sensation of being read passes over you like cold water. Something vast and hungry has noticed you are here. It has twelve names already. It is considering a thirteenth.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Back away. Slowly. Entities like this respect nothing, but they respect distance. `back_away_carefully`
      - result: The presence recedes as you put ground between you. Whatever it is, it does not follow — not yet. The road normalizes behind you. You take a different route.
    - [blue] Greet it correctly — by speaking to what it is, not what it looks like. `address_its_nature` — requires black_magic 5
      - result:
        > You name its nature — not a name but a category, the oldest classification for entities born from shattering. The presence goes very still.
        >
        > Then, something shifts. The hunger is still there, but turned sideways. Curious.
        >
        > "You know what I am," it says. The voice comes from nowhere in particular.
        >
        > "Yes."
        >
        > "No one has said that before without running afterward."
        >
        > A form coalesces at the edge of sight — something like a person, the way that lightning is something like light. "I will walk with you for a while," it says. "I want to see what you do with that knowledge."
    - [blue] Offer it something other than a soul to absorb — a perspective from outside the hunger. `offer_perspective` — requires space_magic 4
      - result:
        > You open yourself to the emptiness rather than filling it — show it the space between things, where hunger has no object. For a moment the presence is genuinely disoriented.
        >
        > Then fascinated.
        >
        > "That is not a thing I have encountered," it says slowly. "Twelve names and none of them knew that."
        >
        > The form that solidifies is almost gentle. "Show me more of that."
    - [yellow] Let it read you — and don't come apart while it does. `hold_yourself_together` — requires roll focus vs difficult · failure: xp: -20
      - success:
        > The scrutiny is total. Every surface of yourself is turned over and examined. Most people fragment under that kind of attention — become something easier to absorb.
        >
        > You don't.
        >
        > A long pause. "You stayed yourself," it says, almost puzzled.
        >
        > "Yes."
        >
        > "Interesting. I should like to understand how." The form that takes shape beside you is curious rather than hungry — for now. "Lead on."
      - failure:
        > The scrutiny is too complete. For a moment you are not entirely sure which thoughts are yours. You stumble back, gasping.
        >
        > The presence withdraws, satisfied with the inspection if not the meal. You are whole — mostly. The road ahead feels different for a while.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_sinner_gang:
- **The Sinner Gang** `hell_sinner_gang` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A group of damned souls has made camp around a fire — not for warmth, none of them need warmth, but for the feeling of it. A former soldier, a tax collector, an artist, a merchant. They've made rules, share what they find, keep watch in shifts. It is, against all odds, working.
    >
    > One of them looks up as you approach.
    >
    > 'You're alive. Actual living. We don't get many of those.' A pause. 'Sit down. We're not going to hurt you.'
  - choices:
    - [grey] Share a meal and hear their stories `stories` — result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You sit with them and the stories come out — what they did, what they understand now about what they did, what they are still working out.
        >
        > The soldier burned a village on orders. The tax collector took more than was owed, always. The artist spent a life accepting credit for other people's work. The merchant let a business partner take the fall for a shared crime.
        >
        > None of them are done yet. But they are thinking clearly about it, which is more than many here manage. You leave feeling, strangely, less alone.
    - [grey] Trade supplies with them `trade` — result: xp: 4 · items: ['health_potion']
      - result:
        > They have things scavenged from wandering souls — small items, coins, a potion someone dropped. You have things from the living world. You trade fairly, taking what you need, giving what you can spare.
        >
        > The merchant among them negotiates with professional precision, which makes everyone laugh, including the merchant. 'Habits,' they say. 'Even here.'
    - [blue] Inspire them to give their suffering more purpose `inspire` — requires persuasion 2 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You talk to them for a long time — about suffering as instruction, about the difference between enduring and understanding, about what it would mean to actively help other souls in the hell realm rather than simply outlasting it.
        >
        > The words land differently here than they would in the living world. One of them begins to cry. Another says quietly, 'We could actually do something with our time here.'
        >
        > When you leave, they are still talking. Their camp looks like the beginning of something.
    - [blue] Help them organize more effectively `assign_roles` — requires leadership 3 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You spend an hour with them, helping them think through what they're actually trying to do and who is best suited to what. The soldier takes watch. The artist keeps morale. The merchant manages what they find. The tax collector, reluctantly, handles records — 'At least I'm using it for something real this time.'
        >
        > The structure clicks into place. They look more purposeful than any group has a right to in this realm.
    - [blue] Set up a sustainable rotation so the suffering doesn't compound `rotation_plan` — requires logistics 3 · result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > You map out their resources: what they have, what they need, what they can acquire, where the choke points are. The pattern of their suffering isn't random — there's a rhythm to it, and rhythms can be managed.
        >
        > You draw up a rotation that gives each of them genuine rest between the harder stretches. The tax collector calls it 'the first fair system I've ever been part of,' and laughs at themselves for saying it.
    - [grey] Watch from a distance without disturbing them `observe` — result: xp: 2
      - result:
        > You stop on the ridge above their camp and watch for a while. The fire. The four figures around it. The quiet conversation.
        >
        > One of them looks up and sees you. They raise a hand. You raise yours. They return to their conversation.
        >
        > That is enough, somehow. For both of you.
    - [blue] There is a game running at the edge of that fire. `gambler_joins` — requires trait: gambler · result: xp: 15 · gold: small · add_trait: gambler
      - result:
        > There is. It is crooked in a way you identify within four throws and decline to mention, since it is crooked in a direction you can work with.
        >
        > You leave before it becomes impolite to keep winning.
    - [blue] Sit down. These are, regrettably, your people. `drunk_belongs` — requires trait: drunk · result: xp: 30 · pressure: fire-10, water+5
      - result:
        > They make room without being asked, which is the thing about the damned — they can spot it.
        >
        > You are welcome here in a way that is not entirely comfortable to be welcome, and you leave with a name to drop and a headache.
    - [blue] They have a fire and a bottle and no particular plans. `night_drinker_stays_late` — requires trait: night_drinker · result: xp: 30 · add_trait: addiction · pressure: fire-15, earth-8
      - result:
        > So do you, now. The talk is good and the bottle is worse than the talk, and at some point in the small hours it stops being an evening and starts being a habit that has followed you into another realm.
        >
        > You will feel this one for a while.
    - [yellow] Join them at the fire and tell a story — one that might make the suffering mean something `tell_story` — requires roll charm vs easy · success: xp: 10 · failure: xp: 4
      - success:
        > They listen. Really listen — something rare here. By the end, someone is laughing in a way that sounds almost clean. Several of them clap you on the back as you leave.
      - failure:
        > 'That's a nice story,' says one of them, not unkindly. 'We've heard nicer. But sit down — you look like you've been walking for years.' You're welcome at the fire anyway.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_suffering_sage:
- **Suffering Sage** `hell_suffering_sage` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A figure sits at the summit of a frozen ridge, encased in ice up to the neck — only their face remains free, eyes open and clear. The oldest devils have forgotten when he appeared. Their expression is that of endless patience. As you come closer, they open their eyes a little.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask about the nature of suffering `suffering` — result: xp: 8
      - result: "All suffering comes from resistance to what is. The cold is not suffering. The resistance to the cold is suffering."
    - [blue] Enter deep meditation to receive their teaching directly `meditate` — requires yoga 3 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > Shivering from the cold gives way to stillness and stillness to a direct transmission beyond words. You see the endless wheels of resistance and acceptance turning. They have been here for a long time, and yet a long time they will stay.
    - [blue] Ask about the history of this realm `history` — requires learning 2 · result: xp: 10
      - result: "I was here when the realm was still young. The first being who entered was a judge convinced he attained true justice. He was here for a very long time."
    - [grey] Leave them to their vigil `leave`
      - result: Their eyes close again.
    - [yellow] Press forward and place your hand on the ice encasing them `touch_the_ice` — requires roll awareness vs difficult · success: xp: 20 · hp_loss: {'amount': 'medium', 'target': 'all'} · failure: xp: 5
      - success:
        > The cold is immense. But through it — something transmits directly, bypassing language: the sage's full experiential understanding of suffering as ground rather than obstacle. Your hand burns. The teaching lands intact. You will be finding its edges for a long time.
      - failure:
        > The cold defeats you. Your hand numbs within seconds and you pull back before contact. The sage's eyes follow you — not disappointed, just patient. They have centuries to wait.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_suspicious_gift:
- **Suspicious Gift** `hell_suspicious_gift` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A neatly wrapped package sits in the center of the path, as though placed deliberately. Red cloth, black cord. A tag: "For whoever needs this most."
    >
    > The package is warm to the touch. Nothing else in the cold hell is warm.
  - choices:
    - [yellow] Examine it carefully before opening `inspect` — requires roll awareness vs easy · success: xp: 8 · gold: 40 · items: ['health_potion'] · failure: xp: 3
      - success: Congratulations on your caution. The trap disarmed, you retrieve your loot safely.
      - failure: Triggered; theatrical but not lethal; package empty; a card: "Better luck with the next one."
    - [blue] Check it for traps with trained eyes `check_magic` — requires guile 1 · result: xp: 6 · gold: 25 · items: ['health_potion']
      - result: You find a magic seal and quickly scratch it until it's unrecognizable. The package opens cleanly with a health potion and some coins inside.
    - [grey] Open it with reckless optimism `open` — result: xp: 4 · gold: 40 · items: ['health_potion']
      - result:
        > A flash, a sound, blinding cold — then you're standing there holding a health potion and forty gold, entirely unharmed. Sometimes things are exactly what they appear to be.
    - [blue] Cut the cord carefully — avoid any trigger mechanisms `careful_cut` — requires daggers 2 · result: xp: 6 · gold: 40 · items: ['health_potion']
      - result:
        > You find the right angle and draw a single precise cut through the cord. The package opens clean, the trap still intact and inert, the contents untouched. A health potion and forty gold, secured without incident.
    - [blue] Assess it with professional eyes — you've handled worse `thievery_bypass` — requires thievery 3 · result: xp: 8 · gold: 45 · items: ['health_potion']
      - result:
        > The trigger mechanism is amateur work — a pressure seal under the bow. You disable it in thirty seconds without opening the package, then open it cleanly. Good loot, poorly protected.
    - [blue] Do not touch it. Find who is watching it. `paranoid_perimeter` — requires trait: paranoid · result: xp: 20 · pressure: air+10
      - result:
        > You spend twenty minutes on the surrounding rocks instead of the package, and you find him — a small demon flat behind a ridge with a good view and a bad hiding place.
        >
        > He runs. The package turns out to be exactly as bad as you assumed, and you do not open it.
    - [blue] It is a box. Walk past the box. `incurious_shrug` — requires trait: incurious · result: xp: 22 · pressure: space-5
      - result:
        > You walk past the box. Some hours later there is a sound behind you that you decline to investigate.
        >
        > Whoever it was for, it was not for you.
    - [grey] Leave it — gifts in hell are seldom genuine `leave`
      - result: You step around it cautiously; behind you, the package waits warm and patient.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_teahouse_cold:
- **Teahouse** `hell_teahouse_cold` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A low building crouches at the edge of the frozen waste, smoke leaking from the roof. Inside, a few silent figures nurse cups of something warm. The barkeeper glances up without expression.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Sit down `#0`
      - result: You take a seat. Nobody bothers you.
    - [blue] Watch how they are making it. Ask for the pot, not the cup. `tea_properly` — requires trait: tea_ritualist · result: xp: 20 · pressure: water+10, fire+5
      - result:
        > The proprietor looks at you for a moment longer than is comfortable, and then hands over the pot without a word, which in this establishment is an honour roughly equivalent to a title.
        >
        > You make it properly. Several of the silent figures relocate closer to the fire while you do.
    - [blue] Say nothing for an hour and listen to everyone else. `gossip_listen` — requires trait: gossip · result: xp: 20 · gold: small
      - result:
        > An hour buys you: two names worth avoiding, one road that is not as closed as the guard post claims, and the current price of a favour in this district.
        >
        > Nobody notices you listening. Nobody ever does.
    - [grey] Move on `#3`
      - result: You keep walking. The smell of smoke follows you longer than it should.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_teahouse_fire:
- **Teahouse** `hell_teahouse_fire` — realm: hell
  - text: A squat building half-buried in ash. The sign is burned off but the smell of tea — strong, smoky, almost pleasant — cuts through the sulphur. The door is open.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Step inside `#0`
      - result: The heat inside is almost comfortable compared to outside.
    - [blue] There is more than tea behind that counter, and you know it. `drunk_relapse` — requires trait: drunk · result: xp: 30 · gold: -20 · add_trait: night_drinker · pressure: fire-12, earth-8
      - result:
        > There is. It is bad, and there is a lot of it, and the proprietor pours without being asked twice.
        >
        > The evening goes somewhere. In the morning the party is short some coin and you are short some hours you would like back.
    - [blue] You know what is behind the counter and you know how many nights this makes. `night_drinker_again` — requires trait: night_drinker · result: xp: 30 · gold: -25 · add_trait: drunk · pressure: fire-12
      - result:
        > You do know how many nights this makes. That is new — the counting is new — and you order anyway, which is the part that settles the question.
        >
        > Nobody in the party says anything. Two of them exchange a look.
    - [grey] Move on `#3`
      - result: You leave the warmth behind.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_tejasimha_fire:
- **The Best Seat** `hell_tejasimha_fire` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A building is burning. Not collapsing, not yet — fully, magnificently on fire, the kind that takes your breath away from ten meters off.
    >
    > A red devil is standing inside it. He is laughing. Not the laughter of someone losing their mind — hearty, genuine, appreciative. He is watching it the way you watch a great performance.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Back away from the lunatic in the burning building. `back_away`
      - result: The laughter follows you down the road. The building eventually collapses. You're not sure what happened to him. Given everything, probably fine.
    - [blue] Step into the fire. Stand beside him. See what he's seeing. `step_into_the_fire` — requires fire_magic 4
      - result:
        > The heat is extraordinary. You let it move around you rather than fighting it. He notices immediately — turns to look at you with something like delight.
        >
        > "You're not burning," he says.
        >
        > "Neither are you."
        >
        > He grins. "I never do. Not on the inside." He gestures at the fire around you. "Beautiful, isn't it?"
        >
        > You stand together in it for a while before he follows you out.
    - [blue] Call something genuinely funny into the burning building. `call_from_outside` — requires comedy 4
      - result:
        > The laugh that comes back from inside the fire is different from before — surprised, real.
        >
        > His head appears at a burning window. "Who said that?"
        >
        > "Me."
        >
        > He stares at you through the smoke and flame for a moment. Then: "Wait there. I'm coming out."
    - [yellow] Hold your ground in the heat until he notices. Don't flinch. `hold_your_ground` — requires roll focus vs normal
      - success:
        > You plant your feet and stay. The heat is punishing. You don't move.
        >
        > His laughter slows. He turns. For the first time, he is actually looking at you — the person standing in a firestorm out of stubbornness or something he can't name yet.
        >
        > "You're interesting," he says. "Come here."
      - failure: The heat wins. You step back, eyes watering. The laughter inside the building doesn't pause. He didn't see you — or if he did, what he saw wasn't enough.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_temple_of_the_naga:
- **Temple of the Naga** `hell_temple_of_the_naga` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > In every world some beings are born innately attuned to the mindstreams of the Naga. Temples arise where they practice, communing with their reptilian friends and patrons through offerings of saffron milk, fruits and flowers.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask about their teachings `#0`

rendered.Events › hell › hell_the_invitation:
- **The Invitation** `hell_the_invitation` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > An ornate envelope rests on a flat rock in the middle of a lava field, as though placed there deliberately. It is sealed with black wax. Your name is written on the outside — not the name you are using in this life, but a name you know with absolute certainty is yours.
    >
    > The handwriting is beautiful.
    >
    > Inside: a map, a time, an address, and the words: 'It would please us greatly if you would attend. We have matters of mutual interest to discuss. Come alone.'
  - choices:
    - [grey] Follow the map `follow` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > The address leads to a formal dining room carved from black obsidian, lit by candles burning with a clean blue flame. A demon of apparent authority waits at the head of a long table — well-dressed, patient, carrying the specific stillness of someone who has planned this meeting carefully.
        >
        > 'We have been observing your journey,' it says. 'With interest. There is a matter we would like to discuss — something that would benefit both of us, if we can reach an agreement.'
        >
        > The conversation that follows is careful and illuminating. You learn things about the hell realm you did not know. You also decline the offer, politely, when it finally arrives.
        >
        > 'The offer stands,' the demon says as you leave. 'When you change your mind, you'll know how to reach us.' It does not say if.
        >
        > You notice, on the way out, that there is only one setting at the table. They knew you'd come alone.
    - [blue] Follow the map but arrive early and observe first `arrive_early` — requires guile 2 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You find the address an hour before the appointed time and settle in a position with a clear view of the entrance.
        >
        > Someone else has already arrived — a damned soul, young, with the hollow eyes of someone who has been suffering long enough to consider anything an improvement. They go inside. Through the wall (obsidian is surprisingly thin) you can hear the shape of the conversation without the words.
        >
        > A deal is being made. The soul wants something specific. The demon is offering it.
        >
        > You could intervene. You could also let them make their own choice — the soul is old enough to know what they're doing, even here.
        >
        > You wait until the soul emerges — lighter, in some way you cannot verify — then slip away before your own appointment time.
    - [blue] Examine the invitation for hidden enchantments `examine` — requires black_magic 2 · result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > You read the letter carefully with trained attention to what is not there.
        >
        > Three layers of enchantment. The first: a location beacon — someone has already noted that the invitation was opened. The second: a subtle compulsion toward compliance, minor enough to be deniable. The third: something you cannot fully name but that feels, precisely and strangely, like recognition — as though whoever wrote this has seen you before, in a context you cannot access.
        >
        > You burn the invitation. For a moment you feel watched from a very specific direction. Then nothing.
        >
        > The name they used for you, you will be thinking about for a while.
    - [grey] Set it back on the rock and walk on `ignore` — result: xp: 3
      - result:
        > You set the envelope back on the rock and continue on your way.
        >
        > Behind you, the envelope waits. A faint sense of disappointment from a specific direction — calm, professional, patient. The kind of disappointment that is already adjusting its timeline.
        >
        > Someday, you think, you will want to know what was in that letter.
    - [yellow] Look for signs of who placed this — tracks, timing, intent written in the ash `read_scene` — requires roll awareness vs easy · success: xp: 8 · failure: xp: 3
      - success:
        > The ash around the rock is undisturbed except for one set of prints — small, deliberate, placed and then retreated. No ambush position. No disturbance in the lava flow. Whoever left this came alone and didn't wait to watch. The invitation might be genuine.
      - failure: A new lava flow has already covered whatever marks were here. The ash tells you nothing. You're left exactly as uncertain as before.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_tormented_soul:
- **Tormented Soul** `hell_tormented_soul` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A ghostly figure sits amid the frost, weeping silently. Unlike the mindless lost souls, this one retains its form — the shape of an old woman in tattered robes.
    >
    > "Can you see me? Truly see me? So few can anymore..."
  - choices:
    - [blue] Use white magic to ease her suffering `help` — requires white_magic 1 · result: xp: 10
      - result: She dissolves into light with a sigh. In life, she was a healer who once turned away a sick wanderer for a lack of payment.
    - [grey] Sit beside her and listen `listen` — result: xp: 6
      - result: She speaks of small cruelties compounded until her breath grows a little longer and slower.
    - [blue] Perform a ritual to release her spirit `exorcise` — requires ritual 3 · result: xp: 12 · items: ['soul_stone']
      - result: You write a mandala of liberation by sight around her. She dissolves into light, leaving a piece of turquoise behind.
    - [grey] Walk past — you have enough of your own problems `ignore`
      - result: The weeping grows quieter, then stops. The cold deepens.
    - [blue] You know what it is like when the memory arrives uninvited. `haunted_knows` — requires trait: haunted · result: xp: 15 · pressure: water+12
      - result:
        > You do not offer advice, because there is none, and you do not tell them it passes, because you would be lying.
        >
        > What you do is stay until the worst of the current one is over. It is apparently not something anyone has done for them before.
    - [blue] Summon a guide spirit to show her the way forward `summon_guide` — requires summoning 3 · result: xp: 14
      - result:
        > You call a guide spirit — one of the patient ones, without agenda — and ask it to wait with her. It settles beside the old woman with the quality of something that has done this before.
        >
        > She looks at it for a long moment. Then at you. 'You can see me.' Not a question anymore. A fact, confirmed.
        >
        > The guide spirit takes her hand. Her form steadies. Something releases in her posture.
        >
        > You leave them together.

rendered.Events › hell › hell_veterans_camp:
- **Veterans' Camp** `hell_veterans_camp` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A sparse camp around a fire. The people here are old — old for hell, which means they have survived something most haven't. One of them watches you approach with calculating eyes.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask about training `#0`
      - result: "We can teach two things. Once each. Make your choices."
    - [blue] Sit down without being invited. They will not mind. `war_hardened_sits` — requires trait: war_hardened · result: xp: 15 · pressure: water+8
      - result:
        > They do not mind. Nobody asks where you served, because the question is not interesting to anyone here — what is interesting is whether you know how to sit at a fire without talking.
        >
        > You do. By morning you have been told three things about the road ahead that are not on any map.
    - [blue] One of them looks at you and knows. `sole_survivor_recognised` — requires trait: sole_survivor · result: xp: 20 · pressure: water+15, space+8
      - result:
        > She does not say anything about it. She moves along the log to make room, and later, when the fire is low, she says: 'It doesn't get quieter. You just get better at the noise.'
        >
        > It is not comfort. It is better than comfort, which is accuracy.
    - [grey] Move on `#3`
      - result: The veteran returns to staring into the fire.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_volcanic_cave:
- **The Volcanic Cave** `hell_volcanic_cave` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A cave entrance glows red with the heat of magma flowing within. The walls pulse with veins of liquid fire, casting dancing shadows. Deep within, you can hear a rhythmic sound — like a heartbeat, or the slow breathing of something enormous.
    >
    > The heat is nearly unbearable, but you can see the glint of valuables deeper inside.
  - choices:
    - [yellow] Brave the heat and explore the cave `enter` — requires roll constitution vs normal · success: xp: 10 · items: ['health_potion', 'fire_resistance_potion'] · failure: xp: 4
      - success:
        > You push through the searing heat, your body screaming in protest. The cave opens into a magma chamber where ancient demon forges still glow with purpose.
        >
        > Among the abandoned tools, you find fire-forged equipment of remarkable quality and a cache of supplies left by the last smith to work here.
      - failure:
        > The heat is too much. You stagger back, skin blistered, gasping for cooler air. You manage to grab a few things near the entrance before retreating, but the deeper treasures remain beyond your endurance.
    - [blue] Use fire magic to protect yourself from the heat `fire_resist` — requires fire_magic 2 · result: xp: 12 · items: ['fire_crystal', 'mana_potion']
      - result:
        > You weave a barrier of controlled flame around yourself, turning the cave's heat aside like water off oiled cloth. The magma parts before you as you walk deeper.
        >
        > The cave holds wonders — natural formations of crystallized fire magic, and at its heart, a forge still burning with the flames that were lit when Naraka was young. You take what you can carry.
    - [blue] Listen to the heartbeat sound from the entrance `listen` — requires learning 2 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You close your eyes and listen. The rhythm is too regular for a creature, too purposeful for nature. After long study, you realize — it's the pulse of the realm itself. Naraka has a heartbeat, and this cave is one of its arteries.
        >
        > The knowledge fills you with a deeper understanding of how the hell realm works. The suffering here isn't random — it has structure, purpose, even a kind of terrible beauty.
    - [blue] Move quickly and lightly between the thermal vents `grace_vent` — requires grace 2 · result: xp: 8 · items: ['health_potion', 'fire_resistance_potion']
      - result: Uncomfortable, but nevertheless doable — like so many things in life. You thread between the vents with quick, precise movements and find what you came for.
    - [grey] The heat is too dangerous — move on `leave`
      - result: You back away from the cave entrance. The glow within seems to pulse with disappointment, but sometimes survival is its own reward.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_wandering_peddler:
- **Wandering Peddler** `hell_wandering_peddler` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A hunched figure dragging a heavy sack waves you down.
    >
    > "Psst! Traveler! You look like you could use some supplies. I've got just the things — all cleaned up nice."
  - choices:
    - [grey] See what the peddler has to offer `browse`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Ask for directions and local knowledge `directions` — result: xp: 3
      - result: He starts talking a lot but making little sense. You catch bits and pieces about frozen ghosts on the lake, wandering monks and torture chambers.
    - [yellow] Grab his pack and run `steal` — requires roll finesse vs easy · success: items: ['iron_dagger', 'leather_cap', 'health_potion'] · pressure: water-15, earth-8
      - success:
        > You snatch the pack and sprint. Behind you, the peddler's shouts fade into confused silence. The bag contains more than you expected — and something that rattles like it's alive.
      - failure:
        > Your foot catches on a frozen rut. The peddler watches you sprawl, unmoved. "Not the first time," he says, gathering his bag. "Not the worst, either." He trudges on without another word. You are left with bruised dignity and nothing else.
    - [grey] Mug him outright `attack`
      - result: The peddler drops the sack. From the shadows, his associates — desperate, hollow-eyed souls — close in. He was never alone.
    - [blue] Haggle for better prices `haggle` — requires trade 2 · result: xp: 4 · gold: small
      - result: The trader seems amused, and after a short back-and-forth, grants you a discount. "Fine, fine. A fair deal." You walk away having spent less than expected.
    - [blue] He has told you the price. Tell him the real one. `scrimper_haggles` — requires trait: scrimper · result: xp: 20 · gold: small
      - result:
        > It takes eleven minutes and involves a detailed excursion into the condition of his sack.
        >
        > He settles well below where he started, calls you something unrepeatable, and shakes your hand.
    - [grey] Decline politely and move on `move_on`
      - result: "Your loss! If you change your mind, I'll be around. I'm always around."
rendered.Events › hell › hell_warden_strongroom:
- **The Warden's Strongroom** `hell_warden_strongroom` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A door of blue iron set into the ice, and behind it a room the cold has kept exactly as it was left: a desk, a ledger, a rack of seals on hooks.
    >
    > One hook is labelled and empty. The rest hold the authority to open every lock in the cold hells, and nobody has been in to count them for a very long time.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Take a warden's seal from the rack `take_seal` — result: xp: 12 · flags: {'cold_warden_seal_found': True}
      - result: Cold blue iron, heavier than it looks, stamped with a sigil that makes your thumb ache where it rests. Whatever this opens, it opens with authority.
    - [blue] Read the ledger before you touch anything `ledger` — requires learning 3 · result: xp: 22 · gold: 60 · flags: {'cold_warden_seal_found': True}
      - result:
        > Every seal is signed out against a prisoner's name and a sentence length. The empty hook belongs to a seal signed out four hundred years ago against a sentence of ninety days, never returned. Somebody is still in a box out there on a warrant that expired before this ice formed.
        >
        > You take a seal, and you take the ledger page too, because a name will matter more than a key.
    - [grey] Take everything that is not nailed down `strip` — result: xp: 10 · gold: 170 · items: ['item_random'] · flags: {'cold_warden_seal_found': True}
      - result: Seals, desk fittings, the good inkwell, and a strongbox that has clearly not been opened since the last audit.
    - [grey] Take nothing from a warden `leave` — result: xp: 4
      - result: You close the blue iron door behind you. The rack of seals stays on its hooks, and every lock in the cold hells stays shut.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_wardens_pit:
- **Warden's Pit** `hell_wardens_pit` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > A fortified post around a deep pit, guards drilling in formation on the parade ground. The warden — a scarred devil in heavy armor — watches them from the parapet.
    >
    > "Outsiders," she says, not looking at you. "You want something. They always do."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask to buy gear `browse`
      - result: She jerks her chin toward the supply depot.
    - [blue] Request combat training `training` — requires spears 1
      - result: She looks you over slowly. "You know how to hold a spear. The rest is discipline. Discipline costs coin."
    - [yellow] Slip into the supply depot while everyone is drilling `steal` — requires roll finesse vs normal · success: items: ['wooden_spear', 'leather_vest']
      - success:
        > The drilling formations create a predictable rhythm. You match it — moving only when boots hit the ground, stopping when they stop. The supply depot yields a spear and some armor before the rotation changes. You are back outside before anyone notices the count is off.
      - failure: The warden's voice carries across the entire pit: "I SAW THAT." She has not moved from the parapet. She does not need to.
    - [grey] Challenge the warden's authority — by force `attack`
      - result: The warden doesn't raise her voice. She just raises one finger. The drilling stops. The soldiers turn. "Show me what you've got," she says.
    - [grey] Leave `leave`
      - result: The drilling continues. You are not relevant to it.
rendered.Events › hell › hell_water_lily:
- **Still Water** `hell_water_lily` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > At the edge of a frozen river in the cold hell wastes, a blue-skinned woman stands alone. She is looking down at the ice. The water beneath it is visible, dark and still.
    >
    > She does not move when you approach. She has been here a while.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave her to her silence. Not every stillness wants company. `leave_her`
      - result: You walk on. The frozen river does not change. Neither does she.
    - [blue] Place your hand on the ice. Commune through it. `reach_through_water` — requires water_magic 4
      - result:
        > The cold travels up your arm. You let it. Something underneath the surface stirs — not the water, but her attention.
        >
        > She looks at your hand on the ice, then at you. "You're not afraid of it," she says.
        >
        > "No."
        >
        > She steps back from the river's edge for the first time in a long while. "Where are you going?"
    - [blue] Sit beside her. Say nothing. Wait. `sit_in_silence` — requires yoga 5
      - result:
        > You sit. You do not speak. The cold hell wind moves across the ice.
        >
        > After a long time — long enough that most people would have given up — she turns and looks at you properly for the first time.
        >
        > "You stayed."
        >
        > "Yes."
        >
        > She does not ask why. She seems to already understand. When you stand to leave, she stands with you.
    - [yellow] Say something to her — something real, not reassurance. `speak_plainly` — requires roll charm vs normal
      - success:
        > What you say is simple. Honest. Not an offer to fix anything — just acknowledgment of what she is looking at and why.
        >
        > She is quiet for a moment. Then: "You didn't try to talk me out of it."
        >
        > "No."
        >
        > She turns from the river. "I'll come with you."
      - failure:
        > She looks at you briefly, then back at the ice. The words weren't wrong, exactly — they just weren't right. She doesn't respond. The river holds her attention more completely than you do.

rendered.Events › hell › hell_yogini_circle:
- **Circle of the Yoginis** `hell_yogini_circle` — realm: hell
  - text:
    > The inward-facing side of this circular stone wall is carved with the bizarre forms of sixty four Yoginis. There is no ceiling, so the witches can land when they come flying from vast space to meet their earthly sisters.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Enter the circle `#0`

rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_alchemist_cam:
- **The Alchemist** `hg_alchemist_camp` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > A dré — a bodiless ghost inhabiting a suit of robes stuffed with dried herbs — floats above a bubbling cauldron. Jars of questionable substances line makeshift shelves carved from bone. It turns as you approach.
    >
    > "Customer or ingredient?" it asks cheerfully.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Browse what it has for sale `buy_potions`
      - result: (empty)
    - [blue] Offer to help with the brewing `assist` — requires alchemy 3 · result: xp: 12 · items: ['item_random']

    - [blue] Ask what's in the cauldron `ask_contents` — requires medicine 2 · result: xp: 10

    - [grey] Knock the cauldron over `knock_over`

rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_ancestor_spir:
- **Ancestor Spirit** `hg_ancestor_spirit` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > The shrine is small and very old and somebody has been maintaining it — swept, the offering-bowl clean, fresh dust patterns raked around the base. Above it hangs a presence rather than a shape.
    >
    > "You are not of my line," it says. It does not sound disappointed. It sounds like it is checking.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Bow and continue `leave` — result: xp: 4
      - result: "Go well," it says, and the presence settles back into the raked dust.
    - [grey] Leave something in the bowl anyway `offer` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > "Not of my line," it observes again, differently this time. The offering is accepted. Something eases in the air around the shrine that had been held for a long time.
    - [blue] Ask who has been sweeping the shrine `who_tends` — requires awareness 13 · result: xp: 20 · pressure: water+15
      - result:
        > Silence. Then: "I do." An ancestor spirit with no descendants left, maintaining its own shrine, raking its own dust, keeping up the observances for a family that ended. It has not admitted this out loud before. You spend an hour helping with the raking and it talks the entire time, about people eight hundred years dead, and you listen.
    - [blue] Somebody has been maintaining this. Take a turn. `mourner_keeps_it_up` — requires trait: mourner · result: xp: 30 · supplies: {'food': -2}
      - result:
        > The offerings are recent and the cloth has been changed within the month, which means somebody is walking a long way to do this and will not always be able to.
        >
        > You do what they have been doing, and you leave the shrine better stocked than you found it.
    - [blue] Offer to carry the line `adopt` — requires ritual 4 · result: xp: 28 · gold: 180 · items: ['item_random'] · add_trait: {'id': 'devout', 'target': 'player'}
      - result:
        > There is a rite for this — adoption across the line of death, so a family that has run out of living can be continued by someone willing to take the observance on. It is not a small thing to accept. You do it properly, with the responses, and the presence at the shrine becomes something with a stake in whether you live.
        >
        > It gives you what it has: its name, its protection, and the contents of a grave nobody else knows about.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_ancient_battl:
- **The Ancient Battlefield** `hg_ancient_battlefield` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > Weapons jut from the earth like iron flowers — spears, swords, shafts of arrows, all corroded past use but too numerous to count. The ground is more bone than dirt. Some of the fallen still twitch between the weapons, trapped between death and something worse, unable to move on.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Search the field for salvageable equipment `scavenge` — result: items: ['item_random']
      - result: You find something worth taking — and something finds you.
    - [blue] Consecrate the field and put the fallen to rest `put_to_rest` — requires white_magic 2 · result: xp: 15
      - result:
        > You walk the length of the field, speaking the words, touching each fallen fighter with blessing. The twitching slows. Stills. The field goes quiet for the first time since before either of your lifetimes.
    - [blue] Raise some of the fallen to fight beside you `raise_reinforcements` — requires black_magic 3 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > The words come up from somewhere old. Three fighters rise — ragged, half-formed, but battle-ready. They follow behind you with the patience of the dead, ready for the next fight.
    - [blue] Train among the fallen `train` — requires martial_arts 3 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > The field is a library of killing techniques if you know how to read it. You practice forms between the weapons for two hours, learning from the preserved evidence of old fighters.
    - [blue] Meditate among the dead `meditate` — requires yoga 3 · result: xp: 14
      - result:
        > "The ocean of samsara is itself a battlefield. I vow to end the battle — first inside, and eventually everywhere." The field is very quiet. The twitching figures slow. You sit with them until you feel the weight of the vow settle into something real.
    - [blue] You can read what happened here from where you are standing. `war_hardened_reads_field` — requires trait: war_hardened · result: xp: 15 · add_trait: war_hardened
      - result:
        > A line held, then folded from the left. The reserve went in late and went in wrong. Everything after that was arithmetic.
        >
        > You walk the field explaining it to nobody in particular, and the party is very quiet, and at the end of it you are more of a veteran than you were that morning.
    - [blue] Something in that jumble is not corroded. `sharp_eyed_spots` — requires trait: sharp_eyed · result: xp: 15 · items: ['item_random']
      - result: Nothing here should have survived. One thing has, under a shield that fell the right way up, and it is in the condition it was in on the day.
    - [blue] Survey the fallen armor — read who these were `survey_armor` — requires armor 3 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You walk the field reading armor the way others read books — construction methods, battle damage, repairs, the wear patterns of years of use. Three factions, at minimum, all fighting each other. The oldest armor is local; the other two came from somewhere else.
        >
        > One piece near the center shows signs of combat on all sides simultaneously. Whoever wore it died surrounded — held their ground far longer than the math suggested was possible.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_ancient_crypt:
- **Ancient Crypt** `hg_ancient_crypt` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > The crypt door is stone, and it is ajar — about a hand's width, which is both an invitation and a warning depending on which side of it opened.
    >
    > Dry air comes out. It smells of dust and cold iron and nothing organic at all.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Pull the door to and walk away `leave`
      - result: The stone grinds shut. It takes both hands and most of your weight, and it feels like the right thing to have done.
    - [grey] Go in `enter`
      - result: Two of them are standing just inside the door, one to each side, in the dark. They have been standing there since the door was last closed.
    - [blue] Listen at the gap before you open it `listen` — requires awareness 14 · result: xp: 18 · gold: 160 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > Nothing breathes in there, but something *shifts* — twice, at an interval, the way a person shifts weight when they have been standing a long time. Two of them, flanking the door. You open it wide instead of squeezing through, and take them from outside with the light behind you, which turns a bad fight into a short one.
    - [blue] Read the door before touching it `seals` — requires ritual 3 · result: xp: 26 · gold: 180 · items: ['item_random']
      - result:
        > The inscription is a service contract. The two inside are not guardians in any hostile sense — they are staff, on a term of duty that expired four hundred years ago because the family that hired them stopped existing. You go in and tell them so. There is a pause you would describe as stunned. Then they hand over the keys, formally, and lie down in the alcoves they were meant to occupy in the first place.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_black_lodge:
- **Black Lodge** `hg_black_lodge` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > A mound of bones marks the entrance, a khatvanga hung with a skull and streaming black silk. As you enter, the darkness swallows sound. Something in the corner shifts — it may not be fully alive. A slow turn. A waiting smile.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask to learn `#0`
      - result: The movement stills. A bony hand gestures to a list scratched into the wall. Spells. Prices. No explanation offered.
    - [blue] Say nothing at the door. That is the password. `secret_bearer_admitted` — requires trait: secret_bearer · result: xp: 20
      - result: It is. You are inside before you have decided whether you wanted to be, and what is discussed there is not written down anywhere, including here.
    - [grey] Back out `#2`
      - result: You step back into the pale light. The khatvanga watches you leave.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_body_possessi:
- **Uninvited Guest** `hg_body_possession` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > One of your party stops walking. Turns around. Smiles.
    >
    > It is not their smile. The face is doing something faces do not do, and when it speaks the voice is right and the cadence is entirely wrong: "Oh, this is a *good* one. Strong legs. Do you know how long I've been on foot?"
  - choices:
    - [grey] Beat it out `beat_out` — result: hp_loss: {'amount': 'light', 'target': 'random'} · add_trait: harrowed
      - result: It abandons the body the instant real damage starts — vetala are pragmatists — and comes out fighting in its own shape, furious about the inconvenience.
    - [grey] Negotiate for its departure `bargain` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > It wants passage, not the body specifically — it is simply tired of walking. You pay it off. It leaves without argument and with genuine thanks, and your companion drops to their knees swearing in a language nobody knew they spoke.
    - [blue] Put it out properly `exorcise` — requires white_magic 3 · result: xp: 20 · pressure: space-10
      - result:
        > The rite is short and extremely unpleasant for everyone in the room. It comes out backwards, complaining bitterly about professional courtesy, and is gone before it hits the ground. Your companion is fine. Your companion is going to want to talk about this later.
    - [blue] Whatever is in there is in one of yours. Do not let go. `grudge_bearer_holds_on` — requires trait: grudge_bearer · result: xp: 22 · pressure: water-8
      - result:
        > You do not let go. This is the one circumstance in which the thing that is wrong with you is exactly the thing required.
        >
        > It tries several exits. You are still holding the arm at the end of it, and the face that comes back is the right one.
    - [blue] It is in there. Ask it things while it is `question` — requires black_magic 4 · result: xp: 26 · gold: 80 · items: ['item_random'] · pressure: space-15
      - result:
        > A possessing spirit is, briefly, a captive audience — it cannot leave without giving up the body, and it does not want to give up the body. You spend a fascinating and deeply unethical twenty minutes interrogating it about the charnel grounds, the courts, and who exactly rules here. Then you let it out. Your companion is going to want to talk about this too, and rather more loudly.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bog_hermit:
- **Bog Hermit** `hg_bog_hermit` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > A gaunt figure crouches in the reed beds, sorting through bundles of grey-green herbs with practiced hands. It is alive — or near enough to count. It looks up without alarm.
    >
    > "You find herbs growing in the shade," it says by way of greeting, as if this explains everything. It holds up a sprig of something. "Helps with the rot. Mostly."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Ask what the herbs are for `ask_herbs` — result: xp: 4 · items: ['herb_bundle']
      - result: "Keep the living alive. Slow the dead down. Somewhere in between there's a tea that tastes almost good." It hands you a bundle without ceremony. You take it.
    - [blue] Discuss the pharmacopoeia of the dead realm `medicine_check` — requires medicine 2 · result: xp: 14
      - result:
        > You name what you recognise. The hermit corrects you once, with precision, then settles into a real conversation — the first, you suspect, it has had in some time. You leave knowing more than you arrived with.
    - [blue] Sit with it a while — you have nowhere better to be `yoga_meditation` — requires yoga 1 · result: xp: 8
      - result: You sit. The hermit works. The bog makes its sounds. After a long silence it says: "Most people run through here." Another silence. "Thank you for not running."
    - [grey] Ask if it trades `trade`
      - result:
        > "I trade in knowledge, mostly. I already have everything else I need." It gestures at the grey sky, the toxic water, the rustling reeds. It seems to mean it. You move on.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_arena_ev:
- **The Bone Pit** `hg_bone_arena_event` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > A circular pit ringed with skull-topped posts. Skeletons sit in the stands, clicking their jaws in anticipation. A skeleton announcer with an elaborate wig of woven hair calls out over the crowd: "Fresh meat! Who wants to test the newcomer?"
  - choices:
    - [grey] Step into the pit `accept` — result: xp: 10 · gold: moderate
      - result: The crowd clacks with approval.
    - [yellow] Bet on a fight instead `bet` — requires roll luck vs normal · success: gold: moderate
      - success: The underdog wins in a way no one predicted. You collect double.
      - failure: The favorite wins. Of course it does.
    - [blue] Demand to fight the champion directly `fight_champion` — requires strength 15 · result: xp: 18 · gold: large · items: ['item_random']
      - result: The announcer's wig falls off from excitement. The crowd goes silent.
    - [yellow] Work the crowd as an entertainer instead `work_crowd` — requires roll performance vs normal · success: xp: 8 · gold: small
      - success: You become the entertainment. The skeletons appreciate variety. Tips rain down from the stands — mostly coins, occasionally something that used to be a coin.
      - failure: Booing. A rib bone bounces off your head. The announcer wags a finger: "Not what they came for, friend."
    - [blue] There is money moving in those tiers. `gambler_finds_odds` — requires trait: gambler · result: xp: 15 · gold: small
      - result:
        > There is, and the odds are being set by someone who has not watched the third fighter closely enough.
        >
        > You have. You bet accordingly and collect with a straight face.
    - [blue] You are not going to sit in the tiers. `duelist_steps_down` — requires trait: duelist · result: xp: 30 · gold: small · hp_loss: {'amount': 'light', 'target': 'random'}
      - result:
        > You were never going to sit in the tiers. You are over the rail before the current bout has finished and the crowd's noise changes shape.
        >
        > It is close. You win it, barely, and the barely is what they will remember.
    - [blue] Propose an archery contest as an alternative spectacle `archery_contest` — requires ranged 3 · result: xp: 10 · gold: moderate
      - result:
        > The announcer considers with a long click of its jaw. 'Unusual. We have never done that.' A pause. 'We will try it.'
        >
        > Targets are assembled from spare ribs and skulls with remarkable speed. The contest draws a crowd intrigued by novelty. You hit every target cleanly. The skeletons are not sure if they like this more or less than combat — but they are watching.
        >
        > The gold reflects the attendance.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_bridge:
- **The Bone Bridge** `hg_bone_bridge` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > A bridge of interlocking bones spans a chasm of howling darkness. Halfway across, a figure blocks the way — a massive bone horror, assembled from dozens of skeletons, looming in perfect silence. It does not speak. It does not need to.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Fight it head-on `fight_headon`
      - result: (empty)
    - [blue] Look for the binding spell `find_weakness` — requires awareness 15 · result: xp: 8
      - result: There — the keystone bone, the one the spell anchors to. If that goes, the rest follows.
    - [yellow] Collapse the bridge behind you and leap `collapse_leap` — requires roll finesse vs difficult · success: xp: 12
      - success:
        > You trigger the collapse and run. The bridge drops away beneath you and you catch the far edge with both hands, hauling yourself over as the horror falls into the dark below.
      - failure: You both go over. You catch the edge. It does not.
    - [blue] It is made of people and it is over a hole that howls. `timid_will_not_cross` — requires trait: timid · result: xp: 22 · supplies: {'food': -4} · pressure: air-12
      - result:
        > It is, and you cannot, and the party has to spend an hour finding a way that does not involve it.
        >
        > The hour costs supplies. Nobody says anything about it, which somehow does not help.
    - [blue] Somebody crosses first or nobody crosses. `brave_goes_across` — requires trait: brave · result: xp: 12 · pressure: air+8
      - result:
        > You go. The bridge says things while you are on it, in several voices, and you keep walking through all of them.
        >
        > On the far side you find you have to sit down for a moment before waving the others over.
    - [blue] Sing to the people inside it `sing_lullaby` — requires performance 3 · result: xp: 20
      - result:
        > You sing something simple, something that belonged to someone once. The horror shudders. The assembled bones tremble against each other. One by one, the fragments that were people hear something they recognize. The thing steps aside, shaking. You cross in silence.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_collecto:
- **Bone Collector** `hg_bone_collector` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > He works the graveyard with a handcart and a system, and he is extremely particular: he takes only certain bones, only from certain graves, and he is keeping a tally on a wax tablet.
    >
    > "Femurs," he says, before you can ask. "Matched pairs. You would be amazed how hard that is."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave him to it `leave`
      - result: The handcart creaks away between the mounds. He is whistling.
    - [grey] Ask what he is building `ask` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > "A bridge," he says, with the patience of a man who gets asked a lot. "Over the chasm on the north road. Been at it eleven years." He shows you the plans. They are competent. He is entirely serious.
    - [blue] Help him find matched pairs `help` — requires medicine 3 · result: xp: 18 · items: ['item_random'] · supplies: {'scrap': 6}
      - result:
        > You know what he does not: matched femurs are far easier to find if you stop opening random graves and start reading the markers for age at death. Inside an hour you have found him six pairs, which is better than his last two months. He is so pleased he gives you his spare tools and a genuinely useful map of the graveyard's dry routes.
    - [blue] Ask whether the dead consented to being a bridge `ethics` — requires yoga 3 · result: xp: 20 · pressure: earth+15
      - result:
        > He stops the cart. It is clear nobody has ever put it to him and equally clear he has put it to himself, many times, at night. "They're not using them," he says, and then, after a while: "I ask. Every one. If it feels wrong I put it back." He shows you the reject pile. It is much larger than the cart.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_gate_kee:
- **Bone Gate Keeper** `hg_bone_gate_keeper` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > The pass through the ossuary wall runs beneath an arch of ten thousand fused skulls. Before it stands a skeleton formation in ancient parade order — warriors, archers, and at their center a bone horror wearing the rusted regalia of a gate captain.
    >
    > Its jaw grinds open: "State. Your. Dead."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Break the formation `fight`
      - result: (empty)
    - [grey] Name your dead, honestly, one by one `name_dead` — result: xp: 10
      - result:
        > You speak the names — companions lost, enemies slain, the lives that ended so you could stand here. The captain's skull tilts with each one, counting. When you finish, the formation parts with a sound like dry applause.
    - [blue] Command them in the tongue of the dead `command` — requires black_magic 4 · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > Your word of command cracks across the pass like a whip. The formation snaps to attention — and holds it, rigid, as you walk through their ranks. The captain's eye sockets track you the whole way.
    - [blue] Return the salute and inspect the honor guard `inspect` — requires leadership 3 · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > You walk the line like a visiting general. Halfway down the rank, the captain decides you are worth testing — but formation discipline binds most of its troops to their posts.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_library:
- **The Bone Library** `hg_bone_library` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > Shelves of bone hold scrolls of dried skin. A bespectacled silver skeleton moves between them, filing and organizing with tireless precision. It turns at your approach.
    >
    > "Knowledge doesn't decay. My work today may help somebody in a thousand years. What can I do for you?"
  - choices:
    - [blue] Research a subject `research` — requires learning 3 · result: xp: 16
      - result: The librarian pulls scrolls without hesitation, knowing exactly where everything is. What you find goes beyond what you expected to find.
    - [grey] Ask about the realm's history `ask_history` — result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > The librarian settles into it with obvious pleasure. The history of the hungry ghost realm is longer than you expected and stranger. You come away with the sense that this place has its own logic, older than any of the beings currently living in it.
    - [grey] Offer a book from the living world `offer_book` — result: xp: 10 · items: ['spell_random']
      - result:
        > The librarian takes it with both hands, holding it carefully away from the bone shelves as if it might be infectious in the best possible way. "I have nothing like this. Nothing written after the living left." It opens the rare section.
    - [yellow] Steal a rare scroll `steal_scroll` — requires roll finesse vs difficult · success: items: ['spell_random']
      - success: You find what you want and leave with it. The librarian doesn't notice.
      - failure: The librarian looks at you. Then at the scroll. Then at you again — not angry, just deeply, genuinely sad. You put it back.
    - [blue] You are not leaving a library. Be reasonable. `curious_stays` — requires trait: curious · result: xp: 8
      - result:
        > The silver skeleton adjusts its spectacles and produces, from somewhere, a second chair.
        >
        > What you find in four hours is not what you were looking for and is considerably better: a name, an obligation, and where the obligation was last recorded.
    - [blue] Do not read them. Index them. `sharp_memory_indexes` — requires trait: sharp_memory · result: xp: 12
      - result:
        > You go through the shelf-marks rather than the scrolls, which the librarian watches with mounting professional respect.
        >
        > By evening you hold the shape of the whole collection, and the shape has a gap in it exactly where something was removed.
    - [blue] Ask if they'd teach you a few things `ask_teach` — requires persuasion 2
      - result: "Well, I suppose. Why not." It pulls a selection of relevant scrolls and begins.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_merchant:
- **Bone Merchant** `hg_bone_merchant_event` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > A skeleton in a tattered merchant's robe sits behind a blanket of wares laid on the dry earth — wrapped bundles, clay jars, glinting objects of uncertain purpose. It clicks its jaw merrily as you approach.
    >
    > "Ah! Customers! Or at least, beings capable of carrying things away! Welcome, welcome — the overhead is low and the bones are FREE."
  - choices:
    - [grey] Browse the wares `browse`
      - result: (empty)
    - [blue] Negotiate the prices down `trade_skill` — requires trade 2 · result: xp: 5
      - result:
        > You counter its opening price with calm authority, citing comparable goods in the living world. The skeleton clacks its teeth together in what might be admiration. "You know your market. Fine — take it for less."
    - [yellow] Wait for its attention to wander and pocket something `rob` — requires roll finesse vs easy · success: items: ['item_random']
      - success:
        > The skeleton turns to argue with a passing rolang. Your hand moves before you've quite decided to move it. By the time it looks back, you're innocently studying the sky.
      - failure: The skeleton's eye sockets swivel with unsettling precision. "I may be dead, but I am not BLIND." It produces a weapon from somewhere in its robes.
    - [yellow] Tell a skeleton joke `comedy` — requires roll comedy vs easy · success: xp: 5 · items: ['item_random']
      - success:
        > "...and the skeleton said, 'I just don't have the guts for it!'" The merchant clacks its jaw so hard a tooth falls out. "HA! Oh — oh, that's GOOD. I haven't laughed like that since — well, since I had muscles to laugh with. Here, take this. Consider it payment for services rendered."
      - failure: The merchant stares at you with hollow sockets. "Was that... a joke? Was it supposed to be funny?" Uncomfortable silence. You browse its wares.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_raft:
- **Bone Raft** `hg_bone_raft` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text: A crude raft of lashed femurs floats slowly past on the current. Something wrapped in waxed cloth sits in the middle. It's addressed to someone.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Let it drift by `let_drift`
      - result: Whoever it's for, it's not you.
    - [yellow] Grab it before it floats out of reach `grab_it` — requires roll finesse vs trivial · success: xp: 8 · gold: small · items: ['health_potion'] · failure: hp_loss: {'amount': 'light', 'target': 'all'}
      - success: You snag it. The cloth is still dry inside.
      - failure: You lean too far. You get wet. The raft keeps going.
    - [blue] Notice the name on the address — read it before it's gone `read_address` — requires awareness 14 · result: xp: 28 · flags: {'found_bone_raft_name': True}
      - result: You can't retrieve it. But you read the name. It means something, even if you're not sure what yet.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_shrine:
- **Bone Shrine** `hg_bone_shrine` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > Skulls set into a cairn in a spiral, each one facing outward, each one with a small offering wedged into the eye socket — a coin, a bead, a folded scrap.
    >
    > It is either a place of great devotion or a place of great warning, and the two are not always different.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Pass without touching anything `leave`
      - result: Every socket you pass is looking somewhere else. That is the intended effect and it works.
    - [grey] Add your own offering to an empty socket `offer` — result: xp: 12 · buffs: [{'stat': 'armor', 'amount': 4, 'combats_remaining': 2}]
      - result:
        > There is exactly one empty socket, at the centre of the spiral, and it takes your coin as though it had been waiting for that specific denomination. The air over the cairn goes briefly warm.
    - [yellow] Empty the sockets `rob` — requires roll finesse vs difficult · success: xp: 12 · gold: 190
      - success: Forty-odd offerings, some of them very old and one of them gold. You are three miles away before you stop feeling watched, and you never entirely stop.
      - failure: The spiral is a ward and the offerings are what holds it closed. The third socket you empty opens it.
    - [blue] Read the spiral `read_spiral` — requires ritual 3 · result: xp: 22
      - result:
        > It is a containment, wound outward, and the offerings are the seal — each one a small debt paid on behalf of whatever is under the cairn. It has been maintained by passing strangers for centuries without any of them knowing what they were maintaining. You pay your share, tighten the two sockets that had gone loose, and leave it in better repair than you found it.
rendered.Events › hungry_ghost › hg_bone_tower:
- **Bone Tower** `hg_bone_tower` — realm: hungry_ghost
  - text:
    > Nine storeys of fused bone, tapering, with a stair spiralling up the outside and no rail. It serves no obvious purpose. Nothing lives in it. It simply goes up.
    >
    > At the base, cut into the lowest course, one word in an old script: HIGHER.
  - choices:
    - [grey] Leave it standing `leave`
      - result: It is visible from a very long way off, in every direction, for the rest of the day.
    - [yellow] Climb it `climb` — requires roll finesse vs difficult · success: xp: 22 · items: ['item_random'] · pressure: air+20 · failure: xp: 6 · hp_loss: {'amount': 'light', 'target': 'random'} · pressure: air-12
      - success:
        > Nine storeys of no rail. At the top there is a flat platform, a stone bench, and a view of the entire charnel grounds — every fire, every court, every road — laid out like a map somebody drew for you. You sit on the bench for an hour and learn more about this realm than in all the walking that got you here.
      - failure:
        > Somewhere around the sixth storey the wind gets under the party and everyone's nerve goes at once. Coming down is worse than going up. Somebody is sick over the side from a great height.
    - [blue] Work out what it is for `read_tower` — requires learning 4 · result: xp: 20 · pressure: space+15
      - result:
        > It is a practice structure.
